(M, K, TK.) ― -b3- And A^atati AlnaAqapu , inf. n. as above, The she-camel returned her fore legs, [ drawing the feet back towards the body, and lifting them high, ] in her going. (M.) You say, maA A^aHosana A^atowa yadaYo h*ihi Aln~aAqapi , and A^atoYa yadayohaA , How good, or beautiful, is this she-camel's returning of her fore legs in her going! i. e. rajoEa yadayohaA fiY sayorihaA . A=tuwhu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. A_iytaA='N ; (T;) The palm-tree [and the tree ] bore: (S:) or put forth its fruit: or showed its being in a good state: (M, K:) or bore much: (T, M, K:) and AtA=' signifies also the increasing, or thriving, of seed-produce. (T.) ― -b2- And A^atati AlmaA$iyapN , inf. n. A_itaA='N , [in a copy of the M A^ataA='N ,] The cattle, or camels &c., increased, or yielded increase. (M, K. sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1, q. v. -A2- A way, course, mode, or manner. (M, K.) You say, of speech, or language, (M,) and of a speaker, or reciter of a xuTobap , (IAar, M,) maA zaAla EalaY A^atow waAHd It, and he, ceased not to follow one [ uniform ] way, &c. (M.) -A3- An impulsion; a propulsion; particularly an act of shooting an arrow from a bow: so in a trad., where it is said, kun~aA naromiY AlA^atowayoni We used to shoot one shooting and two shootings; meaning, of arrows from bows, after the prayer of sunset. (TA.) -A4- Death: or [so in the T, but in the K “and,”] a trial; or an affliction. (T, K.) You say, A^ataY EalaY fulaAnK A^atowN Death came upon such a one: or a trial; or an affliction. (ISh, T.) And A_ino A^ataY Eal~aY A^atowN fagulAmiY Hur~N If I die, [or if death befall me, ] my slave shall be free. (T.) ― -b2- A vehement sickness or disease: (T, K:) or the fracture of an arm, or of a leg. (T.) -A5- A gift. (S, K.) ― -b2- Butter; (S;) as also ↓ A^ataA='N , (A,) or ↓ A_itaA='N . (TA: [in which it is said to be like kitaAbN ; but this I think a mistake: see A^ataA='N below.]) You say, when a skin of milk is agitated, and its butter comes, qado jaA='a A^atowuhu [ Its butter has come ]. (S, TA.) And you say, ↓ labanN *uw AtA='K Milk having butter. (A, TA.) -A6- A great body or corporeal form or person ( $axoSN EaZiymN ). (AZ, Sgh, K.)

sourceDefinition: (S, M, Sgh, K) and A^utiY~N [respecting which see what follows] and A_itiY~N , (Sgh, K,) of all which, the first is said by A'Obeyd to be the form used by the Arabs, (TA,) [and all belong to art. AtY , as well as to the present art.,] and ↓ A^ataAwiY~N (M, Sgh, K) and A^utaAwiY~N and A_itaAwiY~N , (Sgh, K,) all these, and the three preceding them, mentioned by Sgh on the authority of AA, but the last of all said by him to be strange, (TA,) A rivulet for which a man makes a way or channel, or an easy course or passage, to his land: (S, M, K:) or a torrent, or flow of water, from another region or quarter: (M, K: [both these meanings mentioned in the M in art. Atw , and the former in art. Aty also, of that work:]) or A^atiY~N signifies a conduit of water; and any channel in which water is made to have an easy course; as also A^utiY~N , mentioned by Sb; or, as some say, this is a pl.: (M:) or any rivulet: (As, T:) or a rivulet less than the [ trench called ] nuw^oY : (IB:) and sayolN A^atY~N (Lh, T, S, M) and A^ataAwiY~N , (Lh, S, M,) a torrent, or flow of water, that comes one knows not whence: (M:) or that comes when the rain that has produced it has not fallen upon the people to whom it comes: (Lh, S, M:) or that comes from a land upon which rain has fallen to a land upon which rain has not fallen. (T, Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, (T, M,) or the reverse is the case, (T, M, Msb,) all the words above, (AA, T, K,) or A^atiYa and A^ataAwiY~u , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, [the last said in the T to be the most approved,]) A stranger; or a man not of one's own people, or not of one's own kindred: (AA, T, S, M, Mgh:) or a man who asserts his relation to a people of whom he is not: (Msb:) or A^atiY~N signifies one who is among a people of whom he is not: (As, T:) and A^ataAwiY~N , a stranger, who is not in his own country; or, accord. to Ks, a stranger, who is not in his own home: (T:) the pl. of this last is A^ataAwiy~uwna : (S:) [the fem. sing. is A^ataAwy~apN :] and the pl. fem. A^ataAwy~aAtN . (T, S, M.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. xaraAjN [i. e. A tax, a tribute, or an impost ], (T, S, M, K,) such, for instance, as is levied on land, (TA in the present art.,) and such as is imposed on a slave; (TA in art. Drb ;) and any tax or other exaction that is taken by compulsion, or against the will, or that is apportioned to a people: (M: [in the TA “to a place” instead of “to a people:”]) and also, a bribe: or, (accord. to some, M,) particularly, a bribe for water: (M, K:) the pl. is A^ataAwaY , (T, M, K, TA, [but in some copies of the K A^ataAwiY~u , and accord. to copies of the S it is A^ataAwK , being written, with the article, AlA^ataAwiY ; both of which appear to be wrong; for it is said to be] like EalaAwaY and haraAwaY , pls. of EilaAwapN and hiraAwapN , (M, TA,) and like sakaAraY ; (TA;) changed, [in the accus. case, with the article prefixed,] at the end of a verse, into AlA^ataAwiyaA , for the sake of the rhyme: (M, TA:) this occurs in a verse of El-Jaadee: (S:) it has also for a pl. A_itaAwaAtN , (T,) and A^ut~ay , [in the CK, erroneously, AatiY~N ,] which is extr., (M, K,) as though its sing. were A^utowapN , being like ru$~aY , pl. of ru$owapN , (M,) and like Eur~aY , pl. of EurowapN . (TA.) You say, A^ad~aY A_itaAwapa A^aroDihi [ He payed the tax of his land ]; i. e. xaraAjahaA : and Duribato Ealayohimu AlA_itaAwapu [ The tax, or tribute, or impost, was imposed upon them ]; i. e. AljibaAyapu : and some assert it to be tropical. (TA.) You say also, $akama faAhu biAloA_itaAwapi [ He stopped (lit. bitted ) his mouth with the bribe ]; i. e. baAl~ri$owapi . (TA.)

definition: [an epithet variously explained].
sourceDefinition: [an epithet variously explained]. One says, in reviling, (S, TA,) but not when the object is a female, (TA,) A^aboEada Aall~`hu AlA^axira , (Th, S, A, &c.,) and ↓ AlA=xira (M, &c.,) or this latter is wrong, (Meshárik of 'Iyád, Mgh, Msb,) as is also ↓ AlA=xara , (Meshárik of 'Iyád,) meaning (tropical:) May God alienate, or estrange, from good, or prosperity, or may God curse, him who is absent from us, (A, Msb, TA,) distant, or remote: (A, Msb:) or the outcast; the alienated: (Msb:) or him who is put back, and cast away: so says Sh: or, accord. to ISh, him who is put back, and remote from good: and he adds, I think that ↓ AlA^axiyr is meant: (L:) or the base fellow : or the most ignoble: or the miserable wretch: (Et-Tedmuree and others:) or the last speaker: (Nawádir of Th:) or AlAxr is here a metonymy for the devil: (Lb:) it is a word used [for the reason explained voce A^aboEadu ] in relating what has been said by one of two persons cursing each other, to the other; (Expositions of the Fs;) and the phrase above mentioned is meant to imply a prayer for those who are present [by its contrasting them with the person to whom it directly applies]. (A.) One also says, laA maroHabFA biAloA^axiri , [alluding to a particular person,] meaning [ May the place, or land, not be ample, or spacious, or roomy,] to the remote from good. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of Mázin, A_in~a AlA^axiraqado zanaY Verily the outcast, (Mgh, Msb,) or he who is remote, and held back, from good, , (Mgh, * TA,) hath committed adultery, or fornication: the speaker meaning himself; (Mgh, Msb;) as though he were an outcast. (Msb.) And in another trad. it is said, AlmasoA^alapu A^axiru kasobi Almaro'i Begging is the most ignoble [mode of] gain of man: but El-Khattábee relates it with medd, [i. e. ↓ A=xiru ,] explaining it as meaning begging is the last thing whereby man seeks sustenance when unable to gain [by other means]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: a subst., of the measure A^afoEalu , but implying the meaning of an epithet, (S,) from A^ax~ara in the sense of taA^ax~ara , (TA,) Another; the other; a thing [or person ] other than the former or first; (L;) i. q. gayorN ; (K;) as in the phrases, rajulN A=xaru another man, and vawobN A=xaru another garment or piece of cloth: (TA:) or one of two things [or persons ]; (S, Sgh, Msb;) as when you say, jaA='a Alqawomu fawaAHidN yafoEalu ka*aA waA=xaru ka*aA The people came, and one was doing thus, and one [i. e. another] thus: (Sgh, Msb:) originally meaning more backward: (TA:) fem. ↓ A^uxoraY (S, Msb, K) and ↓ A^uxoraApN ; (K) which latter is not well known: (MF:) pl. masc. A=xaruwna and A^uxaru ; (S, K;) [the latter irreg. as such;] and, applied to irrational things, A^awaAxiru , like as A^afaADilu is pl. of A^afoDalu : (Msb:) and pl. fem. A_uxorayaAtN and A_uxaru ; (S, Msb, K;) which latter is imperfectly decl.; for an epithet of the measure A^afoEalu which is accompanied by mino has no [dual nor] pl. nor fem. as long as it is indeterminate; but when it has the article Al prefixed to it, or is itself prefixed to another noun which it governs in the gen. case, it has a dual and a pl. and a fem.; but it is not so with A=xaru ; for it has a fem. [and dual] and pl. without mino and without the article Al and without its being prefixed to another noun: you say, mararotu biraxulK A=xara , and birijaAlK A^uxara and A=xariyna , and biANmoraA^apK , and binisowapK [ I passed by another man, and by other men, and by another woman, and by other women; ] therefore, as it [namely A_uxaru ] is thus made to deviate from its original form, [i. e. A=xaru , (I' Ak p. 287,) which is of a class of words used, when indeterminate, alike as sing. and dual and pl.,] and is [essentially and originally] an epithet, it is imperfectly decl., though a pl.: but when you name thereby a man, it is perfectly decl., when inderminate, accord. to Akh, or imperfectly decl. accord. to Sb. (S, L.) The dim. of A=xaru is ↓ A^uwayoxiru ; the A with the ' suppressed following the same rule as the A in DaAribN : (TA:) and the dim. of A_uxoraY is ↓ A^uxayoraY . (S.) See also AlA^uxoraY voce A=xirN . ― -b2- laA A^afoEaluhu A^uxoraY All~ayaAliY , (S, K,) or AxrY Almanuwni , (K,) means I will not do it ever: (S, K:) or the latter, I will not do it to the end of time. (S.) And A^uxoraY Alqawomi , The last of the people. (S, K.) One says, jaA='a fiY A^uxoraY Alqawomi He came among the last of the people. (TA.) And jaA='i fiY A^uxorayaAti Aln~aAsi He came among those who were the last of the people. (S, A, K.) [See also A=xirN .] ― -b3- In A^aboEada All~`hu AlA=xara , the last word is a mistake for AlA^axira q. v. (Meshárik of 'Iyád.)

A=xaruwna and A^uxaru ; (S, K;) [the latter irreg. as such;] and, applied to irrational things, A^awaAxiru , like as A^afaADilu is pl. of A^afoDalu : (Msb:) and pl. fem. A_uxorayaAtN and A_uxaru ; (S, Msb, K;) which latter is imperfectly decl.; for an epithet of the measure A^afoEalu which is accompanied by mino has no [dual nor] pl. nor fem. as long as it is indeterminate; but when it has the article Al prefixed to it, or is itself prefixed to another noun which it governs in the gen. case, it has a dual and a pl. and a fem.; but it is not so with A=xaru ; for it has a fem. [and dual] and pl. without mino and without the article Al and without its being prefixed to another noun: you say, mararotu biraxulK A=xara , and birijaAlK A^uxara and A=xariyna , and biANmoraA^apK , and binisowapK [ I passed by another man, and by other men, and by another woman, and by other women; ] therefore, as it [namely A_uxaru ] is thus made to deviate from its original form, [i. e. A=xaru , (I' Ak p. 287,) which is of a class of words used, when indeterminate, alike as sing. and dual and pl.,] and is [essentially and originally] an epithet, it is imperfectly decl., though a pl.: but when you name thereby a man, it is perfectly decl., when inderminate, accord. to Akh, or imperfectly decl. accord. to Sb. (S, L.) The dim. of A=xaru is ↓ A^uwayoxiru ; the A with the ' suppressed following the same rule as the A in DaAribN : (TA:) and the dim. of A_uxoraY is ↓ A^uxayoraY . (S.) See also AlA^uxoraY voce A=xirN . ― -b2- laA A^afoEaluhu A^uxoraY All~ayaAliY , (S, K,) or AxrY Almanuwni , (K,) means I will not do it ever: (S, K:) or the latter, I will not do it to the end of time. (S.) And A^uxoraY Alqawomi , The last of the people. (S, K.) One says, jaA='a fiY A^uxoraY Alqawomi He came among the last of the people. (TA.) And jaA='i fiY A^uxorayaAti Aln~aAsi He came among those who were the last of the people. (S, A, K.) [See also A=xirN .] ― -b3- In A^aboEada All~`hu AlA=xara , the last word is a mistake for AlA^axira q. v. (Meshárik of 'Iyád.)

(TK in art. jhm .) You say, jaA='i A=xirFA and ↓ A^axiyrFA and ↓ A^uxurFA and ↓ biA^axarapK , all meaning the same [ He came lastly, or latterly ]: and in like manner, ↓ maA Earafotuhu A_il~aA A^axiyrFA and ↓ Al~A biA^axarapK [ I did not know it save at the last, or lastly, or latterly ]: (S:) or ↓ jaA='i A^axiyrFA and ↓ A^uxurFA and ↓ A^axorapN and ↓ biA^uxorapK and ↓ A^uxarapK and ↓ biA^uxarapK (K,) or ↓ A^uxorapN and ↓ biA^uxorapK (Lh, L,) and biA=xirapK (TA) and ↓ A_ixoriy~aA and ↓ A^uxoriy~aA and ↓ A_ixiriy~aA and ↓ A=xiriy~aA (K) mean he came lastly of everything. sourceDefinition: A court; or an open or a wide space in front of a house, or extending from its sides; (S, M, K;) a dial. var. of waSiydN , (S,) which is the more common form: (M:) or the extreme and exterior part of a house: (Mirkát el-Loghah, and Meyd, as rendered by Golius:) or an intermediate place between the threshold or door and the house; a place which looks neither upon the public nor upon the interior parts, whether it be an area or a vestibule. (Ibn-Maaroof, as rendered by Golius.)

definition: A hill, or mound, syn.
sourceDefinition: A hill, or mound, syn. tal~N , (Msb, K,) [in an absolute sense, or] of what is termed quf~ [q. v.], (K,) or, as in the M, (TA,) of a single collection of stones: or it is inferior to mountains: or a place that is more elevated than what is around it, and is rugged, not to the degree of being stone: (K:) or an isolated mountain: (K voce jabalN :) or an eminence like what is termed raAbiyap : a collection of stones in one place, sometimes rugged and sometimes not rugged: (Msb:) or i. q. quf~N , except that the Akmp is higher and greater: (ISh, TA:) or what is higher than the quf~ , compact and round, rising into the sky, abounding with stones: (TA:) pl. A^akamaAtN (S, Msb) and ↓ A^akamN , [or this is rather a coll. gen. n. of which A^akamapN is the n. un.,] (S, Msb, K,) and A_ikaAmN , (K, TA,) or this is pl. of A^akamN , (S, Msb, TA,) and A^ukumN , (K, TA,) or this is pl. of A_ikaAmN , (S, Msb, TA,) and A=kaAmN [a pl. of pauc.], (K,) or this is pl. of A^ukumN , (S, Msb, TA,) and A=kumN [which is also a pl. of pauc.], (IJ, K,) or this is a pl. of A^akamN : (TA:) IHsh says that A^akamN is the only word like vamarN in its series of pls.; for its sing. [or n. un.] is A^akamapN , and the pl. of this [or the coll. gen. n.] is A^akamN , and the pl. of this is A_ikaAmN , and the pl. of this is A^ukumN , and the pl. of this is A=kaAmN , and the pl. of this is A^akaAmiymu [or A^awaAkiymu ?]. (MF in art. vmr .) It is said in a prov., used in ridiculing any one who has told of his committing some fault, not desiring to reveal it, jusotumuwniY wawaraA='a AlA^akamapi maA waraA='ahaA [in which I think the first word to be a mistranscription, for jiy^otumuwniY , and the literal meaning to be, Ye have come to me; but behind the hill is what is behind it ]: related on the authority of Zeyd Ibn-Kethweh. (TA.) And one says, laA tabulo EalaY A^akampK , meaning (tropical:) Publish not what is secret of thine affair. (TA.)

[in a sense different from that explained above, i. e.] as meaning kav~arotuhu . (TA.) You say, A^amarahu bihi , (S, M, K,) and A^amarahu A_iy~aAhu , suppressing the prep., (M,) He commanded, ordered, bade, or enjoined, him to do it. (M, K.) And A^marotuka A^ano tafoEala , and litafoEala , and biA^no tafoEala , I commanded, ordered, bade, or enjoined, thee to do [such a thing]. (M.) And [you use it transitively, saying,] Ay^tmr AlA^amora He obeyed, or conformed to, the command. (S.) And laA yaA^otamiru ru$odFA He will not do right of his own accord. (A.) Imra el-Keys says, (S,) or En-Nemir Ibn-Towlab, (T,) wayaEoduw EalaY Almaro'i maA yaA^otamiro [ And that which man obeys wrongs him, or injures him ]; meaning, that which his own soul commands him to do, and which he judges to be right, but in which often is found his destruction: (S:) or, accord. to Kt, that evil which man purposes to do: (T:) or that which man does without consideration, and without looking to its result. (A 'Obeyd, T.) [See what follows.] ― -b2- He undertook a thing without consulting; (Kt, T;) as though his soul, or mind, ordered him to do it and he obeyed it: (TA:) he followed his own opinion only. (Mgh.) One says, A^amarotuhu fA^otamara waA^abaY A^ano yaA^otamira , (A, Mgh,) meaning I commanded him, but he followed his own opinion only, and refused to obey. (Mgh.) ― -b3- He formed an opinion, and consulted his own mind, and determined upon it. (Sh, T.) And Ay^tmr raA^oyahu He consulted his own mind, or judgment, respecting what was right for him to do. (Sh, T.) ― -b4- Ay^tmrwA , (A, Msb,) inf. n. Ay^otimaArN ; (S, K;) and ↓ tA=mrwA , (A,) inf. n. taA=murN , of the measure tafaAEulN ; (S;) and ↓ tA^m~rwA , (TA,) inf. n. taA^am~urN ; (K;) They consulted together: (S, * A, Msb, K: *) or Ay^tmrwA and ↓ tA=mrwA signify they commanded, ordered, bade, or enjoined, one another; like as one says, AqttlwA and tqAtlwA , and AxtSmwA and txASmwA : (T:) or Ay^tmrwA EalaY AlA^amori and Ealayohi ↓ tA=mrwA , they determined, or settled, their opinions respecting the affair, or case: (M:) and Ay^tmrwA bihi , (S, Msb,) inf. n. as above, (K,) signifies they purposed it, (S, Msb, K, *) namely, a thing, (Msb, K,) and consulted one another respecting it. (S.) It is said in the Kur [lxv. 6], waA^otamiruwA bayonakumo bimaEoruwfK And command ye, or enjoin ye, one another to do good: [such is app. the meaning,] but God best knoweth: (T:) or, accord. to Kt, purpose ye among yourselves to do good. (TA.) And in the same [xxviii. 19], A_in~a AlomalaA^a yaA^otamiruwna bika liyaqotulwuka , meaning Verily the chiefs command one another respecting thee, to slay thee: (Zj, T:) or consult together against thee, to slay thee: (AO, T:) or purpose against thee, to slay thee: (Kt, T:) but the last but one of these explanations is better than the last. (T.) ― -b5- See also 3. ― -b6- Accord. to El-Bushtee, Ay^tmrhu also signifies He gave him permission: but this has not been heard from an Arab. (Az, TA.)

definition: A command; an order; a bidding; an injunction; a decree; an ordinance; a prescript: (S, * Msb, * TA, &c.:) pl. A^awaAmiru : (S, Msb, &c.:) so accord. to common usage; and some writers of authority...
sourceDefinition: A command; an order; a bidding; an injunction; a decree; an ordinance; a prescript: (S, * Msb, * TA, &c.:) pl. A^awaAmiru : (S, Msb, &c.:) so accord. to common usage; and some writers of authority justify and explain it by saying that A^amorN is [originally] maA^omuwurN bihi ; that it is then changed to the measure faAEilN ; [i. e., to A=mirN ;] like A^amorN EaArifN , which is originally maEoruwfN ; and Eiy$apN rADiyapN , originally maroDiy~apN ; &c.; [and then, to A^amorN ;] and that faAEilN becomes in the pl. fawaAEilu ; so that A^awaAmaru is the pl. of maA_omuwrN : others say that it has this form of pl. to distinguish it from A^amorN in the sense of HaAlN [&c.], in which sense it has for its pl. A^umuwrN . (Msb, TA.) [But I think that A^awaAmiru may be properly and originally pl. of A=mirapN , for A=yapN A=mirapN , or the like. MF says that, accord. to the T and M, the pl. of A^amorN in the sense explained in the beginning of this paragraph is A^umuwrN : but he seems to have founded his assertion upon corrupted copies of those works; for in the M, I find nothing on this point; and in the T, not, as he says, AlA^amoruDid~u Aln~ahoYa waAHidu AlA^umuwr , but qaAla All~ayovu AlA^amoru maEoruwfN naqiyDu Aln~ahoYi waAHidu AlA^umuwri , evidently meaning that A^amorN signifies the contr. of nahoYN , and is also, in another sense, the sing. of A^umuwrN .] [Hence,] A^uwluw AlA^amori Those who hold command or rule, and the learned men. (M, K. [See Kur iv. 62.]) And A^amoruAll~`hi The threatened punishment of God: so in the Kur x. 25, and xi. 42, and xvi.1; in which last place occur the words, A^atay A^amoru All~`hi falaA tasotaEojiluwhu , meaning The threatened punishment ordained of God hath, as it were, come: so near is it, that it is as though it had already come: therefore desire not ye to hasten it. (Zj, M, TA.) And The purpose of God. (Bd and Jel in lxv. 3; &c.) And AlA^amoru qariybN The resurrection, or the time thereof, is near. (Mgh, from a trad.) And maA faEalotuhu Eano A^amoriY , in the Kur xviii. 81, I did it not of my own judgment: (Bd:) or, of my own choice. (Jel.) [Hence also AlA^amoru , in grammar, signifies The imperative form of a verb.] ― -b2- Also A thing; an affair; a business; a matter; a concern: a state, of a person or thing, or of persons or things or affairs or circumstances; a condition; a case: an accident; an event: an action: syn. $aA^onN : (M, F, TA:) and HaAlN , (Msb, TA,) and HaAlapN : (Msb:) and HaAdivapN : (K:) and fiEolN : (MF, TA:) and a thing that is said; a saying: (TA voce A^uwluw , at the end of art. Al :) pl. A^umuwrN ; (S, M, K, &c.;) its only pl. in the senses here explained. (TA.) You say, A^amoru fulaAnK musotaqiymN [ The affair, or the like, of such a one is in a right state ]: and Amuwruhu musotaqiymapN [ His affairs are in a right state ]. (S, A.) And $at~ata A^amorahu He dissipated, disorganized, disordered, unsettled, or broke up, his state of things, or affairs. (As, TA in art. $Eb .) [ Amr seems to be here used, as in many other instances, rather in the sense of the pl. than in that of the sing.] ― -b3- A^amorN kul~iY~N [ A universal, or general, prescript, rule, or canon ]. (Msb voce qaAEidapN , KT voce qaAnuwnN , &c.)

sourceDefinition: a subst. from A^amara [q. v.]; Possession of command; the office, and authority, of a commander, governor, lord, prince, or king; (M, * Msb, K;) as also ↓ A_imaArapN (Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ A^amaArapN ; (L, K;) but this last is by some disallowed, and is said in the Fs and its Expositions to be unknown. (MF.) It is said in a trad., laEal~aka sA='a toka A_imorapu Aboni Eam~ika Perhaps thy paternal uncle's son's possession of command hath displeased thee. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, (assumed tropical:) Increase, or abundance, or the like; as also other forms mentioned in what follows.] You say, fiY wajohi maAlika taEorifu A_imoratahu (assumed tropical:) In the face of thy property, [meaning such as consists in camels or the like, and also money,] thou knowest its increase and abundance, and its expense: (S:) or ↓ A_im~aratahu , and ↓ A_im~ratahu , which latter is a dial. var. of weak authority, and ↓ A^am~aratahu , i. e., its increase and abundance: (M:) or ↓ A_im~aratahu as meaning its prosperous state; as also ↓ A^amaAratahu , and ↓ A^amoratahu : (Ibn-Buzurj:) accord. to AHeyth, who reads ↓ tuEorafu A_im~aratuhu , the meaning is, its decrease; but the correct meaning is, its increase, as Fr explains it. (T, TA.) It is said respecting anything of which one knows what is good in it at first sight: (Lh, M:) and means, on a thing's presenting itself, thou knowest its goodness. (T.) One says also, ↓ mA^aHosana A^amaAratahumo (assumed tropical:) How good is their multiplying, and the multiplying of their offspring and of their number! (M.) And ↓ laA jaEala All~`hu fiyhi A_im~arapF (assumed tropical:) May God not make an increase to be therein. (T.)

definition: Stones: (K:) [or a heap of stones: ] or it is the n.
sourceDefinition: Stones: (K:) [or a heap of stones: ] or it is the n. un. of A^amarN , which signifies stones: (M:) or the latter signifies stones set up in order that one may be directed thereby to the right way: (Ham p. 409:) and the former also signifies a hill; (M, K;) and A^amarN is [used as] its pl.: (M:) and a sign, or mark, by which anything is known; (M, K;) as also ↓ A^amaArN and ↓ A^amaArapN ; (As, S;) and A^amarN is [used as] its pl. in this sense also: (M:) or a sign, or mark, set up to show the way; (AA, Fr;) as also ↓ A^amaArN and ↓ A^amaArahN : (K:) or a small sign, or mark, of stones, to show the way, in a waterless desert; (S;) as also ↓ A^amaArN [and ↓ A^amaArapN ]; and any sign, or mark, that is prepared: (TA:) or a structure like a manaArap [here app. meaning a tower of a mosque ], upon a mountain, wide like a house or tent, and larger, of the height of forty times the stature of a man, made in the time of 'Ád and Irem; in some instances its foundation being like a house, though it consists only of stones piled up, one upon another, cemented together with mud, appearing as though it were of natural formation: (ISh, T:) the pl. (in all the senses above, K) [or rather the coll. gen. n.,] is A^amarN . (S, K.) -A2- See also A_imorapN .

definition: and ↓ A^amaArapN A sign, mark, or token.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^amaArapN A sign, mark, or token. (As, S Mgh.) See also each voce A^amarapN , in three places. You say, hiY A^amaArapu maA bayoniY wabayonaka It is a sign, or token, of what is between me and thee. (T, * TA.) And a poet says, A_i*aA TalaEato $amosu Aln~ahaAri faA_in~ahaA A^amaArapu tasoliymiY Ealayoki fasal~imiY [ When the sun of day rises, it is a sign of my saluting thee, therefore do thou salute ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A time: (As, S, K:) so IAar explains the latter word, not particularizing the time as definite or otherwise: (M:) or a definite time: (TA:) or a time, or place, of promise or appointment; an appointed time or place; syn. mawoEidN : (M, Mgh, K:) or, accord. to some, the former word is pl. [or rather col. gen. n.] of the latter. (TA.) El- 'Ajjáj says, A_i*o rad~ahaA bikayodihi faArotad~ati A_ilay A^amaArK waA^amaAri mud~atiY When He (meaning God) brings it, (namely my soul,) by his skilful ordering, and his power, [ and it is thus brought, or it thus comes, to a set time, and ] to the time of the end of my appointed period: AmArmd~tY being as above; the former word being prefixed to the latter, governing it in the gen. case. (IB. [In the S we find waA^amaArN mud~atiY .])

definition: One having, holding, or possessing, command;
sourceDefinition: One having, holding, or possessing, command; (S;) a commander; a governor; a lord; (M, * Msb;) a prince, or king: (M, K:) fem. with p : (S, K:) pl. A_umaraA='u . (M, Msb, K.) ― -b2- A leader of the blind. (M, K.) So in the saying of El-Aashà: A_i*aAkaAna haAdiY AlfataY fiY AlbilaA diSadora AlqanaApi A^aTaAEa AlA^amiyraA [ When the young man's guide in the countries, or lands, or the like, is the top of the cane, he obeys the leader of the blind ]. (M.) ― -b3- A woman's husband. (A.) ― -b4- A neighbour. (K.) ― -b5- A person with whom one consults: (A, K:) any one of whom one begs counsel, or advice, in a case of fear. (TA.) You say, huwa A^amiyriY He is the person with whom I consult. (A.)

definition: A man who consults every one respecting his case;
sourceDefinition: A man who consults every one respecting his case; as also ↓ A^amirN and ↓ A^am~aArapN : (M:) or a man resembling [ in stupidity ] a kid: [see the latter part of this paragraph:] (Th, M:) or, as also ↓ A_im~arapN (S, M, K, &c.) and ↓ A^am~arN and ↓ A^am~arapN , (K,) a man having weak judgment, (S, K,) stupid, (T, M,) or weak, without judgment, (M, L,) or without intellect, or intelligence, (T,) who obeys the command of every one, (T, S,) who complies with what every one desires to do in all his affairs; (K;) a stupid man, of weak judgment, who says to another, Command me to execute thine affair. (IAth.) It is said in a trad., mano yuTiEo A_im~arapF laA yaA^okulo vamarapF [ He who obeys a stupid man, &c., shall not eat fruit: or the meaning is] he who obeys a stupid woman shall be debarred from good. (IAth.) ↓ A_im~arapN is applied to a woman and to a man: when it is applied to a man, the p is added to give intensiveness to the signification. (ISh.) The following saying, A_i*aA TalaEati Al$~iEoraY walaA A_im~arFA , ↓ safarFA falaA turosilo fiyhaA A_im~arapF , in rhyming prose, means [ When Sirius rises in the clear twilight, ] send not thou among them ( meaning the camels ) a man without intelligence [ in a great degree, nor one who is so in a less degree; or a woman without intelligence, nor a man without intelligence; ] to manage them. (Sh.) ― -b2- Also, (M, K,) and ↓ A_im~arapN and ↓ A^am~ara and ↓ A^um~arN , (K,) A young lamb: (M, K:) or the first ( A_imarN ) and the second, a young kid: (M, TA:) or the former of these two, a male lamb: (M, TA:) or a young male lamb: (S:) and the latter of them, a female lamb: (M, TA:) or a young female lamb. (S, M.) One says, ↓ maA lahu A_im~arN walaA A_im~arapN , meaning He has not a male lamb nor a female lamb: (M, TA:) or he has not anything. (T, S, M.)

definition: [ Wont to command ].
sourceDefinition: [ Wont to command ]. [Hence,] Aln~afosu AlA^am~aArapu [ The soul that is wont to command ]; (A;) the soul that inclines to the nature of the body, that commands to the indulgence of pleasures and sensual appetites, drawing the heart downwards, so that it is the abode of evils, and the source of culpable dispositions. (KT.) [See nafosN .]

(M in art. tmr , without ' .) ― -b6- The core, or black or inner part, or clot of blood, ( Hab~ap , M, K, or Ealaqap , TA,) and life, and blood, of the heart: (M, K:) or blood, (As, S, M, in art. tmr , and K,) absolutely: (TA:) and taA^omuwru Aln~afosi signifies the life-blood: (As, S:) or the blood of the body: (S in art. nfs :) and the life of the soul. (M, K.) ― -b7- Also, as being likened to blood, (TA,) (tropical:) Wine; and so ↓ taA^omuwrapN : (M, K:) and ― -b8- (tropical:) A dye: (M, TA:) and ― -b9- (tropical:) Saffron. (S in art. tmr .) ↓ tuw^omuriY~N (M, K) and ↓ tuwmuriY~N (S in art. tmr ) and ↓ taA^omuwriY~N and ↓ taA^omuriy~N (M, K) also signify A man, or human being. (S, * M, K.) You say, speaking of a beautiful woman, A^aHosana minohaA ↓ maA raA^ayotu tuwmuriy~aA I have not seen a human being, or creature, more beautiful than she: (S and M in art. tmr :) and maA raA^ayotu A^aHosana minohu ↓ tuwmuriy~aA [ I have not seen a man more beautiful than he ]. (T and S in art. tmr .) Accord. to some, they are used only in negative phrases; but accord. to others, they are also used in such as are affirmative. (MF.) ― -b2- Also Anything: as in the saying A^akala Al*~iy^obu Al$~aApa famaA taraka minohaA taAmuwrFA [ The wolf ate the sheep, or goat, and left not of it anything ]. (TA.)

definition: The fruit of the [trees called ] EiDaAh : (S, M, K:) n.
sourceDefinition: The fruit of the [trees called ] EiDaAh : (S, M, K:) n. un. with p : (S, M:) in its first stage it is termed fatolapN ; then, bal~apN ; then, baramapN : AHn has erred in saying that the ftlp is above the brmp [in degree]: (M:) that of every kind of EDAh is yellow, except that of the EurofuT , which is white, (S, M,) as though its filaments, or fringe-like appertenances, were cotton, and it is like the button of a shirt, or somewhat larger: (M:) that of the salam is the sweetest in odour, (S, M,) and this is yellow, and is eaten, being sweet, or pleasant: (M:) accord. to AA, the fruit of the TaloH [or acacia gummifera, which is of the trees called EDAh ]: n. un. with p : (T:) sometimes, also, baramapN is applied to a fruit of the A^araAk (M, * K, * TA) before it has become ripe and black; for when ripe, it is called marodN ; and when black, kabaAvN : (TA:) and the pl. is biraAmN (M, K) and buramN , (M,) or baramN . (K: [but the last is a coll. gen. n.]) ― -b2- Also Grapes when they are above, (M,) or when they are like, (K,) the heads of young ants. (M, K.) -A2- (tropical:) One who does not take part with others in the game called Almayosir [q. v.], (As, T, S, M, K,) nor contribute with them anything, (TA,) by reason of his avarice, (Har p. 382,) though he eats with them of the flesh-meat thereof; (As, TA;) but sometimes he shuffles, or deals forth, ( yufiyDu ,) the gaming-arrows for the players: (S in art. jmd :) likened to the barama of the A^araAk , because he is of no use: (Har ubi suprà:) and ↓ baramapN occurs in the same sense; [the man so termed being likened to a baramap of the ArAk ; or] the p being added to give intensiveness to the meaning: (M:) the pl. is A^aboraAmN . (T, S, M, K.) And hence, (tropical:) Avaricious, or niggardly; mean, or sordid: (Har ubi suprà:) or heavy, or sluggish; (K, TA;) destitute of good. (TA.) It is said in a prov., A^aboramFA qaruwnFA (tropical:) [ Art thou ( takuwnu being understood after) one taking no part with others in the game of Almysr , as is implied in the S, or art thou] heavy, or sluggish, (K, TA,) destitute of good, (TA,) yet eating two dates at once each time? (S, K, TA.)

definition: A rope composed of two twists twisted together into one;
sourceDefinition: A rope composed of two twists twisted together into one; as also ↓ muboramN : (S:) or a thread, or string, twisted of two distinct yarns or twists: (T:) or a thread, or string, twisted of white and black yarns: (Ham p. 704:) or a twisted rope in which are two colours, (A'Obeyd, S,) or two threads, or strings, of different colours, (IAar, T, M, K,) red and yellow, (M,) or red and white, (K,) sometimes (A'Obeyd, S) bound by a woman upon her waist, and upon her upper arm: (A'Obeyd, S, K:) a rope of two colours, adorned with jewels, so bound by a woman: (M, K:) or a thread, or string, (Lth, A'Obeyd, T,) with beads strung upon it, (Lth, T,) or of different colours, (A'Obeyd, T,) which a woman binds upon her waist: (Lth, A'Obeyd, T: [see also HawoTN ]:) or a string of cowries, which is bound upon the waist of a female slave. (Aboo-Sahl El-Harawee in art. bzm of the TA.) ― -b2- Anything in which are two colours (T, M, K) mixed together: (M, K:) and any two things mixed together and combined. (M.) ― -b3- An amulet (M, K, TA) that is hung upon a boy; because of the colours therein. (TA.) ― -b4- A garment, or piece of cloth, in which are silk ( qaz~ ) and flax. (T.) ― -b5- Also, (K,) or the dual thereof, (AO, T, S,) which latter is the right, (TA,) The liver and hump [of a camel ], (AO, T, S, K,) cut lengthwise, and tied round with a string or thread, or some other thing, (S, K,) in some copies of the S, or with a gut; (TA;) said to be thus called because of the whiteness of the hump and the blackness of the liver. (S, K.) So in the phrase, Ai$owi lanaA mino bariyamayohaA [ Roast thou for us some of her liver and hump, cut lengthwise, &c.]. (AO, T, S: [in copies of the K, bariymihaA : and in the CK, bariymatihaA .]) ― -b6- Also, the sing., Water mixed with other [water &c.]. (TA.) ― -b7- Tears mixed with [the collyrium termed ] A_ivomid ; (M, K;) because having two colours. (TA.) ― -b8- A mixed company of people. (S.)

definition: in the K, it is said that TrxAn signifies “ a headman, or chief, of high, or noble, rank, ” in the language of Khurásán;
sourceDefinition: in the K, it is said that TrxAn signifies “ a headman, or chief, of high, or noble, rank, ” in the language of Khurásán; and in art. qms , that qwms signifies “ a commander, ” or the like, syn. A^amiyrN ; and. qamaAmisapN , i. q. baTaAriqapN , (TA,) which is pl. of bTryq , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) as also baTaAriyqu , for which baTaAriqu is used in a verse of Aboo-Dhueyb: (TA:) it is an arabicized word; (S, TA;) [app. from the Latin “ patricius; ”] or, as some say, of the language of the rwm and of Syria: or Arabic, agreeing with the foreign word, and of the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz: accord. to El-Jawáleekee and others, in the language of the rwm it is btrk : some say that it signifies skilled in war and its affairs, in the language of the rwm ; and he who is so has rank, or office, and is sometimes made foremost, among them: (TA:) and (some say, TA) a proud and self-conceited man; (JK, K;) so says Ibn-'Abbád: (TA:) and fat; applied to a bird (JK, K) &c.: (JK:) pl. baTaAriqapN . (K.) ― -b2- [See also baTorakN , and jaAvaliyqN .]

(S.)

sourceDefinition: aor. yaboqaY , inf. n. baqaA='N (JK, S, Msb, K) and baAqiyapN ; (Msb; [but see this latter below;]) [and accord. to the CK, baqFY and baqoYN ; but this is a mistake; wabaqaY w baqoyFA being there erroneously put for baqaY baqoyFA , explained by what here follows;] and baqaY , [by some written baqaA ,] (JK, S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (JK,) inf. n. baqoYN , (K,) of the dial. of Belhárith Ibn-Kaab, (TA,) or of that of Teiyi, (JK, S, TA,) who in like manner say baqato instead of baqayato , (S, TA,) and the like is done in other verbs of the same class, (S, Msb,) whether the kesreh and the Y be original, as in baqiYa and nasiYa and faniYa , or accidental, as in the pass. verbs hudiYa and buniYa ; (Msb;) [ He, or] it, namely, a thing, remained, continued, lasted, endured: and was, or became, permanent, or perpetual; or continued, lasted, or existed, incessantly, always, endlessly, or for ever: syn. daAma , and vabata ; (Msb;) contr. of faniYa : (K:) baqaA='N signifies a thing's remaining, continuing, lasting, or enduring, in its first state, to a period determined by the will of God, either with respect to its corporeal substance, as in the case of a heavenly orb, or with respect to its kind only, as in the case of the human and other animal races; and the continuing, lasting, or existing, for ever, either by self, as in the instance of God alone, or otherwise, and thus either with respect to the corporeal substance, as in the case of an inhabitant of Paradise, or with respect to kind only, as in the case of the fruits of the inhabitants of Paradise. (Er-Rághib, TA.) [Hence,] daAru AlbaqaA='i [ The abode of everlasting existence; ] the world to come. (T in art. dwr .) The verb is said of a thing; and in like manner of a man, as in baqiYa zamaAnFA TawiylFA , i. e. He lived [or continued in life ] a long time. (S.) [You say also, baqiYa EalaY HaAlihi He, or it, remained, or continued, in his, or its, state, or condition; i. e., as he, or it, was. And baqiYa EalaY Al$~id~api He endured, or bore up against, difficulty, distress, or adversity. ] And baqiY mina Al$~aYo'i baqiy~apN [ A remain, remainder, remnant, relic, or residue, of the thing remained. ] (S.) And baqiYa minohu ka*aA Such a thing remained, over and above, and behind, thereof; as also ↓ tbq~Y . (Msb.) -A2- baqaAhu , with Y and with w for the last radical, (K,) first pers. baqayotuhu (Lh, S) and baqawotuhu , (Lh, TA,) aor. of the former , (S,) inf. n. baqoYN , [of the former verb,] (K,) He looked at him, or it: (Lh, S, K:) or [so in the K, but in the S “ and, ”] he watched, or observed, him, or it: (S, K:) and baqayotuhu I looked, watched, or waited, for him, or it; (TA in art. bqw ;) as also baqawotuhu ; (K in that art.;) but the former is the more approved. (TA in that art.) [See also art. bqw .] You say also, fulaAnN yaboqiY Al$~aYo'a bibaSarihi Such a one looks at the thing, and watches, or observes, it. (JK.) And it is said in a trad., baqayonaA rasuwla A@ll~`hi We looked, watched, or waited, for the Apostle of God. (S.)

definition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ bq~Ahu and ↓ tbq~Ahu (S, K) all signify the same, (S,) and ↓ AstbqAhu likewise, (K,) He made, or caused, [and he suffered, ] him, or it, to remain, continue, last;
sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ bq~Ahu and ↓ tbq~Ahu (S, K) all signify the same, (S,) and ↓ AstbqAhu likewise, (K,) He made, or caused, [and he suffered, ] him, or it, to remain, continue, last; to be, or become, permanent, or perpetual; to continue, last, or exist, incessantly, always, endlessly, or for ever; he continued it; he perpetuated it. (Msb, K *) You say, AbqAhu A@ll~`hu [ God preserved him, or prolonged his life; or may God preserve him, or prolong his life; or] God made him, or caused him, or may God make him, or cause him, to continue in life. (S.) And A^aboqaY A^aSola Al$~aYo'i wajaEala vamarahu fiY sabiyli A@ll~`hi He made the thing itself to remain unalienable, not to be inherited nor sold nor given away, and assigned the profit arising from it to be employed in the cause of God, or of religion. (TA in art. Hbs .) And A^aboqayotu maA bayonanaA I was sparing of marring, i. e., forbore from marring much, or exceedingly, that [ state of union or amity ] which subsisted between us. (K.) And naEolayoka waA@bo*ulo qadamayoka ↓ baq~i [ Pre- serve thou, or spare thou, thy sandals, and use freely, or unsparingly, thy feet ]: a prov. (Meyd. See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 149.) And ↓ tabaq~aho watawaq~aho Preserve thou the soul ( Aln~afosa ↓ Aisotaboqi ), expose it not to destruction, [meaning preserve thyself, ] and guard against evils, or calamities: a trad.: the h in each verb is that of pausation. (TA.) [And AbqY mina Al$~aYo'i baqiy~apF He left, or reserved, of the thing, a remain, remainder, remnant, &c.:] and mina Al$~aYo'i ↓ AstbqY He left a portion of the thing; (S, K;) as also ↓ tbq~Y ; whence the prov., used to incite to liberality, ↓ laA yanofaEuka mino zaAdK tabaq~K Leaving a portion of travel-ling-provision will not profit thee. (JK.) [And AbqY Al$~aYo'i and ↓ AstbqAhu He reserved the thing for a future time or use &c.] And ↓ AstbqAhu as meaning [ He spared him; he let him live; ] he left him alive; (S, K;) [as also AbqAhu ; for] men say to their enemies when the latter have overcome, A^aboquwnaA wa laA tasotaA^oSiluwnaA [ Spare ye us, and destroy us not entirely ]: (TA:) [or AbqAhu , in a case of this kind,] and AbqY Ealayohi and ↓ AstbqAhu signify He pardoned him, [ and forbore to slay him, ] when slaughter was his due: (TA:) and ↓ AstbqAhu signifies also He pardoned, or forgave, his fault, wrong action, or lapse into sin, and preserved his love, or affection. (JK, TA. *) And [hence,] A^aboqayotu EalaY fulaAnK signifies also I showed mercy to such a one [ by sparing him, or letting him live, or by pardoning him, or otherwise ]; had mercy on him; pitied, or compassionated, him; syn. A^aroEayotu Ealayohi and raHimotuhu . (S.) One says, laA A^aboqaY A@ll~`hu Ealayoka A_ino A^aboqayota EalaY~a [ May God not show mercy to thee if thou show mercy to me: a prov., said in derision to one who affects to show mercy when unable to take revenge]. (S, Meyd.) And laA tuboqi A_il~aA EalaY nafosika [ Show not mercy save to thyself: another prov., similar to the former]. (Meyd.) And it is said, in a trad., of the fire [of Hell], laA tuboqiY EalaY mano taDar~aEa A_ilayohaA , i. e. It will not pity [ him who abases himself to it: or rather it will not spare &c.: and in like manner, laA tuboqiY walaA ta*aru , in the Kur lxxiv. 28, is generally understood as meaning It (namely, Hell,) will not spare, nor leave unburned]. (TA.)

definition: (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ baqoyaA (TA) and ↓ baqowaY (JK, S, Msb, K) and ↓ buqowaY (Th, K) and ↓ (JK, K,) the ↓ third and ↓ fourth with Y changed into w , like as w is changed into Y in dunoyaA and EuloyaA and quSoyaA , (ISd, TA,) [substs. in the sense of A_iboqaA='N , inf. n. of 4, signifying The making, or causing, and suffering, to remain, continue, last, &c.; preservation of a person in life, and of a thing in being; and the sparing, letting live, or leaving alive; ] substs. from A^aboqaAhu : (Msb, K:) or [the showing mercy by sparing or letting live, or by pardoning, or otherwise; having mercy; pitying, or compassionating; ] substs. from A^aboqayotu EalaY fulaAnK . (S.) Thus one says of a pilgrim, that he put gum, or something glutinous, upon his head, and so caused his hair to become compacted, buqoyaA Ealayohi to preserve it in the state in which it was (expl. by A_iboqaA='F Elyh ), lest it should become shaggy, or dishevelled, &c. (L in art. lbd .) And one says, na$adotuka A@ll~`ha waAlbuqoyaA and ↓ AlbaqowaY [ I conjure, or beg, or beseech, thee by God and by the preservation of thy life ]. (JK.) And maA liY Ealayoh raEowaY walaA ↓ baqowaY [ I have no mercy nor pity to bestow upon him ]. (JK. [There expl. by the words A^aYo A^aroEayotu Ealayohi waA^aboqayotu ; but A^aYo is evidently a mistranscription for mino , i. e. from.]) A poet (El-La'een ElMinkaree, TA) says, famaA buqoyaA EalaY~a tarakotumaAniY wal`kino xifotumaA Sarada Aln~ibaAli [ And it was not to show mercy by sparing me that ye two left me; but ye feared the transpiercing of the arrows ]. (S.) And another says, on his having refused to accept an offer of seven bloodwits, A^u*ak~aru biAlbuqoyaA EalaY mano A^aSaAbaniY wabuqoyaAYa A^an~iY jaAhidN gayoru muw^otaliY i. e. Am I required [or exhorted or reminded ] to show mercy to him who slew my relation, when the mercy that I show to him is that I am labouring to slay him, and not falling short, or being remiss: by bqyAY is meant A_iboqaAy^iY Ealayohi ; though AlA_iboqaA=' is not Aljahod : the meaning is, that this is done by me in lieu of that: AlbuqoyaA is a subst. from AlA_iboqaA=' , syn. therewith; and the w prefixed to it is a denotative of state. (Ham p. 119. [This verse is also cited in the TA, but with the substitution of ↓ biAlbaqowaY and wabaqowaAY for the corresponding words above.] ↓ Albaqiy~apa is said by men to their enemies when the latter have overcome; meaning [We ask, or beg, the being spared, or mercy, or quarter; a verb, whereby it is governed, being understood: or] A^aboquwnaA walaA tasotaA^oSiluwnaA [ spare ye us, and destroy us not entirely ]. (TA.)

definition: A remain, remainder, remaining portion, remnant, relic, residue, or the remains, or rest, of a thing;
sourceDefinition: A remain, remainder, remaining portion, remnant, relic, residue, or the remains, or rest, of a thing; (KL, PS, &c.;) a subst. from baqiYa as signifying “ it remained over and above, ” and “ it remained behind: ” pl. baqaAyaA and baqiy~aAtN : (Msb:) ↓ baAqiyapN , also, [pl. bawaAqK and baAqiyaAtN ,] has the same meaning as baqiy~apN ; (TA;) [i. e., as explained above; and so has ↓ baAqK , for $aYo'K baAqK &c.] You say, baqiYa mina Al$~aYo'i baqiy~apN [explained before: see 1]. (S.) [And humo baqiy~apu Als~ayofi , and baqaAyaA Als~ayofi , They are those who have been spared by the sword ]. ― -b2- [Hence,] fulaAnN mino baqiy~api Alqawomi Such a one is of the best of the people, or company of men: because a man reserves the most excellent of the things that he produces. (Bd in xi. 118.) And fulaAnN mino baqiy~api A^aholihi Such a one is of the most excellent of his people, or family. (Ham p. 78.) And fulaAnN baqiy~apu Alqawomi Such a one is the best of the people, or company of men: pl. baqaAyaA . (Kull p. 96.) ― -b3- A^uwluw baqiy~apK , in the Kur xi. 118, hence means Persons possessed of excellence: [see a phrase mentioned voce balalN :] or possessing a relic of judgment and intelligence: (Bd:) or persons of religion and excellence: (Jel:) or persons of understanding (K, TA) and discrimination: (TA:) or persons of obedience: (TA:) or having the quality of preserving themselves (Az, Bd, K, *) from punishment, (Bd,) by their holding the approved religion: (Az, TA:) and this last explanation is confirmed by another reading, which is ↓ AwlwA baqoyapK [ possessing a quality of watching, or observing, and hence, of guarding, or preserving ]; baqoyap being the inf. n. of un. of baqaAhu , aor. yaboqiyhi , signifying “ he watched, ” or “ observed, ” &c., “ him, ” or “ it. ” (Bd.) See also buqayaA , in two places. baqiy~apN is also a subst. from A^aboqayotu maA bayonanaA [explained before: see 4: app. meaning Forbearance from marring much, or exceedingly, the state of unity, or of amity, subsisting between two persons, or parties: and such may be its meaning in the phrase above-mentioned ( AwlwA bqy~p )]. (K.) ― -b4- baqiy~apu A@ll~`hi , in the Kur xi. 87, [after the command, in the next preceding verse, to give full measure and weight,] means God's sustenance that remains for you after your giving full measure [and weight]: (Jel:) or that which God has preserved for you, of what is lawful, (Fr, Bd,) after [your] keeping aloof from that which he has forbidden you: (Bd:) or the good state, or condition, remaining for you: (Zj, K:) or the fear ( muraAqabap ) of God; accord. to some: (Fr, TA:) or the obedience of God, and (as Aboo-'Alee says, TA) the looking for his recompense: (K, TA:) or baqiy~apN and ↓ baAqiyapN signify any religious service whereby one seeks to obtain the recompense of God; and such is the meaning of the former in this instance. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b5- See also baAqiyapN .

sourceDefinition: : see baqiy~apN , first sentence. ― -b2- AlbaAqiyaAtu AlS~aAliHaAtu [in the Kur xviii. 44, and xix. 79,] means Any righteous, or good, work, (K, TA,) of which the recompense remains: (TA:) or acts of obedience, (Bd and Jel in xix. 79,) or good works, (Bd in xviii. 44,) of which the fruit remains for ever: (Bd in both those places, and Jel * in the former:) and, as included therein, [so Bd, but in the K “ or, ”] the five prayers; (Bd, K;) and the performance of the pilgrimage; and the keeping the fast of Ramadán; (Bd in xviii. 44;) and [so Bd, but in the K “ or, ”] the saying, suboHaAna A@ll~`hi wa AlHamodulil~`hi wa laA A_il~aA A@ll~`hu wa A@ll~`hu A^akobaru ; (Bd and Jel in xviii. 44, and K;) to which some add, wa laA Hawola wa laA quw~apa A_il~aA biA@ll~`hi : (Jel ibid.:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, the correct meaning is any religious service whereby one seeks to obtain the recompense of God: see also baqiy~apN , last explanation. (TA.) ― -b3- baAqiyapN is sometimes put in the place of an inf. n.; (S, K;) or it is an inf. n.; (Msb;) syn. with baqaA='N ; (S, Msb, TA;) with which ↓ baqiy~apN , also, is syn. (TA in art. srE .) So in the Kur [lxix. 8], fahalo taraY lahumo mino baAqiyapK [ And dost thou see them to have any continuance? ]; (S, TA;) so says Fr: (TA:) or, as some say, the meaning is, baqiy~apK [i. e. a remnant ]: (TA:) or jamaAEapK baAqiyapK [ a company remaining ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or nafosK baAqiyapK [ a soul, or person, remaining ]: (Bd, Jel:) or the p is an intensive affix; (Jel;) [or a restrictive to unity;] i. e. one remaining; (Jel, TA;) and this is also allowable and good: one says, likewise, maA baqiyato baAqiyapN wa laA wa qaAhumo mina A@ll~`hi waAqiyapN [ One remaining remained not, nor did one preserver preserve them from God ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , in the pass. form, (Kt, Msb,) inf. n. bahorajapN , (K,) (assumed tropical:) It (a thing) was taken otherwise than by, or in, the right way: (Msb:) or (tropical:) it was turned away, or conveyed by turning away, (Kt, K, TA,) from the beaten way or road, (Kt, TA,) or from the direct, or right, main road. (K, TA.) And bahoraja bihimo (tropical:) It (the road, A) lead them otherwise than in the beaten track. (T, A, TA.) [See bahorajN , from which the verb is derived.] ― -b2- (tropical:) It (a man's blood) was made to be of no account, to go for nothing, unretaliated, or uncompensated by a mulct; was made allowable to be taken or shed. (Mgh.) And bahoraja damahu (tropical:) He made his blood to be of no account, &c. (TA.) ― -b3- Hence, (TA,) A^amaA A_i*o bahorajotaniY falaA A^a$orabuhaA A^abadFA (K, * TA) (tropical:) Verily, since thou hast made me [meaning my offence] to pass unnoticed, or hast taken no account of me, ( hadarotaniY ,) by annulling in respect of me the prescribed castigation, (K, TA,) I will not drink it (i. e. wine) henceforth: (TA:) said by Aboo-Mihjen (K, TA) Eth-Tha- kafee, (TA,) to Ibn-Abee-Wakkás. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, bahoraja AlmakaAni (assumed tropical:) He made the place free to the people in general to pasture their beasts in it. (IAar, L.)

definition: an arabicized word, (T, S, Mgh, L, TA,) from nabahoraho , (T, Mgh, L, TA,) which is Persian;
sourceDefinition: an arabicized word, (T, S, Mgh, L, TA,) from nabahoraho , (T, Mgh, L, TA,) which is Persian; (L, TA;) or, as some say, it is an Indian word, originally nabaholaho , meaning Bad, whence the Persian nabahoraho , and hence the arabicized bahorajN ; (TA;) applied to a dirhem, as meaning bad; (Kr, S;) false; (S, El-Marzookee;) adulterated; (Shifá el-Ghaleel, El-Marzookee;) of bad silver; (A, Mgh, L, Msb;) with which one cannot buy: (IAar, TA:) or, as some say, in which the silver is predominant: or, accord. to IAar, of which the die has been falsified: (Mgh:) or not coined in the government-mint: (Lb, TA:) and ↓ muboharajN signifies the same, applied to a dirhem; (Lh, A, Mgh;) and so ↓ nabahorajN ; (Lh, El-Marzookee;) but [Mtr says,] I have not found it with n , except on the authority of Lh (Mgh;) and IKh says that it is a word of the vulgar: (TA:) the pl. [of bhrj ] is bahaAriju , and [of nbhrj ,] nabahorajaAtu . (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, metaphorically, (Mgh,) (tropical:) Bad; (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K;) and false, or of no account; (S, A, Mgh, K;) applied to a thing (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb) of any kind: (A, Mgh, L:) anything rejected; not received or accepted; rejected as wrong or bad; as also ↓ nabahorajN : (TA:) and a thing is termed ↓ mubahorajN when it is as though it were cast away, and not an object of emulous desire or envy, or not in request. (El-Marzookee, TA.) You say, kalaAmN bahorajN (tropical:) Bad language. (A, L.) And EamalN bahorajN (tropical:) A bad action. (A, L.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Allowed or allowable [ to any person, to be taken or let alone, or to be possessed or made use of or done ]; made allowable, free, or lawful. (K.) You say, damN bahorajN (tropical:) Blood made to be of no account, to go for nothing, unretaliated, or uncompensated by a mulct; allowed to be taken or shed; (A, L;) as also ↓ mubahorajN . (K.) definition: and tuHafapN (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: and tuHafapN (S, Msb, K, &c.) i. q. bir~N [as meaning A gratuitous gift, or favour; or a bounty, or benefit ]; and laTafN [meaning a present; i. e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour ]; (K;) in some copies of the K, luTof ; (TA;) [i. e.] AltHfp signifies maA A^atoHafota bihi Alr~ajula mina Albir~i waAll~aTafi ; (S;) or [simply] maA A^atoHafota bihi gayoraka : (Msb:) and a Turofap [which properly signifies a gift not given to any one before; or of which the recipient did not possess the like, and which pleases him; ] (K, TA;) of fruit, and of sweet-smelling flowers: (TA:) [it generally means simply a present; or a rare, or pleasing, or rare and pleasing, present: ] pl. tuHafN . (S, K.) Accord. to some, it is originally wuHofapN : (K, TA:) Az says that its t is originally w : (Msb:) and tawaH~afa is quasi-pass. of A^atoHafahu : (Lth, TA:) so that it should be mentioned in art. wHf : (K, TA:) being like tuhamapN and tuxamapN &c. (TA.) It is said in a trad., tuHofapu AlS~aAy^imi Ald~uhonu wa Almijomaru [ The pleasing present for the faster is oil, and aloes-wood or the like ]; i. e., these dispel from him the grievousness and distress occasioned by the fasting. (TA.) And in another, respecting dates, tuHofapu Alkabiyri waSumotapu AlS~agiyri [i. e. The date is the pleasing gift for the big, or full-grown, or old, and the quieter of the little one, or child ]. (TA.) And in another, tuHofapu Almuw^omini Almawotu [ The boon for the believer is death ]. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) the most chaste of the forms here mentioned, (Az, Msb, MF, TA,) a pl., (AHát, MF, TA,) [or rather a coll. gen. n.,] and ↓ turunojN , (AZ, S, Msb, K, &c.,) [which is Persian,] a dial. var. of weak authority, (Msb,) by some disallowed, (MF, TA,) used by the vulgar, (TA,) the n in which is by common consent held to be augmentative, (MF, TA,) likewise a pl., (TA,) [or coll. gen. n.,] and ↓ A^utorunojN , mentioned by Ibn-Hishám El-Lakhmee, in his Faseeh, and also used by the vulgar, (TA,) and by some of the people of Hims, (Lth cited in the L voce HaZ~N , q. v.,) [and this is likewise a coll. gen. n.,] and A^utoruj~apN , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) which is the sing. of the first, (AHát, MF, TA,) or its n. un., (L, Msb,) also pronounced A^utorujapN , without teshdeed, (TA,) and ↓ turunojapN , (AZ, S, L, &c.,) likewise a n. un., (L,) A certain fruit, (Msb,) well known, (L, Msb, K,) plentiful in the land of the Arabs, but not growing wild, (L, TA,) [ of the species citrus medica, or citron; of which there are two varieties in Egypt; one, of the form of the lemon, but larger, there called turunoj baladiY~ ; the other, ribbed, and called turunoj muSab~aE : accord. to Golius, citrons of a large size, which have a sweeter peel than others, and are of a size nearly equal to that of a melon: ] the sour sort allays the lust of women, clears the complexion, and removes the [ discoloration of the face termed ] kalaf , (K, TA,) that arises from phlegm; (TA;) the peel thereof, put among clothes, preserves them from the moth-worm: (K, TA:) it is also beneficial as an antidote against the various kinds of poison; the smelling it in times of plague, or pestilence, is beneficial in the highest degree; and jinn, or genii, do not enter the house in which it is; wherefore a reciter of the Kur-án is appropriately likened to it: (TA:) the pl. of A^utoruj~apN is A^utoruj~aAtN as well as A^utoruj~N : [or rather the latter is a coll. gen. n., as stated above:] but one should not say turunojaAtN [app. because it is vulgar; for it is agreeable with analogy as pl. of turunojapN ; as is also A^utorunojaAtN as pl. of ↓ A^utorunojapN ]. (AHát, MF, TA.)

definition: [ Wealth, or what God bestowed upon him, ] made him to behave exorbitantly;
sourceDefinition: [ Wealth, or what God bestowed upon him, ] made him to behave exorbitantly; to be excessively disobedient or rebellious; to exalt himself, and be inordinate in infidelity; or to be extravagant in acts of disobedience and in wrongdoing: (S, K:) and so saEapu AlEayo$i [ plentifulness and easiness of life ]: and in like manner, ↓ tar~afatohu it caused him to exult, or to exult greatly, or excessively, and to behave insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully. (TA.) And [ Wealth, or what God bestowed upon him, ] made him to enjoy, or lead, a plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life; or a life of ease and plenty; as also ↓ tar~afatohu . (K.) ― -b2- Atrf Alr~ajula He gave the man the object of his eager desire; or of his yearning, or longing, or appetency. (Lh, M.) ― -b3- See also 2. -A2- Atrf also signifies He persevered in, or persisted in, or resolved upon, transgression, wrongdoing, or deviation from the right way. (El-'Ozeyzee, K.)

definition: A sort of kaAnuwn [or fire-place ];
sourceDefinition: A sort of kaAnuwn [or fire-place ]; (M;) the thing, (S, Msb,) or kAnwn , (K,) in which bread is baked; (S, Msb, K;) but different from the furon : (S in art. frn :) [it is a kind of oven, open at the top, in the bottom of which a fire is lighted, and in which the bread, in the form of flat cakes, is generally stuck against the sides; either portable, and made of baked clay, wide at the bottom, and narrow at the top, where it is open; and if so, the bread is sometimes stuck upon the outside, to bake; or fixed, and in this case made of baked clay likewise, or constructed of bricks; or it is a hole made in the ground, and lined with bricks or tiles or the like, against which the bread is stuck, to bake; and sometimes flesh-meat, cut into small pieces, is roasted in it, or upon it, on skewers: ] such, accord. to some, is the meaning in the Kur xi. 42 and xxiii. 27; (T;) and the word is said to have the same meaning in every language; (Lth, T, M;) but this is not correct: (Ham p. 793:) it is an arabicized word; (T, M;) not genuine Arabic; (AHát, Msb;) originally Persian: (M:) [in Hebrew XXX :] Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà [i. e. Th, as is stated in Ham, ubi suprà,] says that it is of the measure tafoEuwlN from Aln~aAr , (M, and Ham ubi suprà,) or from Aln~uwr ; originally tanowuwrN ; (Ham;) but this is wrong: (M:) the pl. is tanaAniyru . (M, Msb.) Mo- hammad is related to have said to a man wearing a garment dyed with bastard-saffron, “ If thy garment were in the tn~wr of thy family, or beneath their cooking-pot, it were better: ” whereupon he went away, and burned it: but he meant, “ Wert thou to spend its price for flour to make bread, or for fire-wood with which to cook, it were better for thee: ” as though he disliked a garment so dyed. (IAth.) ― -b2- The surface of the ground: (T, S, M, K:) so in the Kur ubi suprà, (T, S,) accord. to 'Alee (S) and I'Ab. (TA.) ― -b3- The highest part of the earth or ground: so in the same passages of the Kur accord. to Katádeh. (TA.) ― -b4- Any place from which water pours forth. (M, K.) ― -b5- A place where the water of a valley collects. (M, K.) ― -b6- The shining of the dawn: so accord. to some in the Kur ubi suprà: (T:) and 'Alee is related to have said that wafaAra Alt~an~uwru means and daybreak rose or rises: (TA:) or it relates to the welling forth of water from the place of the mosque of El-Koofeh: (T:) or Alt~n~wr here signifies a well-known spring of water: (Hr, TA:) or a certain mountain near El-Maseesah; (I'Ab, K, TA;) i. e., (TA,) 'Eyn-el-Ward, in El-Jezeereh; (I'Ab, T, TA;) or 'Eyn-Wardeh. (Bd in xi. 42.)

sourceDefinition: , [of the masc. gender, as is shown by the phrase twtyA' maEodaniY~N , and therefore perfectly decl.,] an arabicized word, (S, Msb,) [ Tutia, or tutty; an impure protoxide of zinc; ] a certain stone [or mineral ], (S, K,) well known, (M, K,) employed as a collyrium. (S, Msb.) [It is also applied in the present day to several kinds of vitriol; the sulphates of zinc and of copper and of iron. De Sacy says, on the authority of Ibn-Beytár, that there are two species thereof; one which is found in mines; the other, in the furnaces in which copper is melted, like cadmia; and this latter species is what the Greeks call pompholyx: of the fossil tutia there are three varieties; one is white; another, greenish; the third, yellow, with a strong tinge of red: the white is the finest variety; the green, the coarsest. (Chrest. Arabe, 2nd ed., iii. 453; where see more.) Golius, on this word, in his Lex., says, “ Optima est quæ vel naturalis, sc. Indica, cærulea, et pellucida; vel artificialis, sc. Carmanica, alba cum partis viridioris strictura. Zein. ” i. e. Zeyn El-' Attár. “ Ex plumbi præstantissimi, quod dicitur qlEY , fuligine concrescere præstantissimum genus, commune vero ex fuligine æris, tradit Jacutus ex Abulfed. ”.]

sourceDefinition: , [inf. n. of vb~Y , mentioned in the T and K, in all its senses, in art. vbY , and so in the M, except in the first of the following senses, which is there mentioned in art. vbY and also in art. vbw ,] The act of collecting (K, TA) in successive assemblages (↓ vubapF vubapF ). (TA.) You say, vb~Ahu He collected it, namely, a thing, (M,) and water: (M * and TA in art. vbw :) and he added to it, and collected it. (M, TA.) ― -b2- The collecting what is good: and also, what is bad, or evil: thus bearing two contr. significations. (K.) ― -b3- [And hence,] The praising a man in his life-time: (AA, S, K:) or praising him time after time in his life-time: (TA:) or praising him much; as though relating to him collections (↓ vubaAt ) of praise: (Z, TA;) or the mentioning of the sundry good qualities or actions: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and the magnifying [a person]; or honouring [him]. (T, * K.) You say, vb~Y Alr~ajula , (M,) or vb~Y EalaY Alr~ajuli , (T,) He praised the man in his life-time: (T, M:) because the doing so implies the collecting his good qualities or actions. (T, * M.) ― -b4- [Hence also the contr. signification,] The blaming, or censuring, much; collecting blame, or censure, from this and that source. (TA. [The act. part. n. is rendered in the M agreeably with this explanation.]) ― -b5- The act of completing [ and augmenting a thing]. (K.) You say, vab~i maEoruwfaka Complete and augment [ thy beneficence, or bounty, or favour ]. (T.) And vb~Y A@ll~`hu laka Aln~iEama [ May God complete and augment to thee benefits, or blessings: or] may God send to thee benefits, or blessings. (TA.) [See also 1.] ― -b6- The putting a thing into a good, right, or sound, state, and augmenting it. (T, K. *) ― -b7- vb~Y AlmaAla He kept, preserved, guarded, or took care of, the property. (Kr, M.) -A2- vab~ayotu EalaY Al$~aYo'i , (As, S,) inf. n. tavobiyapN , (As, T, S, M, K,) I kept constantly, or perseveringly, to the thing. (As, T, S, M, K.) ― -b2- The inf. n. signifies also The keeping, (T,) or pursuing, (K,) the way, course, mode of acting, or the like, of one's father: (T, K:) or the doing, or acting, like one's father. (M.) ― -b3- Also The complaining of one's state, or case, and of one's want; and asking aid, or assistance, and vengeance, or avengement. (K.) [One of the meanings assigned to the verb by Golius, as on the authority of the K, and by Freytag after him, is “ Disposuit paravitque se: ” app. from the former's having found AlAisotiEodaAdu written in a copy of the K for AlAisotiEodaA='u .] -A3- A^anaA A^aEorifuhu tavobiyapF I know him, or it, with a seeming, not a certain, knowledge. (T, TA.)

definition: A company (T, S, M, K) of men;
sourceDefinition: A company (T, S, M, K) of men; (T, M;) as also ↓ A^uvobiy~apN ; (M, K; [in the CK erroneously written Aavobiyap ;]) and A^uvoy^iy~apN : (TA:) a company in a state of separation or dispersion; or a distinct body, or company, of men: (T:) and a troop of horsemen; such as is termed EuSobap : (M, K: [in the CK, AlEaSabapu is erroneously put for AlEuSobapu :]) the pl. is vubaAtN and vubuwna (T, S, M, K) and vibuwna (S, M) and (the pl. of A^uvobiy~apN , TA) A^avaAbiY~u and A^avaAbiyapN , in which last the p is a substitute for the last Y [of A^avaAbiY~u ]: (M, TA:) or [accord. to some,] A^avaAbiY~u , which signifies companies, has no sing.; but, as some say, its sing. is ↓ A^avobiy~apN , of the measure A^ufoEuwlapN , [originally A^uvobuwyapN ,] which means a numerous company: (Ham p. 796:) [it is also said that] vubFY is a pl. of vubapN as meaning a company; (L in art. vwb , and Ham p. 271;) and hence the phrase Alv~ubaY AlEaAliY , for Alv~ubaY AlEaAliyapu , [ the high, or exalted, companies, ] the former word being made masc. because it is like zulamN [which is sing. and masc.]; but some say that this word here means the assemblies of the nobles: (Ham ubi suprá:) IAar says, Alv~ubaY AlEaAliY mino majaAlisi AlA^a$oraAfi ; but [ISd observes,] this is extraordinary, and I have not heard it except in the poetry of El-Find EzZimmánee. (M.) Accord. to some, it is from vaAba , being originally vuwbapN ; and its dim. is vuwayobapN : (T:) or it is originally vubaYN : (S:) accord. to Er-Rághib, the letter elided from vubapN as meaning “ a company, ” but not as relating to a wateringtrough or tank, is Y ; and ISd holds it to be Y : and [if so,] its dim. is ↓ vubay~apN : (TA:) [but ISd adds,] IJ says that the elided letter is w , because it is this in most cases, as in A^abN and A^axN and sanapN and EiDapN &c. (M in arts. vbw and vbY .) [See also art. vwb . It seems to signify also An assemblage, or a collection, of things of any kind:] see 2, in two places. ― -b2- Also The middle of a wateringtrough or tank, (T, S, M, K,) to which the water returns [ when it has been emptied ], (S,) or to which what remains of the water returns: (T:) and the place where the water collects in a valley or low ground: (Aboo-Kheyreh, T:) but this is from vaAba ; (T, S; *) the p is a substitute for the w , the medial radical, which is suppressed; for it is originally vuwabN : (S:) or it is originally vuwbapN : (T:) or it may be from vab~ayotu “ I collected: ” but Aboo-Is-hák makes it to be from vaAba AlmaA='u , aor. yavuwbu ; and this he infers to be the case from their saying that the dim. is vuwayobapN . (M.) [See also art. vwb .]

definition: , (T, A, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, A, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. vagorN , (T,) He broke it; (T, A;) namely, a part of a wall; (A;) he demolished it: this is [said to be] the primary signification: he demolished it, or pulled it down; namely, a wall: (T:) and he broke it (namely, anything, [as a wall and a vessel, &c.,] A) so as to make a gap in it, or a hollow in its edge. (A, K.) ― -b2- Also, (IAar, S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (Msb, K,) He broke his vagor [or front teeth ], (S, Msb, K,) or his teeth. (IAar, and TA as from the K.) And vugira , in the pass. form, inf. n. vuguwrN , He (a boy) had his vagor [or front teeth] broken. (Msb.) ― -b3- vagarotu sin~ahu I pulled out his tooth. (El-Hujeymee, TA.) And vugira He (a man) had a tooth, or teeth, pulled out. (As, TA.) ― -b4- Also vugira , (AZ, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. vagorN , (AZ, Msb,) He (a boy) shed his central milk-teeth, (AZ, S, Mgh, K,) or his vagor [or front teeth ]: (AZ, Msb:) or ↓ A^avogara has this latter meaning, (A, K,) or ↓ Ait~agara ; (As, TA;) and vagira , (K,) or ↓ Ait~agara , (Sh, TA,) or ↓ Ait~agara , (Msb,) signifies he shed his teeth: (Sh, Msb, K:) vugira is said to have this last signification in the Kifáyet el-Mutahaffidh; and ↓ Av~gr and ↓ At~gr are there said to have the contr. signification, explained below [see 8]. (Msb.) ― -b5- vugira also signifies He had his mouth bruised; and so ↓ A^uvogira . (K.) -A2- vagara Alv~ulomapa , aor. , He stopped up, or obstructed, the gap, or breach: thus the verb bears two contr. significations. (K.) And vagaronaAhumo We stopped up, or obstructed, against them the gaps, or passes of the mountain; (S, TA;) we stopped up, or obstructed, against them the place of exit, so that they knew not what way to take. (A.)

sourceDefinition: Sitting upon his knees: or standing upon the extremities of his toes: (K:) and [simply] sitting: or [ kneeling with his body and thighs erect, or nearly so; i. e.] putting down his knees [ upon the ground ] and raising his buttocks: (TA:) [see also 1, of which it is the part. n.:] pl. juviYN and jiviY~N ; (K;) or these may be pls., like bukY~N and bkYN , pls. of baAk ; or inf. ns. used as epithets [as is indicated in the S]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) You say qawomN juviY~N [ A company of men sitting upon their knees ]; (S, Msb;) like as you say jalasa juluwsFA and qawomN juluwsN . (S.) And hence, in the Kur [xix. 73], wana*aru AlZ~aAlimiyna fiyhaA juviy~FA , and jiviy~FA also, with kesr to the j because of the kesr of the letter following it, [ And we will leave the wrongdoers therein, sitting upon their knees. ] (S.) And fulaAnN mino juviY~i jahan~ama : see juvFA . (TA.) And, in the Kur [xlv. 27], wataray kul~a A^um~apK jaAviyapF (TA) And thou shalt see every people sitting upon the knees, (Bd, Jel,) in an upright posture, not at ease: (Bd:) or congregated; (Bd, Jel;) from javowapN signifying “ a company, ” or “ congregated body. ” (Bd.) Whence, (TA,) suwrapu AljaAviyapi The [ forty-fifth ] chapter, of the Kur-án, next after that called Ald~uxaAn . (S, TA.) ― -b2- [ AljaAviY , or AljaAviY EalaY rukobatayohi , (assumed tropical:) The constellation Hercules. ]

definition: , inf. n. mujaAdalapN and jidaAlN , (S, Mgh, K,) He contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, with him: (S, TA:) or did so vehemently, or violently, (Mgh, K,) and ably, or powerfully:...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. mujaAdalapN and jidaAlN , (S, Mgh, K,) He contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, with him: (S, TA:) or did so vehemently, or violently, (Mgh, K,) and ably, or powerfully: (K:) [or he did so obstinately, or merely for the purpose of convincing him; for] mjAdlp signifies the disputing respecting a question of science for the purpose of convincing the opponent, whether what he says be wrong in itself or not: (Kull p. 342:) [ he wrangled with him: ] or jAdl , inf. n. mjAdlp and jdAl , as above, signifies originally he contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, by advancing what might divert the mind from the appearance of the truth and of what was right: and accord. to a later usage, of the lawyers, he compared evidences [ in a discussion with another person, or other persons, ] in order that it might appear which of those evidences was preponderant: and the doing this is commendable if for the purpose of ascertaining the truth; but otherwise it is blameable: (Msb:) accord. to Er-Rághib, jdAl signifies the competing in disputation or contention, and in striving to overcome [ thereby ]; from jadalotu AlHabola , meaning, “ I twisted the rope firmly; ” as though each of the two parties twisted the other from his opinion: or, as some say, it originally means the act of wrestling, and throwing down another upon the jadaAlap [or ground ]: accord. to Ibn-El-Kemál, a disputing that has for its object the manifesting and establishing of tenets or opinions. rawSourceText: , inf. n. mujaAdalapN and jidaAlN , (S, Mgh, K,) He contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, with him: (S, TA:) or did so vehemently, or violently, (Mgh, K,) and ably, or powerfully: (K:) [or he did so obstinately, or merely for the purpose of convincing him; for] mjAdlp signifies the disputing respecting a question of science for the purpose of convincing the opponent, whether what he says be wrong in itself or not: (Kull p. 342:) [ he wrangled with him: ] or jAdl , inf. n. mjAdlp and jdAl , as above, signifies originally he contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, by advancing what might divert the mind from the appearance of the truth and of what was right: and accord. to a later usage, of the lawyers, he compared evidences [ in a discussion with another person, or other persons, ] in order that it might appear which of those evidences was preponderant: and the doing this is commendable if for the purpose of ascertaining the truth; but otherwise it is blameable: (Msb:) accord. to Er-Rághib, jdAl signifies the competing in disputation or contention, and in striving to overcome [ thereby ]; from jadalotu AlHabola , meaning, “ I twisted the rope firmly; ” as though each of the two parties twisted the other from his opinion: or, as some say, it originally means the act of wrestling, and throwing down another upon the jadaAlap [or ground ]: accord. to Ibn-El-Kemál, a disputing that has for its object the manifesting and establishing of tenets or opinions. definition: , (A, Mgh, K,*) or jas~ahu biyadihi , (S Msb,) aor , (Mgh, Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (A, Mgh, K,*) or jas~ahu biyadihi , (S Msb,) aor , (Mgh, Msb,) inf.n. jas~N , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) He felt it with his hand (S, A, Mgh, K) for the purpose of testing it, that he might form a judgment of it; (Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ Ajts~hu . (S, Msb, K.) You say, jas~ahu AlT~abiybu , (Mgh,) and jas~a yadahu , (A,) The physician felt him, (Mgh,) and felt his arm, or hand, (A,) to know if he were hot or cold. (Mgh.) And jas~a Al$~aApa He felt the sheep, or goat, to know if it were fat or lean. (A, Mgh.) ― -b2- jas~N is also, sometimes, with the eye. (IDrd, S, Msb. *) You say, jas~ahu biEayonihi (IDrd, S, A, K) (tropical:) He looked sharply, or intently, or attentively, at him, or it, for the purpose of investigation and clear perception. (K, TA.) IDrd cites as an ex. a verse (of 'Obeyd, or 'Abeed, [for I find it written without any syll. signs,] the son of Eiyoob El-'Amberee, TA,) in which occurs the expression jas~uwhu biA^aEoyunihimo : (S:) but Sgh says that the right reading is Has~uwhu . (TA.) ― -b3- jas~a AlA^aroDa (assumed tropical:) He traversed the land. (Aboo-Sa'eed El-Yeshkuree, TA.) ― -b4- jas~a AlA^axobaAra , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ tajas~asahaA , (S, A, Msb, K,) (tropical:) He searched, or sought, for, or after, news or tidings; inquired, or sought for information, respecting news or tidings; searched or inquired or spied into, investigated, scrutinized, or examined, news or tidings: (S, K:) he searched, or sought, repeatedly, or leisurely and by degrees, for news or tidings. (Msb.) You say also, fulaAnFA ↓ tjs~s , and mino fulaAnK (tropical:) He inquired, or sought for information, respecting such a one; as also tHs~s , which latter verb occurs in an extr. reading of verse 87 of ch. xii. of the Kur: or the former signifies he sought after him for another; and the latter, "he sought after him for himself:" or ↓ tjs~s signifies [he acted as a spy;] he inquired respecting, or searched or inquired or spied into, things which others veiled or concealed by reason of disdainful pride or of shame or pudency; and tHs~s , "he listened:" (TA:) in the last of the senses here assigned to it, the former verb is used in the Kur, xlix. 12, where it is said, ↓ walaA tajas~asuwA , for tatajas~asuwA ; (Mujáhid, Bd, K;) ↓ or the meaning here is, and do not ye inquire respecting, or search or inquire or spy into, private circumstances: or take ye what appeareth, and leave ye what God hath concealed. (Mujáhid, K.) You also say, lahumo A^amori Alqawomi ↓ Ajts~ He examined or spied into, and sought out, for them, the circumstances of the people. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: (A, TA) and ↓ majas~apN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) The place which one feels with his hand, (A,* Mgh, K, TA,) for the purpose of testing it, that he may form a judgment of it: (Mgh:) and ↓ the latter, the place which the physician feels [to know if a patient be hot or cold]: (S, Msb:) pl. majaAs~u . (S, A, Msb, K.) You say, ↓ majas~atuhu HaAr~apN [The place in which one feels him is hot]. (A, TA.) And kayofa taraY majas~ahaA [How dost thou find the place in which one feels her?]; referring to a sheep or goat; to which one answers, "Indicative of fatness." (A.) ― -b2- [Hence, (assumed tropical:) Anything external which indicates the internal condition. ] It is said in a prov., (S, A, Msb, K,) relating to camels, (Msb,) A^afowaAhuhaA majaAs~uhaA , (S, A, K,) or majaAs~uhaA A^afowaAhuhaA , (Msb,) or A^aHonaAkuhaA majaAs~uhaA , (A, K,) (assumed tropical:) [ Their mouths, or their palates, are the things which indicate their internal condition: ] for if they eat well, he who looks at them sufficiently knows their fatness, (S, Msb, K,) without feeling them: (S, K:) if one see them eat well, it is as though he felt them: (A, TA:) or, accord. to AZ, they feel the herbage, to test it, with their heads [or mouths] and their palates: so that, accord. to his explanation, the term mjAs~ is tropically applied to these parts. (TA.) The prov. relates to external evidences of things explaining their internal qualities. (K) [And hence,] raEati AlA_ibilu AlkalaA^a bimajaAs~ihaA , (K) (tropical:) The camels cropped the herbage with their mouths. (TA.)― -b3- You say also, fulaAnN waAsiEu Almajas~i , like as you say raHobu Al*~iraAEi (tropical:) [app. meaning Such a one is liberal, munificent, or generous ]: and in the contrary case, Day~iqu Almajas~i , (A,) or ↓ Almajas~api , (K,) or both, (TA,) signifying gayoru raHobi AlS~adori (tropical:) [app., not liberal ]; (K, TA;) and not waAsiEu Als~arobi [which is explained as meaning of ample bosom, and judgment, and love; and of ample way, or course of proceeding: but I rather incline to think that the right reading is waAsiEu Als~irobi , and the meaning, of ample, or large, mind, or heart ]. (TA.) You also say, laDiyqFA ↓ A_in~a fiY majas~atika (A) or majas~ika (TA) (tropical:) [app,. Verily in thy bosom, or mind, or heart, is narrowness; or in thee is illiberality. ]
