sourceDefinition: , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. jafaA='N ; and ↓ tjAfY ; It did not keep, or cleave, to its place. (K.) You say, jafaA janobuhu Eani AlfiraA$i , (Mgh,) and Eanohu ↓ tjAfY , (S, Mgh,) His side did not rest, or was restless, or uneasy, upon the bed; or shrank from it; (S, Mgh;) and heaved, or rose, from it: (Mgh:) or the former, his side did not keep, or cleave, to its place upon the bed: and the latter, it became withdrawn, or removed, from it. (TA.) And jafaA Als~aroju Eano Zahori Alfarasi , (S Msb, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above; (Msb;) and ↓ tjAfY ; (S, Msb;) The saddle heaved, or rose, from the back of the horse: (S, Msb:) or did not keep, or cleave, to its place upon his back. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] it is said in a trad. of 'Omar, A_in~iY A^ajofuw Eano A^a$oyaA='a mina AlEilomi Verily I recoil, shrink, or am averse, from some matters of knowledge, or science, and ignore them, or neglect them. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also jafaA , (Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (Msb,) [and so the inf. n.,] said of a garment, or piece of cloth, It was thick, coarse, or rough: (Msb, TA:) and in like manner said of a reed-pen, it was thick, coarse, or rough, in its nib. (TA.) ― -b4- [And hence, (see jafaA='N , below, and jaAfK ,) He was, or became, thick, gross, coarse, rough, or rude, of make: and, more commonly, coarse, rough, or rude, of nature or disposition, or in his intercourse and dealings with others; unkind, hard, churlish, uncivil, or surly. (See also 10.)] It is said in a trad., mano badaA jafaA , i. e. [ He who abides in the desert ] becomes coarse, rough, or rude, of nature or disposition; [or unkind, hard, churlish, &c.;] by reason of mixing little with men. (TA.) ― -b5- jafaA Ealayohi ka*aA Such a thing was, or became, heavy, onerous, burdensome, or oppressive, to him. (K.) -A2- jafaA janobahu Eani AlfiraA$i : and jafaA Als~aroja : see 3. ― -b2- jafati Alqidoru zabadahaA The cooking-pot cast forth its froth, or foam; as also ↓ Ajft ; (TA;) [like jafaA^at and AjfA^t ;] originally without ' . (Er- Rághib, TA.) And jafaA Als~ayolu The torrent drove away [things in its course]. (Msb.) ― -b3- jafaA Alr~ajula , aor. as above, He turned away from the man; avoided him; or shunned him: or he drove away the man; from jfA Als~ayolu , explained above: sometimes meaning, with hatred. (Msb.) And jafaAhu He withdrew, or removed, far, or to a distance, from him: whence the saying of Mohammad Ibn-Sookah, lam~aA qal~a maAliY jafaAniY A_ixowaAniY [ When my property became little, my brethren withdrew far from me ]. (TA) ― -b4- And jafaA maAlahu He did not keep, or cleave, or hold fast, to his property. (K.) ― -b5- And jafaAhu , (S, K,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. jafaA='N (S, K) and jafowN , (K,) He treated him, or behaved towards him, coarsely, roughly, rudely, unkindly, hardly, churlishly, uncivilly, or surlily: (S, K:) you should not say jafayotu . (S.) The pass. part. n. is ↓ majofuw~N and ↓ majofiY~N : (S, and K in art. jfY :) the latter formed in accordance with jufiYa , in which the w is changed into Y . (Fr, S.) ― -b6- He did to him what displeased, grieved, or vexed, him; did to him what he disliked, or hated; did evil to him. (TA.) So in the trad., mano Haj~a walamo yazuroniY faqado jafaA [ He who performs the pilgrimage to Mekkeh and does not visit me, i.e. does not visit my tomb afterwards, either on his homeward journey or by journeying to ElMedeeneh for that special purpose, does what displeases me]. (TA.) ― -b7- jafati AlmaroA^upu waladahaA The woman neglected to take care of her child, or to pay frequent attention to it. (TA.)

definition: [Said of a person prostrating himself, or lying down, it means He drew up his body from that on which he rested.
sourceDefinition: : see 1, in three places. [Said of a person prostrating himself, or lying down, it means He drew up his body from that on which he rested. definition: , (S, Mgh, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, K,) aor. , (Mgh, TA,) inf. n. jan~N , (TA,) It veiled, concealed, hid, covered, or protected, him; (S, Mgh, K;) said of the night; (S, K;) as also jan~a Ealayohi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. junuwnN , (S,) or jan~N , (K,) or both; (TA;) so in the Kur vi. 76, meaning it veiled him, concealed him, or covered him, with its darkness; (Bd;) and ↓ Ajn~hu : (S, Msb, K:) or this last signifies he, or it, made, or prepared, for him, or gave him, that which should veil him, conceal him, &c. : accord. to Er-Rághib, the primary signification of jan~N is the veiling, or concealing, &c., from the sense. (TA.) And jun~a Eanohu means It (anything) was veiled, concealed, or hidden, from him. (K.) ― -b2- He concealed it; namely, a dead body; as also ↓ Ajn~hu : (S, TA:) or the latter, he wrapped it in grave-clothing: (K:) and he buried it. (TA.) And Al$~aYo'a fiY SadoriY ↓ A^ajonanotu I concealed the thing in my bosom. (S.) And waladFA ↓ A^ajan~ato , (S,) or janiynFA , (K,) said of a woman, (S,) or a pregnant female, (K,) She concealed [or enveloped in her womb a child, or an embryo, or a fœtus ]. (TA.) -A2- jan~a , aor. , inf. n. jin~N , It (an embryo, or a fœtus,) was concealed in the womb. (K.) ― -b2- Also, [inf. n., probably, jin~N and junuwnN and janaAnN , explained below,] It (the night) was, or became, dark. (Golius on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof.) -A3- jun~a , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. junuwnN (S, K) and jin~apN (S) and jan~N ; (K;) and ↓ Ausotujin~N , and ↓ tjn~n , and ↓ tjAn~ ; (K;) He (a man, S) was, or became, majonuwn [originally signifying possessed by a jin~iY~ , or by jin~ ; possessed by a devil or demon; (see Bd li. 39;) and hence meaning bereft of reason; or mad, insane, unsound in mind or intellect, or wanting therein: the verbs may generally be rendered he was, or became, possessed; or mad, or insane ]. (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- jun~a Al*~ubaAbu , (S, A, TA,) inf. n. junuwnN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) The flies made much buzzing: (S:) or made a gladsome buzzing in a meadow. (A, TA.) ― -b3- jun~a Aln~abotu , inf. n. junuwnN , (tropical:) The herbage became tall, and tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, and put forth its flowers or blossoms: (S, TA:) or became thick and tall and full-grown, and blossomed. (M, TA.) And jun~ati AlA^aroDu , (Fr, K,) inf. n. junuwnN , (K,) (tropical:) The land produced pleasing herbage or plants: (Fr, TA:) or put forth its flowers and blossoms; as also ↓ tjn~nt . (K, TA.)

definition: The darkness of night;
sourceDefinition: The darkness of night; as also ↓ junuwnN and ↓ janaAnu , (K, TA,) the last [written in the CK junAn , but it is] with fet-h: (TA:) or all signify its intense darkness: (TA:) or all, the confusedness of the darkness of night: (K:) [all, in these senses, are app. inf. ns.: (see 1:)] the last, ↓ janaAnN , also signifies night [itself]: (K:) or [so in copies of the K, accord. to the TA, but in the CK “ and, ”] the dense black darkness of night: (S, K:) and ↓ junuwnN , the veiling, or concealing, or protecting, darkness of night. (ISk, S.) ― -b2- Concealment: so in the phrase, laA jin~a bih`*aA AlA^amori There is no concealment with this thing. (K, * TA.) One of the Hudhalees says, walaA jin~a biAlbagoDaA='i waAln~aZari Al$~azori [ And there is no concealment with vehement hatred and the looking with aversion ]. (TA.) -A2- [The genii; and sometimes the angels; ] accord. to some, the spiritual beings that are concealed from the senses, or that conceal themselves from the senses; all of such beings; (Er-Rághib, TA;) the opposite of A_inosN ; (S, Mgh, Msb, Er-Rághib, TA;) thus comprising the angels; all of these being jin~ ; (Er-Rághib, TA;) thus called because they are feared but not seen: (S:) or, accord. to others, certain of the spiritual beings; for the spiritual beings are of three kinds; the good being the angels; and the evil being the devils ( $ayaATiyn ); and the middle kind, among whom are good and evil, being the jin~ ; as is shown by the first twelve verses of ch. lxxii. of the Kur: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or it here means intelligent invisible bodies, predominantly of the fiery, or of the aerial, quality: or a species of souls, or spirits, divested of bodies: or human souls separate from their bodies: (Bd:) or the jin~ are the angels [ exclusively ]; (K;) these being so called in the Time of Ignorance, because they were concealed, or because they concealed themselves, from the eyes: so, accord. to some, in the Kur [xviii. 48], where it is said that Iblees was of the jin~ : and so, as some say, in the Kur [vi. 100], where it is said that they called the jin~ partners of God: (TA:) but some reject the explanation in the K, because the angels were created of light, and the jin~ of fire; and the former do not propagate their kind, nor are they to be described as males and females; contrary to the case of the jin~ ; wherefore it is generally said that in the phrase [in the Kur xviii. 48, above mentioned] A_il~aA A_iboliysa kaAna mina Aljin~i , what is excepted is disunited in kind from that from which the exception is made, or that Iblees had adopted the dispositions of the jin~ : (MF, TA:) or, as some say, the jin~ were a species of the angels, who were the guardians of the earth and of the gardens of Paradise: (TA:) ↓ jin~apN , also, signifies the same as jin~N : (S, Msb, K:) so in the last verse of the Kur: (S:) in the Kur xxxvii. 158 meaning the angels, whom certain of the Arabs worshipped; (TA;) and whom they called the daughters of God: (Fr, TA:) a single individual of the jin~ is called ↓ jin~iY~N , [fem. with p :] (S, TA:) and ↓ jaAn~N , also, is syn. with jin~N : (Msb:) or AljaAnN means the father of the jin~ ; (S, Mgh, TA;) [i. e. any father of jin~ ; for] the pl. is jin~aAnN , like HiyTaAnN pl. of HaAy^iTN : (S, TA:) so says El-Hasan: it is said in the T, on the authority of AA, that the jAn~ is, or are, of the jin~ : (TA:) or jaAn~N is a quasi-pl. n. of jin~N ; (M, K;) like jaAmilN and baAqirN : (M, TA:) so in the Kur lv. 56 and 74: in reading the passage in the Kur lv. 39, 'Amr Ibn- 'Obeyd pronounced it jaA^anN : (TA:) it is related that there were certain creatures called the jaAn~ , who were upon the earth, and who acted corruptly therein, and shed blood, wherefore God sent angels who banished them from the earth; and it is said that these angels became the inhabitants of the earth after them. (Zj, TA.) baAta fulaAnN Dayofa jin~K [ Such a one passed the night a guest of jn~ ] means, in a desolate place, in which was no one that might cheer him by his society or converse. (TA.) The saying of Moosà Ibn-Jábir, famaA nafarato jin~iY walaA ful~a miboradiY may mean And my companions, who were like the jin~ , did not flee when I came to them and informed them, nor was my tongue, that is like the file, deprived of its sharp edge: or by his jn~ he means his familiar jn~ , such as were asserted to aid poets when difficulties befell them; and by his mbrd , his tongue: (Ham p. 182 [where other explanations are proposed; but they are far-fetched]:) or by his jn~ he means his heart; and by his mbrd , his tongue. (S.) The Arabs liken a man who is sharp and effective in affairs to a jin~iY~ and a $ayoTaAn : and hence they said, nafarato jin~uhu , meaning (assumed tropical:) He became weak and abject. (Ham ubi suprà.) ― -b2- The greater, main, or chief, part, or the main body, or bulk, of men, or of mankind; as also ↓ janaAnN ; (K;) because he who enters among them becomes concealed by them: (TA:) or the latter means the general assemblage, or collective body, of men: (IAar, S, * TA:) or what veils, conceals, covers, or protects, one, of a thing. (AA, TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) The flowers, or blossoms, of plants or herbage. (K, TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) The prime, or first part, of youth: (S, K, TA:) or the sharpness, or vigorousness, and briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, thereof. (TA.) You say, kaAna *`lik fiY jin~i $abaAbihi (tropical:) That was in the prime, or first part, of his youth. (S, TA.) And A^afoEalu *`lika AlA^amora bijin~i *`lika (tropical:) I will do that thing in the time of the first and fresh state of that. (S, TA.) jin~N may also signify (assumed tropical:) The madness, or insanity, of exultation, or of excessive exultation. (TA.) And one says, Ait~qi Aln~Aqapa faA_in~haA bijin~i DiraAmihaA , meaning (assumed tropical:) Fear thou the she-camel, for she is in her evil temper on the occasion of her bringing forth. (TA.) ― -b5- Also i. q. jd~ [app. jid~N , as meaning (assumed tropical:) Seriousness, or earnestness ]; because it is a thing that is an accompaniment of thought, or reflection, and is concealed by the heart. (TA.)

definition: A [ garden, such as is called ] busotaAn : (S, Mgh:) or a garden, or walled garden, ( Hadiyqap , Msb, K,) of trees, or of palm-trees, (Msb,) or of palms and other trees: (K:) or only if containing palm-trees and grape-vines;
sourceDefinition: A [ garden, such as is called ] busotaAn : (S, Mgh:) or a garden, or walled garden, ( Hadiyqap , Msb, K,) of trees, or of palm-trees, (Msb,) or of palms and other trees: (K:) or only if containing palm-trees and grape-vines; otherwise, if containing trees, called Hdyqp : (Aboo-'Alee in the Tedhkireh, TA:) or any bstAn having trees by which the ground is concealed: and sometimes concealing trees: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and palm-trees: (S:) or tall palm-trees: (Mgh:) or shadowing trees; because of the tangling, or luxuriousness of their branches; as though concealing at once what is beneath them: then a bstAn ; because of its dense and shadowing trees: (Bd in ii. 23:) or a bstAn of palms and other trees, dense, and shadowing by the tangling, or luxuriousness, and denseness, of their branches; as though it were originally the inf. n. of un. of jan~ahu , and meaning “ a single act of veiling ” or “ concealing ” &c.: (Ksh ib.:) then, with the article Al , [ Paradise, ] the abode of recompense; because of the jinaAn therein; (Ksh and Bd ib.;) or because the various delights prepared therein for mankind are concealed in the present state of existence: (Bd ib.:) [and] hence Aljan~aAtu [ the gardens of Paradise], (so in a copy of the S,) or jan~aAtu EadonK [ the gardens of continual abode ]: (so in another copy of the S:) [for] the pl. of jan~apN is A^ajin~apN (Mgh, Msb, K) and jinayonap (Msb, TA) and jun~apN , but this last is strange. (MF, TA.) [Dim. ↓ junayonapN , vulgarly pronounced jinayonap , and applied to A garden; as though it were a little Paradise. ]

sourceDefinition: A shield; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) because the owner conceals, or protects, himself with it; (Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ mijan~apN (Lh, K) and ↓ junaAnN and ↓ junaAnapN : (K:) pl. majaAn~u . Sb held it to be of the measure fiEal~N , from mjn ; but his opinion is opposed by the fact that the word is of the form which is significant of an instrument, by the doubling of the n , and by the syns. jnAn and jnAnp . (MF, TA.) It is said in a trad., that the hand [of a thief] shall not be cut off save for the value of a mijan~ ; which in the time of the Prophet was a deenár, or ten dirhems; for this is the lowest amount for which that punishment is to be inflicted. sourceDefinition: , (Msb, K,) [aor. yaHobuw ,] inf. n. Hubuw~N , (K,) He, or it (a thing, Msb, TA), was, or became, or drew, near. (Msb, K.) And hence, (TA,) Habawotu liloxamosiyna I was, or became, or drew, near to fifty [years]; (S, ISd, TA;) [as also Hbwt Alxamosiyna ; for] IAar says that HabaAhaA and HabaA lahaA both have this signification. (TA.) ― -b2- Habati AlA^aDolaAEu A_ilaY AlS~ulobi The ribs joined to the backbone; (K;) and in like manner, with the same meaning, one says of the entrails: and the ribs were near to the backbone. (TA.) And Habati Al$~araAsiyfu , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) i. e. [ The extremities of the ribs, projecting over the belly, ] were long, so that they were near one another. (K.) And HabaA Almasiylu The water-course, or channel of a torrent, became [ contracted, ] so that one part thereof was near to another. (K.) -A2- HabaA , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. yaHobuw , (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. HabowN , said of a child, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) before he stands; (Lth, TA;) as also HabaY , aor. yaHobiY , inf. n. HaboYN , which, however, is rare; (Msb;) He crept, or crawled, [or dragged himself along, ] upon his posteriors; (Mgh;) or so HbA EalaY A@sotihi : (S:) or he went along upon his posteriors, protruding his chest: (K:) or went along on four [or, as we say, on all fours ]: in this last sense it is used by the lawyers. (Mgh.) And, said of a man, He went along upon his hands, or arms, and his belly: (K:) or upon his hands, or arms, and his knees: or upon his posteriors: or upon his elbows and knees: (TA:) [or he crept, or crawled: for] you say, maA jaA='a A_il~aA HabowFA , meaning He came not save creeping, or crawling: and maAnajaAfulaAnN A_il~aA HabowFA [ Such a one escaped not save creeping, or crawling ]. (TA.) Also, said of a camel having his fore shank bound up to his arm, He crept, or crawled, along: [or he dragged himself along on the ground: ] and, said of a camel, he lay down, and crept, or crawled, [or dragged himself along, ] by reason of fatigue: or, as some say, being constrained to ascend a difficult tract of sand, he protruded his chest, and then crept, or crawled. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] said of an arrow, It glided along the ground, and then hit the butt: (S:) or so HbA A_ilaY AlgaraDi . (Msb.) ― -b3- And HbA AlmaAlu , (K,) inf. n. HabowN , (TA,) The cattle clave to the ground, motionless, by reason of emaciation. (K.) ― -b4- And Habati Als~afiynapu , (K,) inf. n. HabowN , (TA,) The ship ran. (K.) -A3- HabaA lahu It (a thing) presented itself, or its breadth, or width, or its side, to him, or it; syn. AiEotaraDa , (K,) or EaraDa ; (Mgh;) as do, for instance, waves to a ship; (TA;) and as clouds, like a mountain, before they cover the sky. (S.) And HbA Alr~amolu , aor. yaHobuw , inf. n. HabowN , The sands rose up, extending sideways ( muEotariDFA ): (TA:) or extended widely. (IAar, TA.) -A4- HabaAhu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. HabowN (TA) and HabowapN , (S, TA,) or this is a simple subst, (K,) and the inf. n. is HibaA='N , (Msb,) or this last also is a simple subst., (S, * K,) He gave him (S, Msb, K) a thing (Msb) without any compensation (Msb, K) and without [ receiving ] any favour, or benefit: or in a general sense. (K. [See also HibaA='N below.]) You say, HabaAhu ka*aA and bika*aA He (God, or a man,) gave him such a thing without [ receiving ] any favour, or benefit, and without requital. (Ham pp. 327 and 654.) ― -b2- And also, (K,) aor. as above, inf. n. HibaA='N , (TA,) He denied him, refused him, or refused to give him; (K, TA;) on the authority of IAar only. (TA.) Thus the verb bears two contr. significations. (K.) ― -b3- HbA maA Hawolahu He defended, protected, or guarded, what was around him; (As, S, K;) as also ↓ Hb~Ahu , inf. n. taHobiyapN . (S, K.) J cites as an ex. of the former verb, from a poem of Ibn-Ahmar, the phrase lamo yaHobuhaA faHolN [as though meaning A stallion did not defend them ]; referring to she-camels: but accord. to AHn, it means did not regard them; being occupied with himself. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, fulaAnN yaHobuw qaSaAhumo and yaHuwTu qaSaAhumo [ Such a one fights in their defence; or defends them in a distant quarter: but generally meant ironically: see 1 in art. HwT ]: both signify the same. (Abu-l-'Abbás, TA.)

definition: He drew together and confined his back and his shanks (S, Mgh, Msb, and Har p.
sourceDefinition: He drew together and confined his back and his shanks (S, Mgh, Msb, and Har p. 179) with his ridaA=' , (S,) or with a garment, or piece of cloth, or with some other thing, (Mgh, Msb, and Har ubi suprà,) when sitting, to be like him who is leaning [ his back against a wall ]: (Har ubi suprà:) he drew his legs against his belly with a garment, or piece of cloth, confining them therewith, together with his back, and binding it, or making it tight, upon them, so as to preserve him from falling, [ when he sat, ] like a wall: (IAth, TA:) and ↓ tHb~Y signifies the same: (TA:) or AHtbY biAlv~awobi he inwrapped himself with the garment: or he drew together and confined his back and his shanks with a turban or the like: (K:) for the Arabs not having walls in their deserts to lean against in their assembling, the man used to set up his knees in his sitting, and put against them a sword, or surround them [and his back] with a piece of cloth, or knit his hands, or arms, together upon them, and rest against them; this standing him in stead of leaning. (Har ubi suprà.) The doing this in one garment is forbidden, in a trad., lest, by accident, what decency requires to be concealed should become exposed. (IAth, TA.) You say also, AHtbY biyadayohi [ He confined his legs against his belly with his hands, or arms, in sitting, to support himself by so doing ]. (S, Msb. *) [See also qurofuSaA='u .] AlAiHotibaA='u with the sword is practised on the occasions of making a covenant for mutual protection, or war, or appointing a chief, and the like; because the sword may be wanted in these cases. (Ham p. 711.)

AiHotibaA='N : and also] a turban, or piece of cloth, or some other thing with which a man performs what is termed AlAiHotibaA='u : (Har p. 179:) pl. HubFY (Yaakoob, TA) and HibFY . (Yaakoob, S, TA.) (TA.) AlHbwp on Friday, when the Imám is reciting the khutbeh, is forbidden; because AlAiHotibaA=' induces sleep, and exposes the purity of the worshipper to be annulled. (TA.) -A2- See also HibaA='N .

sourceDefinition: Near; applied to thing of any kind. (S.) [Hence,] HaAbiY AlHuyuwdi Having the heads of the ribs connected [ by means of the cartilages ], one with another. (Az, TA.) And A_in~ahu laHaAbiY Al$~araAsiyfi Verily he is protuberant in the two sides. (S.) ― -b2- Having the shoulder-joints elevated to, or towards, the neck; (K;) applied to a man, and likewise to a camel. (TA.) -A2- An arrow that creeps along (Kt, K) upon the ground (Kt) to the butt, (Kt, K,) having fallen short of it: (Kt:) or an arrow that glides along the ground, and then hits the butt: pl. HawaAbK . (Msb.) Hence the saying, in a trad., A_in~a HaAbiyFA xayorN mino zaAhiqK , i. e. An arrow such as is termed HaAbK , though weak, having hit the butt, is better than one that goes beyond the butt by its vehemence of passage, and its force, not having hit it: meaning, by the two arrows, one who attains the truth, or right, or a part thereof, though weak; and another who goes beyond it, and far from it, though strong. (TA.) -A3- A thing presenting itself, or its breadth, or width, or its side; as also ↓ HabiY~N ; (K;) as in the saying of El-'Ajjáj, describing a [vessel such as is called] quroquwr , fahowa A_i*aA HabaA lahu HabiY~u i. e. [ So it, ] when waves present themselves, or their breadth, &c., to it. (TA.) [Hence,] ramalN HaAbK Overpeering sands presenting themselves, or their breadth, &c. (TA.) And jabalN HaAbK A heavy, overpeering mountain. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A certain plant: (K:) so called because of its height. (TA.) And HaAbiyapN A tract of sand ( ramolapN ), (K, TA,) elevated and overpeering, (TA,) producing that plant. (K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (IAmb, K, &c.,) inf. n. muHaA$aApN , (KL,) He set him aside as excluded from the description of them; [ excluded him from them; ] did not include him among them: (IAmb, TA:) from Ha$FY meaning the “side” of a thing: (Az, TA;) he excepted him from them; as also ↓ tH$~Ahu . (Lh, K, TA.) You say, $atamotuhumo wa maA HaA$ayotu minohumo A^aHadFA and ↓ mA taHa$~ayotu , i. e. [ I reviled them and ] I did not say [ of any one of them ] HaA$aY lifulaAnK [ Far is such a one from being included among those of whom I speak! or from any cause of reproach!]; or I did not except, of them, any one. (Lh, TA. [The same saying is repeated in the TA, in the supplement to this art. of the K, but with the substitution of H$yt for HA$yt ; perhaps by a mistake of the copyist: or it may be inferred from a statement of Fr and IAmb, which will be found below, that one also says mA ↓ Ha$ayotu .]) And En-Nábighah [Edh-Dhubyánee] says, (Mbr, S.) wa laA A^araY faAEilFA fiY Aln~aAsi yu$obihuhu wa maA A^uHaA$iY mina AlA^aqowaAmi mino A^aHadi [ And I shall not see an actor among mankind resembling him; and I do not except, of the companies of men, any one ]: which shows HaA$iY to be a verb perfectly inflected. (Mbr, S, Mughnee.) And hence the trad. of the Prophet, qaAl A^usaAmapu A^aHab~u Aln~aAsi A_ilaY~a maA HaA$aY faATimapa , i. e. [ He said, Usámeh is the most beloved of men to me: ] he did not except Fátimeh: mA being here a negative; not, as Ibn-Málik imagines, supposing this clause to be of the words of the Prophet, the mA which, with a verb following it, conveys the meaning of an inf. n. (Mughnee.) ― -b2- HaA$aY also denotes exception as a particle, or as a verb (S, Mughnee) having but one tense and no inf. n., (Mughnee,) according as it governs a gen. or an accus. case. (S.) You say, zayodK ↓ Darabotuhumo HaA$aY [ I beat them, except Zeyd ], using it as a particle; and Drbthm HA$Y zayodFA , using it as a verb. (S, I 'Ak * p. 169.) And sometimes one says, qaAma Alqawomu maA HaA$aY zayodFA [ The party stood, except Zeyd ]; (Mughnee, I' Ak p. 169;) like maA xalaA ; though Ibn-Málik [like Sb] disallows it: (I' Ak:) this being shown to be allowable by the saying of the poet, raA^ayotu Aln~aAsa maA HaA$aY qurayo$FA faA_in~aA naHonu A^afoDaluhumo faEaAlaA [ I have seen mankind, except Kureysh, that we are the most excellent of them in conduct ]. (Mughnee, I' Ak p. 170.) The agent of HA$Y [used as a verb having but one tense and no inf. n.] is a pronoun implied, relating to the inf. n. of the preceding verb, or to its act. part. n., or to a portion of what is meant by the [preceding] general noun: so that when one says, qaAma Alqawomu HaA$aY zayodFA , the meaning is, [ The party stood, but] their standing, or the stander of them, or a portion of them, was apart from Zeyd. (Mughnee.) [In the K, its use as a verb of this kind is not mentioned; but it is there said to govern the gen. case, like Hat~aY .] ― -b3- It also denotes remoteness from imperfection or the like, or freedom therefrom; as in the phrase ll~`hi ↓ HaA$aY [ I ascribe unto God remoteness from every imperfection or the like, or freedom therefrom; generally implying wonder or admiration, so that it may be rendered, how far, or how free, is God from every imperfection! ]: (Mughnee:) or this phrase means maEaA*a A@ll~`hi [ I seek protection by God; or, as often used by late writers, and in the present day, God forbid! ]; as also ll~`hi ↓ HaA$a ; (S, K;) the former being the original expression: (S:) it occurs, read in both these ways, in the Kur xii. 31 and 51; where it implies wonder at the power of God as manifested in the creation of such a person as Joseph. (Ksh, Bd.) Mbr and IJ and the Koofees hold that it is a verb; and that, in the [latter] verse the meaning is, Joseph hath kept aloof from disobedience for the sake of God; but such an interpretation as this is not suitable in the case of [the former verse,] HaA$a ll~`hi maA h`*aA ba$arFA : the truth is, that it is a noun, syn. with Altanoziyh or AlbaraA='ap , [accord. to different copies of the Mughnee, meaning tanoziyhFA or baraA='apF ,] as is shown by another reading, ll~`hi ↓ HaA$FA , with tenween, like baraA='apF ll~`hi ; and by the reading of Ibn-Mes'ood, A@ll~`hi ↓ HaA$a , like maEaA*a A@ll~`hi : some assert that it is a verbal noun, meaning A^atabar~aA^u [ I assert myself to be free, or clear, to God], or tabar~aA^otu [ I have asserted myself &c.]; but its being decl. in some dials. contradicts this. (Mughnee.) One says also, ↓ HaA$aAka and laka ↓ HaA$aY [ Far art thou from being included among those of whom I speak! or from any cause of reproach! or the like]; both meaning the same. (S, K.) And some of the Arabs say ↓ Ha$aY , (Fr, IAmb, TA,) dropping the A (IAmb, TA.) ― -b4- Sb says, (S, Mughnee,) with most of the Basrees, (Mughnee,) that it is only a particle governing the gen. case, (S, Mughnee,) syn. with A_il~aA ; (Mughnee;) because, if it were a verb, it would be allowable to make it a connective to maA , like xalaA ; and this he asserts to be not allowable. (S.) Mbr says that it is sometimes a verb; as is shown by the verse of En-Nábighah cited above; and by the saying HaA$aY lizayodK , because a particle cannot be made to precede immediately another particle; and because it suffers elision, as in the phrase HaA$a lizayodK , seeing that elision takes place in nouns and verbs only, exclusively of particles: (S, Mughnee *:) and IJ and the Koofees say the like: but Mbr also holds, in common with El-Jarmee and El-Mázinee and Zj and Akh and AZ and Fr and Aboo-'Amr EshSheybánee, that it is often a particle governing the gen. case, and seldom a trans. verb having but one tense and no inf. n., because syn. with A_il~aA . (Mughnee.) -A2- See also 5, in two places.

definition: [ He went aside, apart, or aloof, or he removed, withdrew, or retired to a distance, ] is from AlHaA$iyapu ;
sourceDefinition: [ He went aside, apart, or aloof, or he removed, withdrew, or retired to a distance, ] is from AlHaA$iyapu ; like tanaH~aY from Aln~aAHiyapu : (TA:) and [↓ tHA$Y has a similar meaning:] you say, taHaA$ayotu mino ka*aA I kept aloof from, shunned, or removed myself far from, such a thing; from AlHa$aA [or AlHa$aY ] meaning Aln~aAHiyapu . (Har p. 194.) ― -b2- And tH$~Y minohu ; (IAar, K;) and minohu ↓ HA$Y , (Har p. 294,) inf. n. muHaA$aApN ; (KL;) He abstained, or refrained, (IAar, K, KL, Har,) from him, (IAar, K, Har,) or it, (IAar, KL,) through disdain and pride; or he disdained, or scorned, or was ashamed of, him, or it. (IAar, K, Har.) ― -b3- And laA yataHa$~aY , (El-Báhilee, TA,) and lA ↓ yuHaA$iY , (Har p. 294,) He will not care, mind, heed, or regard. (El-Báhilee, Har, TA.) -A2- See also 3, in two places, first and second sentences.

sourceDefinition: , [in some copies of the S written with a final A (see Ha$FA in art. H$w ,)] The contents of the ribs; or what the ribs enclose: (S:) or the contents of the belly, below the HijaAb [or diaphragm ], consisting of the liver and the spleen and the kari$ [or stomach, properly that of a ruminant, but also applied to that of a man,] and what succeeds to this: or the portion between the shortest rib, which is in the extremity of the side, and the hip, or haunch: or the exterior of the belly: (K: [in the CK, Aw ZAhiri AlbaToni is erroneously put for Aw ZAhiru AlbaToni :]) and, accord. to the copies of the K, the HiDon : [in the CK, wAlHiDoni :] but correctly, the xaDor [or waist ]: (TA:) the dual is Ha$ayaAni , (Az, TA,) and the dual of Ha$FA is Ha$awaAni : (TA in art. H$w :) and the pl. [of both these sings.] is A^aHo$aA='N [generally meaning the bowels, or intestines ]. (S, TA.) [It is often used as meaning The belly: and the waist. ] You say rajulN xamiySu AlHa$aY A man lank in the belly. (S and K in art. xmS .) And huwa laTiyfu AlHa$aY He is slender in the waist: and of a woman, hiYa DaAmirapu AlHa$aY : and of women, hun~a DawaAmiru AlA^aHo$aA='i . (TA.) ― -b2- A side, quarter, region, or tract: (S, K:) a vicinage, or neighbourhood: shelter, or protection. (Z, K, * TA.) You say, A^anaA fiY Ha$aAhu I am in his quarter, vicinage, or protection: (Z, K:) [see also Ha$FA , in art. H$w :] and ↓ h`w^ulaA='i HaA$iyatahu These are in his quarter, or vicinage, and shadow, or protection. (TA.) -A2- Also inf. n. of Ha$iYa [q. v.]. (S, * K.)

(Mgh. definition: The windpipe, or passage of the breath;
sourceDefinition: The windpipe, or passage of the breath; (T, Mgh, TA;) by the cutting, or severing, of which, and of the mariYo' [or œsophagus] and wadajaAni [or two external jugular veins], the lawful slaughtering of an animal is completed: (T, TA:) accord. to the S and K, [and to the Msb, in art. Hlq , though it is there correctly and fully explained as meaning the windpipe, ] i. q. HaloqN : but in the M it is explained [agreeably with general usage] as the passage of the breath, and of coughing, from the jawof [or chest ]; consisting of a series of successively-superimposed cartilages ( A^aTobaAqu garaADiyfa ), before which, in the exterior of the throat, is nothing but skin; having its lower extremity in the lungs, and its upper extremity at the root of the tongue: from it pass forth the breath and the wind and the saliva and the voice: [see also another explanation voce HaloqN , from Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán, ” and the Msb:] pl. HalaAqimu and HalaAqiymu . (TA.) Accord. to some, the m is augmentative: accord. to others, radical. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] they say, nazalonaA mivola Huloquwmi Aln~aEaAmapi , meaning (assumed tropical:) We alighted in a strait, or confined, place. (TA.) And HalaAqiymu AlbilaAdi means (assumed tropical:) The strait, or confined, parts of the country, or of countries: (Mgh:) or the lateral, and extreme, parts thereof. (TA.)

definition: , originally, A natural wryness: and particularly an inversion of the foot, so that the upper side becomes the lower: so says IDrd;
sourceDefinition: , originally, A natural wryness: and particularly an inversion of the foot, so that the upper side becomes the lower: so says IDrd; (Mgh;) or a crookedness in the leg, or foot; (S, O, K;) i. e., (S, O, but in the K “ or ”) a turning of one of the great toes towards the other: (S, O, K:) or [ a distortion that causes ] one's walking on the outer part of the foot, on the side in which is the little toe: (K: [and so accord. to an explanation of ↓ A^aHonafu by IAar cited in the S:]) or an inclining [app. inwards ] in the fore part of the foot. (Lth, K.) ― -b2- Accord. to Ibn- 'Arafeh and the K, it signifies also A right state or condition or tendency; and accord. to the former, the epithet ↓ A^aHonafu is applied to him who has a wry leg, or foot, only by way of presaging a right state: but Er-Rághib explains HanafN better, as signifying an inclining, from error, to a right state or tendency. (TA.)

definition: The persons called in relation to the Imám Aboo-Haneefeh [ because they hold his tenets ];

sourceDefinition: Inclining to a right state or tendency: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or right, or having a right state or tendency; (Akh, S, TA;) thus applied in like manner as A^aEowaru is applied to a crow: (S:) [and particularly] inclining, from one religion, to another: (Ham p. 358:) or inclining, from any false religion, to the true religion: (Mgh:) or inclining in a perfect manner to El-Islám, and continuing firm therein: (K:) and any one who has performed the pilgrimage: (As, K, TA:) so say I'Ab and El-Hasan and Es-Suddee; and Az says the like on the authority of Ed-Dahhák: (TA:) or one who is of the religion of Abraham, (K, TA,) in respect of making the Sacred House [ of Mekkeh ] his kibleh, and of the rite of circumcision: (TA:) [and] a Muslim; (S, Mgh, Msb;) because he inclines to the right religion: (Msb:) but in this last sense, it is a conventional term of the professors: (Mgh:) [or,] accord. to AO, the worshipper of idols, in the Time of Ignorance, called himself thus; and when El-Islám came, they thus called the Muslim: accord. to Akh, it was applied in the Time of Ignorance to him who was circumcised, and who performed the pilgrimage to the [ Sacred ] House; because the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance held nothing of the religion of Abraham except circumcision and that pilgrimage: accord. to Ez-Zejjájee, it was applied in the Time of Ignorance to him who made the pilgrimage to the [ Sacred ] House and performed the ablution on account of janaAbap and was circumcised; and when El-Islám came, it was applied to the Muslim, because of his turning from the belief in a plurality of gods: (TA:) also one who devotes himself to religious exercises; or applies himself to devotion: (Msb:) its predominant application is to Abraham: (Mgh:) pl. HunafaA='u . (AO, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] HasabN HaniyfN Recent [ grounds of pretension to respect or honour ]; of the time of El-Islám; not old. (TA.) -A2- Short. (K.) -A3- A maker of sandals. (K.)

definition: , (A, TA,) aor. yaHuwSu , (A, K,) inf. n. HawoSN (S, A, Mgh, K) and HiyaASapN , (A, TA,) He sewed it, or sewed it up or together; (S, * A, Mgh, * K, TA;) namely, a garment, or piece of cloth: (A,...
sourceDefinition: , (A, TA,) aor. yaHuwSu , (A, K,) inf. n. HawoSN (S, A, Mgh, K) and HiyaASapN , (A, TA,) He sewed it, or sewed it up or together; (S, * A, Mgh, * K, TA;) namely, a garment, or piece of cloth: (A, TA:) or he sewed it with stitches far apart: (IB, TA:) or he sewed it without a patch; and only said of a skin, or of skin, and of a camel's foot. (TA.) Hence the prov., A_in~a dawaA='a Al$~aq~i A^ano taHuwSahu [ Verily the remedy for the rent is that thou sew it up ]. (A, K.) [And hence the saying,] laA^aToEanan~a fiY HawoSihimo (S, A) (tropical:) I will assuredly mar what they have repaired: (A:) or I will assuredly make a hole in what they have sewed up, and I will assuredly mar what they have repaired. (S, IB.) Or laA^aToEanan~a fiY HawoSika (tropical:) I will assuredly circumvent thee, ( laA^akiydan~aka [so in copies of the K, and in the TA, but in the CK, erroneously, laAkobidan~aka ,]) and I will assuredly labour for thy destruction. (AZ, K.) And it is said in a prov., TaEana fiY HawoSi A^amorK layosa minohu fiY $aYo'K , (K,) and A^amorK ↓ HuwSi , and A^amorK ↓ HuwSaY , (Yoo, K,) (tropical:) He laboured at that which he could not do well, and tasked himself to do that with which he had no concern. (ISh, K.) Or TaEanota fiY HawoSi A^amorK lasota minohu fiY $aYo'K (tropical:) Thou hast spoken of a thing with which thou hast no concern. (A.) You say also, qabola A^ano A^adoxula HawoSi Aln~aAsi A^aTomaEu fiY Darobihimo (tropical:) Before I penetrate into the case of the people, and test them, I am ambitious of smiting them. (A.) And maA TaEanota fiY HawoSihi (tropical:) Thou hast not attained the object of thy desire [ with respect to him or it: or perhaps the right reading is HawoSika , in which case the addition which I have made should be omitted]. (IB, as quoted in the L and TA.) ― -b2- HuSotu Eayona AlbaAziY , (S,) or Eayona AlS~aqori , (A,) aor. as above, and inf. n. of both the forms mentioned above, (S,) [ He seeled the falcon, or hawk; closed its eyes by running a thread through their lids. ] ― -b3- HaASa siqaA='ahu He closed a rent in his skin for water or milk by inserting into it two pieces of stick or wood; not having a siraAd with which to sew it. (TA.) ― -b4- HawoSN also signifies The making a coarctation between two things; (S, K;) and so HiyaASapN . (K.) You say HaASa bayonahumaA [ He contracted the space between them; meaning two things]. (TK.) -A2- HawiSato Eayonuhu , (A, Msb,) aor. taHowaSu , inf. n. HawaSN , (Msb,) His eye was, or became, narrow, or contracted, in its outer angle. (A, Msb.) [But see HawaSN below.] And HawiSa , (S, K,) aor. HawaSN , (TA,) said of a man, (S,) he had, in his eye, or eyes, what is termed HawaSN [as explained below]. (S, K.) [See also xawiSato Eayonuhu .]

definition: Anything that does not remain in one state;

(IAth.) ― -b2- The mirage; syn. saraAbN : (S, K:) or what remains of the latter part of the mirage, when it becomes dispersed, and delays not to pass away and come to nought. (Kr, L.) ― -b3- [ Gossamer; i. e.] what descends from the air in a time of intense heat, like spiders' webs; (S;) a thing like spiders' webs, which appears in a time of heat, (K,) descending from the sky, (TA,) resembling threads, (K,) or white threads, (TA,) in the air. (K.) [See luEaAbu Al$~amosi , in art. lEb .] ― -b4- The present world or life. (K.) ― -b5- The devil: (Fr, K:) or the devil of the 'Akabeh, called A^azab~u AlEaqabapi (IAth.) ― -b6- The [ imaginary creature called ] guwl : (S, K:) because it changes its appearance. (TA.) ― -b7- A certain insect, (K,) of a black colour, (TA,) that is upon the surface of water, and that does not remain in one place (K) save as long as the time of the winking of an eye. (TA.) ― -b8- A perfidious, or an unfaithful, man. (TA.) ― -b9- A woman whose affection does not last: (TA:) a woman evil in disposition: (K:) likened to a guwl inasmuch as her love does not last. (TA.) ― -b10- The wolf: (S, K:) because of his unfaithfulness. (TA.) ― -b11- The lion: (K:) because of his perfidiousness. (TA.) ― -b12- A calamity; syn. daAhiyapN . definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xatomN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and xitaAmN , (Lh, K, TA,) with kesr, (TA,) [in the CK, erroneously, xataAm ,] i. q. TabaEahu [ He sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed, it ]: (Msb, K:) or he put the xaAtam [or signet ] upon it: (Mgh:) namely, a thing, (S, Mgh,) or a writing or book and the like: and xatama Ealayohi signifies the same [or he put a seal, or the impression of a signet, upon it ]. (Msb.) Accord. to Er-Rághib, xatomN and TaboEN signify The impressing a thing with the engraving of the signet and stamp: and the former [as is indicated, but not plainly expressed, as distinguished from the latter,] is tropically used, sometimes, as meaning the securing oneself from a thing, and protecting [ oneself ] from it; in consideration of protection by means of sealing upon writings and doors: and sometimes as meaning the producing an impression, or effect, upon a thing from another thing; in consideration of the impress produced [by the signet]: and sometimes it is used as relating to (assumed tropical:) the reaching the end [of a thing]: (TA:) or the primary signification of xatomN is the act of covering over [a thing]: (Az, TA:) accord. to Zj, the proper meaning of xatomN and TaboEN is the covering over a thing, and securing oneself from a thing's entering it: some say that the former signifies the concealing a notification of a thing, [ as ] by putting one's fingers over it, by way of guarding oneself thereby. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, xatomu Al$~ahaAdapi [ The sealing of the testimony ]; which is thus described by El-Hulwánee: the witness, when he wrote his name upon a Sak~ [q. v.], caused his written name to be beneath a piece of lead, [i. e. covered it with a piece of lead,] and put upon it the impress of his signet, in order that there might be no falsification of it or substitution for it. (Mgh.) ― -b3- As to xatomu AlA^aEonaAqi [ The sealing of the necks ], the case is related, in the “Risáleh Yoosufeeyeh,” to have been this: 'Omar sent Ibn-Honeyf to seal the Euluwj [or unbelievers] of the Sawád; and he sealed five hundred thousand of them, in classes; that is, he marked them twelve dirhems, and twenty-four, and forty-eight; tying a thong upon the neck of each, and putting upon the knot a seal of lead. (Mgh.) ― -b4- xatomN also signifies The protecting what is in a writing by marking [or stamping ] a piece of clay [upon it, or by means of a seal of any kind ]. (TA.) ― -b5- And you say, of a man, xatama Ealayoka baAbahu [ He sealed his door against thee ]; meaning (tropical:) he turned away from thee, avoided thee, or shunned thee. (TA.) ― -b6- And xatama laka baAbahu [ He sealed for thee his door ]; meaning (tropical:) he preferred thee to others. (TA.) ― -b7- xatama EalaY qalobihi [which may be rendered He sealed his heart ] means (tropical:) he made him to be such that he understood not, and such that nothing proceeded from him; or he made his heart, or mind, to be such that it understood not, &c. (K, TA.) xatama A@ll~`hu EalaY quluwbihimo , in the Kur [ii. 6], is like the phrase in the same [xvi. 110 and xlvii. 18] TabaEa A@ll~`hu EalaY quluwbihimo : (TA:) it points to what God has made to be usually the case when a man has ended in believing what is false and in committing that which is forbidden, so that he turns not his face to the truth; this occasioning, as its result, his becoming inured to the approval of acts of disobedience, so that he is as though this habit were impressed upon his heart: the assertion of ElJubbáee, that it means God hath put a seal upon their hearts, as a sign, to the angels, of their infidelity, is nought: (Er-Rághib, TA:) Alxatomu is explained by IAar as meaning the preventing of the heart from believing. (L in art. xdE .) [See also TabaEa .] ― -b8- xatama Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. xatomN , also signifies [as indicated above] (assumed tropical:) He reached the end of the thing. (K.) And Al$~aYo'a ↓ Aixotatamotu (assumed tropical:) [ I ended, or finished, the thing, ] contr. of AifotataHotuhu . (S, TA.) You say, xatama AlquroA=na (assumed tropical:) He reached the end of the Kur-án [ in reciting it ]; (S, Er-Rághib;) [ he recited the whole of the Kur-án; ] he completed [ the recital of ] the Kur- án: (Mgh:) [and] he retained in his memory the last portion of the Kur-án; meaning he retained the whole of it in his memory. (Msb.) It is said of Suleymán El-Aamash, kaAna yaqoraA^u xatomFA , meaning (assumed tropical:) He used to recite the whole of the Kur-án; at one time, according to the reading of Ibn-Mes'ood; at another time, from the edition of 'Othmán. (Mgh.) ― -b9- You say also, xatama A@ll~`hu lahu bixayorK (assumed tropical:) [ May God make his end to be good ]. (S.) ― -b10- xatama Alba*ora (assumed tropical:) He covered over the sown seed: (Az, TA:) or xatamuwA EalaY Alba*ori (assumed tropical:) they turned up the earth over the sown seed, and then watered it: (Et-Táïfee, TA:) or xatama Alz~aroEa , (JK, K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. xatomN , (TA,) (tropical:) he watered the seed-produce, or sown field, the first time; (JK, K, TA;) because, when it is watered, it is finished ( xutima ) with the rHA [app. raHaA , which here seems to mean the “roller,” as being likened to a mill-stone, though I find no authority for this meaning]; (TA;) as also xatama Ealayohi : (K:) or xatamuwA EalaY zuruwEihimo means (assumed tropical:) they watered their sown fields while these were as yet kiraAb [app. meaning clear of vegetation ]. (JK, TA.) ― -b11- xatama Aln~aHolu (tropical:) The bees filled with honey the place in which they deposited it: (JK, A, TA:) or xatomN signifies bees' collecting some thin wax, thinner than the wax of the comb, and smearing with it the orifices of their xalaAyaA [or hives ]. (M, K, TA.)

Mohammad; (S;) also called ↓ AlxaAtamu and ↓ AlxaAtimu . (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) The last portion of anything that is drunk [&c.]. (TA.) xitaAmuhu misokN , in the Kur [lxxxiii. 26], means (assumed tropical:) The last that they will perceive thereof will be the odour of musk: (S, TA:) or, accord. to 'Alkameh and Mujáhid, its admixture shall be musk: accord. to Ibn-Mes'ood, its result shall be the taste of musk: Fr says, ↓ xaAtamN and ↓ xaAtimN and xitaAmN are nearly the same in meaning; whence the reading of 'Alee, misokN ↓ xaAtamuhu : and the explanation is this; that when any one shall drink thereof, he will find the last cup thereof to have the odour of musk: Er-Rághib says that the meaning is, the end, and the last draught, i. e. what shall remain, thereof shall be in perfume [like] musk: and that the assertion that it means it shall be sealed with musk is nought. [ A=miyna (or Amen ) is ] the seal, or stamp, and the mark, [ of the Lord of the beings of the whole world upon his servants the believers, ] which removes from them accidents, and causes of mischief; for the seal of the writing protects it, and precludes those who look from [seeing] what is within it. (TA.) ― -b3- See also xitaAmN , in seven places. [It is nearly syn. with xitaAmN , as Fr says: and thus,] it signifies also, (JK, K,) and so does ↓ xaAtimapN , (S, K,) (assumed tropical:) The end, or last part or portion, (JK, S, K,) and result, or issue, (K,) of a thing (JK, S, K) of any kind: (JK, K:) ↓ the latter [particularly] signifies (assumed tropical:) the last part or portion (JK, Msb) of a chapter of the Kur-án, (JK,) and of the Kur-án itself: (Msb:) [and (assumed tropical:) a concluding chapter or section: an epilogue: and an appendix: ] and ↓ muxotatamN signifies [in like manner] the contr. of mufotataHN ; as in the saying, Alt~aHomiydu mufotataHu A@loquroA=ni wa A@liAsotiEaA*apu muxotatamuhu (assumed tropical:) [ The declaration of the praises of God is the opening portion of the Kur-án, and the prayer for the protection of God is its closing portion ]; (A, TA;) and it is a chaste word, of frequent occurrence, though the contr. has been asserted. (TA.) One says also, AlA^aEomaAlu bixawaAtiymihaA [ Actions are characterized, or to be judged, as good or evil, by their results ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, i. e. xaAtamN , of a mare, (tropical:) The lower ring ( AlHaloqapu Ald~unoyaA [app. meaning the extremity, in which is the orifice, see HaloqataA Alr~aHimi and Haloqapu Ald~uburi , in art. (TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) The hollow ( nuqorap ) of the back of the neck; (JK, K, TA;) which is the cuppingplace. And see an ex. in a verse of Lebeed cited in art. dkn .] ― -b3- (tropical:) [The hymen; as being the seal of virginity; as also ↓ xaAtamN .] You say, zuf~ato A_ilayoka bixitaAmihaA (tropical:) [ She was conducted as a bride to thee with her seal of virginity ], and rab~ihaA ↓ bixaAtami [ with the seal of her Lord ]. (TA.) And [hence, app.,] siyqato hadiy~atuhumo A_ilayohi bixitaAmihaA (tropical:) [if it mean, as I suppose it to do, Their present was sent to him with what rendered it perfect or complete, or with what appertained to it ]. (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The furthest part of a valley. (JK, TA.) (assumed tropical:) The last of a company of men; (Lh, TA;) as also ↓ xaAtamN and ↓ xaAtimN : (K:) whence Aln~abiy~iyna ↓ xaAtamu (assumed tropical:) [ The last of the prophets ], in the Kur [xxxiii. 40]; accord. to one reading, ↓ xaAtum , with damm to the t ; (TA;) or xAtmu AlA^anobiyaA='i , i. e. Mohammad; (S;) also called ↓ AlxaAtamu and ↓ AlxaAtimu . (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) The last portion of anything that is drunk [&c.]. (TA.) xitaAmuhu misokN , in the Kur [lxxxiii. 26], means (assumed tropical:) The last that they will perceive thereof will be the odour of musk: (S, TA:) or, accord. to 'Alkameh and Mujáhid, its admixture shall be musk: accord. to Ibn-Mes'ood, its result shall be the taste of musk: Fr says, ↓ xaAtamN and ↓ xaAtimN and xitaAmN are nearly the same in meaning; whence the reading of 'Alee, misokN ↓ xaAtamuhu : and the explanation is this; that when any one shall drink thereof, he will find the last cup thereof to have the odour of musk: Er-Rághib says that the meaning is, the end, and the last draught, i. e. what shall remain, thereof shall be in perfume [like] musk: and that the assertion that it means it shall be sealed with musk is nought. (TA.) [See also xaAtamN and xaAtimapN .] -A3- Also, (IAar, K,) and ↓ xaAtimN , (K,) or, accord. to IAar, ↓ xataAmN , (TA,) sings. of xutumN , which signifies (assumed tropical:) The places of separation ( fuSuwS [q. v.]) of the joints ( mafaASil ) of horses. (IAar, K.) xaAtamN (JK, S, Msb, K) and xaA^otamN (TA) and ↓ xaAtimN , (S, Msb, K,) which is more commonly known than xaAtamN , (Msb, [but see what follows,]) and ↓ xaAtaAmN and ↓ xiytaAmN (JK, S, K, the last in the CK and TA ↓ xayotaAm ) and ↓ xitaAmN (K and TA but omitted in the CK) and ↓ xatamN (ISd, IHsh, K) and ↓ xatomN (Ez-Zeyn El-'Irákee, TA) and ↓ xayotamo (Ibn-Málik, TA) and ↓ xayotuwmN (EzZeyn El-'Irákee, TA) and ↓ xaAtiyaAmN (K) signify the same; (JK, S, Msb, K, TA;) [ A signet; generally a signet-ring; i. e.] a certain ornament ( HaloYN , M, K) for the finger, (K,) app., at the first, used for sealing, or stamping, therewith; so that the word is of the same class as TaAbaEN : afterwards, in consequence of frequency of usage, applied to one not used for that purpose: (ISd, TA:) or a ring having a faS~ of a substance different therefrom [ set in it; i. e., having a stone, or gem, set in it ]: if without a faS~ , it is called fataxapN : (Msb:) or ↓ xaAtimN signifies the agent [i. e. the person sealing, or stamping ]: (JK, Az, Msb:) xaAtamN , the thing that is put upon the piece of clay [or wax, for the purpose of sealing, or stamping ]: (Az, Msb, K:) the pl. [of xaAtamN and xaAtimN ] is xawaAtimN (K) and [properly of xaAtaAmN ] xawaAtiymu : (S, in which the former pl., though more common, is not mentioned, and K:) Sb says that those who use the latter pl. make it to be pl. of a sing. of the measure faAEaAlN , though it be not in their language; which shows that he knew not xaAtaAmN : the pl. of xatomN is xutuwmN . (TA.) ― -b2- xaAtamN also signifies A seal, or stamp, and a mark: so in a trad., in which it is said, A=miyna xaAtamu rab~i AlEaAlamiyna EalaY EibaAdihi Almuw^ominiyna , i. e. [ A=miyna (or Amen ) is ] the seal, or stamp, and the mark, [ of the Lord of the beings of the whole world upon his servants the believers, ] which removes from them accidents, and causes of mischief; for the seal of the writing protects it, and precludes those who look from [seeing] what is within it. (TA.) ― -b3- See also xitaAmN , in seven places. [It is nearly syn. with xitaAmN , as Fr says: and thus,] it signifies also, (JK, K,) and so does ↓ xaAtimapN , (S, K,) (assumed tropical:) The end, or last part or portion, (JK, S, K,) and result, or issue, (K,) of a thing (JK, S, K) of any kind: (JK, K:) ↓ the latter [particularly] signifies (assumed tropical:) the last part or portion (JK, Msb) of a chapter of the Kur-án, (JK,) and of the Kur-án itself: (Msb:) [and (assumed tropical:) a concluding chapter or section: an epilogue: and an appendix: ] and ↓ muxotatamN signifies [in like manner] the contr. of mufotataHN ; as in the saying, Alt~aHomiydu mufotataHu A@loquroA=ni wa A@liAsotiEaA*apu muxotatamuhu (assumed tropical:) [ The declaration of the praises of God is the opening portion of the Kur-án, and the prayer for the protection of God is its closing portion ]; (A, TA;) and it is a chaste word, of frequent occurrence, though the contr. has been asserted. (TA.) One says also, AlA^aEomaAlu bixawaAtiymihaA [ Actions are characterized, or to be judged, as good or evil, by their results ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, i. e. xaAtamN , of a mare, (tropical:) The lower ring ( AlHaloqapu Ald~unoyaA [app. meaning the extremity, in which is the orifice, see HaloqataA Alr~aHimi and Haloqapu Ald~uburi , in art. Hlq ,]) of the Tuboyap [evidently here used as a dial. var. of TuboY , i. e. the teat, though I do not find it mentioned in its proper art. in any lexicon; unless mino TuboyatihaA be a mistranscription for mn TuboyihaA ]: (K, TA:) so called by way of comparison [to a signet or seal]. (TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) The hollow ( nuqorap ) of the back of the neck; (JK, K, TA;) which is the cuppingplace. (TA.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The least waDaH [or whiteness ] of the legs (JK, K, TA) of horses; (JK, TA;) i. e. a slight whiteness in the parts next the hoof, less than what is termed taxodiymN . (TA.)

definition: and ↓ xaziyrapN A kind of food like EaSiydap with flesh-meat;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ xaziyrapN A kind of food like EaSiydap with flesh-meat; (K;) made of flesh-meat (S, TA) that has remained throughout a night, (TA,) cut into small pieces, and put into a cooking-pot with abundance of water, (S, TA,) and with salt; (TA;) and when it is thoroughly cooked, some flour is sprinkled upon it, (S, TA,) and it is stirred about with it, and seasoned with any seasoning that the maker pleases to add: (TA:) when there is no flesh-meat, it is called EaSiydap : (S, K, TA:) or a broth made with the water in which bran has been soaked, (Mgh, K, TA,) which water is strained, and then cooked: (Mgh, TA:) this is what is called by the Persians sabuwsabaA : (Mgh:) [see also HariyrapN :] or xaziyrap is flour thrown upon water or upon milk, and cooked, and then eaten with dates, or supped: it is also called saxiynapN and saxuwnapN and nafiytapN and Hu*oruq~apN : Hariyarp is thinner: (AHeyth, on the authority of an Arab of the desert:) and a soup made of grease or gravy (K) and flour; (TA;) as also ↓ xazarN : (K:) but no one except the author of the K mentions this last form: in the other lexicons, soup of grease or gravy is said only to be called xaziyrN and xaziyrapN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [The swine; the hog; the pig; ] a certain foul animal, (Msb,) well known; (K;) said to be forbidden [ to be eaten ] by every prophet: (Msb:) [fem. with p :] pl. xanaAziyru : (S, Msb, K:) not, as some say, xuzorN : [though this is an epithet applicable to swine:] (TA:) accord. to some, it is of the measure fiEoliylN ; because n is not [generally] added as a second letter: but accord. to others, of the measure finoEiylN ; because n is sometimes added as a second letter, and because it is held to be derived from xazira , since all xnAzyr are xuzor ; as it is said in the A, kul~u xinoziyrK A^axozaru . (TA.) ― -b2- xanaAziyru also signifies A well-known disease; (S;) [ scrofula; or glandular swellings in the neck; ] ulcers, (K,) or hard ulcers, (S,) which arise in the neck: (S, K:) or ganglions, or hard or nodous lumps beneath the skin, in the neck, and in soft parts, such as the armpits; but most frequently in the neck. (Mgh.)

definition: , (S, K, &c.,) vulgarly pronounced xayozaraAn , (TA,) [a coll. gen. n., The kind of cane called rattan; so in the present day;] a kind of Indian tree, which consists of roots extending upon the...
sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) vulgarly pronounced xayozaraAn , (TA,) [a coll. gen. n., The kind of cane called rattan; so in the present day;] a kind of Indian tree, which consists of roots extending upon the ground; as also ↓ xayozuwrN : (K:) or [ a kind of tree ] not growing in the country of the Arabs, but only in that of the Greeks; whence the saying of En-Nábighah El-Jaadee, bilaAduhumo bilaAdu AlxayozuraAni [ Their lands are the lands of the kheyzurán ]: it is a kind of plant with pliable and smooth twigs: (ISd:) or a kind of tree, (S,) the roots of the qanaA [by which are app. meant the canes of which spear-shafts are made ]: (S, Msb:) pl. xayaAziru . (S.) ― -b2- Reed, or reeds; cane, or canes. (S, K.) ― -b3- And hence, Musical reeds or pipes. (TA.) ― -b4- Spears: (IAar, K:) because of their pliableness: (TA:) [or because commonly made of canes:] pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b5- Any pliable twig or rod; (Mbr, K;) any piece of wood that is pliable. (AHeyth.) [Often applied in the present day to the osier; as well as to the rattan: n. un. with p .] ― -b6- The rod which kings hold in their hands, and with which they amuse themselves ( yataEab~avuwna ) and make signs. (Ham p. 710.) ― -b7- The pole with which a ship, or boat, is pushed or propelled, (Mbr, K,) when pliable, or bending; as also ↓ xayozaArapN . (Mbr, TA.) ― -b8- Also, (AO, Msb, K,) and with p , (S, TA,) The suk~aAn (S, Msb, K) of a ship, (K,) i. e. its kawoval [meaning the rudder ]: (TA:) or, accord. to 'Amr Ibn-Bahr, the lijaAm [lit. the bridle and bit, app. meaning the tiller ] of a ship, by means of which the suk~aAn , which is the *anab , is directed. (TA: [but instead of AltY bhA yqwm Als~uk~Anu whw fY Al*nb , I read Al*Y bh yuqaw~amu Als~uk~aAnu whwAl*~anabu .]) En-Nábighah says, describing the Euphrates in the time of its increase, or fulness, yaZal~u mino xawfihi Almal~aAHu muEotaSimFA biAloxayozuraAnapi baEoda AlA^ayoni waAln~ajadi [ By reason of his fear, the sailor becomes in a state of cleaving, or laying fast hold, upon the xyzrAnp , (which may here mean the pole above mentioned, or the rudder, or the tiller, ) after fatigue and distress ]. (S, TA.) In a trad. it is said that the devil, when he had been commanded by Noah to go forth from the ark, mounted upon the xyzrAn of the ark, i. e. its suk~aAn . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A man having narrow and small eyes: (S, A, Msb, K:) or having eyes of which the sight is contracted, naturally: (K:) or who looks from the outer angle of his eye: (A:) or who is as though he so looked: (S:) or who looks as though on one side: or who opens and closes his eyes; (K;) or, his eye: (M:) or who has a distortion ( HawalN ) of one of his eyes: (K:) or whose eyes look towards his nose: (TA:) [or whose eyes look towards their outer angles: (see xurorapN :)] and A^axozaru AlEayoni one who looks askew, or sideways; as also AlEayoni ↓ xaziru , an epithet applied to an enemy: (TA:) the fem. of A^axozaru is xazoraA='u : (A, Msb:) and the pl. is xuzorN . (K.) You say also A^aEoyunN xuzorN [meaning Eyes that are narrow and small: &c.]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O,) inf. n. xaDoxaDapN , (S, O, K,) He agitated it; moved it about; stirred it; shook it; namely, water, (S, O, K,) and the like, (S, O,) and sawiyq , and the like. (O, K.) You say also, xaDoxaDotu dalowiY fiY AlmaA='i [ I agitated, or dashed about, my bucket in the water ]. (O, TA.) Sakhr-el-Gheí El-Hudhalee says, describing a water to which he had come for drink, faxaDoxaDotu DufoniYa fiY jam~ihi xiyaADa AlmudaAbiri qidoHFA EaTuwfaA (O, TA,) i. e. [ And I dashed about my leathern bucket in the main body thereof, ] as he who is overcome in the game of el-meysir introduces among the other arrows a borrowed arrow [ that comes forth winning ], in the luck of which he has confidence. (TA in art. xwD .) This verb, though mentioned here, is [said to be] from xaADa , aor. yaxuwDu ; not from xaD~a ; therefore the poet here uses xayiAD for its inf. n. (O, TA.) You also say, jaA='ahu biAlxanojari faxaDoxaDa bihi baTonahu [ He came to him with the dagger, and stirred about with it his belly ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence a meaning of the inf. n. explained in the first paragraph of art. jld .]

definition: signifies The striking, or slapping, (JK, S, K,) a thing, [ so as to make a slight sound, ] with a dir~ap [q.
sourceDefinition: signifies The striking, or slapping, (JK, S, K,) a thing, [ so as to make a slight sound, ] with a dir~ap [q. v.], (JK, K,) or with something broad. (JK, S, K.) You say, xafaqahu , (Mgh, Msb,) aor. [and ], inf. n. xafoqN , (Msb,) He struck, or slapped, him, or it, [ so as to make a slight sound, ] with something broad, (Mgh, Msb,) such as a dir~ap . (Msb.) And xafaqahu , aor. and , He struck him slightly, [or so as to make a slight sound, ] with a sword, (S, K,) and with a whip, and with a dir~ap . (TA.) And xafaqa AlA^aroDa binaEolihi He struck the ground [ so as to make a sound ] with his sandal. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And hence, i. e. from xafaqahu as first explained above, (Mgh,) The sounding [ of the patting, or pattering, ] (JK, Mgh, K) of the sandal, (JK, K,) or of the sandals, (Mgh,) and the like: (TA:) and xafoqu AlA^aqodaAmi EalaY AlA^aroDi [ the sounding of the patting, or pattering, of the feet upon the ground ]. (Az, in TA, art. hms .) You say, xafaqa Aln~aEolu The sandal made a sound, or sounds. (Msb.) ― -b3- And xafaqati Alr~aAyapu , aor. and , inf. n. xafoqN and xafaqaAnN (S, K) and xufuwqN , (TA,) The banner, or standard, was, or became, in a state of commotion; moved, or went, to and fro; trembled; fluttered; or quivered; (S, K;) as also ↓ Axtfqt : (JK, K:) and in the same sense the former verb is used in speaking of the heart; (S, Msb;) xafaqaAnu Alqalobi signifying the fluttering, or palpitating, of the heart; (JK, T, K;) and in like manner xafaqaAnu AljinaAHi the fluttering, or flapping, of the wing: (JK:) so, too, the former verb is used in speaking of the mirage; (S, K;) and ↓ the latter verb likewise; (Lth, K;) and Ru-beh, by poetic license, makes the f of [the inf. n.] Alxafoq to be with fet-h, in his saying, mu$otabihi AlA^aEolaAmi lam~aAEi Alxafaqo [ Indistinct in respect of the signs of the way, glistening much in the quivering, or fluttering ]: (S, K:) in like manner, also, the former verb is used in speaking of lightning, (S, * TA,) inf. n. xafoqN ; (S;) and of a sword, and of the wind, and the like: and ↓ Axfq , said of the heart, and of lightning, and of a sword, and [ Axfqt said] of a banner, or standard, and of the wind, signifies the same: (TA:) or xafaqati Alr~iyHu , (S,) inf. n. xafaqaAnN , (S, TA,) signifies The wind made a rustling, or murmuring, or confused and continued, sound. (S, TA. *) And xafaqati Aln~aAqapu The she-camel broke wind, with a sound. (K.) ― -b4- xafaqa said of a bird, [because of the flapping, or sound, of its wings,] It flew. (S, K.) See also 4, first sentence. And said of an arrow, [because of its whizzing,] It went swiftly. (TA.) And xafaqa fiY AlbilaAdi , inf. n. xufuwqN , He went away into, or in, the countries, or lands, &c. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, said of a man, [in the CK, fulaAnFA is erroneously put for fulaAnN ,] He moved, or shook, his head, (S, K,) or bent [ down ] his head, (TA,) [or nodded, ] being drowsy, or dozing; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ Axfq : (Sgh, K:) or he drowsed, or dozed: (Mgh:) or he had a fit of drowsiness, or dozing, and then awoke: (TA:) or he slept; (JK, TA;) so says Ibn-Háni; (TA;) aor. and , (JK,) inf. n. xufuwqN . (TA.) And xafaqa biraA^osihi A^awo xafoqatayoni ↓ xafoqapF , (Mgh, Msb,) occurring in a trad., (Mgh,) He bent [ down ] his head, without the rest of his body, [or nodded, ] once, or twice, being taken by a fit of drowsiness, or dozing. (Msb.) It is said in another trad., kaAnato ruw^uwsuhumo A^awo xafoqatayoni ↓ taxofiqu xafoqapF [ Their heads used to nod by reason of drowsiness, or dozing, once or twice ]. (S.) And in another, kaAnuwA yanotaZiruwna AlEi$aA='a Hat~aY taxofiqu ruw^uwsuhumo , i. e. [ They used to wait for nightfall until ] they slept so that their chins dropped upon their breasts. (TA.) ― -b6- xafaqati Aln~ujuwmu , inf. n. xufuwqN , The stars set, or disappeared. (S.) And xafaqa Aln~axomu , (JK, Mgh, K,) aor. , inf. n. xufuwqN , (K,) The star, or the asterism, [or the Pleiades, ] set, or disappeared; (JK, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ Axfq : (JK:) or the former signifies the star, &c., went down in the place of setting; and in like manner the verb is used in speaking of the moon; (TA;) and of the sun: (IAar, TA:) and Aln~ujuwmu ↓ Axfqt signifies the stars retired to the place of setting: (S, K:) or, as some say, shone with a flickering light, or glistened, or shone brightly: [because of their twinkling, or apparent quivering: or] as though the A in the verb had a privative effect. (TA.) One says, waradotu xufuwqa Aln~ajomi , meaning [ I came ] at the time of the setting of the Pleiades; making the inf. n. an adv. n. [of time]. (S, TA.) ― -b7- Hence, (Mgh, TA,) or, as some say, from the same word as signifying “ the act of striking [or slapping], ” (TA,) Alxafoqu signifies The act of inserting; (Mgh;) [i. e.] the causing the penis to become concealed in the vulva; (K;) or the act of copulation: (JK:) or [rather] the penis' becoming concealed in the vulva. (Az, TA.) ― -b8- xafaqa All~ayolu The night for the most part passed away: (JK, K:) [and in like manner the verb is said of the day:] see xaAfiqN . ― -b9- xafaqa AlmakaAnu The place was, or became, void, or unoccupied. (TA.) ― -b10- xufuwqN in a horse is The being slender, or lean, in the belly. (AO, K. [See xafiqN .])

sourceDefinition: [ A single nodding of the head, by reason of drowsiness, or dozing ]: see 1, in two places: (Mgh, Msb:) a slight, or light, sleep. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting Ed-Dejjál [or Antichrist], yaxoruju fiY xafoqapK mina Ald~iyni , explained as meaning [ He will come forth ] in a time when religion will be drowsy, or dozing, by reason of weakness. (TA.) ― -b2- maDaY xafoqapN mina All~ayoli means A period ( saAEapN ) of the night passed. (TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, in two places.

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of xafaqa in all its senses]. It is applied as an epithet to the saraAb [or mirage, as meaning Quivering ]: and so ↓ xafuwqN [but with an intensive signification]. (JK.) And [the fem. pls.] xawaAfiqu and xaAfiqaAtN are used as [substs.] signifying Banners, or standards, [because of their fluttering. ] (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a man, Moving, or shaking, his head, or bending it [ down, or nodding ], when drowsy, or dozing. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, app.,] raA^ayotu fulaAnFA xaAfiqa AlEayoni (tropical:) I saw such a one with the eye cast down, and depressed in the head [as though drowsy]. (TA.) ― -b4- A^ay~aAmu AlxaAfiqaAti Certain days in which the stars [ in great number ] became scattered ( tanaAvarato [in the CK, erroneously, tanASarato ]), [causing a belief that the day of judgment was at hand, (see Kur lxxxii. 2,)] in the time of Abu-l-'Abbás and Aboo-Jaafar, (K, TA,) the 'Abbásees. (TA.) ― -b5- AlxaAfiqaAni is a term applied to The place of sunrise and the place of sunset, (AHeyth, JK, Mgh, K,) by the attribution of predominance to the latter; for AlxaAfiqu , meaning the disappearing, is applied to the place of sunset: (AHeyth, TA:) or the horizon ( A^ufuq ) of the place of sunrise and that of the place of sunset; (S, K;) accord. to Lth (TA) and ISk, (S, TA,) because the night and the day for the most part pass away (↓ yaxofiqaAni , so in the T and S, but in the K, erroneously, yaxotalifaAni , TA) between them, (T, TA,) or in them: (S, TA:) or the two [ opposite ] extremities of the heaven and the earth: (As, Sh, K:) or the end of the heaven and earth: (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, K:) or two vacant spaces ( hawaAA=ni ) next to the two [ opposite ] sides of the earth: (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA:) and xawaAfiqu Als~amaA='i signifies The regions of the heaven from which issue the four [ cardinal ] winds. (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, K.) One says, maAbayona AlxaAfiqayoni mivoluhu There is not between the place of sunrise and the place of sunset the like of him. (TA.) And A^aloHaqahu A@ll~`hu biAlxaAfiqi and biAlxawaAfiqi [ May God remove him to the place of sunset and to the four cardinal regions of the heaven or earth]. (TA.) ― -b6- xaAfiqN also signifies A place void of, or unoccupied by, any one to cheer by his presence. (TA.)

definition: , applied to a desert ( falaApN ), Wide, (S, K,) in which the saraAb [or mirage ] quivers.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a desert ( falaApN ), Wide, (S, K,) in which the saraAb [or mirage ] quivers. (S.) ― -b2- Applied to a horse or mare, (JK, S, K, TA,) mostly to a female, (IDrd, TA,) and a she-camel, (IDrd, JK, K,) and a male ostrich, (IDrd, S, K,) Quick, or swift: (K:) or very quick or swift: (JK, S:) and ↓ xanofaqiyqN , (so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ xayofaqiyqN , (so in other copies of the K and in the JK and O, and so written by A'Obeyd,) each correct, the n in the former and the Y in the latter augmentative, (MF, TA,) is applied to a she-camel and a male ostrich, (JK, K,) in the former sense, as is also xayofaqN , (JK,) or in the latter sense. (A'Obeyd, K.) Accord. to some, applied to a she-camel, it signifies Lean, or lank, in the belly; having little flesh. (TA.) And, applied to a woman, Long in the rufogaAni [app. here meaning the two inguinal creases ], slender in the bones, and wide in step. (El-Kilábee, K.) Also, applied to a woman, Quick and bold; and so ↓ xanofaqiyqN : (TA:) or the latter, so applied, signifies light, active, or agile, and bold: and Sb says that the n in it is augmentative; deriving it from xafoqu Alr~iyHi [explained above: see 1]. (S.) ― -b3- Also i. q. daAhiyapN [meaning either A calamity, or, as an epithet, very cunning ]; (AA, K;) and so ↓ xanofaqiyqN ; which latter occurs in a verse, variously related, applied to a child brought forth by a woman who had been in labour a whole night; (S, K;) meaning dAhyp ; or, as some explain it, in this instance, meaning imperfectly formed; (TA;) [and is also used as a corroborative of dAhyp ; for] one says ↓ daAhiyapN xanofaqiyqN [ a great, or severe, calamity; or extremely cunning ]. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , (K,) aor. , (TK,) inf. n. dajolN , (T, TA,) He smeared a camel with tar; (K) as also ↓ dj~l : (TA:) or he smeared him over his whole body with tar: (K:) or dajolN signifies the smearing in the part that is mangy, or scabby, with tar: (T, TA:) and ↓ tadojiylN , [inf. n. of daj~ala ,] the smearing a camel over his whole body with tar: (T, S:) and the putting the tar upon the masaAEir [or armpits, and inner parts of the roots of the thighs or other similar parts, only,] is termed das~N . (S.) ― -b2- He lied: [as though meaning he concealed the truth with falsehood: for, accord. to the KL, dajolN signifies the concealing the truth: (not, as Golius understood the explanation, its being concealed:)] and confounded or perplexed [such as heard him]. (K, TA. [In the CK, AaHoraqa is erroneously put for A^axoraqa .]) ― -b3- [And app. He enchanted, or fascinated: for] dajolN is also syn. with siHorN . (TA.) ― -b4- He compressed; coivit, or inivit. (As, K.) ― -b5- He tra versed the regions, or tracts, of the earth, or land. (K.) ― -b6- The primary signification of dajolN is [app. The act of covering; like tadojiylN : but it is said to be] the act of mixing, or confusing. (JM.) -A2- Accord. to Fr, one says, huwa yadojulu biAld~alowi and yadoluju bihaA [ He transfers the bucket from the mouth of the well to the watering-trough, &c.]: the former verb being formed by transposition. (TA.) -A3- dajolN also signifies The having one eye and one eyebrow. (KL.) [See daj~aAlN , last sentence.]

definition: [in its primary application app.
sourceDefinition: [in its primary application app. signifies A person, or thing, that covers anything in any manner; or that does so much, or often. ― -b2- And hence,] A gilder or silverer. (Th, Msb.) ― -b3- And [hence,] A liar: (Msb, TA:) [one who conceals the truth with falsehood: a falsifier: and] one who deceives, deludes, beguiles, circumvents, or outwits, much, or often; very deceitful, &c.; or a great deceiver, &c.: (JM:) pl. daj~aAluwna (Msb, TA) and dajaAjilapN . (TA.) Hence, in a trad. relating to Aboo-Bekr's demanding Fátimeh in marriage, qado waEadotuhaA liEaliY~i walasotu bidaj~aAlK , meaning [ I have promised her to 'Alee, and I am not ] a liar. (TA.) ― -b4- And i. q. ↓ daj~aAlapN , (S,) which signifies A great company of men journeying together, (S, K, TA,) covering the ground by their multitude: or a company of men journeying together, carrying goods for traffic. (TA) ― -b5- Also, (thus correctly written, but in [some copies of] the K, and by Sgh, written ↓ dujaAlN , like guraAbN , TA,) Gold: or gold-wash for gilding. (K, TA.) ― -b6- And The diversified wavy marks, or streaks, or grain, ( firinod ) of a sword. (K.) ― -b7- Ald~aj~aAlu , (S, Msb, K,) i. e. AlmasiyHu Alka*~aAbu [ The False Christ, or Antichrist ], (S, K, *) said to be a certain man of the Jews, who is to come forth in the last days of our people, (TA,) is so called from dajala , because he will cover the earth [with his adherents] (K, TA,) like as the tar covers the body [of the mangy camel]: (TA:) or because of his lying, (K, * TA,) in arrogating to himself godship: (TA:) or because he will traverse most of the regions of the earth: (Abu-l-'Abbás, K, * TA:) or from daj~ala , “ he covered, ” (K,) because he will cover mankind with his infidelity; (TA;) or because he will cover the earth with the multitude of his forces; (Msb, TA;) or because he will cover the truth with falsehood: (TA:) or from the same verb signifying “ he gilded; ” because he will involve men in confusion, or doubt, by falsehood, (K, * TA,) or will deceive them, or will manifest the contrary of what he conceives or conceals: (TA:) or from daj~aAlN signifying “ gold, ” or “ gold-wash for gilding; ” because treasures will follow him wherever he goes: (K, * TA:) or from the same word as signifying the “ firinod of a sword: ” or from daj~aAlapN explained above: or from dajaAlN ; because he will defile the ground: or from daj~ula Aln~aAsu . (K.) [Accord. to one trad., he will have but one eye and one eyebrow: and hence, app., it is said that] ― -b8- daj~aAlN also signifies Having one eye and one eyebrow. (KL.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, &c.,) aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. das~N (M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and das~iysaY , (K,) like xiS~iySaY , (TA,) He hid it, or concealed it, (Lth, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) namely, anything, (A, Mgh, Msb,) in the earth or dust, (S, Mgh,) or beneath a thing: (A, Mgh:) he buried it (A, Msb, K) in the earth or dust, (Msb,) or beneath a thing: (K:) or he put it in, or inserted it, beneath: (M:) or, accord. to some, he put it in, or inserted it, with force; he thrust it in: (TA:) and ↓ das~asahu and ↓ das~aAhu , (M, K, *) in the latter of which one of the s is changed into Y because the reduplication is disliked, (M, * TA,) signify the same as das~ahu , (M, K, *) [or, probably, have an intensive signification.] It is said in the Kur [xvi. 61], A^amo yadus~uhu Alt~uraAbi Or whether he shall bury it in the dust: meaning, his female child, which he buried alive: the pronoun agreeing with the word mA [which precedes in the same verse]. (T, TA.) It is also said in the Kur [xci. 9 and 10], qado A^afolaHa mano zak~aAhaA waqado ↓ xaAba mano das~aAhaA , (M, K, *) in which ds~AhA is for ↓ das~asahaA , like taZan~ayotu for taZan~anotu , (K,) because the niggardly conceals his place of sojourning and his property, but the liberal makes his place of sojourning upon an open and elevated spot that he may not be concealed from guests and those who desire to come to him: (Fr, Zj, K: *) or the meaning is, He is successful who maketh it (namely his soul) pure and believing, and he is unsuccessful who introduceth it among the good when he is not of them: (IAar, Th, M, K: *) or [ he is successful who maketh it to increase in grace by good works, ] and he is unsuccessful who maketh it vile and little by evil works: (M:) or the latter clause means, and he is unsuccessful who hideth it, and maketh it obscure and of no reputation, by the neglect of almsgiving and of obedience [ to God in other matters ]: (TA:) or the soul is unsuccessful that God rendereth obscure [so I render, here, ds~AhA ]. (Fr, K.) -A2- das~a AlbaEiyra , aor. , inf. n. das~N , He anointed the camel with tar, not thoroughly, [ but only in the arm-pits, and the inner parts of the roots of the thighs or other similar parts: ] (M:) [for it is said that] dus~a AlbaEiyru signifies the camel was anointed with tar in the parts called the masaAEir : (S: [see dajala :]) or the latter signifies the camel became swollen in the parts so called. (M.) Hence the prov., layosa Alhano'u biAld~as~i [which see explained in art. hnA^ ]. (TA in art. hnA^ . [In the S and M and TA, in the present art., instead of Alhano'u , we find AlhinaA='u : but the former is the preferable reading.])
