definition: signify the same: (Fr, K and TA in art.
sourceDefinition: signify the same: (Fr, K and TA in art. dEY :) the aor. of the former is A^adoEuw , (TA in that art.,) sec. pers. fem. sing. tadoEiyna and tadoEuwiyna and tadNEuyona , the last with an inclination to the sound of a dammeh in the vowel of the E [so that it is between a kesreh and a dammeh], and sec. pers. masc. and fem. pl. tadoEuwna : (S, TA:) aor. of the latter verb A^adoEiY : inf. n. duEaA='N . (TA in art. dEY .) duEaA='N [generally] signifies [or implies] The act of seeking, desiring, asking, or demanding. (KT.) ― -b2- You say, daEaA A@ll~`ha , (K,) first pers. daEawotu , aor. A^adoEuw , (Msb,) inf. n. duEaA='N (Msb, K) and daEowaY , (K,) in which latter the alif [written Y ] is to denote the fem. gender, [and therefore the word is without tenween,] (TA,) He prayed to God, supplicated Him, or petitioned Him humbly, (Msb, K, TA,) desiring to obtain some good that He had to bestow. (Msb, TA.) And daEawotu A@ll~`ha lahu [ I prayed to God for him ]; and Ealayohi [ against him ]; inf. n. duEaA='N : (S:) [and daEawotu lahu I prayed for him, or blessed him; and daEawotu Ealayohi I prayed against him, or cursed him: ] and daEawotu lahu bixayorK [ I supplicated for him good ]; and daEawotu Ealayohi bi$ar~K [ I imprecated upon him evil ]. (TA.) ― -b3- daEaA biAlkitaAbi He desired, or required, or requested, that the writing, or book, should be brought. (TA.) And daEaA A^anofuhu AlT~iyba His nose, perceiving its odour, desired the perfume. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence,] daEaA bihi , said of anything in the earth, means It needed it; or required it: [and so daEaA A_ilayohi : one says of a wall, daEaA A_ilaY A_iSolaAHihi It needed, or required, its being repaired: (see 10 in art. rm :) and] one says to him whose clothes have become old and worn out, qado daEato viyaAbuka [ Thy clothes have become such as to need thy putting on others; or] thou hast become in need of putting on other clothes. (Aboo-'Adnán, TA.) [See also 10.] ― -b5- daEawotuhu , (S, MA, Mgh, Msb,) and daEawotu bihi , (MA, [and of frequent occurrence,]) inf. n. [ duEaA='N and] daEowN , (TA, [but the former is more common,]) also signify I called him, called out to him, or summoned him, (S, MA, Mgh, Msb,) syn. naAdayotuhu , (Mgh, Msb,) or Ald~uEaA='u is to the near and Aln~idaA='u is to the distant, (Kull p. 184,) and desired him to come, to come forward, or to advance; (Msb;) and ↓ AisotadoEayotuhu signifies the same, (S, MA,) [i. e.] I called him to myself. (MA.) One says, daEaA Almuw^a*~inu Aln~aAsa A_ilaY AlS~alaApi [ The mw^*~n called the people to prayer ]. (Msb.) And the saying of En-Nahdee kun~aA nadoEuw wanadaEu means We used to call, or invite, them to ElIslám at one time, and to leave doing so at another time. (Mgh.) And daEawotu Aln~aAsa , (Msb,) inf. n. duEaA='N and daEowapN , (S,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) and madoEaApN , (S, [app. there mentioned as an inf. n., agreeably with many other instances,]) means also I invited people to eat with me, or at my abode. (Msb.) ― -b6- [Hence,] maA daEaAka A_ilaY h`*aA AlA^amori What drew, led, induced, or caused, and constrained, or drove, thee to do this thing? (TA.) And daEaAnaA gayovN waqaEa bibaladK qado A^amoraEa , i. e. [ Rain that fell in a region which had become abundant in herbage invited us thither, or] was the cause of our seeking its herbage. (TA.) And yadoEuwmaA baEodahu , (S, Mgh, K, *) or yadoEuwmaA waraA='ahu mina All~abani , (Nh, TA,) [ It draws, or attracts, what is to come after it, of the milk, ] said of some milk left in the udder. (S, Nh, Mgh, K, TA.) And daEaAhu A_ilaY AlA^amiyri He drove him, or urged him to go, [but more commonly meaning he summoned him, ] to the prince, or commander. (K, * TA. definition: signifies (tropical:) The proposing an enigma or enigmas to a person;
sourceDefinition: signifies (tropical:) The proposing an enigma or enigmas to a person; or the contending with another in doing so; syn. muHaAjaApN . (S, K, TA.) You say, daAEayotuhu (tropical:) I proposed to him an enigma or enigmas; &c. (TA.) A poet says, A^udaAEiyka maA musotaSoHabaAtN maEa Als~uraY HisaAnN wamaA A=vaAruhaA biHisaAni [(assumed tropical:) I propose to thee an enigma: What are things that are taken as companions in night-journeying, good, and the effects whereof are not good? ]: meaning swords. (S.) ― -b2- And The asking a thing of one much, so as to weary; as also muHaAjaApN . (K.) ― -b3- daAEayonaA AlHaAy^iTa Ealayohimo (tropical:) We pulled down, or demolished, the wall upon them, from the sides [or foundations ] thereof. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- [Golius assigns other significations to daAEaY , for which I find no authority: namely, “ Convocavit ad Deum propheta, præco sacer, ” followed by an accus.: and “ Contendit contra alium: Provocavit: pecul. rem vindicans sibi vel arrogans. ”]

definition: signifies The calling, summoning, or convoking, one another.
sourceDefinition: signifies The calling, summoning, or convoking, one another. (Mgh.) You say, tadaAEawo liloHarobi [ They called, summoned, or convoked, one another for war: and hence,] (assumed tropical:) they prepared themselves for war. (TA.) And tadaAEawoA Ealayohi , (Msb, K,) or EalaY baniY fulaAnK , (T, M,) They collected themselves together, (K,) or called one another so that they assembled together, (M,) or leagued together, and called one another to mutual aid, (T, Msb, *) against him, (Msb, K,) or against the sons of such a one. (T, M.) And tadaAEaY Ealayohi AlEaduw~u mino kul~i jaAnibK (assumed tropical:) The enemy advanced against him from every side. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] tadaAEati Als~aHaAbapu biAlbaroqi waAlr~aEodi mino kul~i jaAnibK (assumed tropical:) The cloud lightened and thundered from every quarter. (TA.) And tadaAEaY AlbunoyaAnu , (Mgh, Msb,) or AlbinaA='u , (TA,) (tropical:) The building cracked in its sides, (Msb,) or became much broken, (TA,) and gave notice of falling to ruin: (Msb, TA:) or cracked in several places, without falling; and in like manner, tadaAEati AlHiyTaAnu , (Mgh,) the walls cracked in several places, without falling: (Mgh, K: *) and tadaAEati AlHiyTaAnu liloxaraAbi the walls fell to ruin by degrees; syn. tahaAdamat : (S:) [but Mtr says,] tadaAEato A_ilaY AlxaraAbi is a vulgar phrase; not [genuine] Arabic. (Mgh.) And tdAEY said of a sand-hill, (assumed tropical:) It, being put in notion, or shaken in its lower part, poured down. (Msb.) And [hence,] tadaAEato A_ibilu baniY fulaAnK (tropical:) (tropical:) The camels of such a one became broken by emaciation. (TA.) ― -b3- tadaAEawo biAlA^aloqaAbi They called one another by surnames, or nicknames. (Msb.) ― -b4- Alt~adaAEiY also signifies (assumed tropical:) The trying one another with an enigma or enigmas; or contending, one with another, in proposing an enigma or enigmas; syn. Alt~aHaAjiY . (TA in art. Hjw .) You say, bayonahumo A^udoEiy~apN yatadaAEuwona bihaA (assumed tropical:) [ Between them is an enigma with which they try one another; or by proposing which they contend, one with another ]. (S, K. *) ― -b5- yatadaAEawona faSola AlxiTaAbi (assumed tropical:) They compete, one with another, [ as though each one challenged the others, ] in discoursing of the science of chasteness of speech, and eloquence. (Har p. 446.) ― -b6- See also 8, in two places. -A2- [It is also used transitively:] you say, tadaAEawuA Alqawoma They [ together ] called the people. (Mgh in art. nqD . [See 6 in that art.])

definition: He asserted a thing to be his, or to belong to him, or to be due to him, either truly or falsely: (K, * TA:) he claimed a thing;
sourceDefinition: He asserted a thing to be his, or to belong to him, or to be due to him, either truly or falsely: (K, * TA:) he claimed a thing; laid claim to it; or demanded it for himself: and he desired a thing; or wished for it. sourceDefinition: [as an inf. n. of un.] signifies A single time or act (S, Msb) [ of prayer and of imprecation, as is indicated in the S, and also, though less plainly, in the TA]. See duEaA='N . ― -b2- [Also, as such, A call. ] You say, huwamin~iY daEowapu Alr~ajula (K, TA) and Alkalobi , and daEowapa Alr~ajuli and Alkalobi , in the former case dEwp being used as a simple subst., and in the latter case as an adv. n., (TA,) meaning qadoru maA bayoniY wabayonahu *aAka [i. e. He, or it, is distant from me the space of the call of the man and of the dog ]. (K, TA.) And lahumu Ald~aEowapu EalaY gayorihimo The call is to them before the others of them: (K, TA: [ yabodaA^u in the CK is a mistake for yubodaA^u :]) accord. to the T and the Nh, in the case of gifts, or pay, or salary. (TA.) ― -b3- The call to prayer: whence, in a trad., Ald~aEuwapu fiY AlHaba$api [meaning The office of calling to prayer rests among the Abyssinians ]; (JM, TA;) said by the Prophet in preference of his muw^a*~in Bilál. (JM.) ― -b4- A call, or an invitation, to El-Islám. (Mgh.) You say, A^adoEuwka bidaEowapi AlA_isolaAmi and AlslAm ↓ diEaAyapi and AlAslAm ↓ daAEiyapi , meaning I call thee, or invite thee, by the declaration of the faith whereby the people of false religions are called: daAEiyapN being an inf. n. syn. with daEowapN , like EaAfiyapN and EaAqibapN : (JM:) daEowapu AlA_isolaAmi and ↓ daEAyatuhu and ↓ daAEiyatuhu signify the same: and daEowapu AlHaq~i [in like manner] means the declaration that there is no deity but God. (TA.) ― -b5- An invitation to food, (S, M, Msb, K, TA,) and to beverage; or, accord. to Lh, specially a repast, feast, or banquet, on the occasion of a wedding or the like: (TA:) thus pronounced by most of the Arabs, except 'Adee of Er-Rabáb, who pronounce it, in this sense, ↓ diEowapN : (A 'Obeyd, S, M, Msb:) it is an inf. n. in this sense, (S,) or a simple subst.: (Msb:) and ↓ duEowapN signifies the same; (K;) or, as some say, this, which is given as on the authority of Ktr, is a mistake: (TA:) and so does ↓ madoEaApN [app. an inf. n.]. (S, Msb, K.) You say, kun~aAfiY daEowapi fulaAnK and ↓ madoEaAtihi , meaning [ We were included in ] the invitation ( duEaA=' [see 1]) of such a one to food: (S, Msb: [but in the latter, naHonu , in the place of kun~aA :]) [or we were at the repast, or feast, or banquet, of such a one; for] you say [also] daEaAhu A_ilaY Ald~aEowapi and ↓ AlY AlmadoEaApi [ He invited him to the repast, or feast, or banquet: and in this sense daEowap is commonly used in the present day]. (MA.) ― -b6- See also diEowapN : ― -b7- and daEowaY . ― -b8- Also i. q. HalifN or HalofN (accord. to different copies of the K) [both in the sense of Confederation to aid or assist ]: (K, TA:) [whence] one says, daEowapN fulaAnK fiY baniY fulaAnK [meaning The confederation of such a one is with the sons of such a one ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is an inf. n. of 1; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ daEowaY : (K:) the former is originally duEaAwN : (S:) [both, used as simple substs., signify A prayer, or supplication, to God:] and the pl. of the former is A^adoEiyapN . (S.) IF says that some of the Arabs, for ↓ daEowapN , say ↓ daEowaY , with the fem. alif [written Y ]. (Msb, TA.) One says, Aall~`hum~a Almusolimiyna ↓ A^a$orikonaA fiY daEowaY , meaning [ O God, make us to share ] in the prayer ( duEaA=' ) of the Muslims. (TA.) And hence, in the Kur [x. 10], fiyhaA suboHaAnak A@ll~`hum~a ↓ daEowaAhumo [ Their prayer in it shall be sbHAnk All~`hm~ ]. (TA.) sourceDefinition: [ Blood; ] one of the [ four ] A^axolaAT [or humours ], (M,) well known: (T, M, K:) accord. to some, (Msb,) it is originally damawN : (S, Msb:) or it is originally damFY ; (Zj, Mbr, S, M, Msb, K;) thus in the correct copies of the K; (TA; [in some copies damoYN , and in the CK damaYN ;]) though deviating from other words of the same form in respect of its pl. [which see below]; (Mbr, S;) as is shown by its dual, (Zj, M,) which is damayaAni , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) whereby [also] the letter gone from it is shown to be Y ; (Mbr, S;) but it has also for its dual damaAni ; (T, M, Msb, K;) and some of the Arabs say damawaAni ; (S, M;) in which last, however, [accord. to ISd,] the w is substituted for Y , though generally w is changed into Y : (M:) and this original form is used by a poet, [namely, Hoseyn Ibn-El-Homám, accord. to one of my copies of the S,] in his saying, falasonaA EalaY AlA^aEoqaAbi tadomaY kuluwmunaA ↓ wal`kino EalaY A^aqodaAminaA yaqoTuru Ald~amaY [ And we have not our wounds bleeding upon the heels; but upon our feet the blood drops ]: (S:) or it is originally damoYN ; (Sb, T, S, M, Msb;) as is shown by its pls., (Sb, S,) which are dimaA='u (Sb, T, S, M, K) and dumiY~N , (Sb, S, M, K,) also pronounced dimiY~N ; (TA;) like as ZaboYN and dalowN have for their pls. ZibaA='u and ZubiY~N and dilaA='N and duliY~N ; for if it were like qafFA and EaSFA , it would not have such pls. (Sb, S.) dam~N is ignored by Ks; but is used by poetic license; (M;) or it is a dial. var. of damN . (K in art. dm .) ↓ damapN has a more special signification than damN , the two words being like bayaADapN and bayaADN ; (S;) [i. e.] it signifies A portion of blood: (T, M, K:) or it is a dial. var. of damN , (M, K,) accord. to IJ. (M.) The dim. of damN is ↓ dumaY~N . (S.) [Hence,] rajulN *uw damK A man seeking to obtain, or prosecuting for, [ the revenge of ] blood. (TA.) damu fulaAnK fiY vawobi fulaAnK is a saying of the Arabs, meaning (assumed tropical:) Such a one is the slayer of such a one. (Ham p. 632.) Ald~amu Ald~amu waAlhadomu Alhadomu , or waAlhadama Alhadama , is a saying of the Arabs, meaning If thy blood be sought, my blood shall be sought; and if thy blood go for nought, my blood shall go for nought: or, accord. to the latter reading, as is said in the Nh, and where thou shalt be buried, I will be buried: or thine abode shall be mine abode. (JM in art. hdm , q. v.) See also an ex. voce dumoyapN . ― -b2- damu AlA^axawayoni [ The red, resinous, inspissated juice called dragon's blood; ] what is called AlEanodamu ; (S;) i. q. damu AlgazaAli ; (K voce maZ~N ;) now called AlqaATiru Alamik~Y~u ; or a species thereof; (TA;) [vulgarly qaTor mak~ap ; and also called damu Alv~uEobaAni ;] what is called in Pers. xuwn siyaAwu$aAn (K.) ― -b3- damu AlgizolaAni A certain herb, or leguminous plant, having a beautiful blossom: (M, K:) accord. to Lth, AlgizolaAni ↓ dumoyapu is the name of a certain herb, or leguminous plant, having a blossom. (T.) ― -b4- banaAtu damK A certain plant, (M, K,) well known; (K;) a certain red plant. (T in art. bnY .) -A2- Ald~amu The cat: (M, K:) mentioned by En-Nadr in “ The Book of Wild Animals. ” (M.)

sourceDefinition: An image, or effigy, (S, M, Mgh, K,) of ivory and the like, (S,) or of marble, (M, K,) variegated, decorated, embellished, or coloured, (M, Mgh, K,) in which is redness like blood: (Mgh:) or an image, or effigy, in a general sense: (Kr, M, K:) accord. to Abu-I-'Alà, because originally painted with red, as though from Ald~amu : and any beautiful female is likened thereto, because adorned: (TA:) metonymically applied to (tropical:) a woman: (IAar, T:) or anything that is deemed beautiful in respect of whiteness: (TA:) and an idol: (Lth, S, K:) said in the R to be so called because of the shedding of blood at the place thereof for the purpose of propitiation; but MF says that this derivation requires consideration: more probably because it is decorated: (TA:) pl. dumFY . (S, Mgh, K.) Accord. to MF, it is also pronounced ↓ dimoyapN . (TA.) One says, A^aHosanu mina Ald~umoyapi , meaning More beautiful than the image of ivory. (Har p. 611.) And laAwa Ald~umaY is an oath of the Pagan Arabs, meaning No, by the idols: or, as some relate, it is ↓ laA wa Ald~imaA='i meaning No, by the blood of what is sacrificed upon the stones set up to be worshipped: so in the Nh. (TA.) ― -b2- The pl., dumFY , also signifies Garments upon which are pictures or effigies. (S.) ― -b3- See also damN , last sentence but two.

sourceDefinition: Red; applied to a garment, or piece of cloth: (M:) or anything in the colour of which is blackness and redness : (T:) [ of a dark red colour, like blood :] or anything intensely red : (S:) applied in this last sense [particularly] to a horse &c.: (S, K:) or, applied to a horse, of a sorrel colour ( A^a$oqaru ) intensely red, like the colour of blood : (T:) or, so applied, of an intense sorrel colour : (M:) and kumayotN mudam~FY of an intensely red bay colour : (S, TA:) or of an intense red colour like that of blood : (TA:) or intensely red in the back [ and ] as far as the thin and soft parts of the belly : and A^a$oqaru mudam~FY of which the sorrel colour is overspread, in its upper portion, with a yellowness like the colour of the yellow [or gilded ] bay : (A 'Obeyd, T:) and lawonN mudam~FY a colour in which is blackness. (M.) sahomN mudam~FY An arrow upon which is the redness of blood (S, K) that has adhered to it so that it inclines to blackness : a man, when he shot at the enemy with an arrow, and hit, and the enemy then shot it at him with blood upon it, used to put it in his quiver, auguring good from it: or, as some say, it means an arrow which the archers shoot by turns, one at another; an explanation reducible to that before mentioned: (S:) or an arrow which one shoots at his enemy and the latter then shoots at the former: (M:) or an arrow shot once. (T.)

definition: a word of well-known meaning, (S, K,) The domestic cock;
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning, (S, K,) The domestic cock; i. e. the male of the dajaAj : (Msb, TA:) pl. (of mult. TA) diyakapN and duyuwkN (S, Msb, K) and (of pauc. TA) A^adoyaAkN . (K.) Sometimes it is employed as meaning dajaAjapN , (K,) [which is a n. un., applied to the male and to the female,] and is therefore made [grammatically] fem., (TA,) [though still applying to the male, agreeably with a common license in the case of a masc. noun that has a fem. syn., and vice versa,] as in the saying, dajaAjapNwaz~aqati Ald~ayku biSawotK zaq~aA [ And the cock muted with a sound, with vehement muting ]; (K;) because the dyk is also a dajaAjap : so says ISd. (TA.) ― -b2- diyku Aljin~i [ The cock of the jinn, or genii; ] a certain little creeping thing, or insect, ( duwayob~ap ,) found in gardens. (Kzw.) And the surname of the poet 'Abd-Es-Selám. (K.) -A2- Solicitously affectionate; compassionate: (K:) or solicitously affectionate; affectionate to off spring; applied to a man, in the dial. of ElYemen: so accord. to El-Muärrij; who says that hence the dyk [or domestic cock] is thus called. (TA.) -A3- (assumed tropical:) The [ season called ] rabiyE [here meaning spring ]; as though so called because of the various colours of its plants, or herbage, (K, TA,) and thus likened to the dyk [or domestic cock]. (S, M.) And accord. to IAar, one says, *arati Alr~iyHu , and ↓ A^a*orat , [elliptically,] meaning *arati Alt~uraAba [i. e. The wind raised the dust, or made it to fly, &c.]. (T.) ― -b2- [Hence,] *araA Alr~iwaAyapa *arowa Alr~iyHi Alha$iyma (assumed tropical:) He carried on the relation uninterruptedly and rapidly [ like as the wind carries away the dry herbage that is broken in pieces. ] (TA.) ― -b3- Hence also, *araA Aln~aAsu AlHinoTapa [ The people winnowed the wheat ]. A^a*oruwhaA , inf. n. *arowN ; (IAar, T;) and ↓ *ar~ayotuhaA ; (M;) I winnowed the wheat: (M, K: *) or AlT~aEaAma ↓ *ar~ayotu , inf. n. ta*oriyapN ; (Msb;) and *arayotuhu and *arawotuhu ; (T;) I cleared the wheat from its straw. (Msb.) And *arawotuhu , (S, M,) and *arayotuhu , but the former is more approved; and ↓ *ar~ayotuhu ; (M;) I made it to fly, and go away; (S, M;) namely, a thing, (S,) or grain, and the like. (M.) definition: , also written *arFA , (or, accord.
sourceDefinition: , also written *arFA , (or, accord. to some copies of the S, ↓ *urFY ,) A thing [ such as dust &c. ] that the wind has raised, or made to fly, and carried away: (S:) or it signifies what one has winnowed; (M;) or maA ta*oruwhu [ what thou winnowest, as is indicated by the context of this explanation]; like as nafaDN signifies maAtanofuDuhu . (T.) ― -b2- And *arFY or ↓ *urFY (accord. to different copies of the S) Tears poured forth: (S:) or so ↓ *ariY~N [or damoEN *ariY~N ]. (M, TA.) -A2- Also A shelter; (M, TA;) anything by which one is protected, or sheltered: (S, Msb:) a shelter from the cold wind, consisting of a wall, or of trees: and particularly a shelter that is made for camels such as are termed $awol , by pulling up trees of the kind called Earofaj &c. and placing them one upon another in the direction whence blows the north, or northerly, wind, in the camel's nightly resting-place. (T.) [Hence,] one says, fulaAnN fiY *araY fulaAnK Such a one is in the protection of such a one. (T.) And A^anaA fiY Zil~i fulaAnN wafiY *araAhu I am in the protection of such a one, and in his shelter. (S.) And [hence, perhaps,] A_in~a fulaAnFA lakariymu Al*~araY (assumed tropical:) Verily such a one is generous in disposition. (AZ, T.) ― -b2- Also The court, or yard, ( finaA=' ,) of a house. (Har pp. 56 and 442.) -A3- see also *arowN , in two places.

definition: and ↓ *urowapN The upper, or uppermost, part of a thing (S, M, Msb, K) of any kind;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ *urowapN The upper, or uppermost, part of a thing (S, M, Msb, K) of any kind; (M, Msb;) and so, accord. to Et-Takee Esh-Shemenee, ↓ *arowapN : (TA:) and particularly, of a camel's hump, (S, M,) and of the head: (M:) and a camel's hump itself: (TA:) pl. *urFY . (S, TA.) It is said in a trad., A^ataY biA_ibilK gurari Al*~uraY [or gur~i Al*~uraY ?] He brought camels having white humps. (TA.) And in another trad., EalaY *irowapi kul~i baEiyri $ayoTaAnu [ On the hump of every camel is a devil ]. (TA.) And in a prov., maA zaAla yafotilu fiY Al*~irowapi waAlgaAribi [ He ceased not to twist the fur of the upper part and the fore part of the hump: originating from, or occurring in, a trad., which see explained in art. grb ]: it means, (tropical:) he ceased not to render familiar, or tame, [or rather to endeavour to do so, ] and to remove refractoriness. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] tazaw~aja minohumo fiY Al*~irowapi wa Aln~aASiyapi (T, M *) (assumed tropical:) He married among the noble and high of them. (T.)

sourceDefinition: (AO, S, M voce *aA , Msb, * K) and *ayoti wa*ayoti and *ayotu wa*aytu , (K,) the last of which is unknown, except as mentioned by IKtt, (TA,) and *ay~apa wa*ay~apa (M, K) and *ay~aA='a wa*ay~aA='a , (K,) i. q. kayota wakayota : (AO, S, M, Msb, * K:) so in the saying, kaAna mina AlA^amori *ayota wa*ayota [&c., Some of the circumstances of the case were thus and thus, or so and so, or such and such things ]. (AO, S, M.) It is plainly implied in the K [and the S] that the t in *yt is a radical letter, the last radical letter of the word: but AHei says that the t in *yt and kyt is substituted for Y ; that they are originally *ay~apa and kay~apa ; and that the p is elided, and the Y which is the last radical letter is changed into t : [in like manner also says ISd in the M, voce *aA :] and most of the leading authorities on inflection assert the same: therefore, [though most persons would look for them among words of which the last radical letter is t ,] they are incorrectly placed in the K [and in the S]. (MF.) Or *ayota is formed from *ayowN , by eliding the w and doubling the Y and then substituting for the teshdeed t ; and if you elide the t and replace it by h , you must restore the teshdeed, and say, kaAna *ay~aho wa*ay~aho . (S at the end of art. *w .)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. rubuwDN (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and raboDN (Msb, K) and raboDapN , (K,) [the last an inf. n. of un.,] said of the sheep and goat, (S, A, Mgh, K,) and of the gazelle, (S, A,) and of the ox-kind, and the horse, (S,) or beast, (Msb,) and of the dog, (S, A,) [signifying He lay down, or laid himself down, upon his breast, ] is like baraka said of a camel, (S, Msb, K,) and javama said of a bird, (S, TA,) or jalasa said of a man. (Mgh.) Said of a man, it means [(assumed tropical:) He lay down: and he sat: or] he sat upon his knees: and it may also mean he sat upon his thighs and his buttocks. (Har p. 172.) [And hence, (assumed tropical:) He remained fixed, or stationary, like an animal lying upon its breast; as is shown by what here follows: whence a signification of rab~aDa , q. v.] The saying of Mohammad to Ed- Dahhák, when he sent him to his people, A_i*aA A^atayotahumo faA@robiDo fiY daArihimo ZaboyFA , means When thou comest to them, remain in their abode in security, or without fear, like the gazelle in his covert: (IAar, ISd, K:) or trust them not, but be vigilant, like a wild animal, ready to spring up, for thou wilt be in the midst of the unbelievers; (Az, ISd, K; *) so, if anything induce in thee suspicion, thou mayest flee from them like the gazelle: (Az, ISd, TA:) accord. to each interpretation, ZbyA is in the accus. case as a denotative of state; the subst. being put in the place of the act. part. n., as though for mataZab~iyFA : the former of the two explanations is said to be the more agreeable with the circumstances of the case. (TA.) You say also, rabaDa AlA^asadu EalaY fariysatihi , and Alqironu EalaY qironihi , The lion laid himself down upon his breast ( baraka ) on his prey, and the adversary on his adversary. (K.) ― -b2- He (a beast) lodged, and abode, in a place. (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) He (a man) became heavy, and slept, stretched upon the ground. (TA.) ― -b4- rabaDa Eani Alganami , (S, A, K,) inf. n. rubuwDN , (S,) (tropical:) He (a ram) abstained from tupping, or covering the ewes, and avoided it, (S, A, * K, *) or them, (TA,) being fatigued: (S:) or was unable to cover them: (K:) one does not say, of a ram, jafara . (S.) You say also of a ewe when she is pregnant, qado rubiDa EanohaA . (Ibn- 'Abbád, A.) And you say of a man, rabaDa Eano maEaAliY AlA^umuwri (assumed tropical:) He abstained, or held back, from seeking the means of acquiring eminence, or nobility. (TA.) ― -b5- rabaDa All~ayolu (A, K) (tropical:) The night cast its darkness [lit. itself (expl. by A^aloqaY bnafosihi ) upon the earth ]. (K.) -A2- rabaDahu , aor. and , (IAar, O, K,) but the latter aor. was afterwards rejected by IAar, (TA,) He betook himself, or repaired, to him for lodging, covert, or refuge. definition: The lodging-place of sheep or goats;
sourceDefinition: The lodging-place of sheep or goats; (S, A, * K;) because they lie therein upon their breasts; and in like manner of wild animals: (TA:) the nightly lodging-place of sheep or goats: (Msb:) and ↓ marobiDN signifies the same: (S, * A, Mgh, Msb:) pl. of the former A^arobaADN : (S, A, * TA:) and of the latter maraAbiDu : (S, K: *) the mrAbD of sheep or goats are like the maEaATin of camels. (S.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A place of abode: a place of abode of a people by itself: (A, TA:) pl. as above. (A.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Anything to which a man betakes himself, or repairs, for lodging, covert, or refuge, (ISk, S, A, * Msb, K,) and at which, or with which, he finds rest, or ease; (K;) such as a house or tent, (S, A, K,) and the like, (S, K,) and a wife, (ISk, S, A, Msb,) or relations, (ISk, A, Msb,) or a family, and a relation, and property, (K,) and sheep or goats, and means of subsistence, and food; (TA;) and hence, (S,) milk which sustains a man, and suffices him for food: (S, K: *) pl. as above: (K:) rabaDN and ↓ raboDN and ↓ ruboDN (IAar, Sgh, K) and ↓ rubuDN (K) are applied to a wife liA^an~ahaA tarobiDu zawojahaA , (so in copies of the K and in the TA, but in the CK turab~iDu ,) i. e. because she undertakes, or manages, the affairs of her husband, and gives him lodging, or refuge; (TA;) or because she fixes him, ( turab~iDuhu , i. e. tuvab~ituhu ,) so that he does not quit his place: (L, TA:) or to the mother; or the sister; who undertakes, or manages, the affairs of ( tuEaz~ibu [so in copies of the K and in the TA, in the latter of which it is thus explained, but in the CK tuqar~ibu ,]) her relation. (K.) A poet says, jaA='a Al$~itaA='u walam~aA A^at~axi*o rabaDFA yaA wayoHa kaf~aY~a mino Hafori AlqaraAmiySi (S, Mgh) i. e. [ The winter has come, and I have not yet made for myself ] a lodging: [ O, wo to my two-hands, in consequence of digging ] hollows in which to sit for protection from the cold. (Mgh.) And from rabaDN applied to “ milk which sustains a man, and suffices him for food, ” originated the prov., (K, TA,) minoka rabaDuka waA_ino kaAna samaArFA , meaning (tropical:) Thy family and thy servants (S, K) and those to whom thou betakest thyself for lodging or refuge, (S,) are appertenances of thine, though they be persons falling short [ of their duty ]: (S, K:) or thy manager of affairs, &c., though he be not a good manager of thine affairs : (L, TA:) and rabaDN also signifies any woman who undertakes, or manages, the affairs of a house : but in the T we find ↓ ruboDuka , thus written, as by Th, on the authority of IAar, but not restricted by a measure, and explained as meaning the person who undertakes, or manages, the affairs of thy house; and so in the book of proverbs by As: and in the margin of a copy of the S, we find the above-cited prov. thus written, waA_ino kaAna samaArFA ↓ minoka rubuDuka , as from the “ Book on Goats ” by Ibn-Zeyd, and expl. as meaning the sons of thy father are appertenances of thine, though they be evil persons, in whom is no good. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) The wall of a city: (K, TA:) the environs of a city, (S, A, Mgh,) and of a qaSor [or palace &c.], (A,) consisting of houses or dwellings, (A, Mgh,) or of open country: (TA:) and ↓ ruboDN signifies the same: (TA:) or this latter signifies the foundation, or basis, of a building; and of a city also: (K:) IKh writes it ↓ rubuDN : and some say that ↓ ruboDN and rabaDN signify the same: (TA:) the former of these two signifies also the part, of a thing, that touches the ground: (K, TA:) so says Sh: accord. to ISh, AlA^aroDi ↓ ruboDu signifies what touches the ground, of a thing: (TA:) and rabaDN also signifies a lateral, or an outward or adjacent, part: (K:) or lateral, or outward or adjacent, parts of a thing: (Ks, S:) also the space immediately pertaining to a mosque: and [the pl.] A^arobaADN is explained by El-Karkhee as applied to the quarters, or districts, of a town, or city. (Mgh.) ― -b5- rabaDN also signifies (tropical:) The rope of the [ camel's saddle called ] raHol , (A, K,) with which the rHl is bound; (A, TA;) one of the A^arobaAD , or ropes of the raHol : (S, A:) or the part that is next the ground thereof; (K;) i. e., of the rope of the rHl ; (TA;) not what is above the rHl : (K:) accord. to Lth, the part [ of the belly ] of the camel that is next the ground when he lies down; (L, TA; *) and the belly of the she-camel; and in like manner IAar explains the pl. A^arobaADN as meaning the bellies of camels; but Az says that this is a mistake. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A girth of a raHol , like the niTaAq [q. v.], which is put upon the flanks of the she-camel, so as to have the haunches behind it, (K, TA,) on either side, having at its two ends two rings, to which are tied the [ woven, or plaited, thongs called ] A^anosaAE : the rHl is bound with it. (TA.) ― -b6- Also (tropical:) The maSaAriyn [or guts, or intestines, ] of the belly, that have a winding, or coiled, form; (Lth, A, TA;) such as are in the belly of a sheep or goat: (Lth, TA:) or the folding intestines of beasts: (AHat, TA:) or the guts, bowels, or intestines, into which the food passes from the stomach; syn. A^amoEaA='N : (S, K:) or the contents of the belly, (K, TA,) consisting of the maSaAriyn &c., (TA,) except the heart (K, TA) and the lungs. (TA.) (assumed tropical:) The part that comprises the HawaAyaA [or winding, circling, or coiled, guts or intestines ]; (IAar, TA;) as also ↓ rabiyDN and ↓ marobiDN and ↓ marobaDN : (IAar, K, TA:) some describe the rabaD as below the navel; and the ↓ marobaD , as beneath the navel and above the pubes. (TA.)

definition: Sheep, or goats, with their pastors, collected together in their lodging-places;
sourceDefinition: Sheep, or goats, with their pastors, collected together in their lodging-places; (S, A, K;) as though it were a quasi-pl. n.; as also ↓ riboDapN and ↓ riboDN : (TA:) and hence, (L, TA,) ↓ the former of these two, (assumed tropical:) a company of men: (L, K:) and ↓ the latter of them, [accord. to the K,] a herd of bulls, or cows, in their lodgingplace; from the author of the book entitled kitaAbu Almuzodawiji mina All~ugaAti , only: (K, * TA:) but what this author says is, that ↓ riboDN signifies the lodging-places of bulls or cows [app. with the beasts in them ]: and that the primary application of this word ( riboDN ) and ↓ riboDapN is to sheep or goats; and that by a subsequent usage they have been applied to bulls or cows and to men. (TA.) See also raAbiDN . ― -b2- One says also, Sab~a A@ll~`hu Ealayohi Hum~aY rabiyDFA [app. meaning (assumed tropical:) May God send (lit. pour ) upon him a fever that shall cleave to him like as an animal lying upon its breast cleaves to the ground]. (TA.) -A2- See also rabaDN , last sentence.

definition: Lying upon his breast;
sourceDefinition: Lying upon his breast; applied to a sheep or goat [&c.]; and so ↓ rabuwDN applied to a hare; so too ↓ rab~aADN [but app. in an intensive or a frequentative sense] applied to a lion, as is also raAbiDN , and to a man lying on his adversary: (TA:) and [hence] ↓ Alr~ab~aADu is an appellation of the lion: (K:) the pl. [of raAbiDN ] is rub~aDN and rubuwDN : and the phrase Alganami ↓ karabiyDapi , occurring in a trad., means kaAlganami Alr~ub~aDi [ Like the sheep, or goats, that are lying upon their breasts ]. (TA.) It is said in a prov., kalobN jaw~aAlN xayorN mino A^asadK raAbiDK or rabaDa [ A dog that roams about is better than a lion lying upon his breast or that has laid himself down upon his breast ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, because of his cleaving to the ground,] (tropical:) A sick man. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also the phrase,] A^aronabatuhu raAbiDapN EalaY wajohihi (tropical:) The end of his nose is flat, and spreading upon his face. (A.) ― -b4- Alr~aAbiDaAni is an appellation applied to The Turks and the Abyssinians. (K, TA.) These are meant in the trad. of Mo'áwiyeh, laA taboEavuwA Alr~aAbiDayoni , i. e. Rouse not ye against you the two [peoples] that are remaining quiet as long as they do not pursue you: it is like another trad., in which it is said, AutorukuwA Alt~uroka maA tarakuwkumo wadaEuwA AlHaba$apa maA wadaEuwkumo [Leave ye alone the Turks as long as they leave you alone, and let ye alone the Abyssinians as long as they let you alone]. (TA.)

definition: [as a subst. from raAbiDN , made so by the affix p , An animal lying upon its breast ]. One says of a man who kills when he shoots, and more commonly of him who kills when he smites with the [evil]...
sourceDefinition: [as a subst. from raAbiDN , made so by the affix p , An animal lying upon its breast ]. One says of a man who kills when he shoots, and more commonly of him who kills when he smites with the [evil] eye, fulaAnN maA taquwmu raAbiDatuhu [ Such a one is so effective in his aim that his animal lying upon its breast does not rise ]: (ISk, S, TA:) and in like manner, maA taquwmu lahu raAbiDapN : it is a prov. (TA.) ― -b2- It is said in a trad., faA@nobaEava lahu waAHidN mina Alr~aAbiDapi [ And there rose and went to him one of the raAbDp ]: (Lth, A, TA:) Alr~aAbiDapu means (tropical:) certain angels who were sent down [ from Paradise ] with Adam, (Lth, A, K, TA,) who direct those that err from the right way: (Lth, A, TA:) perhaps (Lth, TA) so called from their remaining upon the earth: (Lth, * A, TA: *) and [so in the K, but correctly “ or, ”] the remainder of the Bearers of Evidence ( Hamalapi AlHuj~api [meaning those angels whereof every individual of mankind has two appointed to attend him constantly for the purpose of their bearing evidence of his good and evil deeds, which two are termed in the Kur l. 16 Almutalaq~iyaAni ,]) whereof the earth will never be destitute. (S, K.) ― -b3- And in another trad., respecting the signs of the coming of the resurrection, the Prophet is related to have said that one of those signs will be, that the ↓ ruwayobiDap will speak respecting the affairs of the community: (T, TA:) Alr~uwayobiDapu is the dim. of Alr~aAbiDapu (T, K, TA) signifying The pastor of rabiyD [q. v.]; (T, TA;) and means (assumed tropical:) the mean, contemptible man, (S, K,) who speaks respecting the affairs of the community: thus expl. by the Prophet himself: (K: [in the CK, Aln~Aqihu is erroneously put for Alt~aAfihu :]) or he explained it as meaning (assumed tropical:) the vitious, or wicked, who speaks respecting the affairs of the community: A 'Obeyd compares this trad. with another, in which it is said that one of the signs above mentioned will be, that the pastors of sheep or goats will be the heads of the people: and Az says that AlrwybDp means the pastor of sheep or goats: some say that it means (assumed tropical:) he who abstains, or holds back, from seeking the means of acquiring eminence, or nobility; and Alr~aAbiDapu signifies [the same, or] impotent to attain eminence: in this latter, the p is added to give intensiveness to the signification: and Az thinks it most probable that each of these is applied to the mean man because of his remaining in his house, or tent, and seldom rising and going forth to occupy himself in great affairs. (TA.)

(Ksh in xxxiii. 60.) And ArjfwA fiY Al$~aYo'i (S, Msb, K) and bihi , (Msb, K,) inf. n. A_irojaAfN , (Msb,) i. q. xaADuwA fiyhi [mean- ing They said what was false respecting the thing ]: (S, O, K:) or they told many evil tales, and uttered many discordant lying sayings, respecting the thing, in order that the people might become in a state of commotion, agitation, convulsion, tumult, or disturbance, in consequence thereof: whence, in the Kur [xxxiii. 60], fiY Almadiynapi ↓ waAlmurojifuwna [ and they who tell many evil tales, &c., in the city: ] (O, * Msb:) or ArjfwA fiY Albaladi bika*aA they told, in the town, or country, of such a matter, in order that they might cause commotion, or agitation, &c., to befall the people, without there being aught [ thereof ] true in their estimation; from Alr~ajafaAnu signifying “ violent commotion or agitation ” &c. (Har pp. 218, 219.) And ArjfwA , alone, They said what was false ( xaADuwA ) in [ relating ] tales of conflicts and factions, or seditions, or discords, or dissensions, and the like: whence, ↓ waAlmurojifuwnu fiY Almadiynapi [cited above]. (K.) ― -b3- And Arjft Aln~aAqapu The she-camel came in a state of fatigue, with her ears flaccid, shaking them ( bihimaA ↓ tarojufu ). (O, K.)

sourceDefinition: A camel, (As, T,) or a thing, (S,) of which the redness is mixed with yellowness, (As, T, S, K,) like waros [q. v.]: (As, T:) hence the epithet raAdiniY~N is applied to a he-camel, (S, TA,) and with p to a she-camel: (As, T, S:) or raAdiniY~N is applied to a he-camel as meaning having crisp, or curly, fur, of generous race, (Lth, T, M,) beautiful, (Lth, T,) and inclining a little to blackness: (Lth, T, M:) or intensely red; (TA, and Ham p. 218;) or it has this meaning also: (M:) or between yellow and red: accord. to some, from raAdinN signifying “ saffron; ” (Ham ubi suprà;) but As says, I know not in relation to what thing the camel is called by this epithet. definition: Camels in a state of separation, or dispersion;
sourceDefinition: Camels in a state of separation, or dispersion; and in like manner, men, and goods, and plants or herbage: (A:) or camels pasturing by themselves, (S, K,) the pastor seeing them, (S,) or looking at them, (K,) near or far off: (S:) you say, A_ibilN rafoDN (S, K,) and ↓ rafaDN also, and ↓ raAfiDapN : (S, A, K:) and the pl. of rafaDN is A^arofaADN : (S, K:) [and ↓ rufuwDN seems to be a pl. of rafoDN .] Also A herd of gazelles in a state of separation, or dispersion: pl. rifaADN . (TA.) You say also ↓ naEaAmN rafaDN Ostriches in separate flocks. (S.) And fiY Als~afari ↓ Aln~aAsu A^arofaADN The men are in a state of separation, or dispersion, in journeying. (TA.) And Aln~aAsi ↓ rufuwDu The different parties of men. (S, K.) And mino kalaA^K ↓ rufuwDN Scattered pieces of herbage or pasturage, (Jm, S, K,) distant one from another. (Jm, S, O.) And AlA^aroDi ↓ rufuwDu Land which is deserted after having been prohibited to the public: (S:) or which has no possessor: (O, L, K:) so says IDrd; but he adds, or, accord. to some, deserted land (L, TA) between two cultivated pieces of land, (L,) or between two pieces of land belonging to two tribes. (TA.) ↓ rafaDN also signifies What is large, and in a state of separation or dispersion, of a thing: pl. A^arofaADN . (TA.) ― -b2- And rafoDN , A side, or a part, or portion, (syn. jaAnibN ,) of a thing. definition: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. yarum~u (T, S, M, Msb, K) and yarim~u (S, Msb, K,) the latter [irreg. as aor. of a trans. v. of this class, and] said by MF to be unknown, but there are other instances of the same kind, as har~ahu , aor. yahur~u and yahir~u and Eal~ahu , aor. yaEul~u and yaEil~u , (TA,) inf. n. ram~N (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and maram~apN , (Lth, T, S, Mgh, K,) He repaired it; or put it into a good, sound, right, or proper, state; (Lth, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) after a part thereof had become in a bad state; (Lth, T;) namely, a thing, (Lth, T, S,) as, for instance, a rope becoming old and worn-out, or a house, (Lth, T,) or a building, (Mgh,) or a wall, &c.; (Msb;) as also ram~a $aA^onahu , (S,) or $aA^onahaA referring to a house ( daAr ): (Lth, T:) and in like manner, he rectified it, namely, an affair, after it had become disorganized, or disordered: (Lth, T:) and ↓ rm~m signifies the same in an intensive sense; [i. e. he repaired it, &c., much, or well: ] (Msb:) and ↓ ramorama he repaired, or rectified, his affair, case, state, or condition. (TA.) The saying, kun~aA A^ahola vam~ihi waram~ihi , (T, S,) occurring in a trad., (S,) accord. to the relaters thereof ↓ vum~ihi warum~ihi , but A'Obeyd holds the former reading to be the right, (T, S,) means, accord. to AA, We were the fit persons to put it into a good, sound, right, or proper, state: (T:) or, accord. to A'Obeyd, to put it into such a state, and to eat it. (T, S. [See another explanation of the verb in what follows.]) ― -b2- You say also, ram~a sahomahu , meaning (tropical:) [ He made his arrow even, or straight, by means of his eye; or] he looked at his arrow until he made it even, or straight. (TA.) -A2- ram~N also signifies The act of eating; and so ↓ AirotimaAmN . (ISh, T.) You say, ram~ahu , (T, S, K,) aor. yarum~u (T, S,) inf. n. ram~N , (TA,) He ate it. (T, S, K.) And it is said in a trad., Ealayokumo biA^alobaAni Albaqari faA_in~ahaA tarum~u mino kul~i Al$~ajari [ Keep ye to the milk of cows, for they eat of all the tress ]; (T, S, * TA;) i. e. taA^okulu : or, accord. to one reading, it is ↓ tarotam~u . (TA.) ram~ati Al$~aApu AlHa$iy$a aor. tarum~u , inf. n. ram~N , means The sheep, or goat, took the dry herbage, or fodder, with its lips. (M.) And ram~ati Al$~aApu mina AlA^aroDi , and ↓ Artm~t , The sheep, or goat, ate from the land. (S.) And ram~ati Albahomapu , (M,) or Albahiymapu , (K,) inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ Artm~t ; i. e. [ The lamb, or kid, or the beast, or quadruped, ] reached and took the branches (M, K) with its mouth. (K.) And kul~a rumaAmK ↓ huwa yataram~amu He eats every [ kind of ] rumaAm [q. v.]. (T.) And AlEaZoma ↓ trm~m He ate off the flesh from the bone; syn. taEar~aqahu : or he left the bone like the rim~ap [q. v.]: in [some of] the copies of the K, taram~ama is erroneously explained by taEaz~aqa ; [in my MS. copy, by taEar~afa ; and in the CK, by tafar~aqa ;] the right reading being taEar~aqa , as in the A. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., respecting the she-cat, walaA mino xa$aA$i AlA^aroDi ↓ A^arosalotuhaA turamorimu , meaning [ And I did not send her ] for her to eat [ of the creeping things of the earth ]. (TA.) -A3- ram~a AlEaZomu , aor. yarim~u (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. ram~N (T, M,) or rim~apN , (S,) or both, (K, TA, [the former written in the CK rim~ ]) and ramiymN ; (M, K;) and ↓ Arm~ ; (M, K; [but see what follows;]) The bone became such as is termed rm~ap ; (M, TA;) [i. e.,] became old and decayed; (MA, KL;) syn. baliYa . (T, S, Mgh, Msb, K.) Accord. to IAar, one says, ram~ato EiZaAmuhu , and ↓ A^aram~ato , meaning His bones became old and decayed; syn. baliyato : but others explain AlEaZomu ↓ Arm~ differently, as below: see 4. (T.) In the saying, mentioned in a trad., yaA ↓ rasuwla A@ll~`hi kayofa tuEoroDu SalaAtunaA Ealayoka waqado A^aramota , meaning baliyta [i. e. definition: , said of a bone, It had in it, or contained, rim~ , i.
sourceDefinition: , said of a bone, It had in it, or contained, rim~ , i. e. marrow, (T, S, K,) running therein. (S.) One says of a sheep or goat (S, M) that is lean, or emaciated, (S,) and of a she-camel, (M,) maA yurim~u minohaA maDoribN , (S, M,) meaning Not a bone of her that is broken and from which the marrow is [ sought to be ] extracted [ contains any marrow ]: (M:) i. e., if any of her bones be broken, no marrow will be found in it. (S.) definition: The remains of a rope after it has become ragged, or dissundered: (T:) or a piece of a rope (S, M, Msb, K) that is old and worn out or rotten;
sourceDefinition: The remains of a rope after it has become ragged, or dissundered: (T:) or a piece of a rope (S, M, Msb, K) that is old and worn out or rotten; (S;) as also ↓ rim~apN : (M, K:) pl. [of mult.] rumamN (T, S,) or rimamN (M, K,) and rimaAmN (S, M, K) and [of pauc.] A^aromaAmN : (M, K:) and they said also HabolN A^aromaAmN and rimamN [or rumamN ] and rimaAmN ; (M, K;) [like HabolN A^aromaAvN and vawobN A^axolaAqN &c.;] thus using the pl. as though every part [of the rope] were termed a single thing. definition: A bone old and decayed: (S, M, Msb, K:) and ↓ rumaAmN signifies the same (K, TA) in an intensive sense: (TA:) or the former is like rim~apN ;
sourceDefinition: A bone old and decayed: (S, M, Msb, K:) and ↓ rumaAmN signifies the same (K, TA) in an intensive sense: (TA:) or the former is like rim~apN ; (A 'Obeyd, T, and Ksh in xxxvi. 78;) i. e. it is a subst., signifying the old and decayed, of bones; (Ksh and Bd ibid.;) not of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure faAEilN or mafoEuwlN : (Ksh ibid.:) or it is used in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , [meaning eroded, ] from ramamotuhu [“ I ate it ”]: (Bd ibid.:) its pl. is in most instances A^arim~aA='u [when it is used as a subst. or as an epithet], like A^adil~aA='u pl. of daliylN [or A^aqoribaA=' pl. of qariybN ]; and rimaAmN also occurs [when it is used as a subst., for rim~apN , of which rimaAmN is a pl., or when it is used as an epithet], like kiraAmN pl. of kariymN : (Msb:) or you say A^aEoZumN ramaAy^imu , and ramiymN also; or ramiymN may have the meaning of a gen. n., and therefore be used in the place of a pl. (M.) It is said in the Kur ubi suprà, mano yuHoyiY A@loEiZaAma wahiYa ramiymN [ Who will quicken the bones when they are old and decayed &c.?]; the last word being without p because it is a subst., as expl. above, (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) not an epithet; (Ksh, Jel;) or because it is used in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , as stated above; (Bd;) or because words of the measures faEiylN and faEuwlN are sometimes used alike as masc. and fem. [and sing.] and pl., like SadiyqN and rasuwlN and Eaduw~N . (S.) And Hátim, or some other, says, A^amaA waAl~a*iY laA yaEolamu Als~ir~a gayoruhu wayuHoyiY AlEiZaAma AlbiyDa wahoYa ramiymu [ Verily, or now surely, by Him beside whom none knoweth the secret, and who quickeneth the white bones when they are old and decayed &c.]; in which rmym may have the meaning of a gen. n., as observed above. (M.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Anything old and decayed or worn out. (M.) One says, A^aHoyaY ramiyma AlmakaArimi (tropical:) [ He revived what had become decayed of generous qualities or actions or practices ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) The remains of the herbage of the next preceding year: (Lh, M:) from the same word in the sense first expl. above. (M.) -A2- ramiymu is one of the names of The east, or easterly, wind; AlS~abaA : and is also a proper name for a woman. (M.)

(TA.) ― -b2- Also A voice, or sound: (S, K:) and cries, shouts, or noises, and clamour. (TA. definition: The name of a certain devil;
sourceDefinition: The name of a certain devil; (Lth, K;) to which some add, insolent and audacious in pride and rebellion: (TA:) or a certain chief of the jinn, or genii: (S, K:) said to be one of those, nine or seven in number, spoken of in the Kur-án [xlvi. 28], as listening to the Kur-án. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, zawobaEapN , (S, K,) and (K,) or as some say, (S, TA,) A^um~u zawobaEapK , (S, and so in some copies of the K,) or A^um~u zawobaEapa , (as in other copies of the K,) and, (K,) as the children of the Arabs of the desert call it, (Lth,) A^abuw zawobaEapK , or A^abuw zawobaEapa , (accord. to different copies of the K,) i. q. A_iEoSaArN ; (Lth, S, K;) i. e. A whirlwind of dust [or sand ] rising into the sky; (TA;) a wind that raises the dust [or sand ] and rises towards the sky as though it were a pillar: (S:) [I have measured several of these whirling pillars of dust or sand, with a sextant, in circumstances peculiarly favourable to accuracy, in Upper Egypt, and found them from five hundred to seven hundred and fifty feet in height:] it is said [in the present day] that in the zwbEp is a devil, insolent and audacious in pride and rebellion. (K.) ― -b3- zawaAbiEu [is the pl., and also] signifies Calamities, or misfortunes. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (Msb, TA,) and zabana bihi , (TA,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. zabonN , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) He pushed it, or thrust it; or pushed it, or thrust it, away; (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K, * TA;) namely, a thing: (Msb, TA:) or a thing from another thing. (M, * TA.) You say of a she-camel, tazobinu HaAlibahaA She pushes, or thrusts, or she pushes, or thrusts, away, her milker. (Mgh, Msb, TA.) And zabanato , (S,) or zabanato bivafinaAti rijolihaA , (TA,) She (a camel) struck with her stifle-joints (TA) on the occasion of being milked: zabonN being [generally] with the stifle-joints; and rakoDN , with the hind leg; and xaboTN , with the fore leg. (S, TA.) And tazobinu waladahaA Eano DaroEihaA birijolihaA She (a camel) pushes, or thrusts, away her young one from her udder with her hind leg. (M, TA.) And zabanahumo He pushed, or thrust, them away; put them away, or removed them from their place. (TA.) And of war, or battle, ( Harob ,) one says, tazobinu Aln~aAsi , meaning (tropical:) It dashes men [one against another], and pushes, or thrusts, them. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And zabanota Ean~aA hadiy~ataka wamaEoruwfaka , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) Thou hast turned away from us thy present and thy bounty, or favour: accord. to Lh, properly meaning thou hast turned them away from thy neighbours and acquaintance to others: or, accord. to the A, (tropical:) thou hast withdrawn, and withheld, from us thy present &c. (TA.) ― -b3- zabonN also signifies The selling any fruit upon its trees for [ other ] fruit by measure: (K:) whence ↓ AlmuzaAbanapu (see 3): it has been forbidden, because of the fraud, or deceit, and the ignorance, attending it: and is thus termed because either of the two parties, when he repents, repels the other [if able to do so] from the obligation that he has imposed upon him. (TA.)

definition: One who pushes, or thrusts, or who pushes, or thrusts, away, [or who pushes &c.
sourceDefinition: One who pushes, or thrusts, or who pushes, or thrusts, away, [or who pushes &c. much or vehemently, or who is wont to push &c.,] a thing. (Msb.) A she-camel that pushes, or thrusts, or that pushes, or thrusts, away, (Mgh, Msb, K,) or that kicks, or strikes, and pushes, &c., (S, TA,) her milker, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) with her hind leg (Msb) [or with her stifle-joint: see 1]: or that is wont, or accustomed, to push, &c., her milker. (TA.) Hence, (A,) one says HarobN zabuwnN (S, A, Msb, K) meaning (tropical:) A difficult, or stubborn, war or battle; likened to the she-camel termed zbwn : (A, TA:) or that dashes men [ one against another ], and pushes, or thrusts, them: (S:) or in which one portion pushes, or thrusts, or pushes or thrusts away, another, by reason of multitudinousness: (K:) or it is thus called because it repels the valiant men from advancing, through fear of death. (Msb.) ― -b2- As meaning gabiY~N [i. e. (assumed tropical:) Unintelligent, or having little intelligence ], and HariyfN [syn. with muEaAmilN , and hence, as will be seen from what follows, app. here used in the sense of (assumed tropical:) a dealer with others in buying and selling, a meaning which muEaAmilN often has, though, as I have shown in art. Harf , I do not know any authority for assigning this meaning to HariyfN ], (S, K, [the latter explanation thus written in my copies of the S and in my MS. copy of the K and in the CK, but in the TA, and hence in the TK, xryf , which has no meaning, that I know of, appropriate in this instance,]) it is post-classical, (K,) not of the language of the people of the desert: (S:) it signifies (tropical:) a simpleton, or fool, who is endamaged, or defrauded, ( yugobanu ,) much; by a tropical attribution [of the meaning of a pass. part. n. to a word which has properly the meaning of an act. part. n.; because the person thus termed is as though he were pushed, or thrust, away]: (Mgh:) it signifies also (assumed tropical:) a purchaser; because he pushes away another from the thing that is sold; [or because he is often duped; ] and in this sense, [a sense in which it is commonly now used, or as meaning a customer, and also a dupe, ] it is a post-classical word, not of the language of the people of the desert. (Msb.) [The pl. now commonly used is zabaAy^inu , and some say zabuwnaAtN .] It is said in a post-classical prov., Alz~abuwnu yaforaHu bilaA $aYo'K [which I would render (assumed tropical:) The dupe rejoices without anything, or at nothing ]: (Meyd:) or Alz~abuwnu yaforaHu biA^adonaY $aYo'K , meaning [(assumed tropical:) The dupe rejoices at the least, or the meanest, thing: or] the dealer ( AlmuEaAmilu ), or the purchaser ( Almu$otariY ), as the word signifies in the dial. the people of El-Basrah. (Har p. 76, q. v. [The editors of the sec. ed. of De Sacy's Har, to which reference is here made, say, (Notes, p. 90,) “ Nous pensons que le mot Alzbwn , dans l'acception qu'il prend dans ce proverbe dérive du chaldéen זַבֵּן 'vendre.'” (This verb is written in the Lex. of Gesenius זְבַן .) See also De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., pp. 186 — 190.] -A2- Also A well in which is a receding in its mavaAbap [or place where the water collects, or place reached by the water when it returns and collects after one has drawn from it, &c.; (see art. vwb ;) as though its casing were pushed back in that part]. (K.) -A3- And [ An inner vest; so in the present day; pl. A^azobinapN ;] a thing that is cut so as to fit the body, and worn. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- And Alz~ubaAnayaAni , (Ibn-Kunáseh, S, Kzw,) or zubaAnayaA AlEaqorabi , (K,) [the former the more common,] (assumed tropical:) The two horns [or claws ] of Scorpio; [which, like the constellation Leo, the Arabs extended much beyond the limits that we assign to it, and which they thus made to include a portion of Libra;] (Kzw;) two stars, widely separated, (Ibn-Kunáseh, Kzw,) [ that rise ] before AlA_ikoliyl [q. v.]; (Ibn-Kunáseh;) between which (Ibn-Kunáseh, Kzw) is the measure of a spear ( rumoH [q. v.]), more than the stature of a man, (Ibn-Kunáseh,) [or,] in appearance, the measure of five cubits: (Kzw:) two bright stars, (S, K,) in, or upon, (K,) the two horns [or claws ] of Scorpio: (S, K:) [ a and g of Libra, accord. to those who make Aln~awo' to mean “ the auroral setting; ” and perhaps the same, or α and β of Libra, accord to those who make Aln~awo' to mean “ the auroral rising: ”] one of the Mansions of the Moon, (S, Kzw,) namely, the Sixteenth Mansion. (Kzw. [See manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl .]) The saying EaD~a biA^aToraAfi Alz~ubaAnaY qamaruho [lit. His moon bit the extremities of the claw of Scorpio ], cited by IAar, is expl. as meaning “ he is uncircumcised, except the part from which the qamar has contracted; ” his qulofap being likened to the zubaAnaY [and his kamarap to the qamar ]: and he is related to have said that he who is born when the moon is in Scorpio is unprosperous: but Th says, I asked him respecting this saying, and he disallowed it, and said, No, but he is a low, or mean, or sordid, person, who does not give food in winter; and when the moon [in winter] bites the extremities of the zubaAnaY , [i. e. enters Scorpio,] it is most intense cold. (TA.) -A2- See also zabaAniyapN .

sourceDefinition: is a pl., of which the sing. is ↓ ziboniyapN , (Akh, Zj, S, K,) as some say, or ↓ zabaAnK , (Akh, S,) or ↓ zubaAnaY , like sukaAraY , (TA,) or ↓ zaAbinN , (Akh, S,) or ↓ riboniY~N , (Ks, K,) the pl. of this last being originally zabaAniY~u , the p [in zabaAniyapN ] being substituted for the [last] Y : (Bd in xcvi. 18:) but the Arabs hardly, or in nowise, know this [attribution of a sing. to zabaAniyapN ], holding it to be a pl. having no sing., like A^abaAbiylu and EabaAdiydu . (Akh, S.) With the Arabs [of the classical age] it signifies The $uraT [app. in the earlier sense of the braves of an army, or in the later sense of the armed attendants, officers, or soldiers, of the prefect of the police ]: (S:) this is the primary signification: (Bd in xcvi. 18:) the sing. being syn. with $uroTiY~N : and also signifying the mutamar~id [i. e. one who exalts himself, or is insolent and audacious, in pride and in acts of rebellion or disobedience, &c.,] of the jinn, or genii, and of mankind: (K:) and i. q. $adiydN [i. e. strong, &c.]: (Secr, K:) each of these two significations [and the first also] being from the meaning of “ pushing, ” or “ thrusting. ” (TA.) ― -b2- Alz~abaAniyapu signifies also Certain angels, [ the tormentors of the damned in Hell, ] so called because of their thrusting the people of the fire thereto; (Katádeh, S, Msb; *) the angels mentioned in the Kur [lxvi. 6] as gilaAZN $idaAdN , (Zj,) i. e. rough in speech or in disposition, strong in deeds or in make. (Bd.)

definition: (S, M, K) with ka*aA following it, and saA^alahu Eano ka*aA and bika*aA , (S, * K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: (S, M, K) with ka*aA following it, and saA^alahu Eano ka*aA and bika*aA , (S, * K,) aor. yasoA^alu , (M,) inf. n. suw^aAlN and masoA^alapN , (S, M, K,) which latter is also pronounced masalapN , without the hemzeh, (TA,) and tasoA=lN and saA=lapN , (M, K,) and saA^alapN or saA^olapN , (accord. to different copies of the K, the former of these two accord. to the TA, [and it appears from a statement that will be found below, voce suw^olN , that one of these is correct, but in an excel-lent copy of the M, in the place thereof, I find, and ↓ saA='alahu , as a verb, doubly trans., first thus by itself, and secondly by means of Eano , as shown by an ex. in a verse cited below, (see 3,) and this also is correct,]) all [sometimes] signify the same, (S, * K,) i. e. He asked him such a thing; or asked him, interrogated him, questioned him, or inquired of him, respecting such a thing: but En k*A is more common than bk*A : when saA^ala means the asking, or demanding, of property, it is trans. [only] by itself or by means of mino [so that you say saA^alahu ka*aA and saA^ala minohu ka*aA meaning he asked, or demanded, of him such a thing ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and one says also saAla , aor. yasaAlu , (Akh, S, M, Msb, K,) like xaAfa , aor. yaxaAfu ; (Msb, K;) which is of the dial. of Hudheyl; the medial letter of this being originally w , as is shown by the phrase, mentioned by AZ, humaA yatasaAwalaAni : (TA:) [respecting this dial. var., see what follows:] the imperative (S, Msb, K, TA;) of saA^ala (S, Msb, TA) is AisoA^alo ; (S, M, Msb, K, TA;) and (S, K, &c.) that of saAla , (S, Msb, TA,) salo , (S, Msb, K, TA,) dual. salaA , and pl. saluwA , [these two being] irregular; (Msb;) and AAF mentions that Aboo-'Othmán heard one say Aisalo , [a form omitted in some copies of the K, but mentioned in the CK,] meaning AisoA^alo , suppressing the ' , and transferring its vowel to the preceding letter, like as some of the Arabs said laHomaru for AlA^aHomaru [as many do in the present day]: (M:) accord. to ISd, (TA,) the Arabs universally suppress the ' in the imperative except when they prefix to it fa or wa ; (M, TA;) saying faA@soA^alo and waA@soA^alo : (TA:) or when wa [or fa ] is prefixed, it is allowable to pronounce the ' and also to suppress it, as in saying waA@soA^aluwA and wasaluwA : (Msb:) and for the pass. suy^ila , one may say siyla , and suyila , in this instance making the kesreh to partake of the sound of dammeh, and suwla ; and also suyila , in which the middle letter is pronounced with a sound between that of ' and that of Y , or resembling that of w . (IJ, TA.) As Er-Rághib says, suw^aAlN signifies The asking, or demanding, knowledge, or information, or what leads thereto: and the asking, or demanding, property, or what leads thereto. (TA.) saA^alotuhu Eani Al$~aYo'i means I asked of him information respecting the thing: (IB, TA: [and the like is said in the Msb:]) and saA^alotuhu Al$~aYo'a [is sometimes used in the same sense, as has been shown above, but generally] means I asked him to give me the thing: (IB, TA:) you say, saA^alahu maAlFA He asked, demanded, or begged, of him property, and in like manner, saA^ala minohu and saA^ala A_ilayohi [followed by maAlFA ]: (MA:) and saA^alotu A@ll~`ha AlEaAfiyapa , inf. n. suw^aAlN and masoA^alapN , I begged, or sought, of God health, or freedom from disease, &c. (Msb.) The saying in the Kur [lxx. 1], saA^ala saAy^ilN biEa*aAbK waAqiEK means Eano Ea*aAbK [i. e. An asker asked respecting a falling punishment ]: (S:) [for] one says, xarajonaA nasoA^alu Eano fulaAnK and bifulaAnK [meaning We went forth asking respecting such a one ]: (Akh, S:) or the phrase in the Kur means a caller called [ for a falling punishment ]: (TA:) and some read saAla saAy^ilN bE*Ab wAqE , (Bd, TA,) [likewise] from Als~uw^aAlu : (Bd:) or this means saAla waAdK bE*Ab wAqE [i. e. a valley flowed with a falling punishment ]; (Bd, TA;) so some say; (TA;) from Als~ayalaAnu . (Bd.) The saying, in a trad., nahaY Eano kavorapi Als~aw^aAli [ He (Mohammad) forbade much questioning or inquiring ] is said to relate to subtile questions or inquiries, that are needless; like another trad., mentioned below, voce, masoA^alapN : or to the begging, of men, their property needlessly. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, TA,) inf. n. musaA='alapN : (TA:) see 1, first sentence. Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, A^asaA='alota rasoma Ald~aAri A^amo lamo tusaAy^ili Eani Als~akoni A^amo Eano Eahodihi biAlA^awaAy^ili [ Didst thou ask the remains of the dwelling, or didst thou not ask, respecting the inhabitants, or respecting their knowledge of the former occupants? ]. (M, TA.) ― -b2- In the saying of Bilál Ibn-Jereer, wajadota bihimo Eil~apF HaADiraho A_i*aA Difotahumo A^awo saA=yalotahumo [ When thou becomest their guest, or askest of them, thou findest with them a ready excuse ], saA=yalotahumo is a combination of two dial. vars.; the ' being in the original phrase saA='alotu zayodFA , and the Y being a substitute in the phrase saAyalotu zayodFA ; the measure of saA=yalotahumo being faEaAyalotahumo : (M, K: *) so said Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, [i. e. Th,] who had at first ignored the expression: (M:) and it is an instance of which we know not a parallel in the language. (M, K. *) ― -b3- [Accord. to analogy, saA='alaha also signifies He asked him, &c., being asked by him, &c. ― -b4- And Freytag states that Reiske has explained saA='ala as meaning He always demanded that another should express wishes for his health: but I know not any instance of its being used in this sense.]

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K, &c.,) [aor. ,] inf. n. sujuwdN , (Msb,) He was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive; syn. xaDaEa , (S, A, K, TA,) or taTaAmana , and *al~a : (Msb:) or he bent him-self down towards the ground: (Aboo-Bekr, TA: [and such is often meant by xaDaEa and by taTaAmana :]) [or it has both of these significations combined; i. e. he was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive, bending himself down; for] the primary signification of Als~ujuwdu is ta*al~ulF together with taTaA^omunN [or taTaAmunN ]. (Bd in ii. 32.) And ↓ Asjd He lowered his head, and bent himself; (AA, S, Mgh, K;) said of a man; (AA, S, Mgh;) and put his forehead on the ground: (Mgh:) and likewise said of a camel; (S, A;) in the latter case tropical; (A;) as also sajada ; (A, Mgh, Msb;) meaning (tropical:) he lowered his head, (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) to be ridden, (S, Mgh,) or to his rider, (A,) or on the occasion of his being ridden, or mounted. (Msb.) ― -b2- The sujuwd of prayer is from sajada in the first of the senses expl. above; (S;) and means The [ prostrating oneself; ] putting the forehead on the ground: (S, Mgh:) sajada , (ISd, Msb, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (ISd, TA,) signifies he put his forehead on the ground: (ISd, Msb, TA:) but sujuwd to God denotes a particular manner [of doing this; i. e. the prostrating oneself in prayer by dropping gently upon the knees, placing the palms of the hands on the ground, a little before the place of the knees, and then putting the nose and forehead on the ground, the former first, between the two hands ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- It is said of Kisrà, in a trad., kaAna yasojudo lilT~aAliE , i. e. He used to lower himself, or bend himself down, to the arrow passing beyond the butt, going over it; which they used to reckon like that which hit the butt; meaning that he used to concede to the shooter thereof: or, accord. to Az, it means that he used to lower his head when his arrow was elevated [too high] above the object shot at, in order that the arrow might be rightly directed, and might hit the circle. (TA.) ― -b4- And [as salutation is often accompanied with a bending of the body,] sujuwdN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The act of saluting. (L, TA.) [You say, sajada lahu (assumed tropical:) He saluted him. And also (assumed tropical:) He paid respect, or honour, to him; or magnified him; see Ham p. 294.] ― -b5- You say also, sajadati Aln~axolapu (tropical:) The palm-tree bent, or inclined, (AHn, Mgh, TA,) by reason of the abundance of its fruit. (Mgh.) And Als~afiynapu tasojudu lilr~iyHi (tropical:) The ship bends, or inclines, by the influence of the wind. (A, TA.) ― -b6- wa A@ln~ajomu wa A@l$~ajaru yasojudaAni , in the Kur [lv. 5], means, accord. to Fr, (assumed tropical:) [ And the herbs and the trees ] turn towards the sun and incline with it until the afternoon-shade becomes broken: (TA:) or the herbs and the trees humbly submit to his will. (Bd, Jel.) The sujuwd of inanimate things to God we understand, in the Kur, as denoting obedience to that whereto they are made subservient, and as a fact to be believed without inquiry into the manner thereof. (I'Ab, L.) -A2- Also He stood erect: (Lth, Msb, K:) so in the dial. of Teiyi. (Msb.) It is said in the K, immediately after the mention of the first signification and this last, that thus the verb has two contr. meanings: but it may be said that there is no [necessary, or absolute,] contrariety between AlxuDuwE and AlAinotiSaAb . (MF.) -A3- sajidato rijoluhu , aor. , (tropical:) His leg became inflated, or swollen. (K, TA.)

He used to lower himself, or bend himself down, to the arrow passing beyond the butt, going over it; which they used to reckon like that which hit the butt; meaning that he used to concede to the shooter thereof: or, accord. to Az, it means that he used to lower his head when his arrow was elevated [too high] above the object shot at, in order that the arrow might be rightly directed, and might hit the circle. [You say, sajada lahu (assumed tropical:) He saluted him. And also (assumed tropical:) He paid respect, or honour, to him; or magnified him; see Ham p. 294.] ― -b5- You say also, sajadati Aln~axolapu (tropical:) The palm-tree bent, or inclined, (AHn, Mgh, TA,) by reason of the abundance of its fruit. (MF.) -A3- sajidato rijoluhu , aor. , (tropical:) His leg became inflated, or swollen. (K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ Any place in which one performs the act of sujuwd , or acts of worship or devotion; and particularly a mosque; a Muslim temple; an oratory; ] a house in which one performs the act of sujuwd ; (IB;) a house of prayer; (Mgh, Msb;) any place in which one performs acts of worship or devotion: (Zj:) a word of well-known meaning; (K;) sing. of masaAjidu ; (S, Mgh, K;) and also pronounced ↓ masojadN : (S, K:) this latter word signifies, accord. to IAar, the miHoraAb [here meaning oratory, or place of private prayer, ] of a house; and the place of prayer of the congregations; (TA;) or it signifies any of the parts of the ground, as well as of the body, that are the places of sujuwd : (Lth, L:) or the place of the forehead [ on the ground in the act of prostration in prayer ]. (IB.) Fr says, (S,) the mafoEl of every verb of the class of faEala having its aor. of the measure yafoEulu is with fet-h to the medial radical letter, whether it be a subst, or an inf. n., (S, K,) without any difference, so that you say, daxala madoxalFA , and h`*aA madoxaluhu ; (S;) except some words (S, K) among substs., (S,) as masojidN and maToliEN (S, K) and magoribN (S) and ma$oriqN and masoqiTN and maforiqN and majozirN and masokinN and marofiqN (S, K) from rafaqa , aor. yarofuqu , (S,) and manobitN and manosikN (S, K) from nasaka , aor. yanosuku ; (S;) these being with kesr (S, K) to the medial radical letter (K) as a sign of their being substs.; but sometimes some of the Arabs pronounce it with fet-h in the subst.: masokinN and masokanN have been transmitted; and we have heard Almasojidu and ↓ Almasojadu , and AlmaToliEu and AlmaTolaEu : and he further says, (S,) fet-h is allowable, (S, K,) in all of these, (S,) even if we have not heard it: but when the verb is of the class of faEala having its aor. of the measure yafoEilu , the n. of place [or time] is with kesr, and the inf. n. is with fet-h, to distinguish the one from the other; so that you say, nazala manozalFA , meaning nuzuwlFA , and h`*aA manozilupu , meaning daAruhu . definition: , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_isoraArN ; (Msb;) [and accord. to the TA sar~ahu ; but see the first sentence of this art.;] He concealed it; suppressed it; kept it secret; (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) namely, a story, or the like: (A, Mgh, Msb:) and, contr., he manifested it; revealed it; published it; made it known. (S, M, Msb, K.) Both of these significations have been assigned to the verb in the phrase waA^asar~uwA A@ln~adaAmapa , in the Kur [x. 55 and xxxiv. 32]: (S:) some say, that the meaning is They will manifest repentance: Th says, they will conceal it from their chiefs: the former [says ISd] is the more correct: (M:) the former meaning is also given on the authority of AO; but Sh says, I have not heard it on the authority of any other; and Az says that the lexicologists most strongly disapprove of the saying of AO; and it is said that the meaning is, they, the chiefs of the polytheists, will conceal repentance from the lower class of their people, whom they shall have caused to err; and in like manner say Zj and the [other] expositors. (TA.) In like manner also the two contr. significations are assigned to the verb in the saying of Imra-el- Keys, [in his Mo'allakah,] lawo yusir~uwna maqotaliY , which As used to quote with $ , thus, lawo yu$ir~uwna maqotaliY , meaning that they might publish, or make known, my slaughter. (S.) You say also, A^asar~a A_ilayohi HadiyvFA He revealed unto him a story (S, K) secretly. (TA.) An ex. occurs in the Kur lxvi. 3. (TA.) And A^asorarotu A_ilayohi Almawad~apa , and biAlmawad~api , I showed, or manifested, to him love, or affection. (S.) It is said in the Kur [lx. 1], tusir~uwna A_ilayohimo biA@lomawad~api , meaning, Ye reveal to them the news of the Prophet by reason of the love that is between you and them; the objective complement of the verb being suppressed: or Almwd~p may be an objective complement, the b being a redundant corroborative, as in A^axa*a AlxiTaAma and A^axa*a bihi : (Msb:) and this interpretation is correct; for A_isoraArN to a person necessarily implies revealing a secret to him and at the same time concealing it from another. (B.) ― -b2- waA^asar~uwhu biDaAEapF , in the Kur xii. 19, signifies And they concealed, or kept secret, his case, making him as an article of merchandise: (Jel:) or they conjectured in their minds that they should obtain, by selling him, merchandise. (TA.) [See also an ex. voce AirotagaY , in art. rgw .] ― -b3- Asr~ AlfaAtiHapa , and biAlfaAtiHapi , He recited the Fátihah [or First Chapter of the Kur-án] secretly, or inaudibly: (Msb:) or the latter form of expression is a mistake. (Mgh.) ― -b4- A^asorarotuhu also signifies nasabotuhu A_ilaY Als~ir~i [which may mean either I attributed it to secrecy, or, like many phrases of this kind, by inversion, I attributed to him secrecy, or mystery ]. (Msb.)

definition: , (M, K,) and ↓ Astsr~ , (K,) He took to himself a concubine-slave.
sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) and ↓ Astsr~ , (K,) He took to himself a concubine-slave. (M, * K, * TA.) And tasar~arotu jaAriyapF , and tasar~ayotuhaA , (S,) and ↓ Aisotasar~ayotuhaA , (TA,) I took to myself a girl, or young woman, as a concubine-slave. (S, * TA.) tasar~arotuhaA is [said to be] thus changed to tasar~ayotuhaA , (T, S, Msb,) for alleviation of the pronunciation, (Msb,) on account of the three r s following one another, (T,) being like taZan~anotu and taZan~ayotu . (M.)

definition: He, or it, became concealed;

(AO, S.) -A2- Astsr~hu He took extraordinary pains in concealing it, or keeping it secret. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 5, in four places. ― -b3- Aisotasar~aniY He revealed to me his secret. (TA.) -A3- See also 1; and see 6, last sentence.

definition: A secret; a thing that is concealed, or suppressed, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) in the mind; (TA;) as also ↓ sariyrapN : (S, M, A, K:) or the former has the above-mentioned signification, and the latter...
sourceDefinition: A secret; a thing that is concealed, or suppressed, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) in the mind; (TA;) as also ↓ sariyrapN : (S, M, A, K:) or the former has the above-mentioned signification, and the latter signifies a secret action, whether good or evil: (Lth:) [and the former, also, a mystery: ] pl. of the former, A^asoraArN ; (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) and of the latter, saraAy^iru . (S, A, K.) It is said in a prov., maA yawomu Haliymapa bisir~K [ The day of Haleemeh is not a secret ]: applied to anything commonly known: alluding to Haleemeh the daughter of El-Hárith the son of Aboo-Shemir El-Ghassánee; for, when her father sent an army to El-Mundhir the son of Má-es-Semà, she took forth for the soldiers some perfume in a vessel ( mirokan ), and perfumed them with it. (S.) [You say also, huwa mawoDiEu sir~iY He is the depositary of my secret, or secrets. ] The words of the Kur [lxxxvi. 9] ↓ yawoma tubolaY Als~araAy^iru signify In the day wherein the secret tenets and intentions shall be tried and revealed: (Jel:) or by AlsrAy^r is here meant fasting, and prayer, and alms-giving, and ablution on account of the pollution termed janaAbap . (TA.) [See also a verse cited in the third paragraph of art. ErD .] ― -b2- A thing that is revealed, appears, or is made manifest: thus it has two contrary significations. (MF.) ― -b3- Als~ir~u [for maHal~u Als~ir~i , (assumed tropical:) The heart; the mind; the recesses of the mind; the secret thoughts; the soul; ] is a syn. of AlD~amiyru . (K in art. Dmr . [See also sariyrapN .]) [ laA tutoEibo sir~aka (assumed tropical:) Weary not thy heart, or mind, is a common modern phrase. And one says, of a deceased holy man, qad~asa A@ll~`hu sir~ahu (assumed tropical:) May God sanctify his soul. ] ― -b4- sir~N also signifies Secrecy; privacy; contr. of EalaAniyapN . (S in art. Eln .) You say sir~FA waEalaAniyapF [ Secretly and openly; or privately and publickly ]. (Kur ii. 275, &c.) ― -b5- Concealment. (S.) ― -b6- Suppression; contr. of A_iEolaAnN . (Msb.) [So in the phrase takal~ama sir~FA He spoke with a suppressed, or low, voice; softly. ] ― -b7- [ One having private knowledge of a thing. You say,] fulaAnN sir~u h`*aA AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) Such a one has [ private ] knowledge of this thing. (TA.) ― -b8- (tropical:) The penis (T, S, M, K) of a man: (T:) and (tropical:) the vulva, or external portion of the organs of generation, of a woman. (K.) One says, AilotaqaY Als~ir~aAni (tropical:) The two pudenda met. (A.) ― -b9- (tropical:) Concubitus. (AHeyth, S, Mgh, K.) ― -b10- (tropical:) Marriage: (M, A, Msb, K:) pl. A^asoraArN . (TA.) You say, waAEadahaA sir~FA (tropical:) He promised her marriage, she promising him the same. (A.) So, accord. to some, in the Kur ii. 235. (TA.) ― -b11- (tropical:) Plain declaration of marriage: (K:) i. e., a man's offering himself in marriage to a woman during her Eid~ap : so expl. as occurring in the Kur ubi suprà: (TA:) or a man's demanding a woman in marriage during her Eid~ap . (Mujáhid.) ― -b12- (tropical:) Adultery, or fornication: (AHeyth, (K:) so, accord. to Aboo-Mijlez and El-Hasan, in the Kur ubi suprà. (TA.) Hence the saying, laA yurojaY mino waladi Als~ir~i bir~N (tropical:) One does not hope for filial piety from the offspring of adultery, or fornication. (TK.) ― -b13- (assumed tropical:) Origin; syn. A^aSolN ; (M, K;) as in the phrase huwa kariymu Als~ir~i kaviyru Albir~i He is of generous origin, of much filial piety. (TK.) ― -b14- (assumed tropical:) The commencement, or first night, of a lunar month: (K, TA:) or its middle; (K;) app. meaning what are called AlA^ay~aAmu AlbiyDu : (TA:) but Az says, I know it not in this sense. sourceDefinition: The navel; i. e. the place from which the navel-string ( sur~ ) has been cut off; (S;) the small cavity, or hollow, of the belly, (M, TA,) in the middle thereof; (TA;) what remains of the sirar : (M:) [see sur~N :] pl. surarN [in the CK erroneously sirarN ] and sur~aAtN . (S, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] sur~apu Alfarasi (assumed tropical:) [ The navel of the horse, ] the star, of Pegasus, that is in the head of Andromeda. (Kzw.) ― -b3- [Hence likewise] sur~apN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A perforation in the middle of a jar such as is termed muzam~alap [q. v.], in which is fixed a tube of silver or lead, whence one drinks. (Har p. 548.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) The place where the water rests, in the furthest part, of a watering-trough, or tank. (K, TA.) ― -b5- See also sir~N , in two places, in the latter part of the paragraph.
