sourceDefinition: , (inf. n. taSogiyrN , TA,) He made him, or it, small, or little; as also ↓ ASfrhu . (S, K.) You say, Alqirobapa ↓ ASgr He sewed the water-skin [ so as to make it ] small. (S, K.) ― -b2- Sg~rhu fiY Euyuwni Aln~aAsi He, or it, rendered him [ small, or little, i. e.,] contemptible, vile, base, or ignominious, [ in the eyes of men: ] (A:) and [in like manner] he, or it, rendered him vile, base, or ignominious, (TA,) or content with vileness, baseness, abasement, or ignominy. (K.) ― -b3- Sag~arotu $aA^onahu (TA in art. gmz ) and mino $aA^onihi (S and TA in the same art.) [ I lessened his rank, or dignity ]. ― -b4- Sg~r AlAisoma , inf. n. taSogiyrN , He changed the noun into the diminutive form. (Msb.) This is done for several purposes: to denote the smallness of the thing signified, in itself; as in the instance of duwaborapN [“ a small, or little, house ”]: to denote its smallness in the eye of the speaker, when it is not small in itself; as in the saying *ahabati Ald~araAhimu A_il~aA durayohimFA [“ the dirhems went, except a small dirhem ”]: to denote nearness; as in the instance of qubayola AlS~uboHi [“ a little before daybreak ”]: to denote affection and benevolence; as in the expression yaA bunaY~a [“ O my little (meaning dear) son ”]: to denote the greatness of the thing signified; as in the phrase sunay~apN HamoraA='u [“ a very severe year ”]: to denote praise; as when a man is described as kunayofN muliy^a EilomFA [“ a little pastor's-bag filled with knowledge ”]: to denote blame; as in the expression yaA fuwayosiqu [“ O thou little transgressor ”]. (L, TA.) [The inf. n., taSogiyrN , is also applied to A diminutive noun itself; as also AisomN muSag~arN .] ― -b5- See also 10.

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. SalaEN , (S, * O, * Msb, K, * TA,) He (a man, S, O, K *) was, or became, bald in the fore part of the head: (S, * O, * Msb, K: * but in the Msb it is said in this sense of the head:) or in the fore part of the head to the kinder part thereof: and likewise in the middle of the head. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SaliEati AlEurofuTapu , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) The ErfTp [a species of mimosa] dropped the heads of its branches: and had them eaten by the camels. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 7. -A2- SalaEa raA^osahu [perhaps a mistranscription for ↓ Sal~aEa , and primarily signifying He made his head bald in the fore part: ] (tropical:) he shaved his head. (TA.)

definition: One of a pair, (AHn, S, M, K,) or of three, (S, M,) or of more than two, (K,) or of more than three, (M,) or of five, or of six, (TA,) of palmtrees, (S, M, K,) or of any trees, (AHn, M, K,) or of...
sourceDefinition: One of a pair, (AHn, S, M, K,) or of three, (S, M,) or of more than two, (K,) or of more than three, (M,) or of five, or of six, (TA,) of palmtrees, (S, M, K,) or of any trees, (AHn, M, K,) or of trees resembling one another, (M,) growing from one root; (AHn, S, M, K;) each [or every one] of such being called the Sinow of the other [or others growing with it]; (AHn, M;) as also ↓ SunowN , (M, K,) mentioned by Zj: (M:) two of such are termed SinowaAni (S, K) and SunowaAni and SanowaAni , [which last implies that ↓ SanowN as well as SunowN is a dial. var. of SinowN ,] and also SinoyaAni and SunoyaAni and SanoyaAni , [which imply that SinoYN and SunoYN and SanoYN are also dial. vars. of SinowN and SunowN and SanowN ;] (K;) and the pl. is SinowaAnN (AZ, S, M) and [of pauc.] A^aSonaA='N , (M,) the former pl. differing from the first of the duals mentioned above by being perfectly decl. (AZ, S, * TA.) Hence, in the Kur [xiii. 4], SinowaAnK wagayorui SinowaAnK , (TA,) i. e. Palmtrees having one root and [others] having distinct roots: Hafs read SunowaAn , like qunowaAn pl. of qinowN ; of the dial. of Temeem. (Bd.) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) A brother; but not so called unless coupled with another: (Sh, TA:) or a brother by the same father: (Az, TA:) [or a brother by the same mother; as is indicated by an explanation of one of the pls in what follows:] or a brother such as is termed $qiyq , (M, K,) which means by the father and mother: (TA in art. $q :) and a son; (M, K;) because he has branched forth from one stock [with his father]: (TA:) and a paternal uncle; (M, K;) but this last meaning is taken from a trad. cited in what follows: (TA:) the fem. is with p : and the pl. is A^aSonaA='N [a pl. of pauc.] and SinowaAnN [as above]. (M, K.) It is said in a trad., Eam~u Alr~ajuli Sinowu A^abiyhi (tropical:) [ The paternal uncle of the man is the Sinow of his father ]; (T, S;) meaning that the stock of both is one. (T, TA.) [And it is said that] SanowaAnN wgayoru SinowaAnK , relating to a man's children, means (assumed tropical:) Sons of one mother by different fathers, and children of different mothers by one father. (Har p. 608.) ― -b3- [Hence the pl.] A^aSonaA='N signifies also (assumed tropical:) Likes, or fellows. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- And rakiy~ataAni SinowaAni (tropical:) Two wells near together, (AZ, S, M, K, TA,) or (so in the TA and in some copies of the K) that yield water from one spring. (AZ, S, K, TA.) ― -b5- SinowN also signifies A widened well ( HafarN ) from which water is not drawn and of the water of which no use is made: (Ibn-Buzurj, K:) pl. SinowaAnN . (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.) ― -b6- See also what follows.

(S &c.) ― -b2- [In the Kur xii. 72,] some read nafoqidu Sawoga Almaliki [meaning We miss, or see not, or find not, the King's molten vessel, or vessel made of melted metal ]: in this instance, Sawog is an inf. n. (O, K, TA) used as a subst., (O, TA,) in the sense of ↓ AlmaSuwg , which means maASiyga [i. e. the thing that has been melted, and poured forth into a mould; &c.]; like ↓ AlmuSaAgu [a pass. part. n. of a verb which is not mentioned]: (TA:) it is like Darob in the phrase h`*aA dirohamN Darobu AlA^amiyri , (O, K, * TA,) meaning maDoruwbuhu : (O, TA:) and Er-Rághib says that it [i. e. the vessel thus termed] is held to have been made of molten gold: (TA:) some read [in the Kur xii. 72] ↓ SuwaAg , as though this also were [originally] an inf. n. (O, K, TA) from SaAga , (O, TA,) like buwaAlN and quwaAmN (O, K, TA) from baAla and qaAma . (O, TA.) [See also SaAEN , with the unpointed E .] ― -b3- One says also, h`*aA Sawogu h`*aA This is of the measure of this; or is the like in measure of this: [as though of the make, form, fashion, mould, or cast, of this: (see also SiygapN :)] (S, O, Msb:) and h`*aA AlmaA='u Sawogu AlA_inaA='i This water is of the measure of the vessel; or is the like in measure of the vessel: and everything that is the like in measure of another thing is said to be Sawoguhu . (O.) ― -b4- And humaA SawogaAni They two are likes: (S, O, K:) or they two are coëtaneans; syn. lidapN [which is properly a sing., though here used as a dual]. (IDrd, O, K.) ― -b5- And huwa Sawogu A^axiyhi (AA, O, K) He is he who was born immediately after his brother; and [in like manner, before him, for] he may be above him and he may be below him, (O,) like sawoguhu ; as also A^axiyhi ↓ Sawogapu , (K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, Auxotihi ,]) like sawogapu A^axiyhi : (TA:) and hiYa A^uxotuka Sawoguka and ↓ Sawogatuka [ She is thy sister who was born immediately after thee; or before thee ]: (O, TA:) the pl. is A^aSowaAgN . (TA voce sawogN .)

definition: (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ DadiydN (S, L, K) and ↓ DadiydapN (Th, M) The contrary, or opposite, (AA, IAar, S, * M, Msb, K,) of a thing: (AA, Msb:) or Did~u $aYo'K signifies that which is repugnant to a thing, so that it would overcome it;
sourceDefinition: (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ DadiydN (S, L, K) and ↓ DadiydapN (Th, M) The contrary, or opposite, (AA, IAar, S, * M, Msb, K,) of a thing: (AA, Msb:) or Did~u $aYo'K signifies that which is repugnant to a thing, so that it would overcome it; as black is to white, and death to life: (Lth, L:) [or, accord. to the explanation of mutaDaAd~aAni in the Msb, that which is inconsistent with a thing: ] pl. of the first A^aDadaAdN . (S, Msb, &c.) One says also, huwa Did~uka and ↓ Dadiyduka He is contrary, or opposed, or repugnant, to thee; as when thou desirest what is long, and he, what is short; or thou, darkness, and he, light; or thou, to pursue one course, and he, to pursue another. (AHeyth, L.) And Did~N is sometimes a pl., (K,) or sometimes denotes a collective body; (Akh, S, L;) as in the phrase yakuwnuwna Ealayohimo Did~FA , (S, L, K,) in the Kur [xix. 85], (S, L,) meaning They shall be adversaries, or enemies, to them: ('Ikrimeh, Jel:) or helpers against them. (Fr, Jel.) One says also, Alqawomu EalaY~a Did~N waAHidN , meaning The people are assembled together against me in contention, or altercation, with me. (L.) ― -b2- Did~N in lexicology signifies A kind of mu$otarak [or homonym ]; being a word that has two contrary meanings; as jawonN , which means both “ black ” and “ white; ” and jalalN , which means both “ great ” and “ small ” pl. as above. (Mz, 26th nwE .) [ Did~N is itself a word of this kind, as is shown by what here follows.] ― -b3- Also, (AA, Th, S, L, Msb, K,) and ↓ DadiydN , (S, L, K,) The like, or equal, (AA, Th, S, L, Msb, K,) of a thing. (AA, Msb.) Thus they have two contrary meanings. (K.) One says, laA Did~a lahu and lahu ↓ laA Dadiyda There is no like, or equal, to him, or it. (S, L.) And laqiYa Alqawomu A^aDodaAdahumo The people, or party, found, or met, their equals, or fellows. (L.)

definition: , inf. n. taDomiyrN , He made him (a horse) lean, or light of flesh; [&c.;] as also ↓ ADmrhu . (S.) ― -b2- He prepared him (i. e. a horse) for racing, [or for a military expedition, (see muDam~irN...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taDomiyrN , He made him (a horse) lean, or light of flesh; [&c.;] as also ↓ ADmrhu . (S.) ― -b2- He prepared him (i. e. a horse) for racing, [or for a military expedition, (see muDam~irN ,)] by feeding him with food barely sufficient to sustain him, after he had become fat; as also ↓ ADmrhu . (Msb:) he fed him with food barely sufficient to sustain him, after he had become fat; as also ↓ ADmrhu : (K:) or he fed him with fodder so that he became fat, and then reduced him to food barely sufficient to sustain him; which is done during forty days: (S:) or he saddled him, and put on him a housing, in order that he might sweat under it, and so lose his flabbiness, and become firm in flesh; and then mounted upon him a light boy or young man, to make him run, but not to make him go so quick a pace as that which is termed Eanaq ; by the doing of which, one becomes in no fear of his losing his breath in running, and a quick run does not cut him short: this (says AM) is what I have seen the Arabs practise; and they term it taDomiyrN , and also ↓ miDomaArN . (T, L.) ― -b3- Also He, or it, weakened, and subdued, and diminished, him: and the same signification is assigned to it [tropically] when the objective complement is a word denoting a sensation or passion. (TA.) ― -b4- Alt~aDomiyru also signifies The plaiting well, and the anointing well, the lock of hair termed Damiyrap . (TA.)

definition: A place, or a valley, that is depressed, concealing him who is journeying in it.
sourceDefinition: A place, or a valley, that is depressed, concealing him who is journeying in it. (O.) [Accord. to the K, AlD~imaAru is “ A place; ” i. e. the name of a certain place.] ― -b2- maAlN DimaArN Property of which one hopes not for the return: (K:) or absent property of which one hopes not for the return: (A 'Obeyd, Msb, TA:) if not absent, it is not thus called. (A 'Obeyd, TA.) ― -b3- dayonN DimaArN A debt of which the payment is not hoped for: (S:) or for the payment of which no period is fixed. (K, * TA.) ― -b4- EaTaA='N DimaArN A gift that is not hoped for. (A.) ― -b5- waEodN DimaArN , (S,) and EidapN DimaArN , (A, K, [ mn AlEa*Abi in the CK being a mistranscription for mina AlEidaAti , as in other copies of the K and in the TA, in which latter is added that EidaAt is pl. of EidapN , which is syn. with waEodN ,]) A promise of which the fulfilment is not hoped for: (S, A:) or of which the fulfilment is delayed. (K.) ― -b6- DimaArN also signifies Anything of which one is not confident, or sure. (S.) ― -b7- And A debt of which the payment is deferred by the creditor to a future period; or a sale upon credit, in which the payment is deferred to a definite period; or a postponement, or delay, as to the time of the payment of a debt or of the prince of a thing sold &c.; syn. nasiyoy^apN . (Fr, TA.) ― -b8- Also Unseen; not apparent; contr. of EiyaAnN . (K.) A poet says, censuring a certain man, waEayonuhu kaAlkaAliy^i AlD~imaAri [ And his present gift is a thing not hoped for, like the unseen debt of which the payment is deferred by the creditor: ] meaning, his present gift is like the absent that is not hoped for. (TA.) ― -b9- *ahabuwA bimaAliY DimaArFA means They took away my property by gaming. (Fr, TA.) -A2- Also A certain idol, which was worshipped by El-Abbás Ibn-Mirdás. (O, K, TA. [It is implied in the K that it is with the art. Al ; but it is not so accord. to the O and TA.])

definition: Concealed, (K,) [or conceived, ] in the mind.

(S, TA.)

definition: A training-place in which horses are prepared for racing [or for military service ] by being fed with food barely sufficient to sustain them, after they have become fat: (S, * Msb, K: *) [a hippodrome;
sourceDefinition: A training-place in which horses are prepared for racing [or for military service ] by being fed with food barely sufficient to sustain them, after they have become fat: (S, * Msb, K: *) [a hippodrome; a place where horses are exercised: ] pl. maDaAmiyru . (A.) You say, jaraY fiY AlmiDomaAri [ He ran in the hippodrome, or place of exercise ]. (A.) And AlginaA='u miDomaAru Al$~iEori (tropical:) [app. meaning Singing is that in which the excellences of poetry are displayed, like as the excellences of a horse are displayed in the hippodrome ]. (A.) ― -b2- Also The time, of forty days, during which a horse is reduced to food barely sufficient to sustain him, after his having been fed with fodder so that he has become fat; (S, TA;) the time during which a horse is thus prepared for racing or for an expedition against the enemy: pl. as above. (TA.) It is said in a trad., Aaloyawoma miDomaArN wagadFA A@los~ibaAqu waAls~aAbiqu mano sabaqa A@lojan~apa [ To-day is a time for training, and to-morrow is the race, and the winner is he who wins Paradise: ] i. e., to-day one is to work, in the present world, for the desire of Paradise; like as a horse is trained for racing. (Sh.) definition: (S, M, K, &c.) A kind of vessel of Sufor [or brass ]: (M, TA:) [generally pronounced in the present day Ti$ot and Ta$ot : and mostly applied to a kind of basin of tinned copper, or of brass, or of...
sourceDefinition: (S, M, K, &c.) A kind of vessel of Sufor [or brass ]: (M, TA:) [generally pronounced in the present day Ti$ot and Ta$ot : and mostly applied to a kind of basin of tinned copper, or of brass, or of silver, used for washing the hands &c., figured and described in my work on the Modern Egyptians:] i. q. Tas~N , [q. v.,] (IKt, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) which is [said to be] arabicized from Tasot , the latter being a foreign word; (Mgh;) [but it is from the Pers., Ta$ot ;] it is of the dial. of Teiyi; (S;) and [said to be] formed from Tas~N , one of the two s being changed into t , (IKt, S, Msb, K,) because they are deemed difficult of pronunciation; (IKt, S, Msb;) but in forming the pl. and the dim., the second s is restored, because separated from the former; (S;) for (IKt, S, Msb) the pl. is TisaAsN (S, Mgh, Msb) and TusuwsN , though it has also for its pl. TusuwtN , (IKt, Mgh, Msb,) or, accord. to Zj, TisaAtN ; (Msb;) and the dim. is TusayosN , (S,) or TusayosapN : (IKt, Msb:) it is also pronounced TisotN ; (MF;) and Ta$otN also has been mentioned; (K;) but some say that this is a mistake; and others, that Ta$ot is the original word from which TasotN is arabicized: (TA:) Zj says that, with most of the Arabs, (Msb,) it is fem.: (Mgh, Msb:) sometimes it is masc.: (Lh, M:) IAmb says, on the authority of Fr, that the word used by the Arabs was Tas~apN , save that some said Tas~N , without p ; and that the tribe of Teiyi said TasotN , like as they said liSotN for liS~N : Es-Sijistánee says that it is a foreign word arabicized: and Az, that it is a word adopted into the Arabic language, because T and t do not both occur in an Arabic word. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. and , (S, Msb, K,) the latter allowed by Fr as aor. of the verb in all its senses, (S, Msb,) because of the faucial letter, (Msb,) and heard by him as aor. of the verb in this phrase, but not by Ks in this case nor in relation to the grounds of pretension to respect or honour, (TA,) inf. n. TaEonN , (S, Msb, K,) and maToEanN , (Msb,) and Lth authorizes TaEanaAnN also in this case as well as in the case of TaEana biAlqawoli , (TA,) He smote him and pierced him, or he smote him and he pierced him, [for it does not always signify the causing the weapon to enter,] with the spear; (K;) he pierced him, smote him, or wounded him, with the spear: (MA:) [sometimes TaEanahu means he pierced, stabbed, stuck, or gored, him with a spear, &c.; and sometimes, he thrust, goaded, or poked, him: ] you say, TaEana Ald~aAb~apa biEuwdK A^awo naHowihi [ He goaded the beast with a stich or the like ]. (Mgh and Msb in art. nxs .) ― -b2- [Hence,] TuEina (tropical:) He was smitten by the TaAEuwn i. e. plague, or pestilence; (Z, Msb, K, TA;) said of a man, (Msb, TA,) and of a camel. (TA.) ― -b3- And TaEana fiyhi biAlqawoli , (S, Msb, K,) and Ealayohi , (Msb, TA,) and TaEanahu bilisaAnihi , (TA,) [and TaEana fiY EiroDihi ,] aor. , (Lth, TA,) or, accord. to some, in this case , (TA,) or both, (Msb,) inf. n. TaEonN and TaEanaAnN , (S, Msb, K, TA, [the latter in the CK, erroneously, TaEonaAn , but expressly said in the TA to be biAlt~aHoriyk ,]) (tropical:) [ He wounded him, or attacked him, with words, and with his tongue; and wounded, or attacked, his reputation; ] he blamed, censured, or reproached, him; attributed or imputed to him, charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, fault, or the like; or spoke against him. (Msb, TA.) sourceDefinition: , (A, K,) inf. n. taZofiyrN , (S,) He inserted his nail into it; (S, A, K;) namely, an apple, and the like, (S, K,) a cucumber, and a melon: (A:) and [in like manner] ↓ AiZ~afara , of the measure AifotaEala , he stuck, or fixed, his nail [into a thing]; (S, K, TA;) and so AiT~afara , with the unpointed T . (TA.) You say, Zf~r fulaAnN fiY wajohi fulaAnK Such a one stuck his nail into the flesh of the face of such a one, and wounded it. (TA.) And nay~aba fiY laHomihi waZaf~ara He stuck his dog-tooth and his nail into his flesh, and wounded it. (A.) And Zf~r fulaAnN fiY ka*aA wanay~aba (tropical:) Such a one clung to, caught to, or took fast hold upon, such a thing. (A in art. nyb .) Also Zf~rhu ; and ↓ Zafarahu , aor. ; (M, K;) and ↓ AiZ~afarahu , in the K erroneously written A^aZofarahu ; (TA;) He stuck his nail into his face; (M, K;) and so AiT~afarahu , with T . (TA.) And Zf~rhu [ He clawed it; ] he stuck his nail into it, (namely, anything,) and broke it, or made a mark [or scratch ] upon it. (M.) And ↓ AiZ~afara AlS~aqoru AlT~aAy^ira The hawk seized the bird with his talons. (K.) ― -b2- Zf~r said of baqol [or herbs, or leguminous plants,] (tropical:) They put forth what resembled the A^aZofaAr [or talons ] of the bird. (M, TA.) And said of the Earofaj , (K, TA,) and of the A^aroTaY , (TA,) (tropical:) It put forth what resembled A^aZofaAr , (K, TA,) when it put forth its [ leaves termed ] xuwS . (TA.) And said of the naSiY~ , and of the wa$iyj , and of the barodiY~ , and of the vumaAm , and of the Sil~iyaAn , and of the garaz , and of hadab , (tropical:) It, or they, put forth yellow shoots, resembling the Zufur [or talon ], which are the xuwS thereof, that come forth therefrom having a dustcoloured flower. (M, TA.) [Or,] said of a plant, (Ks, T, S,) inf. n. as above, (Ks, T,) (assumed tropical:) It came forth; (Ks, T;) from AlA^aZofaAr : (T:) or it came forth of the measure of the Zufor [or nail ]. (S.) And Zf~rt AlA^aroDu (assumed tropical:) The land put forth plants, or herbage, that might be uprooted ( yumokinu A@HotifaAw^uhu , so in the M, in the K A@HotifaAruhu ,) with the nail, (M,) or with the fingers. (K.) ― -b3- Zf~r vawobahu , (M, and so in a copy of the K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) (assumed tropical:) He perfumed his garment (M, and thus in that copy of the K) with what is termed Zufor : (M:) or Zf~r vawobahu biAlA^aZofaAri he perfumed his garment with what are termed A^aZofaAr . (So accord. to other copies of the K.) ― -b4- And Zf~r Aljiloda , (K,) or Zaf~arotu Aljiloda , (M,) (assumed tropical:) He, (K,) or I, (M,) rubbed the skin in order that its A^aZofaAr (M, K) which means its creased parts (M) might become smooth. (M, K.) -A2- Zf~rhu also signifies, and so ↓ AZfrhu , [ He caused him to attain, get, get possession of, or acquire, what he desired, or sought: he caused him to succeed, or to be successful: and] He (God) caused him to be victorious, to gain the victory, or to overcome. (A.) You say, Zf~rhu bihi (S, M) and Ealayohi , (M, TA,) inf. n. as above; (S;) and bh ↓ AZfrhu (S, M, Msb) and Elyh ; (M, Msb;) He (God, S, M, or a man, Msb) caused him to gain the victory over him, or to overcome him, (M, Msb,) namely, his enemy. (S, Msb.) ― -b2- And Zf~rhu Ealayohi He declared him to have overcome him: said of one who has been asked which of two persons had overcome. (T.) ― -b3- And Zf~rhu , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He prayed for him that he might attain what he desired, or sought; or that he might be successful, or victorious. (M, K.)

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, A, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ ZufurN , (Msb, K,) which latter is the most chaste form, and the form adopted by the seven readers in the Kur vi. 147, and the former is a contraction of this, [but is the most common form,] (Msb,) and ↓ ZiforN , which is extr., (M, Msb, K,) and disallowed by IDrd, (O,) and ↓ ZifirN , which is also extr., (Msb,) and ↓ A^uZofuwrN , (T, M, A, Msb, K,) which is erroneously mentioned in the S as a pl. of ZuforN , (Sgh, Msb, K,) by an anticipation of the pen; (Msb;) or, accord. to MF, it si said in most of the copies of the S, (but this is not the case,) ZuforN has for its pl. A^aZofaArN ; and A^uZofuwrN [has for its pl.] A^aZaAfiyru ; (TA;) [and this, being the reading in most of the copies of the S seen by MF, is probably what J wrote;] A certain wellknown thing; (M;) [i. e. a nail; and a talon, or claw; ] pertaining to a human being, (M, Ibn-Es-Seed, Msb, K,) and to others; (M, K;) to the beasts and birds mentioned in the next following sentence, [as well as to man,] accord. to the authorities there cited; (TA;) and to every ruminant, as syn. with ZilofN [i. e. a cloven hoof ]: (T and M in art. Zlf :) or to a beast, or bird, that does not prey; [as well as to man;] that of such as preys being termed mixolabN : (M:) [and in the present day applied also to the spur of a cock:] it is of the masc. gender: (Lh, M, Msb:) the pl. (of ZuforN , S, M, Msb, &c.) is A^aZofaArN (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and sometimes A^aZofurN , (Msb,) [both of which are pls. of pauc., but the former is used as a pl. of mult. also,]. and (of A^uZofuwrN , M, Msb, or of A^aZofaArN , and therefore a pl. pl., M) A^aZaAfiyru : (M, Msb, K:) that ↓ A^uZofuwrN is a sing. [and not like A^uboquwrN which is a quasi-pl. n.] is shown by the saying of a poet, maA bayona luqomatihaA AlA^uwlaY A_i*aA A@noHadarato wabayona A^uxoraY taliyhaA qiysu A^uZofuwri (K) or qiydu A^uZofuwri (Msb) [i. e. What is between her first morsel, when it descends into her throat, and another that follows it, is the measure of a finger-nail ]: or, as some relate it, A_i*aA A@zodaradato [ when she swallows ]; and it is thus cited [in the T and] in the “ Basáïr ” of the author of the K. (TA.) The phrase kul~a *iY ZufurK in the Kur vi. 147 comprises camels and ostriches; (so in the T and TS and L; but in the K, AlA^anoEaAm is erroneously put for Aln~aEaAm ; TA;) because their manaAsim are like A^aZofaAr to them: (T, K, TA:) I'Ab says that it comprises camels; and also ostriches, because they have nails like camels: or any bird that has a mixolab , and any beast that has a solid hoof: or, accord. to Mujáhid and Katádeh, every beast and bird that has not divided toes; as the camel and ostrich and goose and duck. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlA^aZofaAru is the name of (assumed tropical:) Certain small stars; (S;) certain stars before Aln~asor [meaning Aln~asor AlwaAqiE i. e. the star a of Lyra: app. because regarded as the talons of the nsr ]: (K:) or a certain dim star in Al$~aloyaAq [q. v., i. e. the constellation Lyra ]. (Kzw.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] A_in~ahu lakaliylu AlZ~ufori , (T,) or A_in~ahu lamaqoluwmu AlZ~ufori , (TA,) (tropical:) Verily he is one who does not slay or wound an enemy: (T, TA:) and A_in~ahu maqoluwmu AlZ~ufori Eano A^a*aY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) Verily he is one who does little hurt to mankind. (T, A, TA.) And huwa kaliylu AlZ~ufori (tropical:) He is weak, or abject, or despicable; (T, S, K, TA;) said of a man; (K, TA;) or so muqal~amu AlZ~ufori : (K: [in the TA, as from the K, muqal~amu AlA^aZofaAri :]) or (tropical:) he is sick, or diseased. (A.) And bihi ZuforN mino maraDK (tropical:) [app. meaning In him is an evil result of a disease, that has clung to him ]. (A, TA. [In the A, this immediately follows what here next precedes it; and is immediately followed by the words wa*ubaAbN Zafira minohu , which seem to be added by way of explanation; thus in my copy; but I think that Zafira minohu here is a mistake for Zaf~ara fiyhi , and have assumed this to be the case in rendering the phrase.]) ― -b4- And qar~aHotuhu mino Zuforihi A_ilaY $uforihi (tropical:) [lit. I wounded him much, from his nail to the edge of his eyelid; but mentioned as tropical; app. meaning from toe to head ]; like as one says, mino qaronihi . (A.) ― -b5- And maA baAld~aAri ZuforN , (K,) or mA bAldAr ZuforN walaA $uforN , (A, O,) (tropical:) There is not in the house any one. (A, O, K.) And maA tarakati Als~anapu ZuforFA walaA $uforFA (tropical:) The year of drought left not anything: and sometimes they said $aforFA , with fet-h, and in this case they said ↓ ZaforFA , for assimilation. (A in art. $fr .) And raA^ayotuhu biZuforihi (tropical:) I saw him himself. (O, K, TA.) ― -b6- Zuforu Aln~asori is the name of (assumed tropical:) A certain plant, (K, TA,) resembling what is [ properly ] thus termed [i. e. the talon of the vulture ]. (TA.) And Zuforu AlqiT~i is the name of (assumed tropical:) Another plant. (K, TA.) ― -b7- And AlZ~uforu , (M,) or AlA^aZofaAru , (T, M, A, Mgh, O, K, &c.,) for this word in the sense here following has no sing. (T, M, O, K) accord. to the author of the 'Eyn, (M,) but sometimes one said waAHidapN ↓ A^aZofaArapN , which is not allowable by rule, and made the pl. of this to be A^aZaAfiyru , (T, O, K, * [mentioned in the M as a pl. of AlZ~uforu ,]) though, if they formed a sing. from it, it should be ZuforN , (T, O, K,) signifies (tropical:) A certain odoriferous substance, (T, Mgh, O, K,) or a sort thereof, (M,) [i. e. unguis odoratus, (called in the present day Zuforu AlT~iybi and Zuforu AlEiforiyti ,) or ungues odorati, ] black, (T, M, O,) resembling a Zufor [or nail ] (T, M, Mgh, O, K) of a man (M) pulled out (in the M and O and K muqotulaf , and in the T muqal~af ,) from the root thereof, (T, M, O, K, [but in the M, the words which I have rendered “ pulled out ” &c. immediately follow the words DarobN mina AlEiTori A^asowadu ,]) or resembling the A^aZofaAr [or finger-nails ], (A,) and put into duxotap [or incense ]: (T, M, O:) and, accord. to the K, ↓ ZafaArN , sometimes imperfectly decl., i. e. ↓ ZafaAru , signifies the same; but this is very strange, for [SM says] I have referred to the M and T and O and other lexicons without finding them to have mentioned in this sense any term but AlA^aZofaAru or AlZ~uforu : accord. to the “ Minháj, ” A^aZofaAru AlT~iybi are pieces of an odoriferous substance resembling the A^aZofaAr [properly so called]; they are said by [the Arabic translator of] Dioscorides to be of the nature of the shards of shells, [so I render mino jinosi A^axozaAfi AlS~adafi , supposing AxzAf to be here used tropically,] found in an island of the Sea of India where is the sunobul [or spikenard ], a sort whereof is [ called ] qulozumiY~ [i. e. of El-Kulzum ], and another which is [ called ] baAbiliY~ [i. e. of Bábil ], black and small, and the best is that which inclines to whiteness, which drifts to El-Yemen and El-Bahreyn. (TA.) [Forskål, in his “ Descr. Animalium ” &c., mentions what here follows, among the animal substances of the materia medica of Cairo, in page 143: “ Unguis odoratus. (Opercula Cochl.) Dofr el afrît, Dfr AlEfryt i. e. unguis dæmonis. E Mochha per Sués. Arabes etiam afferunt. Nigritis fumigatorium est. ” ( Dfr is here written, agreeably with the usual vulgar pronunciation, for Zufor .) See also qusoTN ,] ― -b8- A^aZofaArN signifies also (assumed tropical:) Large qirodaAn [or ticks ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b9- And (assumed tropical:) The creased parts of a skin. (M, TA.) ― -b10- And the Zufor of a bow is (tropical:) The part in the curved end that is beyond the place where the string is tied, to the extremity: (As, T, S, M, * O, K: *) or the end of the bow: (K:) or each end of the bow, beyond the place where the string is tied: (A:) pl. ZifarapN . (M, TA.) ― -b11- See also ZafarapN .

definition: A pellicle that comes over the eye, (T, S, Mgh, O, K,) growing from the side next the nose, (T, S, O,) upon the white of the eye, (S, Mgh, O,) extending to the black: (S, O:) sometimes it is cut off:...
sourceDefinition: A pellicle that comes over the eye, (T, S, Mgh, O, K,) growing from the side next the nose, (T, S, O,) upon the white of the eye, (S, Mgh, O,) extending to the black: (S, O:) sometimes it is cut off: if left, it covers the eye, and obscures the sight: (T:) or a certain disease in the eye, which causes a tegument like the nail to come over it: or a piece of flesh that grows at the inner angle of the eye, extending to the black, and sometimes encroaching upon the black: (M:) it is also called ↓ ZuforN (A 'Obeyd, T, S, M, Mgh, O, K) and ↓ ZuforapN , (T, Mgh,) these two terms being applied to it by the physicians, (Mgh,) and ↓ ZafarN (TA) and ↓ ZifaArapN , (so in a copy of the T, as on the authority of Ibn-Buzurj,) or ↓ ZafaArapN . (So in the O.)

sourceDefinition: , said of a broken bone, (S, K,) or it is peculiarly said of the arm, (K, [i. e. one says Eavamati Alyadu ,]) aor. , (PS,) inf. n. EavomN , (TA,) It became set unevenly, (S, K, TA,) i. e. [ forming a node, or protuberance, like a swelling, not so hard as bone, (see EvomN , below,) or] so as to have an unevenness remaining in it: (TA:) or, said of a broken bone, it approached to a state of consolidation, but was not as yet consolidated; and in like manner, a wound: (ISh, TA:) or it was, or became, in a bad state, and wanting in its former strength, or in its form. (TA.) And Eavima , aor. , inf. n. EavamN , said of a [broken] bone, signifies [the same, or] It was badly set, so that there remained in it an unevenness. (TA.) definition: , (Mgh, K,) first pers.
sourceDefinition: , (Mgh, K,) first pers. Eadawotuhu , (Msb,) aor. yaEoduw , (Mgh, Msb,) [inf. n. EadowN ,] He passed from it, (Mgh, Msb, K,) namely, a thing, or an affair, (K,) to another, (Mgh, Msb,) and left it; (K;) and EadaA Eanohu signifies the same; (K;) as also ↓ tEd~Ah ; (S, * K;) and in like manner one says, ↓ Ead~ayotuhu , inf. n. taEodiyapN ; (Msb;) [but I do not find this elsewhere, and think that correctly one should say, Eanohu ↓ Ead~ayotu ; agreeably with what here follows:] the saying Eano h`*aA ↓ Ead~i means Leave thou this, and turn from it to another; and is app. from the phrase ham~aka ↓ Ead~i A_ilaY gayorihi [ Turn thy anxiety to other than him, or it ]; the objective complement being altogether left out, so that the verb becomes as though it were intrans.; and there are many instances similar to this in the language: (Har p. 478:) one says, Ean~iY Alham~a ↓ Ead~ayotu I turned away from me anxiety: and [hence] you say to him who has pursued you, Ean~iY A_ilaY gayoriY ↓ Ead~i , meaning Turn thou the beast upon which thou art riding towards other than me: (TA:) and Eam~aA taraY ↓ Ead~i , meaning Turn thou thine eye from what thou seest. (S.) [See an ex. of the first of these verbs in the Ham p. 125.] One says also, EadaAhu AlA^amoru and ↓ tEd~Ahu The thing, or affair, passed from him. (TA. [See an ex. in the first paragraph of art. Edm .]) And the Arabs say, A_in~a Aljaraba layaEoduw , meaning Verily the mange, or scab, passes from him that has it to him that is near to him so that the latter becomes mangy, or scabby. (Msb.) And maA EadaA fulaAnN A^ano SanaEa [app. meaning Such a one did not leave, or, accord. to an explanation of the verb in a similar phrase in Har p. 333, did not delay, his doing such a thing]. (S.) Accord. to Er-Rághib, AlEadowu primarily signifies Transition; [whence what here precedes;] or the going, or passing, beyond, or the exceeding, a limit, or the usual limit: and incompatibility to coalesce. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] EadaAhu , aor. as above, [inf. n. EadowN ,] He went, or passed, beyond it; exceeded it; or transgressed it. (S, TA. *) So in the saying EadaA Taworahu [ He went, or passed, beyond his proper limit; exceeded it; or transgressed it ]: and in like manner, AlHaq~a ↓ tEd~Y and ↓ AEtdAhu signify He went, or passed, beyond, &c., what was true, or right; and so Eani AlHaq~i , and fawoqa AlHaq~i . (TA.) A^amaA EadaA mano badaA , a saying in which the vulgar erroneously omit the interrogative A^ , means Does not he transgress that which is right who begins by acting injuriously? (TA.) And it is said EadaA AlqaAriSu faHaraza (tropical:) What was biting to the tongue attained to an excessive degree, so that it became acid: meaning that the affair, or case, became distressing. (S in art. qrS .) ― -b3- And EadaA Ealayohi , inf. n. EadowN and EadaA='N (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and Euduw~N (S, Msb, K) and EudowaAnN (ISd, Msb, K) and EidowaAnN (ISd, K) and EudowaY ; (K;) and ↓ tEd~Y , and ↓ AEtdY ; (S, Msb, K;) He acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically, against him; (S, Msb, K;) and transgressed against him, or exceeded the proper limit against him: (S, Msb:) [and he acted aggressively against him; agreeably with an explanation of the inf. n. of the last of these verbs in what follows: (see an ex. in a verse cited voce riyHN :)] or he acted with excessive wrongfulness, &c., against him: (Mgh:) and ↓ AEdY signifies the same as the other verbs here mentioned; (K, TA;) whence (TA) one says, fiY manoTiqika ↓ A^aEodayota Thou hast deviated from that which is right in thy speech: (S, TA:) ↓ AlAiEotidaA='u is the exceeding what is right; and it is sometimes in the way of aggression; and sometimes in the way of requital; and instances of the usage of its verb in both of these manners occur in the Kur ii. 190: (Er-Rághib, TA:) the first and third of the inf. ns. of EadaA , mentioned above, occur in the Kur vi. 108 accord. to different readings: (S, TA:) and [it is said that] AlEudowaAnu signifies sheer, or unmixed, wrongful or unjust or injurious or tyrannical conduct: (S:) or, as some say, the worst of [ such conduct, i. e., of ] AlAiEotidaA=' , in strength, or deed, or state or condition. (TA.) ― -b4- And EadaA Ealayohi He acted corruptly towards him. (TA.) ― -b5- And EudiYa Ealayohi He had his property stolen, and was wronged. (TA.) And EadaA EalaY AlqumaA$i , inf. n. EadaA='N [said in the TA to be like saHaAbN , but in the CK EadFA ,] and EudowaAnN and EadawaAnN , (K, TA,) but in the M written with damm and fet-h [i. e. EudowaAn and EadowaAn ], (TA,) said of a thief, He stole the qmA$ [meaning goods, or utensils and furniture ]. (K, TA.) And EadaA fiY Zahorihi He stole what was behind him: (A in art. Zhr :) [or he acted wrongfully in respect of what was behind him: for] liS~N EaAdiY ZahorK is expl. by the words EadaA fiY ZahorK fasaraqahu [so that it app. means A thief who has acted wrongfully in respect of what was behind one, and stolen it ]. (O and K in that art.) ― -b6- And EadaA Ealayohi , (K, TA,) inf. n. EadowN , (TA,) signifies also He leaped upon him, or it. (K, TA.) ― -b7- And EadaA , (K,) or EadaA fiY ma$oyihi , (Msb,) aor. yaEoduw , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EadowN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and EadFA and Euduw~N and EadawaAnN and taEodaA='N , (K,) signifies A^aHoDara [i. e. He ran; or rose in his running ]; (S, * K, TA;) said of a man and of a horse: (TA:) or he went a pace nearly the same as that termed harowalapN , (Msb, TA,) not so quick, (TA,) or which is not so quick, (Msb,) as that termed jaroYN : (Msb, TA:) or he went a pace less quick than $ad~N and more so than ma$oYN : (TA in art. sEY :) or [ he went quickly, or swiftly; for] AlEadowu signifies Als~uroEapu : (Mgh:) [or rather he ran, whether gently or moderately or vehemently: that it often signifies he ran vehemently is shown by the prov. mino sulayokK ↓ A^aEodaY More vehement in running than Suleyk, who is said to have outstripped fleet horses; and by numerous exs.:] and ↓ E~Y signifies the same as EadaA , denoting a quick pace. (TA in art. hbS .) ― -b8- And [hence, perhaps,] EadaA AlmaA='u , aor. yaEoduw , (assumed tropical:) The water ran. (TA.) -A2- EadaAhu Eani AlA^amori , (S, K,) inf. n. EadowN and EudowaAnN ; as also ↓ Ed~Ahu ; (K;) signifies He, or it, diverted him; or turned him away, or back; (S, K;) and occupied him so as to divert him; (K;) from the thing, or affair. (S, K.) You say, Eadato EawaAdK . (S, TA. See EaAdiyapN , voce EudawaA='u : and see also the last sentence of the first paragraph of art. Ewd .) ― -b2- EadaAniY minohu $ar~N means balaganiY [i. e., app., Evil, or mischief, reached me from him, or it ]. (TA. [See a signi- fication of 4.]) -A3- Eadiytu lahu signifies I hated him, or it. (ISd, K.) -A4- EadaA is also a verb by which one makes an exception, with maA [preceding it] and without maA : (S, K:) you say, jaA='aniY Alqawomu maA EadaA zayodFA [ The people, or party, came to me, except Zeyd ]; and jaAw^uwniY EadaA zayodFA [which means the like]; putting what follows it in the accus. case; the agent being implied in it: (S: [see this expl. in what has been said of xalaA as used in the same manner:]) accord. to MF, it is a verb when what follows it is put in the accus. case; and when what follows it is put in the gen. case, it is a particle, by common consent: (TA: [and the like is said in the Mughnee; i. e., that it is similar to xalaA in respect of the explanations there given of the different usages of this latter; but that Sb did not know it to have been used otherwise than as having the quality of a verb:]) one says, raA^ayotuhumo EadaA A^axaAka and maA EadaAhu , meaning maA xalaA [i. e. I saw them, except thy brother ]: and sometimes it governs the gen. case without mA : thus in the M: Az says, [as though regarding it as only a particle,] when you suppress [ mA ], you make it to govern the accus. case as meaning A_il~aA and you make it to govern the gen. case as meaning siwaY . (TA.

(TA.) (TA.) And EaAdi rijolaka Eani AlA^aroDi Draw away thy leg, or foot, from the ground. (TA.) (ISh, TA in art. glq .) ― -b3- EAdY $aEarahu He took [ somewhat ] from his hair: or he raised it, (K, TA,) in washing it: or he neglected it, and did not oil it, or anoint it: or he subjected it time after time to the purification termed wuDuwE , and to washing. (TA.) ― -b4- EAdY AlwisaAdapa He folded the pillow. (TA.) ― -b5- EAdY Alqidora He lowered one of the three stones upon which the cooking-pot rested, in order that it (the pot) might incline upon the fire. (TA.) ― -b6- EAdY bayona AlS~ayodayni , (S, * K,) inf. n. EidaA='N (S, K) and muEaAdaApN , (K,) He made a succession, of one to the other, between the two animals of the chase, (S, K,) by throwing down one of them immediately after the other, (S,) in one Talaq [or heat ]. (S, K.) Imra-el-Keys says, [describing a horse,] faEaAdaY EidaA='F bayona vaworK wanaEojapK diraAkFA walamo yanoDaHo bimaA='K fayugosali [ And he made a succession, of one to the other, between a wild bull and a wild cow, by running down one after the other in a single heat, overtaking uninterruptedly, and not breaking out with water (i. e. sweat ) so as to become suffused therewith]. (S. [See EM p. 49.]) In like manner also AlmuEaAdaApu bayona rajulayoni means The piercing, or thrusting, two men, one after the other, uninterruptedly. (TA.) ― -b7- And EaAdayotuhu [sometimes] signifies I vied, or contended, with him in running; i. q. HaADarotuhu , from AlHuDoru . (A in art. HDr .)

definition: He passed from, or beyond, another, to the thing, or affair: so in the K.
sourceDefinition: He passed from, or beyond, another, to the thing, or affair: so in the K. (TA.) But in the M it is said, AEdAhu Ald~aA='u signifies The disease passed from another to him. (TA.) And one says A^aEodaY fulaAnN fulaAnFA mino xuluqihi , or mino Eil~apK bihi , or jarabK , (S, TA,) i. e. Such a one made somewhat of his natural disposition, or of a disease, or malady, that was in him, or of mange, or scab, to pass [ from him ] to such a one; [or infected him therewith; (see two exs., in a verse and a hemistich, cited in the first paragraph of art. jnY ;)] and AEdAhu bihi signifies the same: and AEdY SaAHibahu He made his companion to acquire the like of what was in him. (TA.) And yuEodiY is said of the mange, or scab, &c., meaning It passes from him that has it to another; (S, K;) and in like manner one says of a disease, ↓ ytEd~Y : (Nh, TA:) but it is said in an explanation of a trad., laA yuEodiY $aYo'N $ayoy^FA [i. e. A thing (meaning disease) does not pass by its own agency to a thing ]. (S, TA.) [Therefore] one says, of the mange, or scab, [or the like,] AEdAhu A@ll~`hu God made it to pass from him that had it to one that was near to him, so that he became affected therewith. (Msb.) ― -b2- One says also, of a man, qado A^aEodaY Aln~aAsa bi$ar~K He has made evil, or mischief, to cleave to men. (TA.) -A2- See also 1, near the middle, in two places. -A3- AEdAhu Ealayohi He aided, or assisted, him, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and strengthened him, (K,) against him; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and avenged him of him; (S, Msb;) namely, one who had wronged him. (S, Mgh, Msb.) And AEdAhu He (a judge) heard his accusation against another, and commanded to bring his adversary. (Mgh.) -A4- AEdAhu , (S, Msb, K, TA,) namely, a horse, (S, TA,) and also a man, (TA,) [ He made him to run, whether gently or moderately or vehemently: or, as sometimes used,] he made him, (K, TA,) or desired him, (S,) to go the pace termed HuDor : (S, K, TA:) or he made him to go a pace nearly the same as that termed harowalap , (Msb, TA,) not so quick, (TA,) or which is not so quick, (Msb,) as that termed jaroY : (Msb, TA: [see 1, latter half:]) and ↓ AstEdAhu signifies the same. (S.)

definition: The people, or party, became affected, [or infected, ] or smitten, (S, TA,) one with the disease of another, or one with the like of the disease of another: (S:) or died, one after another, (S, TA,) in one month, and in one year.
sourceDefinition: The people, or party, became affected, [or infected, ] or smitten, (S, TA,) one with the disease of another, or one with the like of the disease of another: (S:) or died, one after another, (S, TA,) in one month, and in one year. (TA.) And tEAdt AlA_ibilu The camels died in great numbers. (TA.) ― -b2- And tEAdY Alqawomu EalaY~a binaSorihimo The people, or party, came upon me consecutively with their aid, or assistance. (TA.) ― -b3- One says also, tEAdY Alqawomu (S, K) from AlEadaAwapu (S) meaning The people, or party, treated, or regarded, one another with enmity, or hostility. (K.) ― -b4- And tEAdY maA bayonahumo (S, K) The case, or affair, that was between them became in a bad, or corrupt, state, (S,) or complicated, intricate, or confused, so as to be a subject of disagreement, or difference, between them. (K.) ― -b5- And tEAdY AlmakaAnu The place was, or became, dissimilar in its several parts; and uneven. (TA.) And [hence] one says, biEunuqiY wajaEN mino taEaAdiY AlwisaAdi mina AlmakaAni AlmutaEaAdiY i. e. [ In my neck is a pain from the unevenness of the pillow from ] the uneven place. You say, AstEdAhu He asked, or demanded, of him (i. e. the prince, or governor, or commander, S, Mgh, Msb) aid, or assistance, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) Ealayohi against him, (S, Mgh, Msb,) namely, one who wronged him: (Mgh, Msb:) [or,] accord. to El-Khuwárezmee (who derives it from AlEadiY~u signifying Alr~aj~aAlapu Al~a*iyna yaEoduwna ), AstEdY [or AstEdY AlqaADiYa ] means he asked, or demanded, of the judge, that he should make his foot-messengers to run in quest of his antagonist and to bring him, for the purpose of exacting from him his right, or due. (De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., iii. 100. [And an explanation similar to this, but not a similar derivation, is indicated in the Mgh by an explanation of A^aEodaAhu , q. v.]) ― -b2- See also 4, last sentence.

EudowapN as signifying “ Atrium, impluvium domus: ” but this the former has app. done from his having found Edwp erroneously written for Ea*irap .] -A2- EudowapN signifies also The kind of plants, or herbage, termed xul~ap ; i. e., in which is sweetness. (TA.)

definition: Mange, or scab, or other disease, that passes, or is transitive, from one to another;
sourceDefinition: Mange, or scab, or other disease, that passes, or is transitive, from one to another; (S, K, TA;) a transitive disease; and such is said to be the jarab , and the baraS , and the ramad , and the HaSobap , and the ju*aAm , and the wabaA=' , and the judariY~ . (Kull p. 259.) You say, laA tuqar~ibohu minohu faA_in~a bihi EadowaY Do not thou bring him near to him, for in him is a disease such as the mange, or scab, that is transitive from one to another. (TK.) ― -b2- And The transition of the mange, or scab, or other disease, from him that has it to another: (S, K, TA, TK:) the subst. from yaEoduw said of the mange, or scab, expl. above, as meaning “ it passes ” &c. (Msb. [See 1, first quarter.]) It is said in a trad., laA EadowaY , i. e. laA yuEodiY $aYo'N $ayoy^FA [ A thing (meaning disease) does not pass by its own agency to a thing ]; (S;) or [lit.] there is no transition of the mange, or scab, or other disease, from him that has it to another. (TK.) ― -b3- And i. q. fasaAdN [i. e. Badness, corruptness, unsoundness, &c.]. (K, TA. [In the CK erroneously written in this sense Eudow`Y ; which, however, being an inf. n. of EadaA in the phrase EadaA Ealayohi , q. v., may be correctly used as having the same, or nearly the same, meaning.]) So in the saying, bihi EadowaY [ In him, or it, is badness, &c.]. (TK.) -A2- Also A demand that one makes upon a prefect, or governor, [or judge, ] to aid, or assist, him against him who has wronged him, i. e. to inflict penal retribution on him, (IF, S, Msb,) for his wrongdoing to him. (IF, Msb.) ― -b2- And Aid, or assistance, against a wrongdoer, (S, Mgh, TA,) required of a judge, for the bringing into his presence the antagonist: and also applied to a signet, or a [ sealed ] piece of clay, given by the judge as a token to denote the summoning of him whose presence is required. (Mgh.)

definition: (S, K) and ↓ EaAdiyapN and ↓ EadaA='N (K) Distance, or remoteness, (S, K, TA,) as also ↓ EidFY , (Ham p.
sourceDefinition: (S, K) and ↓ EaAdiyapN and ↓ EadaA='N (K) Distance, or remoteness, (S, K, TA,) as also ↓ EidFY , (Ham p. 377,) [or particularly] of a house, or an abode, or a dwelling. (S, TA.) [Hence,] one says, TaAlato EudawaAw^uhumo Their distance, or remoteness, one from another, and their separation, was, or became, long. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (i. e. the first and ↓ second and ↓ third words) Occupation, or business, that turns one away, or back, from a thing: (K, TA:) or EudawaA='u signifies a custom, or habit, of occupation or business: (TA:) and EudawaA='u Al$~ugoli , the hindrances, or impediments, of occupation or business: (S, TA:) and one says, jiy^otaniY waA^anaA fiY EudawaA='a Eanoka i. e. [ Thou camest to me when I was engaged ] in an occupation that diverted [me from thee ]: (so in one of my copies of the S:) the pl. of ↓ EaAdiyapN is EawaAdK : (TA:) EawaAdiY Ald~ahori means the accidents, or casualties, of time or fortune, that divert [or intervene as obstacles ] by occupying or busying: (S:) and you say, EawaAdi ↓ Eadato , [lit.] meaning Things, or events, turning away, or back, turned, or have turned, away, or back; [but this phrase, when followed by duwna or bayona , I would rather render, simply, obstacles occurred, or have occurred; ] (S, TA;) thus in the latter of two verses cited voce Hab~a . (S.) ― -b3- EudawaA='u Ald~ahori means The shifting, and varying, of time or fortune. (TA.) ― -b4- And EudawaA='u Al$~awoqi What has severely affected, distressed, or afflicted, its sufferer, of the yearning, or longing, of the soul, or of longing desire. (TA.) ― -b5- And EudawaA='u signifies also A marokab [i. e. beast, or saddle, or thing on which one rides, ] that is not easy: (K:) or, accord. to As, a place where he who sits thereon is not in a state of ease: and one says, jiy^otu EalaY marokabK *iY EudawaA='a i. e. [ I came upon a beast, or saddle, &c.,] that was not easy: (S:) and jiy^otuka EalaY farasK *iY EudawaA='a , the last word imperfectly decl., i. e. [ I came to thee upon a horse ] that was not easy: (TA:) and jalasa EalaY EudawaA='a He sat upon an uneven thing or place; (M, TA;) the last word imperfectly decl., as is said by ISd. sourceDefinition: The herbage of the Sayof [q. v., here app. meaning spring ], after the departure of the rabiyE [q. v., here app. meaning winter ]: (S, K:) it is applied to the young trees which then become green and are depastured by the camels: (S:) or, as some say, the [ plants, or herbage, called ] rabol [q. v.]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The young ones of sheep or goats. (K.) ― -b3- And Female infants [ of the age ] of forty days; (K, TA; [in the CK, nabAt is erroneously put for banaAt ;]) but when their [ hair termed ] Eaqiyqap has been cut off, this appel-lation is no longer applied to them: so says Lth; but Az pronounces him to have erred: (TA:) or it is with g (K, TA) and * , both dotted, or only the former of them dotted, and one of them is called gadiY~N [or gadawiY~N , or ga*iY~N or ga*awiY~N ]: thus in the M, and thus accord. to Az. (TA.)

definition: And enemy, contr.
sourceDefinition: And enemy, contr. of waliY~N , (S,) or of SadiyqN , (K,) or of SadiyqN muwaAlK ; (Msb;) an epithet, but resembling a subst.: (S:) [and (like our word “ enemy ” in military parlance) a hostile party: for] it is used alike as sing. and pl. and masc. and fem.; (Msb, K;) as is said in the “ Muk- tasar el-' Eyn: ” (Msb:) but sometimes it is dualized and pluralized and feminized: (K:) the pl. is A^aEodaA='N ; (S, Msb, K;) and the pl. of A^aEodaA='N is A^aEaAdK ; (Msb, K; *) and EidFY and EudFY are also pls. of Eaduw~N ; (S, Msb, K; [each improperly termed in the K Aisomu jamoEK ; for fiEalN and fuEalN are measures of pls., not of quasi-pl. ns.;]) the former said by ISk to be the only pl. of this measure among epithets; (S, Msb; *) and EudaApN , with damm and with p , is another pl.; (Th, S, Msb;) and is pl. of ↓ EaAdK , (K, TA,) which is syn. with Eaduw~N ; (S, K, TA;) as in the saying of a woman of the Arabs, A^a$omata rab~u AlEaAlamiyna EaAdiyaka [ May the Lord of the beings of the universe make thy enemy to rejoice at thy affliction ]: (S, TA:) the fem. form of Eaduw~N is Eaduw~apN , (S, Msb,) which is said by Az to be used when the meaning of an epithet is intended: (Msb:) it is said by ISk, (S, TA,) and in the “ Bari', ” (Msb,) that there is no instance of the measure faEuwlN in the sense of faAEilN but its fem. is without p , except Eaduw~apN , (S, Msb, K,) in the phrase h`*ihi Eaduw~apN A@ll~`hi [ This woman is the enemy of God ]: accord. to Fr, Eaduw~apN has the affix p to assimilate it to SadiyqapN ; for a word is sometimes formed to accord with its contr.: (S, TA:) AZ says that he heard certain of the tribe of 'Okeyl say, [of some women,] hun~a waliy~aAtu A@ll~`hi and Eaduw~aAtu A@ll~`hi and A^FwoliyaAw^uhu and A^aEodaAw^uhu [i. e. They are the friends of God and the enemies of God ]. (Msb.) [The pl.] EidFY signifies also Persons distant, or remote, one from another: (ISd, K, TA:) and (K) strangers, or foreigners: (ISk, S, K, TA:) and such as are distant, or remote, in respect of relationship; or not relations: (TA:) as well as enemies: (M, TA:) kaAlA^aEodaA='i , which is added in the K after waAlgurabaA='u , should be waAlA^aEodaA='u . (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA.)

definition: A palm-branch from which the leaves have been removed: (T, Msb, TA:) or a straight and slender palm-branch from which the leaves have been stripped off: and one upon which leaves have not grown: (K:)...
sourceDefinition: A palm-branch from which the leaves have been removed: (T, Msb, TA:) or a straight and slender palm-branch from which the leaves have been stripped off: and one upon which leaves have not grown: (K:) or the part, of a palmbranch, a little above the karab [or lower, thick, and broad, portions, ] upon which no leaves have grown; that [or those parts] upon which leaves have grown being termed saEafN : (S, O:) pl. [of mult.] EusubN , (O, Msb, TA,) with two dammehs, (TA,) and EusobaAnN (Msb, TA) and EisobaAnN and EusuwbN and [of pauc.] A^aEosibapN . (TA.) It is said of the Prophet, in a trad., qubiDa waAlquroA=nu fiY AlEusubi waAlquDumi waAlkaraAniyfi [ He was taken, i. e. he died, while the Kur-án was written only upon leafless palm-branches, and skins, or white skins, and stumps of palm-branches ]. (O, TA.*) ― -b2- Also The bone of the tail; and so ↓ EasiybapN : (K:) or the slender part thereof: (TA:) or the part where grows the hair thereof, (K, TA,) i. e. of the tail: (TA:) or Easiybu Al*~anabi signifies the part, of the skin and bone of the tail, where the hair grows. (S, O, TA.) ― -b3- And The outer [here meaning upper ] part of the human foot: and likewise [i. e. the shorter side, or app., accord. to some, the shaft (see ZahorN as used in relation to a feather),] of a feather, lengthwise. (K.) ― -b4- And A cleft, or fissure, in a mountain; as also ↓ EasobapN . (K.)

definition: The king of the bees: (S, O, K: *) the male bee.
sourceDefinition: The king of the bees: (S, O, K: *) the male bee. (A, O, * K.) ― -b2- And hence, (S, O,) (tropical:) The lord, or chief, of his people: (S, A, O:) or a great chief; as also ↓ EasuwbN ; (K;) or this signifies [simply] a lord, or chief, like yaEosuwbN : (O:) pl. yaEaAsiybu . (TA.) It is said in a trad. of 'Alee, When such and such things shall happen (mentioning factions, or seditions), Daraba yaEosuwbu Ald~iyni bi*anabihi ; (A, O, TA;) in which, accord. to As, yEswb Aldyn means the chief of men in respect of religion at that time; (TA;) or it means the leader of the religion: (T and TA in art. Drb :) and it is said that Drb b*nbh here means shall quit the faction, or sedition, and its party, with his partisans in religion; by *nbh being meant his followers; and by Drb , shall go away through the land, journeying, or warring in the cause of the religion: or , as Z says, Drb b*nbh means (tropical:) shall remain, and be firm, together with his religious followers; and accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, the same is said of the locust, when it lays its eggs, thrusting its tail into the ground; and the meaning here is, (assumed tropical:) shall remain firm until the people shall return to him, and the religion become manifest, and spread abroad. (TA. [See also Daraba and *anabN .]) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) Gold; so called because it is that by means of which an affair is managed, or ordered: and [in a larger sense] a thing to which one has recourse for protection or the like; as in a saying of 'Alee, in which wealth is termed the yEswb of the unbelievers or of the hypocrites. (TA.) ― -b4- And A certain flying thing, smaller than the locust; (As, A'Obeyd, K;) or larger; (K;) and having a long tail: (TA:) or a certain flying thing, longer than the locust, that does not contract its wings when it alights; to which a horse is likened for the slenderness of its body: (S, O:) or a kind of moth, or the like, ( faraA$apN ,) of a greenish colour, that flies in the [ season called ] rabiyE . (IAth, TA.) [Golius explains it as “ Insectum oblongum, quaternis pennis volucre, mordella Gazæ, seu orsodacna Aristot. ” ] ― -b5- And A species of Hajal [or partridge ]. (O, K, TA.) ― -b6- And A blaze, or white mark, on a horse's face, (K, TA,) of a long shape, terminating before it extends as far as the upper parts of the nostrils; or extending upwards along the bone of the nose, wide and straight, until it reaches the lower part of the even portion of the forehead, whether it be little or much, if it do not reach as far as the eyes: (TA:) or a white line, or stripe, of the blaze, extending downwards until it touches the fore part of the nose and mouth. (En-Nadr, A'Obeyd, Az, O.) ― -b7- And (accord. to Lth, O) A daAy^irap [or what we term a feather ] in the part of the flank of a horse where the rider strikes it with his foot: (O, K, TA:) but Az says that this is a mistake, and that the correct meaning is that given above on the authority of A'Obeyd. (TA.) ― -b8- The Y in yaEosuwbN is augmentative; because there is no Arabic word of the measure faEoluwlN except SaEofuwqN . (S, O.)

definition: [a coll. gen. n.], n. un. with p ; (TA;) Fresh, green, juicy, soft, or tender, herbs or herbage, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) in the first part of the [ season called ] rabiyE [i. e. rabiyEu AlkalaA^a , which...
sourceDefinition: [a coll. gen. n.], n. un. with p ; (TA;) Fresh, green, juicy, soft, or tender, herbs or herbage, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) in the first part of the [ season called ] rabiyE [i. e. rabiyEu AlkalaA^a , which begins in January and ends in March, O. S.]: (Msb:) not termed Ha$iy$N until drying up: (S, O:) or, in the opinion of the generality of the lexicologists, Eu$obN is applied to such as is fresh and to such as is dry: (ISd, TA voce Ha$iy$N :) or the first, or earliest, of herbage, ( saraEaAnu AlkalaA^i ,) in the rabiyE , that [ afterwards ] dries up, and does not remain; the term kalaA^N being applied by the Arabs to Eu$ob and to other kinds: and Eu$obN is applied to fresh, green, juicy, soft, or tender, herbs or leguminous plants, of the desert, that come forth in the rabiyE : and under this term are included those that are hard and thick, which are termed the *ukuwr thereof; as well as to those that are slender and soft, which are termed the A^aHoraAr thereof: or, accord. to AHn, whatever is destroyed by winter, and grows again from the stocks, or roots, thereof, or the seed: he says also that it is applied to such [ herbage ] as is uninterrupted; as opposed to taEaA$iybu : or, accord. to Th, it is applied to the mature; as so opposed. (TA.) ― -b2- Eu$obapu Ald~aAri [ The green herb of the dwelling ] means that which grows in the dimonap [or patch of ground which people have blackened by their cooking and where their cattle have staled and dunged ] of the dwelling, surrounded by fresh, or green, herbs, in a white [or clean ] part of the ground, and good soil: and hence, (tropical:) The hajiynap [or woman whose father is a free man, or an Arab, and her mother a slave ]; an appellation like xaDoraA='u AlwaDari [app. lit. meaning “ The green herb that grows in the place where the water with which skins have been washed, or the like, is poured out: ” but IbrD thinks that it may be a mistranscription for xaDoraA='u Ald~imani ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [ Eu$obu Al*~iy^obi is Eyptian toad-flax; antirrhinum Aegyptiacum; the name of which is written by Forskål (Flora Aegypt. Arab., pp. lxviii. and 112,) E$b Aldyb and Asjib ed dîb and Aeschib ed dîb. ]

definition: signifies The act of dividing [a thing] into parts, or portions: and the act of distributing: as also ↓ EaDowN [in both of these senses].
sourceDefinition: signifies The act of dividing [a thing] into parts, or portions: and the act of distributing: as also ↓ EaDowN [in both of these senses]. (K, TA.) You say, EaD~ayotu Al$~aApa , (S,) or Al*~abiyHapa , (Msb,) inf. n. taEoDiyapN , (S,) I divided the sheep, or goat, (S,) or the slaughtered animal, (Msb,) into A^aEoDaA=' [i. e. limbs, or members, &c.; I limbed it, or dismembered it ]: (S, Msb:) and Al$~aApa ↓ EaDaA , aor. yaEoDuwhaA , inf. n. EaDowN , he divided the sheep, or goat, into parts, or portions. (TK.) And EaD~ayotu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. as above, I distributed the thing: (S:) and ↓ EaDaAhu , aor. yaEoDuwhu , inf. n. EaDowN , he distributed it. (TA.) It is said in a trad., laA taEoDiyapa fiY miyraAvK A_il~aA fiymaA A@Hotamala Alqasoma [ There shall be no distributing in an inheritance, except in the case of that which is susceptible of division ]; i. e., what is not susceptible of division, such as the bead of precious stone, and the like, shall not be distributed, even though one or more of the inheritors demand its division, because therein would be injury to them or to one or more of them; but it shall be sold, and its price shall be divided among them. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) of which EaZolamN is a dial. var., (MF, TA,) The expressed juice of a species of tree or plant, (Az, K, TA,) the colour of which is like niyl [or indigo ], green ( A^axoDar ) inclining to duskiness: (Az, TA:) or a certain plant, (S, K,) or thing, (Msb,) with which one dyes, (S, Msb, K,) said to be (Msb) called in Pers. niyl [i. e. the indigo-plant ]: (Msb, and so in some copies of the S; other copies of which, for nyl , have tfl :) or i. q. wasomapN [ an appellation now applied to woad; as is also EiZolim ]: (S, Msb, K:) AHn says, one of the Arabs of the desert told me that the EZlm is the male wasomap : he also says that it is a small tree or plant, ( $ujayorapN ), of the [ class called ] rib~ap , that grows in a late season, and the greenness of which is lasting: and in one place he says, an Arab of the desert, of the Saráh ( Als~araAp ), told me that the EiZolimap [which is the n. un.] is a tree or plant ( $ajarapN ) that rises upon a stem about a cubit [ in height ] and has branches at the extremities of which are what resemble the blossoms of the kuzobarap [or coriander ], and it (the tree or plant) is dustcoloured: (TA:) some say that it is the biq~am [or Brazil-wood ]: (Msb:) MF says, it is the xaTomiY~ [or marsh-mallow ]: (TA:) thus says El-Hareeree; but El-'Okbaree says that it is not that: (Har p. 625:) and some say that it is a certain red dye. [ A white, or fair, female, ] whose whiteness [or brightness ] EZlm will not blacken [or darken ]: applied to that which is notable, which nothing will conceal. sourceDefinition: [The scorpion; ] a certain venomous reptile, (TA,) well known: (K, TA:) the word is masc. (TA) and it is fem., (S, O, K, TA,) generally the latter; (T, Msb, TA;) but is applied to the male and the female: (Lth, T, O, Msb, TA:) and the male is called ↓ EuqorubaAnN , (T, S, O, Msb, K, TA,) accord. to some, (O,) when one desires to denote it in a corroborative manner, (Msb, TA,) and ↓ Euqorub~aAnN also; (K;) or these two words are syn. with EaqorabN : (K:) and the female is called ↓ EaqorabapN , (T, S, O, Msb, K,) sometimes, (T, Msb,) and ↓ EaqorabaA='u , which is imperfectly decl.; (S, O, K;) or these two words and EaqorabN , accord. to the “ Tahreer et-Tembeeh, ” all denote the female, and the male is called ↓ EuqorubaAnN : (TA:) or, as some say, the male and the female are called only EaqorabN : (Msb, TA:) and of ↓ EuqorubaAnN it is said by IB, on the authority of AHát, that it does not signify the male of EaqaArib , but [as expl. below] “ a certain creeping thing, having long legs: ” (TA:) IJ says that you may drop the A and n , and say ↓ Euqorur~aAn : (L, TA:) and an instance occurs of ↓ EaqoraAbN , as a coll. gen. n., in the following verse: A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi mina AlEaqoraAbi Aal$~aAy^ilaAti Euqada AlA^a*onaAbi [ I seek protection by God from the scorpions raising the joints of the tails ]: but the A here is said to be inserted for the purpose of what is termed AlA_i$obaAE : (MF, from the “ Mukhtasar el-Bayán: ”) and Al$Ay^lAt is applied as an epithet to a sing. n. because this is used as a coll. gen. n.: (M voce sabosabN :) the pl. of EaqorabN is EaqaAribu . (S, O.) ― -b2- And [hence] AlEaqorabu is the name of (assumed tropical:) A certain sign of the Zodiac, (T, S, O, K,) [i. e. Scorpio, ] to which belong the Mansions of the Moon called Al$~awolapu and Alqalobu [and AlA_ikoliylu ] and Alz~ubaAnayaAni . (T, TA. [See these words, and see also $iybaAnu , and manaAzilu Alqamari in art. nzl . It should also be observed that the Arabs extended the figure of this constellation (as they did that of Leo) far beyond the limits that we assign to it.]) ― -b3- [Hence, likewise,] EaqorabN signifies (assumed tropical:) A thong, or strap, of a sandal, (O, K, TA,) in the form of the reptile of this name. (TA.) [See also Eaqorabap .] ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A thong, or strap, (O, K,) plaited, and having a buckle at its extremity, (O,) by which the crupper of a horse, or the like, is bound to the saddle. (O, K.) ― -b5- And the pl. EaqaAribu signifies also (tropical:) Malicious and mischievous misrepresentations, calumnies, or slanders. (O, K, TA.) One says, A_in~ahu latadib~u EaqaAribuhu (tropical:) Verily his malicious and mischievous misrepresentations, &c., creep along: (TA:) or he traduces, or defames, people behind their backs, or otherwise. (O, K.) And the phrase dab~ato EaqaAribuhu is sometimes used to signify (tropical:) His downy hair crept [along his cheeks]. (MF.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Reproaches for benefits conferred: so in the saying of En-Nábighah, EalaY~a liEamorKw niEomapN baEoda niEomapK liwaAlidihi layosato bi*aAti EaqaAribi (tropical:) [ I owe unto 'Amr favour after favour, for his father, not accompanied by reproaches for benefits conferred ]. (TA.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) Hardships, severities, difficulties, troubles, or distresses. (K.) EaqaAribu Al$~itaA='i means (assumed tropical:) The hardships, severities, &c., of winter: (TA:) or the intense cold thereof: (O, K:) and Eaqorabu Al$~itaA='i , accord. to IB, the assault, and intense cold, of winter. (TA.) And Eayo$N *uw EaqaAriba means (assumed tropical:) An uneasy life: or a life in which is evil and roughness. (TA.) ― -b8- See also the next paragraph.

Scorpio, ] to which belong the Mansions of the Moon called Al$~awolapu and Alqalobu [and AlA_ikoliylu ] and Alz~ubaAnayaAni . (T, TA. [See these words, and see also $iybaAnu , and manaAzilu Alqamari in art. nzl . It should also be observed that the Arabs extended the figure of this constellation (as they did that of Leo) far beyond the limits that we assign to it.]) ― -b3- [Hence, likewise,] EaqorabN signifies (assumed tropical:) A thong, or strap, of a sandal, (O, K, TA,) in the form of the reptile of this name. (TA.) [See also Eaqorabap .] ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A thong, or strap, (O, K,) plaited, and having a buckle at its extremity, (O,) by which the crupper of a horse, or the like, is bound to the saddle. (O, K.) ― -b5- And the pl. EaqaAribu signifies also (tropical:) Malicious and mischievous misrepresentations, calumnies, or slanders. (O, K, TA.) One says, A_in~ahu latadib~u EaqaAribuhu (tropical:) Verily his malicious and mischievous misrepresentations, &c., creep along: (TA:) or he traduces, or defames, people behind their backs, or otherwise. (O, K.) And the phrase dab~ato EaqaAribuhu is sometimes used to signify (tropical:) His downy hair crept [along his cheeks]. (MF.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Reproaches for benefits conferred: so in the saying of En-Nábighah, EalaY~a liEamorKw niEomapN baEoda niEomapK liwaAlidihi layosato bi*aAti EaqaAribi (tropical:) [ I owe unto 'Amr favour after favour, for his father, not accompanied by reproaches for benefits conferred ]. (TA.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) Hardships, severities, difficulties, troubles, or distresses. (K.) EaqaAribu Al$~itaA='i means (assumed tropical:) The hardships, severities, &c., of winter: (TA:) or the intense cold thereof: (O, K:) and Eaqorabu Al$~itaA='i , accord. to IB, the assault, and intense cold, of winter. (TA.) And Eayo$N *uw EaqaAriba means (assumed tropical:) An uneasy life: or a life in which is evil and roughness. (TA.) ― -b8- See also the next paragraph.

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EakomN , (TA,) He bound [or tied up ] the goods, (S, K,) with a string, (S,) or rope, (TA,) in a garment, or piece of cloth, (K, * TA,) [ so as to form a bundle, or the like, ] by spreading the garment, or piece of cloth, and putting the goods in it, and binding it: the goods thus bound being then called ↓ EikomN . (TA.) ― -b2- And Eakama AlbaEiyra He bound, upon the camel, [or, app., upon each side of the camel, ] the Eikom . (S.) ― -b3- And Eakamotu Alr~ajula AlEikoma I bound, for the man, the Eikom . (S.) See also 4. ― -b4- Eakama AlbaEiyra , inf. n. EakomN , signifies also [ He muzzled the camel; ] he bound the mouth of the camel. (TA. [In this sense it is probably formed by transposition from kaEama ; for the latter is better known.]) -A2- Eakamahu Eano ziyaAratihi , inf. n. EakomN , He turned him away, or back, from visiting him. (TA.) And Eukima Ean~aA , (S,) or Eanohu , (K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) He was turned away, or back, from visiting us, or him. (S, K.) -A3- Eakama liA^aroDi ka*aA , (K, [thus in my MS. copy, in the CK AlArDa k*A ,]) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He repaired, or betook himself, [as though properly meaning he bound his goods upon his camel or camels, for the purpose of repairing, ] to such a land. (K.) ― -b2- And Eakama , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, TA,) He expected, or waited. (S, K.) ― -b3- And He returned, or turned back, syn. kar~a , (S, K, TA,) Ealayohi [ against him ], (K, TA,) after fleeing. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And maA Eakama Eano $atomihi He did not hold back from reviling him. (K, * TA.) -A4- Eakamati AlA_ibilu : see what next follows.

definition: A burden that is borne on one side of a camel or other beast, made equiponderant to another burden;
sourceDefinition: A burden that is borne on one side of a camel or other beast, made equiponderant to another burden; syn. EidolN ; (S, Mgh, K;) i. e. one of two such burdens: (S:) so called as long as containing goods: two such burdens are bound upon the two sides of the [women's camel-vehicle called] hawodaj : or, accord. to A'Obeyd, a burden, and a burden such as is described above, containing receptables of various sorts of food, and goods: (TA:) pl. A^aEokaAmN ; (Az, M, K;) accord. to the M, the only pl.; but accord. to Az, EukuwmN also. (TA.) kaEikomaYi AlEayori [ Like the two equiponderant burdens of the ass ] is a prov. applied to two men who are equals in eminence or nobility. (TA.) And one says, waqaEa AlmuSoTariEaAni EikomaYo EayorK , and kaEikomaYo EayorK , meaning The two [ men wrestling ] fell together, neither of them having thrown down the other. (TA. [See also EidolN , last sentence.]) ― -b2- Also A bundle ( kaArap , K, TA) of clothes [&c., put in one piece of cloth and tied up ]: (TA:) pl. EukuwmN . (K.) [See also EakomN .]) ― -b4- See also EikaAmN . ― -b5- Also The bakorap [i. e. pulley, or sheave of the pulley, ] of a well. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (T, K,) inf. n. EamotN ; (T, S, O;) and ↓ Em~t , (O, K,) inf. n. taEomiytN ; (O;) He wound wool (S, O, * K) in an oblong form, (TA,) or in a round form, (S, O, K,) like a ring, (TA,) for the purpose of its being put in the hand and spun (S, O, K) with the spindle: (TA:) or he wound soft hair of the camel, and wool, into the form of a ring, and spun it, putting it in his hand: (T, TA:) the operation termed EamotN is performed after beating, and separating and loosening, the wool, and collecting it together, in order to wind it upon the hand, and spin it with the spindle. (AHeyth, TA.) An ex. of the former verb occurs in a verse cited voce raAjilapN . (TA.) ― -b2- And the former verb signifies also He twisted a rope of [the species of trefoil, or clover, called] qat~ . (TA.) ― -b3- And it is said in the K that Eamata fulaAnFA means He overcame, or subdued, such a one, and made him to refrain, or restrained him; expl. by qaharahu wakaf~ahu : but [SM says that] the correct reading is probably walaf~ahu ; for in the L [and in the O, app. on the authority of Az, to whom the same is ascribed in the TA in art. lf ] we find what here follows: fulaAnN yaEomitu A^aqoraAnahu means yaqoharuhumo wayaluf~uhumo [i. e. (assumed tropical:) Such a one overcomes, or subdues, and throws into confusion, his antagonists: and hence, app., what is said in the K; the author of which probably found yakuf~ahumo erroneously written for yaluf~uhumo in some lexicon, and therefore thought it allowable to make Eamata in this case to have a sing. for its objective complement]: and it is added that this is said in relation to war, and excellence of judgment, and knowledge of the case of the enemy, and the subduing him with the infliction of many wounds. (TA.) ― -b4- Eamatahu also signifies He beat him with a staff, or stick, not caring [for any one]. (K.)

sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K, TA) and ↓ EumoqN , (S, O, K, TA,) or the latter is an inf. n., (Msb,) and ↓ EumuqN , (K, TA,) The bottom ( qaEor ) of a well (S, O, K, TA) and the like, (K, TA,) and of a [road such as is termed] faj~ , and of a valley: (S, O, TA:) or the depth of a well (Msb, TA) and the like; [i. e.] the distance to the bottom: (TA:) [and EumuwqN , which may be a pl. of the first or second, and perhaps of the third, signifies deep places of the ground: (see xasofN :) and ↓ EumoqN signifies also depth of anything; or distance between the two opposite surfaces thereof:] but accord. to IAar, ↓ EumoqN as an attribute of a road signifies distance: and as an attribute of a well it is the length of its cavity, or interior, from top to bottom. (TA.) ― -b2- And EamoqN and ↓ EumoqN signify also The distant, or remote, extremity of a desert, or waterless desert: pl. A^aEomaAqN : (S, O, K, TA:) which is also expl. as signifying sides, regions, or tracts; and extremities; without restriction: and sides, regions, or tracts, of the earth, or of a land. (TA.) Ru-beh says, fiY sabosabK munojaridi AlA^aEolaAqi AlA^aEomaAqi ↓ gayori AlfijaAji Eamiqi [ In a desert, or waterless desert, bared of the beaten tracks, except the far-extending (?) remote in respect of the extremities ]. Eunuw~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) and ↓ EanowapN is the subst. thereof, (Mgh, K, * TA,) [and] so is ↓ EanaA='N , (Msb,) or EanowapN is its inf. n., (MA,) [and so, app., is EanaA='N , in this sense as well as in another sense, accord. to the K,] He was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive; (S, MA, Mgh, Msb, K,) and obedient; (MA, TA;) to the truth, &c. (TA.) You say, EanaA lahu He was, or became, lowly, humble, or submissive, to him; or obedient to him. (MA.) And hence the saying in the Kur [xx. 110], waEanati A@lowajuwhu liloHaY~i Alqay~uwmi (S, TA) And the countenances shall be lowly &c. [ to the Deathless, or Ever-living, the Self-subsisting by Whom all things subsist: or shall be downcast; like the Hebr. phrases ending verses 5 and 6 in Gen. iv.]: or shall be submissive like captives: or the meaning is [ shall be depressed by ] the depressing of the forehead and the knee [or rather knees ] and the hands in the lowering of the head and the prostrating oneself [ in prayer ]: or [ Eanat is here from EanaY , belonging to art. EnY , and Alwjwh is used by a synecdoche for the persons (as being the most noble of all the parts thereof), and the meaning is] shall suffer fatigue, or weariness, and shall toil. (TA.) ― -b2- And EanaA , inf. n. Eunuw~N (M, Msb, K, TA, accord. to some copies of the K [erroneously] EanowN ) and EuniY~N (TA) and EanaA='N ; (K;) and EaniYa ; (M, K;) He became a captive: (K:) and the latter verb signifies also he stuck fast in captivity: (K in art. EnY :) or both of these verbs have this latter signification: (Msb:) [or] you say, EanaA fiyhimo fulaAnN A^asiyrFA Such a one remained among them a captive; and was in a state of confinement: (S:) and EanaA='N signifies also confinement, or imprisonment, in hardship and humiliation. (TA.) Hence the trad., AlxaAlu waArivu mano laA waAriva lahu yafuk~u Euniy~ahu i. e. A^asorahu [ The maternal uncle is the heir of him who has no more nearlyallied heir: he shall loose his (the latter's) captivity ]: meaning [he shall acquit him of] what is incumbent on him, and clings to him, because of the actions that require punishment or retaliation, the way [or custom] of which is that the EaAqilap [q. v., of whom he is a member,] bear the responsibility for them. (Nh, TA.) And ↓ EanowapN is the subst. of the verb in this sense also. (K, * TA.) -A2- And EanaA , aor. yaEonuw , inf. n. EanowapN , He took a thing by force: ― -b2- and also he took it peaceably, or by surrender: thus having two contr. significations. (Msb.) [But see below, where EanowapN is expl. as though it were the subst. of the verb in these two senses.] -A3- Eanawotu Al$~aYo'a I put forth, or produced, the thing: and I made the thing apparent, or showed it: (S:) or it has the latter signification; (K;) as also Eanayotu Al$~aYo'a : (IKtt, TA in art. EnY :) and Eanawotu biAl$~aYo'i has the former signification. (K.) And ↓ EanowapN is the subst. of the verb thus used, (K, TA,) i. e. in these two senses, as well as in others mentioned above. (TA.) And one says, Eanati AlA^aroDu biAln~abaAti , (ISk, S, and K in this art. and in art. EnY ,) aor. taEonuw , inf. n. Eunuw~N ; (ISk, S;) and aor. taEoniY ; (Ks, S;) The land made apparent, or showed, [or put forth, or produced, ] its plants, or herbage; (S, K;) as also ↓ A^aEonatohu . (K.) And lamo taEonu bilaAdunaA bi$aYo'K and lamo taEoni Our country did not give growth to anything. (S.) And AlA^aroDu $ayoy^FA ↓ maA A^aEonati The land did not give growth, or has not given growth, to anything. (S.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] saA^alotuhu falamo yaEonu liY bi$aYo'K I asked him, and he did not ( lamo yanoda and lamo yabiD~a ) to me, or for me, anything. (TA.) -A4- Eanato bihi A^umuwrN Events befell him. (S, K.) [See also 1 in art. EnY .] ― -b2- And EanaA AlA^amoru Ealayohi The event, or affair, was difficult, or distressing, to him; distressed, or troubled, him. (ISd, K, TA.) ― -b3- EanaAhu AlA^amoru , aor. yaEonuwhu : see 1 in art. EnY , first sentence. ― -b4- And EanaA fiyhi AlA^kolu , aor. yaEonuw , inf. n. Eunuw~N : see 1 in art. EnY . -A5- EanaA Alkalobu Al$~aYo'a , (CK, [in the TA and in my MS. copy of the K ll$Y' , but see what follows,]) aor. yaEonuwhu , inf. n. Enw [app., supposing the verb to be trans. by itself, EanowN ], (TA,) The dog came to the thing and smelt it: (K, TA:) and one says, h`*aA yaEonuw h`*aA This comes to this and smells it. (TA.) -A6- Eanati Alqirobapu bimaA='K kaviyrK , (K, TA,) aor. taEonuw , (TA,) The water-skin did not keep, or retain, much water, so that it appeared [ oozing from it ]: (K, TA:) or, as some say, Eanati Alqirobapu signifies the water-skin let flow its water. (TA.) ― -b2- And EanaA , inf. n. Eunw~N , said of blood, It flowed. (IKtt, TA.) -A7- And EanaA , aor. yaEonuw , inf. n. Eunuw~N , signifies also qaAma [ He, or it, stood; &c.]. (IKtt, TA.) -A8- See also Q. Q. 1.
