definition: Force, or constraint: (Mgh, K, TA:) or the taking by force;
sourceDefinition: Force, or constraint: (Mgh, K, TA:) or the taking by force; (Msb, TA;) as inf. n. of EanaA [q. v.]. (Msb.) One says, futiHato mak~apu EanowapF Mekkeh was taken forcibly, or by force. (Mgh.) And A^axa*ahu EanowapF He took it by force. (TA.) And futiHato h`*ihi Almadiynapu EanowapF i. e. [ This city was taken ] by means of conflict; its occupants having been combated until they had it taken from them by superior power or force, and were powerless to keep it, so they left it without there having occurred between them and the Muslims [or invaders ] a treaty of peace. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Love, or affection: (ISd, K, TA:) or submission, and concession: or a consequence of submission and concession, on the part of him from whom a thing is taken: (TA:) or the taking peaceably, or by surrender; as inf. n. of EanaA [q. v.]: (Msb:) thus it has two contr. significations. (Msb, K, TA.) A poet (cited by Fr, TA) says, famaA A^axa*uwhaA EanowapF Eano mawad~apK wal`kin~a Daroba Alma$orafiY~i A@sotaqaAlahaA (Msb, TA;) which is said to mean, [ And they did not take it, or her, or them, ] by concession, and obedience, [arising from love, or affection, ] without fighting: [ but the smiting of the Mesh-rafee sword demanded the renouncing thereof: ] 'Abd-El-Kádir Ibn-'Amr El-Baghdádee asserts the meaning of EanowapN to be submission and concession; adducing as evidence thereof this verse; attributing the contr. meaning to the vulgar: both, however, are correct; and that first mentioned occurs repeatedly in traditions: but the most learned Yákoot Er-Roomee, in his Moajam, says that the verse above-cited may be rendered as meaning and they did not take it, or her, or them, by superior power attended by [or in consequence of ] love, or affection: but they did so by fighting: and that this may be regarded as indicated by the poet's saying Ax*whA ; for otherwise he would have said, famaA sal~amuwhaA : and he says, it is a matter of common consent that EanowapN signifies force, and superior power. (TA.) ― -b3- It is also a subst. from EanaA in the first of senses mentioned in this art.: [i. e. it signifies Lowliness, humility, or submissiveness: ] (Mgh, TA:) [and] so is ↓ EanaA='N : (Msb:) see 1, first sentence. ― -b4- And it is also a subst. from EanaA as meaning “ he became a captive: ” [i. e. it signifies also A state of captivity: ] (TA:) see, again, 1. -A2- And it is also a subst. from EanaA in two other senses, as stated above: [i. e. it app. signifies also The act of putting forth, or producing, a thing: and of making it apparent, or showing, it:] (TA:) see, again, 1.

definition: , of the measure faEiylapN , The urine of the camel, inspissated in the sun, with which such as is affected with mange, or scab, is smeared;
sourceDefinition: , of the measure faEiylapN , The urine of the camel, inspissated in the sun, with which such as is affected with mange, or scab, is smeared; on the authority of AA: (S:) or certain mixtures of urine and dung of camels, with which the camel affected with mange, or scab, is smeared; also termed ↓ taEoniyapN : (K:) or the urine of camels that are caused to void their urine [in my original tusotabaAnu is erroneously written for tusotabaAlu ] in the [ season called ] rabiyE when they are satisfied with fresh pasture so as to be in no need of water, cooked [app. by boiling ] until it becomes thick, when some flowers of some sorts of herbs, and Hab~ AlmaHolab [the prunus mahaleb of Linn.], are thrown upon it, and it becomes inspissated thereby, then put into small [ earthen vessels of the kind called ] basaAtiyq [pl. of busotuwqapN ]: or urine [app. of camels ] mixed with certain things, and kept close for some time: or any hinaA=' [generally meaning tar, or a kind thereof, with which camels are smeared, as a remedy for the mange, or scab ]. (TA.) It is said in a prov., AlEaniy~apu ta$ofiY Aljaraba ; (S, TA;) or Eaniy~atuhu ta$ofiY Aljaraba [for mina Aljarabi , i. e. His Eny~p cures the mange, or scab ]: applied to the man of good judgment [whose advice is like a remedy]. (TA.)

definition: A stallion [camel] of mean origin, which, when excited by lust, is confined in the [ enclosure called ] Eun~ap , because his exercise of the faculty of a stallion is avoided: but it is said that it is originally muEan~anN , from AlEun~apu ;
sourceDefinition: A stallion [camel] of mean origin, which, when excited by lust, is confined in the [ enclosure called ] Eun~ap , because his exercise of the faculty of a stallion is avoided: but it is said that it is originally muEan~anN , from AlEun~apu ; one of the n being changed into Y : (S, TA: *) or of mean origin, of which the legs are bound with a rope, when he is excited by lust, for that reason. (TA.) ― -b2- And A camel of which the people of the Time of Ignorance used to displace the sanaAsin [pl. of sinosinN , q. v.] of one of his vertebræ, and to wound his hump, in order that he might not be ridden, and that no use might be made of his back: this was done when his owner possessed a hundred camels, he being the camel by which they became a hundred: and this act was termed AlA^igolaAqu : it may be from EanaA='N meaning “ fatigue; ” or from the signification of “ confinement from freedom of action. ” (TA.) -A2- See also EunowaAnN .

EawomN , (S, Msb, K,) He swam in the water; syn. sabaHa : (Mgh:) AlEawomu signifying Als~ibaAHapu : (S, K:) or, accord. to the author of the “ Iktitáf, ” the former signifies the coursing along in water with immersion of oneself; and the latter, “ the coursing along upon water without immersion of oneself: ” [but see what follows:] or, as some say, the former is an act of rational beings, and the latter is of irrational; but Bd, on the words kul~N fiY falakK yasobaHuwna [in the Kur xxi. 34], says that Als~ibaAHapu is the act of rational beings. (MF, TA.) It is said in a trad., Eal~imuwA SiboyAnakumu AlEawoma [ Teach ye your young boys swimming ]. (TA.) And one says, AlEawomu laA yunosaY [ Swimming once learned will not be forgotten ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And EAmt Als~afiynapu , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (S, K,) The ship coursed along. (S, K, TA.) ― -b3- And EAmt Aln~ujuwmu , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) The stars coursed along. (TA.) ― -b4- And EAmt AliA_bilu , (TA,) inf. n. as above, (S, K,) (tropical:) The camels marched along, or journeyed, (S, K, TA,) in the desert. (TA.) And yaEumona fiY luj~i Als~araAbi (tropical:) [ They course along in the apparently-boundless expanse of the mirage ]. (A, TA.)

definition: A year syn. sanapN : (S, K;) or HawolN ; [not sanapN ; for] El. Jawáleekee says, the common people do not distinguish between the EAm and the snh , making them both to have the same meaning; but the...
sourceDefinition: A year syn. sanapN : (S, K;) or HawolN ; [not sanapN ; for] El. Jawáleekee says, the common people do not distinguish between the EAm and the snh , making them both to have the same meaning; but the right state of the case is what I have been told on the authority of Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà [i. e. Th], that the snh is from any day from which one commences a reckoning to the like thereof, and the EAm is only [ a period of ] a winter and a summer; and it is also said in the T and in the Bári that the EAm is a Hawol that makes an end of a winter and a summer, so that every EAm is a snp , but every snp is not an EAm ; for when you reckon from a day to the like thereof, that is a snp , and there may be in it half of the summer. and half of the winter, whereas the EAm is only a winter and a summer, without interruption: (Msb, MF: *) Er-Rághib mentions a difference in the uses of the words EaAmN and sanapN [as has been stated in art. snw and snY : see sanapN in that art.] and Suh says, in the R, that the snp is longer than the EAm ; that the former is “ a single revolution of the sun; ” and that the latter is applied to the [ twelve ] Arabian months [ collectively ]: it is said to be called EAm because of the sun's Eawom [or coursing] through all of its zodiacal signs [during the period which it denotes]: (TA:) its pl. is A^aEowAmN , (S, Msb, K,) because the sing. is originally of the measure faEalN [i. e. EawamN ]: (Msb:) it has no other pl. than this. (TA.) ― -b2- One says, lqiytuhu EaAmFA A^aw~ala [ I met him in a former year; generally meaning, the year immediately preceding, or, as we say, last year ]; making the last word imperfectly decl. as being an epithet [and of the measure of a verb]: and laqituhu EaAmFA A^aw~alFA [ I met him in a year before: generally meaning the same as the phrase preceding]; making the last word perfectly decl. as not being an epithet [but an adv.n. and K in art. wA^l ) or the meaning is, in a year ] before this year; even if it be by a number of years: ('Alee El-Kári, on the authority of Seer, in a marginal note in my MS. copy of the K, art. Awl :) and one says also, accord. to AZ and IAar, laqaytuhu EaAma AlA^aw~ali ; (TA in art. wA^l ;) or the is rarely said; (K and TA in that art.;) or should not be said; (ISk, S and TA in that art.;) nor should one say, laqaytuhu EaAma A^aw~ala (ISk TA in the present art.) And [in like manner] one says, mA raA^ayotuhu mu*o EaAmN A^aw~alu , putting the last word in the nom case as being an epithet, (S and K in art. wA^l ,) as though he said A^aw~alu mino EaAminaA [i. e. I have not seen him since a year preceding this one year ]; (S in that art.;) and mu*o EaAmN A^aw~ala , putting the last word in the accus. case as an adv n., (S and K * in that art.,) as though he said mu*o EAmN qabola EaAminaA [ since a year before this our year ]; (S in that art.;) and mu*oEaAmFA A^aw~ala and mu*o EaAmu AlA^aw~ali are also mentioned by different authors (L in art, mn* ) And [using the dim. form] one says, laqituhu *aAta ↓ AlEuwayomi i. e. [ I met him ] in the course of some years; like as one says, laqiytuhu *aAta Alz~umayoni , and *aAta mar~apK : (S:) or the meaning is, ( some few years ago; or] three years ago or more, to ten: (AZ, Az, TA:) and it is like the saying, laqiytuhu muno*u sunay~aAtK : the fem. form is used because they mean by it mar~ap waAHidap . (Az, TA.) ― -b3- One says also naAqapN baAzilu EaAmK and baAzilu EaAmihaA [ A she-camel that has passed a year, and her year, after cutting her tush ], (TA,) and bAzil EaAmayoni that has passed two years after cutting the tush. (MF and TA in art. bzl .) -A2- See also EaAmapN , in two places. -A3- It is also said in the K that AlEaAmu signifies Aln~ahaAru : but this is a mistake and a mistranscription it is AlEayaAmu ; and its place is art. Eym ; as it as mentioned by Az, on the authority of El-Muärrij, (TA.)

definition: aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. gaboTN , (S,) He felt with his hand his (a ram's) A^aloyap [i. e. rump, or tail, or fat of the tail, ] in order to see if he were fat or not: (S, K:) and he felt it (his back)...
sourceDefinition: aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. gaboTN , (S,) He felt with his hand his (a ram's) A^aloyap [i. e. rump, or tail, or fat of the tail, ] in order to see if he were fat or not: (S, K:) and he felt it (his back) with his hand in order to know whether he were lean or fat: (Lth, K: *) and in like manner the verb is used in relation to a she-camel. (TA.) -A2- gabaTahu , aor. ; (ISk, Az, S, Msb, K;) and gabiTahu , aor. ; (Ibn-Buzurj, Sgh, K;) inf. n. gaboTN (ISk, Az, S, Msb, K) and giboTapN , (S, K,) or the latter is a simple subst.; (Msb;) He regarded him [ with unenvious emulation, i. e.] with a wish for the like of his condition, (ISk, Az, S,) meaning a good condition, (Az,) or for the like of that which he had attained, (Msb,) or for a blessing, (K,) and that it might not pass away, (ISk, K,) or without desiring that it should pass away, (Az, S, Msb,) from the latter person: (ISk, Az, S, Msb, K:) the doing so is not HasadN , (Az, S, Msb,) for this implies the desire that what is wished for may pass away from its possessor; (Az, Msb;) or it is a kind of Hasad , of a more moderate quality: (Az:) or giboTapN and gaboTN have the signification shown above, and are also syn. with HasadN ; (K;) this latter meaning is assigned to gaboTN by IAar; and it is said that the Arabs use gaboTN in the sense of HasadN metonymically; (TA;) [so that gabaTahu and gabiTahu may also mean (tropical:) he envied him; &c.; see an ex. in a prov. cited voce baTonN ; but it is said that] HasadN , when it is for courage and the like, is syn. with giboTapN , and then it implies admiration, without a wish that the thing admired may pass away from its possessor. (Msb in art. Hsd .) You say, gabaTahu bihi , (S,) and Ealayohi , (IAth,) and fiyhi , (Msb,) He regarded him with a wish for the like of it, meaning a thing or state which he had attained, without desiring that it should pass away from the latter person. (S, IAth, * Msb.) Mohammad was asked, “ Does AlgaboT injure? ” and he answered, “ Yes, like as AlxaboT injures: ” or, accord. to the relation of A'Obeyd, “ No, save as AlxaboT injures the [trees called] EiDaAh : ” (Az, TA:) [see xabaTa :] by AlgyT meaning, accord. to some, AlHasad : (TA:) or a kind thereof, of a more moderate quality; injurious, but not so injurious as AlHsd whereby one wishes that a blessing may pass away from his brother; AlxbT meaning the beating off the leaves of trees; after which they become replaced, without there resulting any injury therefrom to the stock and branches: moreover, AlgbT sometimes occasions the smiting of its object with the evil eye. (Az, TA.) [See also giboTapN , below.] -A3- Accord. to IKtt, gabaTa signifies also He lied; but perhaps it is a mistranscription for EabaTa , which has this meaning; for it is not mentioned by any other. (TA.)

definition: He was, or became, regarded [ with unenvious emulation, i.
sourceDefinition: He was, or became, regarded [ with unenvious emulation, i. e.,] with a wish for the like of his condition, without its being desired that it should pass away from him: (S:) or he was, or became, in such a condition that he was regarded with a wish for the like thereof, without its being desired that it should pass away from him: (Táj el-Masádir, TA:) or he rejoiced, or became rejoiced, in being in a good condition; (K;) or in blessing bestowed upon him: (TA:) or he was grateful, or thankful, to God for blessing, or bounty, bestowed upon him: (L:) and the same, (K,) or ↓ A^agobaTa , inf. n. A_igobaATN , accord. to the L, (TA,) he was, or became, in a good state or condition; in a state of happiness; (L, K;) and of enjoyment, or wellbeing. (L.) You say, laqiYa maA yugotabaTu Ealayohi [ He met with, or experienced, that for which one would be regarded with unenvious emulation, i. e., with a wish to be in the like condition, without its being desired that it should pass away from him ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A [ camel's saddle of the kind called ] raHol , (S, Msb,) for women, (S,) upon which the [ vehicle called ] hawodaj is bound: (S, Msb:) or an elegant kind of raHol , depressed in its middle: (TA:) or a vehicle like the pads ( A^ukuf [in the CK, erroneously, Aakuf~ ]) of the [ species of camels called ] baxaAtiY~ , (K,) which is tented over with a [ framework such as is called ] $ijaAz , and is for women of birth: (Az, TA:) or, as some say, of which the pad ( qatab ) is made not in the [ usual ] make of pads ( A^aqotaAb ): (TA:) or a rHl of which the pad ( qatab ) and the [ curved wooden parts called ] A^aHonaA=' are one [i. e., app., conjoined ]: (K:) pl. gubuTN . (S, Msb, K.) The pl. is also applied to the pieces of wood in camels' saddles; and to such are likened Persian bows, (S, TA,) because of their curvature. (IAth.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Depressed land or ground: (S, K:) or a wide and even tract of land of which the two extremities are elevated, (K,) like the form of the camel's saddle so called, of which the middle is depressed: (TA:) also (assumed tropical:) a channel of water furrowed in a tract such as is termed quf~ , (K, TA,) like a valley in width, having between it and another such channel meadows and herbage: pl. as above. (TA.)

definition: , aor. yagoluw , primarily signifies He, or it, exceeded the proper, due, or common, limit; was excessive, immoderate, or beyond measure; but the inf. n. differs in different cases, as will be shown...
sourceDefinition: , aor. yagoluw , primarily signifies He, or it, exceeded the proper, due, or common, limit; was excessive, immoderate, or beyond measure; but the inf. n. differs in different cases, as will be shown in what follows: (Er-Rághib, TA:) it is said of anything as meaning it exceeded, or was excessive. (Msb.) ― -b2- You say, galaA fiY AlA^amori , (S, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. guluw~N (S, K, TA) and galaAniyapN ; as also bihi ↓ tgAlY ; (K * and TA in art. glY ; [but belonging to the present art., as is said in the TA;]) He exceeded the proper, due, or common, limit, in the affair; was excessive, or immoderate, therein. (S, K, TA.) And galaA fiY Ald~iyni , aor. as above, inf. n. guluw~N , He acted, or behaved, with forced hardness, or strictness, or rigour, in religion, so that he exceeded the proper, due, or common, limit: whence the usage of the verb in the Kur iv. 169 and v. 81: (Msb, TA:) accord. to IAth, Alguluw~u fiY Ald~iyni is the investigating of the intrinsic states, or circumstances, of things, [ in religion, ] and [ applying oneself to ] the discovery of their causes, and of the abstrusities relating to the rites and ceremonies thereof. (TA.) [See also 3.] ― -b3- And galaA biAls~ahomi , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. galowN (S, Er-Rághib, Mgh, Msb, K) and guluw~N ; (K;) and bihi ↓ gAlY , (Mgh, K,) and ↓ gAlAhu , (K,) inf. n. gilaA='N (Mgh, K) and mugaAlaApN ; (K;) He shot the arrow to the furthest distance (S, Mgh, Msb) that he was able to attain: (S, Mgh:) or he raised his arms with the arrow, desiring [ to attain with it ] the furthest limit. (K, * TA.) And galaA Als~ahomu The arrow rose in its course, and exceeded the [ usual ] limit; (K, TA;) and in like manner, AlHajaru the stone. (TA.) ― -b4- And galaA Als~iEoru , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) aor. as above, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. galaA='N , (S, Mgh, K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) The price, or rate, at which a thing was to be sold, was, or became, high; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) or exceeded the usual limit; (Er-Rághib, TA;) contr. of raxuSa . (K.) ― -b5- And galaA bihaA EZm [i. e. EiZamN , lit. Bigness exceeded the usual limit in her; ] meaning she became plump, or fat: (TA:) one says, glA biAljaAriyapi EZm , and biAlgulaAmi , [ the girl, or young woman, became plump, or fat, and the boy, or young man, ] in the case of their quickly attaining to young womanhood and young manhood. (TA in another part of this art.) ― -b6- And galaA is said of anything as meaning AirotafaEa [i. e. It rose in degree; as is shown by the following ex.]: Dhur-Rummeh says, famaA zaAla yagoluw Hub~u may~apa EinodanaA wayazodaAdu Hat~aY lamo najido maA naziyduhaA [ And the love of Meiyeh ceased not to rise in degree with us, and to increase, so that we found not what more we might give to her ]. (TA.) ― -b7- See also 8. ― -b8- And see 6.

definition: , inf. n. mugaAlaApN , signifies [the same, or nearly the same, as galaA fiyhi ; i. e.] He exceeded the usual, or proper, bounds, or degree, in his affair; acted immoderately therein; or strove or...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. mugaAlaApN , signifies [the same, or nearly the same, as galaA fiyhi ; i. e.] He exceeded the usual, or proper, bounds, or degree, in his affair; acted immoderately therein; or strove or laboured, or exerted himself or his power or efforts, or the like, therein; syn. baAlaga [q. v.]. (Msb.) ― -b2- See also 1, near the middle, in two places. ― -b3- gaAlaY bihi , and gAlAhu , (S, Msb, K,) which latter is used by a poet for gAlY bh , (S,) He bought it at a high, or an excessive, price, namely, flesh-meat; (S, Msb;) as also bihi ↓ AglY ; (S;) and ↓ AglAhu , i. e. water, and flesh-meat [&c.]: (IKtt, TA: [see an ex. in a verse of Lebeed cited in art. dkn :]) or he exceeded what was usual in purchasing it, or in offering it for sale, and mentioning the price. (M, K, TA.) A poet says, nugaAliY All~aHoma liloA^aDoyaAfi niyoy^FA wanuroxiSuhu A_i*aA naDija Alquduwru [ We purchase at a high price flesh-meat, for the guests, raw; and we make it to be low-priced when the contents of the cooking-pots are thoroughly cooked ]: he has suppressed the b [after ngAlY ], meaning it [to be understood]. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And gAlY fiY AlS~idaAqi He made the dowry, or the gift to, or for, a bride, high, or excessive, in amount; [ he was excessive, or exorbitant, therein; ] whence the saying of 'Omar, laA tugaAluwA fiY SaduqaAti Aln~isaA='i [ Be not ye excessive, or exorbitant, in respect of the dowries of women ]. (TA. [See also 6.]) ― -b5- And gAlAhu , inf. n. mugaAlaApN , signifies also He contended with him for superiority in tallness or in beneficence; syn. TaAwalahu . (TA.)

definition: The limit, or utmost extent, of a shot or throw;
sourceDefinition: The limit, or utmost extent, of a shot or throw; (S, Mgh; *) [i. e.] any maromaAp : (K:) [generally, a bow-shot; i. e.] the measure, space, or extent, of a single shooting of an arrow: (Har p. 234:) [or the utmost measure of a bow-shot; i. e.] a shot of an arrow to the utmost possible distance; also termed gaAyapN : (Msb:) said to be from three hundred to four hundred cubits: (Mgh, Msb:) the twenty-fifth part of a complete farosax [q. v.]: (ISd, Z, Mgh, TA:) or it is reckoned by some as four hundred cubits, and by others as two hundred cubits: (Msb voce miylN [q. v.]:) pl. galawaAtN (Msb, K, TA) and gilaA='N . [Thus] galowapN is sometimes used in relation to horse-racing. (TA.)

definition: A certain implement of iron, (M,) with which one digs;
sourceDefinition: A certain implement of iron, (M,) with which one digs; [i. e., a kind of hoe; thus called in the present day; generally having a blade more long than wide, and a short handle; altogether resembling an adz: ] (Kr, M:) and with which one cuts; [i. e., an adz; and an axe; both also thus called in the present day; more commonly the former; used for cutting, cleaving, and splitting, trees and wood, (see faA^asa ,) and for hewing, forming, or fashioning, wood &c.: (see also qaduwmN :)] (M:) a thing well known: (A, K:) [applied also to a pickaxe: (see SaAquwrN :)] the ' in this word may be suppressed: (Msb:) it is of the fem. gender: (M, Msb, K:) the pl. (of pauc., O) is A^afow^usN (M, O, Msb, K) and (of mult., O) fuw^uwsN , (S, M, O, Msb, K,) and, accord. to some, fuw^osN . (TA.) ― -b2- faA^osu All~ijaAmi [ A certain part of the bit; namely,] the [ tongue of ] iron that stands up towards [so I render here the particle fiY ] the Hanak [here meaning the palate, against which it is made to press when the rein is drawn hard for the purpose of checking the horse]; (IDrd in his book on the Saddle and Bridle, [in one part of which he likens to it the tongue of a buckle,] S, M, A, O, K;) the iron that stands up in the $akiymap ; (T;) or, as some say, that which is in the middle of the $kymp , between the misoHalaAni : (ISh:) the $kymp is the iron that lies across in the mouth, [i. e., the bit-mouth, or mouth-piece of the bit,] and the misoHal is an iron [i. e. a ring of iron, one of a pair of rings which are inserted each into the other, in the place of our curbchain,] beneath the Hanak [here meaning the part between the two sides of the lower jaw]: (IDrd:) or, as some say, [and among them Kr.] the transverse iron in the bit; (M;) but this assertion requires consideration. (TA.) You say, fulaAnN yaluwku lisaAnahu fiY AlkalaAmi kamaA yaEoliku Alfarasu faA^osa All~ijaAmi [ Such a one mumbles his tongue in speaking like as the horse moves about in his mouth the fA^s of the bit ]. (A.) ― -b3- faA^osu Alr~aA^osi , (S, O, K,) or faA^osu AlqafaA , (M,) The edge of the qamaHoduwap [or hinder part of the back of the head ], that projects above the back of the neck; [i. e., the small protuberance above the back of the neck: ] (S, O, K:) or the hinder part of the qmHdwp . (M.) ― -b4- faA^osu Alr~aHaY The [ protuberant ] part of the [ nether, or lower, ] mill-stone, in the middle of which is [ fixed ] the axis. (Kzw, description of Ursa Minor.) ― -b5- And hence, AlfaA^osu The Constellation of Ursa Minor. (Idem, same place.) ― -b6- faA^osu Alfami The extremity of the mouth, in which are the teeth. (M.) ― -b7- AijoEalo h`*aA AlA^amora faA^osFA waAHidFA means Make thou this affair to be [ uniform, or] of one way or mode or manner. (ISk, TA in art. bA^j .)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. farojN , He made an opening, or intervening space, [or a gap, or beach, ] between the two things; or he opened the interstice, or interval, between the two things: (Msb:) [and faraja Al$~Yo'a He opened the thing; and particularly by diduction, or so as to form an intervening space, or a gap, or breach; he unclosed it: and in like manner ↓ fr~ij , inf. n. taforiyjN ; for ex.,] you say, Haluwbatihi far~aja maA bayona rijolaYo [ He made an opening, or intervening space, between the hind legs of his milch camel; i. e. he parted her hind legs ]; (S and O and K in art. fHj , &c.;) and fr~j bayona A^aSaAbiEihi He made openings, or intervening spaces, between his fingers. (MA.) ― -b2- The saying in the Kur lxxvii. 9 waA_i*aA A@ls~amaA='u furijato means [ And when the sky ] shall be opened so that it shall become portals: (Ksh:) or shall become cloven, or split, or rent. (Bd and Jel.) ― -b3- And you say, faraja AlbaAba He opened the door. (A, TA.) And faraja faAhu He opened his mouth to die. (TA.) ― -b4- And faraja Alqawomu lilr~ajuli , aor. , inf. n. farojN , [and faraja lahu , aor. , inf. n. farojN and furojapN , seems from the context to be mentioned in this sense in the L,] The people, or party, made room, or ample space, for the man, in the place of standing or of sitting. definition: , occurring in the saying, in a trad.
sourceDefinition: , occurring in the saying, in a trad., laA yutoraku fiY AlA_solaAmi muforajN , [meaning that he who is thus termed shall not be left unbefriended among the Muslims,] is variously explained: As used to say that it is with H ; and disapproved of the saying mfrj , with j : A'Obeyd says, I heard Mohammad Ibn-El-Hasan say, it is related with H and with j ; and he who says mfrj , with j , means A slain person found in a desert tract, not by a town or village, [which signification is mentioned in the K,] the fine for whose blood is to be paid from the government-treasury: AO says that it means one who becomes a Muslim and has no alliance of friendship with any one [ among the Muslims ]; wherefore, if he commits a crime, [such as maiming another, &c.,] the governmenttreasury must make amends for it, because he has no relations or others bound to aid him by paying a bloodwit [or the like]: (S, O: and the like is also said in the Mgh and in the K:) or, accord. to Jábir El-Joafee, it means a man who is among a people to whom he does not belong; wherefore they are bound to pay for him a bloodwit [or the like]: (O, TA:) or it means one who has no kinsfolk, or near relations: so accord. to IAar: (Mgh, TA:) or one who has no offspring: or one who has no wealth, or property: and it is also said to mean one burdened by the obligation to pay a bloodwit, or a ransom, or a debt that must be discharged: and [in like manner] ↓ maforuwjN is said to mean one who is burdened with a debt: but it is correctly with H [unpointed]; (TA;) [i. e.] such is termed muforaHo , with H : (As, Mgh:) and muforajN means one burdened by his family, although he be not in debt. (Az, TA voce muforaHN [q. v.].)

[or rather a coll. gen. n.] thereof, used as such in a verse of Jereer. (TA.) ― -b2- [The pl.] fayaA$ilu signifies also a name of Certain trees. (K.) ― -b3- [Freytag adds as other meanings what belong to a description of the proper name of a certain water and of hills surrounding it, called AlfayaA$ilu .]

definition: , applied to a man, (T, S, M, &c.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a man, (T, S, M, &c.,) Rough; coarse; rude; unkind; hard; churlish; uncivil; surly; hard to deal with; incompliant; unobsequious; (S, M, O, K, and Bd in iii. 153;) evil in disposition; illnatured; (O, K, and Bd and Jel ubi suprà;) hard-hearted; hard, or severe; rough, coarse, or the like, so as to be unduly feared; (Msb;) rough, or coarse, in speech; (Lth, T, M, K;) sour, or austere, therein: (Lth:) [said in the T to be from the same word in the sense next following; but accord. to the M, the reverse seems to be the case:] pl. A^afoZaAZN . (M.) You say, A_in~ahu lafaZ~N baZ~N [ Verily he is rough, coarse, or the like ]; the latter word being an imitative sequent; (M, K;) as such we regard it because Th, who mentions it, does not explan it; (M;) and ↓ faZiyZN baZiyZN [app. signifies the same]. (TA in art. bZ .) -A2- Also The water of the stomach [ of a camel ], (T, S, K,) which is pressed, or squeezed, out, and drunk, (T, K,) on an occasion of want of water, (T,) in the waterless deserts; (T, K;) the water that comes forth from the stomach [ of a camel ]; because it is a coarse, or bitter, beverage: (M:) it may not be used for the purpose of religious purification: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, T:) also, the urine of horses which is drunk on an occasion of thirst: pl. fuZuwZN : thus used by Mutemmem Ibn-Nuweyreh. (M, L.)

definition: The seminal fluid of a woman: or of a stallion: (M, K:) so they assert: but it is not of established authority: (M:) and so say IDrd and Fr: (TA:) accord.
sourceDefinition: The seminal fluid of a woman: or of a stallion: (M, K:) so they assert: but it is not of established authority: (M:) and so say IDrd and Fr: (TA:) accord. to Kr, the seminal fluid of a stallion, in a she-camel's womb: (M, * TA:) or this is the explanation given by Fr: (T:) and ↓ fuZaAZapN is of the measure fuEaAlapN from this word; (K;) as signifying the seminal fluid of a stallion, or the water of the stomach; but El-Khattábee disallows the latter meaning; or from faZ~N : (TA:) and hence the saying of 'Áïsheh to Marwán, wal`kin~a A@ll~`ha laEana A^abaAka waA^anota fiY Sulobihi faA^anota fuZaAZapN mino laEonapi A@ll~`hi [ But God cursed thy father when thou wast essentially in his loins; so thou art seed of the object of the curse of God ]; (K;) i. e., nuTofapN minohaA ; (TA;) or EuSaArapN minohaA [ produce thereof, as though expressed therefrom ]: (Z:) or, accord. to one relation, fuDuDN ; (K;) pl. of faDiyDN , which means water such as is termed gariyD : or, accord. to another relation, faDaDN , meaning nuTofapN : and accord. to another, faDiyDN . (TA.) -A2- See also faZ~N .

definition: The whiteness that is upon the nails of young persons;
sourceDefinition: The whiteness that is upon the nails of young persons; (S, M, O, K;) as also ↓ fawofN ; (T, M, K;) the latter mentioned by Fr, but not known by IAar; (T;) or the former is the more common: (K:) n. un. with ↓ p ; (M, K;) meaning a portion thereof. (M.) ― -b2- And The integument [or pellicle ] that is upon [ what is termed ] the core of the heart, and the stone of the date. ( EalaY Hab~api Alqalobi waAln~awaApi ,) beneath the flesh [or pulpy substance ] of the date: (M, K:) of the white grain [i. e. the embryo, which resembles a white grain,] in the interior of the date stone, from which the palm-tree grows forth [or germinates ]: and it is said that ↓ fuwfapN signifies the integument [or pellicle ] that is upon the date stone (S, O:) [i. e.] the thin integument that is upon the date-stone; also called the qiTomiyr . (T.) ― -b3- [Hence, or from one of the significations mentioned above,] one says, maA A^agonaY Ean~iY fuwfFA i. e. [ He (a man, S, O) did not avail me ] aught. (S, O, K.) And maA *aAqa fuwfaA [ He tasted not ] aught. (T, K.) ― -b4- And fuwfN signifies also Any integument; (M, K;) and so ↓ fuwfapN . (K) ― -b5- And The bladder of an animal of the bovine kind; as also ↓ fawofN : (K.) mentioned by Sgh in the TS. (TA.) ― -b6- Also A sort of the [ garments called ] baruwd of El-Yemen: (M, K:) thin, variegated, or figured, garments of El-Yemen: (IAar, T:) and one says also burodN ↓ fuwfiY~N , and vuwviY~N , which is formed by substitution, and mentioned by Yaakoob, and burodu A^afowaAfK meaning a burod having white stripes. (M.) and so ↓ burodN mufaw~afN ; (S, M, K;) or this last and burodu A^afowaAfK signify a thin burod ; (S, O, K, TA;) and in like manner one says Hul~apu A^afowaAfK . (TA.) A^afowaAfN is pl. of fuwfN : (S, O:) and accord. to Lth, the A^afowaAf are of the [ buruwd called ] EaSob [q. v.] of ElYemen. (O.) ― -b7- Also Flowers or blossoms, syn. zahorN : [in the CK zahar ;] used in this sense by Ibn-Ahmar; being likened by him to the garments called fuwf . (T, K, TA.) ― -b8- And Portions of cotton: (O, K, and so in some copies of the S:) [perhaps meaning] a white thing [ resembling cotton ] which is in the Eu$ar [q. v.]. (Ham p. 784.) ― -b9- [And Freytag mentions its signifying The extreme portion of the penis; as on the authority of the K: but he seems to have confounded fuwfN with fuwqN .]

definition: The scent, smell, or odour, of roast meat;
sourceDefinition: The scent, smell, or odour, of roast meat; (El-Fárábee, S, Msb, K;) or of flesh-meat when roasted upon live coals: this is the sense in which the Arabs use it: (T, TA:) [or] it signifies also that of a cooking-pot: and of burnt bone: (K:) and of aloes-wood, (S,) or of baxuwr , (K,) i. e., aloes-wood which is burnt and with which one fumigates: (TA:) or the last odour of aloes-wood when one fumigates with it: (Fr, in the Kitáb el-Masádir:) or it has not this signification of the odour of aloes-wood, but the Arabs compare the liking of men in a time of dearth for the scent of roast meat to their liking for the odour of aloeswood: (T, TA:) or it signifies the smoke of cooked food: (Msb:) and the scent, or smell, of a man. (El-Basáïr.) ― -b2- It is also sometimes applied by the Arabs to Fat: and flesh. (TA.)

definition: signifies The act of mixing.
sourceDefinition: signifies The act of mixing. (S, Mgh, O, K.) You say, qa$aba , aor. , inf. n. qa$obN , He mixed. (K.) And qu$iba , said of anything, It was mixed. (M.) ― -b2- And qa$abahu , aor. and inf. n. as above, He corrupted, or vitiated, it: (K, TA:) or he mixed it (i. e. anything) with a thing that corrupted, or vitiated, it. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence,] qa$aba AlT~aEaAma , (S, M,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) He poisoned the food; (S;) he mixed the food with poison; as also ↓ q$~bhu : (M, TA:) or qa$aba signifies he mixed poison, and so prepared it that it should take effect upon the body. (IAar, TA.) ― -b4- And qa$abahu , (S, O, K,) aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., He gave him poison to drink; (S, O, K;) and (TA) so lahu ↓ q$~b . (M, TA.) And qa$aba Aln~asora He put poison on flesh- meat for the vulture, that he might eat it and die, and he might take his feathers. (AA, TA.) ― -b5- And [hence] qa$abaniY riyHuhu ; (K, TA;) and (TA) ryHh ↓ qa$~abaniY , inf. n. taqo$iybN ; (S, TA;) His, or its, odour annoyed me: (S, K, TA:) as though meaning it poisoned me. (S, TA.) qa$abahu and ↓ q$~bhu both signify He, or it, annoyed him. (Mgh.) And qa$abahu Ald~uxaAnu means The smoke annoyed him by its odour; and oppressed, or overpowered, him. (O.) qa$obN [in a case of this kind], (O, K,) as inf. n. of qa$aba , aor. , (K,) means The affecting [a person] with what is displeasing, or hateful, and with what is deemed unclean, or filthy: (O, K: [in the former Alqa$obu is expl. by the words AlASAbpu bmA yukorahu wyusotaqo*aru ; which, as well as what here follows, shows that an assertion in the TK (copied from the TA, and adopted by Freytag) respecting the explanation in the K, is erroneous:]) and hence the saying of 'Omar, when he perceived the odour of perfume from Mo'áwiyeh when the latter was a pilgrim, mano qa$abanaA [i. e. Who has affected us with what is displeasing &c.?]; likening the odour of perfume in this case to a stink. (O.) ― -b6- qa$obN also signifies The depriving [one] of reason; (K, TA;) from the same word as signifying the act of “ corrupting, ” or “ vitiating: ” (TA:) and its verb is qa$aba , aor. . (K, TA.) 'Omar said to one of his sons, qa$abaka AlmaAlu (M, O, TA) i. e. Wealth has deprived thee of thy reason: (M:) or has corrupted, or vitiated, thee, and deprived thee of thy reason. sourceDefinition: Poison; (S, M, Mgh, O, K;) because consisting of things mixed together; (Mgh;) as also ↓ qa$abN : (M, K:) pl. of the former A^aqo$aAbN . (S, M.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] A certain plant, (M, O, K,) resembling the maqir , (M, [which is generally said to mean the aloe, and by AHn to be a certain plant consisting of leaves without branches, agreeably with what follows, in the O and K resembling the mafod ,]) from the middle whereof there rises a stalk, which, when it grows tall, bends down its top by reason of its succulence, or suppleness; having upon its head a fruit ( vamarapN , M, O, [in the TA Eqdp ,]) with which birds of prey are killed, (M, O,) being poisoned therewith by its being put into flesh and thrown where they alight: he who prepares it stops up his nose; if he do not, it injures him; and people fear to pasture their cattle near to the places of its growth lest the animals should come in contact with it and should break it or bruise it and it should exhale its odour upon them and kill them: thus says AHn, on the authority of some one or more of the Arabs of the desert, of the Saráh ( Als~araAp ). (O.) ― -b3- And Anything unclean, dirty, or filthy; as also ↓ qa$abN : (M, TA:) or anything that is deemed unclean, dirty, or filthy. (Mgh.) ― -b4- Rust (K, TA) upon iron: (TA:) or dirt upon a sword. (A, TA.) ― -b5- The refuse, that is thrown away, as being of no good, of TaEaAm [i. e. wheat, or other food]. (M, TA.) ― -b6- See also [the pl.] A^aqo$aAbN , voce qaA$ibN . ― -b7- Also, i. e. qi$obN A man in whom is no good; (K, TA;) and (TA) so qi$obN xi$obN ; (S, M, O, TA;) or this means with whom is no good: the latter word is an imitative sequent. (TA in art. x$b .) [See also qi$obapN .] ― -b8- And Dry, or tough, and hard. (M, TA. [Like qasobN .]) -A2- And Alqi$obu signifies The nafos [here meaning jasad , i. e. body, as is shown below, voce qaA$ibN ]. (O, K.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taqoliydN ; (S;) and ql~dhA qilaAdapF ; (Msb, K;) He put a qlAdp [or necklace ] upon her (a woman's, S, Msb) neck; (S, * K;) attired her therewith. (Msb.) [And so,] qaladotuhu Als~ayofa , I hung upon him the sword, putting its suspensory belt or cord upon his neck or shoulder. (A.) [And] ql~d Albadanapa , inf. n. taqoliydN , He hung upon the neck of the camel or cow or bull brought as an offering to Mekkeh for sacrifice something to show that it was such an offering; (T, S, A, L, K, &c.;) namely, an old worn-out sandal, (JK,) or a piece of a skin, (Msb,) or of a sandal, (T, Mgh,) or of a mizaAdap , (Mgh,) or the loop of a mzAdp . (T.) The pagan Arabs used also to hang upon the necks of their camels pieces of the bark ( lisHaA=' ) of the trees of the sacred territory of Mekkeh, as a means of protection against their enemies. (Zj, on verse 2 of ch. v. of the Kur.) ― -b2- Hence, taqoliydu AlwulaApi AlA^aEomaAla (tropical:) [ The investing of prefects, or the like, with offices of administration ]. (S, L, K.) You say, ql~dhu EamalFA (tropical:) [ He invested him with an office of administration ]. (A, L.) qal~dhu niEamahu (tropical:) [ He conferred upon him permanent badges of his favours ]. (A.) [See qilaAdapN : and see also TawoqN and Tw~q .] ― -b3- Hence, also, Alt~aqoliydu fiY Ald~iyni (tropical:) [ The investing with authority in matters of religion ]: (S, L:) Altqlyd means a man's following another in that which he says or does, firmly believing him to be right therein, without regard or consideration of the proof, or evidence; as though the former made the saying or deed of the other a qilaAdap upon his neck. (KT.) -A2- ql~dhu AlA^amora (tropical:) He obliged him, or constrained him, to do the thing, or affair; he imposed upon him the thing, or affair. (L.) -A3- qul~ida fulaAnN qilaAdapa sawo'K (tropical:) Such a one was satirized with that which left upon him a lasting stigma. (A.)

sourceDefinition: [ A necklace; a collar; and the like; ] that which is upon the neck; (S;) what is put upon the neck (L, K) of a human being, and a horse, and a dog, and a camel or cow or bull that is brought as an offering to Mekkeh for sacrifice, [see 2,] and the like: (L:) Esh-Shiháb observes, in the 'Ináyeh, that the measure fiEaAlapN , in the case of a word not an inf. n., denotes a thing that envelops, or that surrounds, another thing; as in the instances of lifaAfapN and EimaAmapN and qilaAdapN : (TA:) pl. qalaAy^idu : (Msb:) qilaAdN also occurs, either as a pl. of qilaAdapN , in which case the kesreh and A in the pl. are different from the kesreh and A in the sing., [being the proper characteristics of the pl.,] or as a coll. gen. n., of which qilaAdapN is the n. un. (ISd, L.) ― -b2- Hasobuka mina AlqilaAdapi maA A^aHaATa biAlEunuqi (assumed tropical:) [ Sufficient for thee is the necklace that surrounds the neck ]. A proverb. (TA.) Said by 'Okeyl Ibn-'Ullufeh, on his being asked why he did not censure his enemies in a longer satire. (Z.) ― -b3- niEomatuka qilaAdapN fiY EunuqiY laA yafuk~uhaA AlmalawaAni (tropical:) [ Thy beneficence is a permanent badge upon my neck which day and night will not loose ]. (A.) ― -b4- liY fiY A^aEonaAqihimo qalaAy^idu niEamK raAhinapN (tropical:) [ To me are owing acknowledgments required by permanent badges of favours firmly fastened upon their necks: see 2]. (A.) [This use of qlAdp in a good sense is more common than the meaning (tropical:) A disgrace attaching constantly or a permanent badge of infamy: see Ham. p. 127.] -A2- qalaAy^idu Al$~iEori , (K,) and ↓ muqal~adaAtuhu , (L, K,) (assumed tropical:) Verses, or poems, that last throughout time. (L, K.) See 2. -A3- AlqilaAdapu A certain asterism. (See Albalodapu .)

definition: (tropical:) Difficulty;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) Difficulty; distress; affliction; trouble. (S, A, L, Msb, K.) Ex. waqaEa fiY kabadK He fell into difficulty, &c. (A.) So in the words of the Kur, [xc, 4,] laqado xalaqonaA A@loA_inosaAna fiY kabadK Verily we have created man in difficulty, &c., (S, L, Jel,) in a state in which he has to contend with the afflictions of the present life and the difficulties pertaining to the life to come: (Zj, * Jel:) or fY kbd here signifies, in a right and just state: (Aboo-Tálib, L:) or in an erect state, and in just proportion: (Fr; L:) or in an erect state, and walking upon his two legs; whereas other animals are not erect: or in the belly of his mother, with his head towards her head; in which state the child remains until near the birth, when it becomes inverted. (L.) ― -b2- And see kaAbidN and kabidN .

definition: , (S, L, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, L, Msb, K, &c.,) the most chaste and best known form of the word, (TA,) and ↓ kibodN , (S, L, Msb, K,) a contraction of the former, (Msb,) and ↓ kabodN , (S, L, K,) also a contraction of the first, (S,) [The liver; ] a certain black piece of flesh on the right of the lungs: (L:) fem., and sometimes masc.; (Fr, L, Msb, K;) or fem. only: (Lh, ISd, L, Msb:) pl. A^akobaAdN (S, L, Msb, K) and kubuwdN ; (L, Msb, K;) the latter seldom used. (Msb) ― -b2- Also, [the first,] (tropical:) The place of the liver, outside: (L;) the side. (K) It is said in a trad., fawaDaEa yadahu EalaY kabidiY , meaning, And he put his hand upon my side externally; or, upon the external part of my side, next the liver. (L.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) The inside of an animal, altogether. (Kr, ISd, K.) Sometimes used in this sense. (Kr, ISd.) ― -b4- (tropical:) The inside, meaning a cave, or ravine, of a mountain. (L.) ― -b5- kabidu AlA^aroDi (tropical:) The interior of the earth: (Msb:) or the minerals ( maEaAdin ) of the earth: (A:) or the gold and silver and the like that are in the mines of the earth: (L:) pl. A^akobaAdN (A, L) and kubuwdN . (L.) It is said in a trad. wataloqiY AlA^aroDu A^afolaA*a kabidihaA (tropical:) And the earth shall cast forth what is hidden in her belly, of treasures and minerals. (L.) ― -b6- (tropical:) The middle of anything, (A, L, Msb, K, *) and its main part. (L, K.) ― -b7- (tropical:) The middle of the sea. (L.) ― -b8- (tropical:) The middle of a butt for archers. (A, L.) ― -b9- daAruhu kabida najodK (tropical:) His house is in the middle of Nejd. (A.) ― -b10- kabidN ; (L;) in the K, ↓ kabadN ; but none [except F] says so; (MF;) The middle of a tract of sand, (L, K,) and its main part. (L.) ― -b11- kabidN ; (S, A, L, Msb;) in the K, ↓ kabadN ; but none [except F] says so; (MF;) and ↓ kabodN , and ↓ kabodaA='u , (K,) and ↓ kubayodaAtN , (S, A, L,) as though they had formed the dim. kubayodapN from kabidN , and then formed the pl.; (S, L;) in the K, kubayodaApN ; but this is wrong; (TA;) and ↓ kubayodaA='u , (L, Msb, K,) dim. of kabidN , contr. to rule, like suwayodaA='u ; (Msb;) [or dim. of kabodaA='u ;] (tropical:) The middle of the sky, (S, A, L, K,) and its main part: (L;) or [the meridian of the sky;] the middle of the sky, wherein is the sun at the time of its declining from the meridian: (L:) or the part of the middle of the sky which faces the spectator. (Lth, L, Msb.) ― -b12- kabidN (Lh, L; in the K, kabadN ;) (assumed tropical:) The air; (Lh, L, K;) as also ↓ kabodaA='u . (L.) ― -b13- kabidN (tropical:) of a bow, The handle: (S, A, Msb:) or the part a little above the handle, (Az, L, Msb,) against which the arrow goes: (Az, L:) or the part between the two extremities of the handle, and that along which the arrow runs: (S, L:) or the part [ midway ] between the two extremities of its suspensory string or cord or the like: (As, L, K:) [see rijolN :] or the space of a cubit from its handle: (L, K:) or each part where the thong of its suspensory string or the like is tied: (L:) in the bow is its kabid , which is the part [midway] between the two extremities of its suspensory string or the like; then, next to this, the kuloyap ; then, next to this, the A^abohar ; then, next to this, the TaAy^if ; then, the siy^ap , which is the curved part of each extremity. (As, L.) ― -b14- fulaAnN tuDorabN A_ilayoh A^akobaAdu AlA_ibili Such a one is a person to whom men journey seeking knowledge &c. (S, L, K.) [See an ex. in the first paragraph of art. Drb .] ― -b15- suwdN AlA^akobaAdi [ Black-livered men;] a designation of enemies, (As, S, L, K,) similar to Suhobu Als~ibaAli [q. v.]: (As, S, L:) they are so called because the effects of rancour, or malevolence, have [as it were] burnt their livers so that they have become black; the liver being the source of enmity. (L.)

definition: i. q. najomN , A star; an asterism; a constellation: as also ↓ kawokabapN : (S, K:) or Alkwkbp is an appellation given to the planet Venus; and for the rest of the stars, the masc. word kwkb is used:...
sourceDefinition: i. q. najomN , A star; an asterism; a constellation: as also ↓ kawokabapN : (S, K:) or Alkwkbp is an appellation given to the planet Venus; and for the rest of the stars, the masc. word kwkb is used: (Az:) but Venus is called also Alkwkb . (MF.) [Pl. kawaAkibu .] ― -b2- Accord. to Lth, kwkb is a quadriliteral-radical word; the w being a radical letter: it is also said to be from wkb , or from kwb ; though k is not one of the letters of augmentation; so that here it must be augmentative contrary to rule. (TA.) [But I rather think that it is an arabicized word, from the Hebrew כוֹכָב ; and that ignorance of its being so has caused the Arabs to dispute respecting its formation.] ― -b3- *ahabuwA taHota kul~i kawokabK They became dispersed [as though under every tract of heaven]. (AO, S, K.) ― -b4- kawokabN (assumed tropical:) Drops [ of dew ] that fall upon herbage in the night, (K,) and become like stars. (TA.) ― -b5- The source, or spring, of a well. (K.) ― -b6- Water. (El-Muärrij, K.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) The lustre, or brightness, or glistening, of iron. (S, K.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) A sword. (K.) ― -b9- A nail: (K:) [or more probably, (assumed tropical:) its head, as in Golius] ― -b10- kawokabN (AZ, K) and ↓ kawokabapN (TA) (assumed tropical:) A whiteness in the eye: (K:) a whiteness in the black part of the eye, whether the sight be gone in consequence thereof, or not. (AZ.) ― -b11- kawokabN A tract, such as is termed xiT~ap , differing in colour from the land in which it lies. (K.) ― -b12- (assumed tropical:) A youth nearly of the age of puberty: (K:) a youth who has attained the period of adolescence, and whose face has become beautiful, is called kawokabN mumotaliy^N (a full star), like as he is called badorN . (TA.) [See $aAdixN , and muTab~ixu .] ― -b13- (assumed tropical:) The chief, lord, or prince, and horseman, or cavalier, of a people. (K.) ― -b14- (assumed tropical:) A man with his arms; an armed man. (K.) ― -b15- (assumed tropical:) What is tall of plants. (K.) ― -b16- A mountain: (K [but Freytag mentions, that in some copies, for jabalN , is read xayolN , horses and horsemen, or a troop of horse: ]) or the main part thereof. (TA.) ― -b17- The greater part, chief part, main, gross, mass, or bulk, of a thing: (S, K:) as of herbage, water, an army. (TA.) ― -b18- (tropical:) The flower, or flowers, of a garden, or meadow. (TS, K.) ― -b19- The fuTor [ toadstool, or mushroom ], a well-known plant: (AHn, K:) I do not mention it, says AHn, from a learned man: but kwkb is [explained by lexicologists only as] the name of a well-known plant, called kwkbu AlA^aroDi : (L:) perhaps a species of the fuTor . (El-Mak- disee, cited by MF.) -A2- Vehemence of heat: (K:) the greater part of the heat. (TA.) ― -b2- The medicament called Taloq , q. v., [which defends the person who is anointed therewith from the burning of fire]. (K: explained by the words AlT~aloqu mina AlA^adowiyapi : in some copies of the K, mn AlA^awodiyapi . [This is wrong: kawokabu AlA^aroDi means Talc: see TalaqN .]) -A3- yawomN *uw kawaAkiba A day of difficulties, distresses, or calamities. (K.) -A4- kawokabN A place of con- finement. (K.)

AqmH [in the CK with x ]: (K:) or he sat in the manner of him who magnifies himself (S, L) in his own mind. (L.) A^akomaxuwA baA^owFA They flourished and increased in self exaltation: or taraAd~uwA . (L.) ― -b2- kamaxahu biAll~ijaAmi He pulled him in [i. e. a horse or the like] by the bridle and bit, in order to check or stop him; (L:) i. q. kabaHahu ; (K;) [or he pulled up his head by the bridle and bit ]. See kamaHa . -A2- kamaxa bihi , (K,) aor. , (L,) inf. n. kmoxN , (S, L,) He voided it, namely his excrement, or ordure; or voided it in a thin state; syn. salaHa . (S, K.) Some bread and kaAmaix [q. v. infra] were offered to an Arab of the desert, and he knew not the latter; so it was said to him, “ This is kAmx ; ” whereupon he said, “ I know that it is kAmx ; ” and added, A^ay~ukumo kamaxa bihi “ which of you voided it? ” Ay~km salaHa bh . (S.) ― -b2- kamaxa bisaloHihi , aor. and inf. n. as above, He (a camel) voided his excrement, or ordure, in a thin state. (L.)

Here lH~A is put in the acc. case as a denotative of state, because what precedes it is determinate. (S.) And you say huwa A@bonu Eam~K laH~K [ He is a cousin on the father's side, ] closely related, (S, K,) in an indeterminate phrase employing laH~K as an epithet to Eam~K . (S.) You say the same in the case of the fem. and dual and pl.; (S;) making no difference between the sing. and dual and pl. and fem. (L.) [See also dinoyFA ; and the contr., ZohrFA .]

sourceDefinition: see 1, in two places. ― -b2- Algz kalaAmahu , (A, K,) and Algz fiY kalaAmihi , (S, A, Msb, K,) signify alike: (K:) or the former, (tropical:) He made his speech, or language, enigmatical, or obscure; not plain: (A:) and the latter, (S, A,) or both, (K,) he made his meaning enigmatical, or obscure, in his speech, or language; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ lg~z : (A:) or the second, he used parabolical language: (Msb:) or both, he concealed a meaning different from that which he made apparent: or he was equivocal, or ambiguous, in his speech, or language, for the purpose of concealment: as in the following verse, cited by Fr: walam~aA raA^ayotu Aln~asora Eaz~a A^abona daA^uyapa waEa$~a$a fiY wakorayohi jaA$ato lahu nafosiY (tropical:) [ And when I saw that the vulture had overcome the raven, and nested in his nest, (lit., in his two nests,) my soul, or stomach, heaved thereat ]: the poet likens hoariness to the vulture, because of its whiteness [or grayness]; and youthfulness to the black raven, because the hair of youth is black. (TA.) You say also, Algz fiY yamiynihi (tropical:) He practised [ equivocation, or ambiguity, (see lug~ayozaY ,) or] concealment, [ by a mental reservation, or otherwise, ] towards the person sworn to, in his oath: the doing of which is forbidden. (A.)

And in like manner, yamiynN ↓ lug~ayozaA='u , accord. to Z, with teshdeed to the g mentioned by Sb with xul~ayoTaA='u , or, accord. to Az, without teshdeed, [ lugayozaA='u ,] which he regards as the dim. of the form with teshdeed, like as sukayotN is of suk~ayotN , (tropical:) An oath in which is equivocation, or ambiguity, and concealment [ by mental reservation or otherwise ]. (TA.)

(K.) -A2- See luwHN -A3- Any broad, or wide, and thin, thing, such as a board or plank or the like, of wood or of bone: (T, M, Msb, K:) pl. A^alowaAHN , and pl. pl. A^alaAwiyHu . (K.) (Sb.) ― -b2- A^alowaAHN i. q. lawaAy^iHu , q. v. ― -b3- The scapula or shoulder-blade, (T, S, Msb, K,) when it is written upon, or inscribed. sourceDefinition: [pl. of laAy^iHapN ] The parts of a thing that are apparent, and that show the signs thereof. (TA.) lawaAy^iHu and ↓ A^alowaAHN The external parts of a thing. (A.) lawaAHiY Al$~ayobi The apparent signs of hoariness, occurs in a verse of Khufáf Ibn-Nudbeh, for lawaAy^iH Al$yb . (TA.) ― -b2- Als~ilaAHi ↓ A^alowaAHu Shining, gleaming, or glistening, weapons; such as the sword, (S, K,) end the like, (K,) and the spear-head; (S;) generally meaning swords, because of their whiteness: (ISd:) or, as some say, the cases, or receptacles, in which are the swords together with their scabbards and suspensory belts or strings, because made of boards. (IB.) 'Amr Ibn-Ahmar ElBáhilee says, tumosiY kaA^alowaAHi Als~ilaAHi watuDo HiY kaA@lomahaApi SabiyHapa AlqaTori [ In the evening she is like shining weapons, (so accord. to the S.) or like sword-cases, (accord. to IB,) and in the early part of the day, after sunrise, she is like the wild cow on the morning of, or after, rain ]. IB says, that the poet means, in the evening she is lean, or slender, like a sword-case; but in the morning, like a wild cow, &c. (L.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. marojN , He (a beast of carriage) fed in a pasture. (Msb.) ― -b2- maraja , (aor. , S,) inf. n. marojN , He sent a beast of carriage to pasture: (S, K:) or left it [app. to pasture wheresoever it would ]: (Kt:) he pastured it; (TA;) and so ↓ A^amoraja : (Kt, K:) or the latter signifies he left it to go wheresoever it would [app. to pasture ]. (TA.) -A2- maraja , inf. n. marojN , (tropical:) He mixed [a thing with another thing, or two things together]. (K.) ― -b2- maraja AlbaHorayoni , [Kur., xxv., 55; and lv., 19,] (tropical:) He hath mixed the two seas, (Zj, K,) so that they meet together, the sweet and the salt, yet so that the salt does not overpass its bounds and mix itself with the sweet: (Zj:) or He hath sent them forth so that they afterwards meet together: but this is only said by the people of Tihámeh: (Fr:) or, as also ↓ A^amoraja , (this latter form is used by some, Akh, S, and is the form used by the grammarians, TA,) He hath let them flow freely, yet so that one does not become mixed with the other: (S, K:) He hath made them flow. (IAar, with reference to the former verb.) ― -b3- maraja , aor. , (assumed tropical:) He marred, or spoiled, his affair. (TA.) ― -b4- mrija , aor. , inf. n. marajN , (tropical:) It (e. g. a deposit, S, and a covenant, and religion, TA) became corrupt; impaired; spoiled; marred; or disordered. (S, K.) ― -b5- marija , aor. , inf. n. marajN ; (S, K;) and maraja ; but the former is the more approved; (TA;) It (a ring, on the finger, S, and an arrow, TA) became unsteady; (S, K,) like jarija . (S.) ― -b6- marija , aor. , inf. n. marajN , (tropical:) It (religion, and an affair, S, and a covenant, TA) became in a confused and disturbed state, (S, K, TA,) so that one found it difficult to extricate himself from perplexity therein. (TA.) It (a covenant), was in a confused state, and little observed. (TA.) ― -b7- marija Aln~aAsu The people became confused. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , a coll. gen. n.; n. un. with p ; (L;) Small pearls: (AHeyth, T, S, K:) or the like thereof: or large pearls: (El-Wáhidee:) or coral, bus~a*N , which is a red gem: or red beads; which is the meaning assigned to the word by Ibn-Mes'ood, and is agreeable with the common acceptation thereof; or, accord. to Et-Tarasoosee (or, as in the TA, Et-Turtooshee, and so correctly accord. to MF) certain red roots that grow up in the sea, like the fingers of the hand: [vulgarly pronounced murojaAn :] the n is said to be an augmentative letter, because there is no Arabic word of the measure faEolaAlN , except such as are reduplicative, like xaloxaAlN : but Az says, I know not whether it be a triliteral-radical word or a quadriliteral: (Msb:) IKtt asserts it to be of the measure faEolaAlN . (TA.) ― -b2- Also A leguminous plant that grows in the season called Alr~abiyE , (K,) rising to the height of a cubit, with red twigs, and broad round leaves, very dense, juicy, satisfying thirst, and having the property of making the milk of animals that feed upon it to become abundant: (TA:) n. un. with p . (K.)

definition: , aor. , (TK,) inf. n. makosN , (Sh, A, K,) He diminished, or deducted from, a thing; (Sh, * A, * K, * TK;) syn. of the inf. n. taqoSN . (Sh, A, K.) Thus Sh explains makos in the saying of Jábir...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (TK,) inf. n. makosN , (Sh, A, K,) He diminished, or deducted from, a thing; (Sh, * A, * K, * TK;) syn. of the inf. n. taqoSN . (Sh, A, K.) Thus Sh explains makos in the saying of Jábir Ibn-Jinnee Et-Taghlibee: A^afiY kul~i A^asowaAqi AlEiraAqi A_itaAwapN wafiY kul~i maA baAEa A@moruw^N makosu dirohami [ Is there bribing in every one of the markets of El-'Irák, and in the case of everything that a man has sold the deducting of a dirhem? ]. (TA.) [Hence,] you say, makasa fiY AlbayoEi , aor. and inf. n. as above; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and ↓ mAks , inf. n. mumaAkasapN and mikaAsN : (S, Mgh, Msb:) both signify He diminished, or deducted from, the price in the selling, or buying: (Msb:) or both signify he desired, or demanded, a diminution of, or deduction from, the price in selling or buying: (Mgh, TA, *) or the former signifies he collected property in selling or buying: (K: [but from what I find in the other lexicons, I think it probable that an early copyist has perverted the text of the K here by making a transposition; writing makasa fiY AlbayoEi yamokisu makosFA jabaY maAlFA wAalmakosu Aln~aqoSu waAlZ~ulomu for makasa yamokisu makosFA jabaY maAlFA waAlmakosu fY AlbayoEi Aln~aqoSu waAlZ~ulomu : in the TK we find jnY mAlA , which is certainly a mistake:]) or makosN signifies the diminishing ( A_inotiqaAS ) of the price of a commodity: (M, TA:) and ↓ mikaAsN , the acting with mutual niggardliness in bargaining; or, accord. to EshShereeshee, the vying in acuteness between a seller and buyer, the former demanding a price and the latter offering less, time after time, until they agree to a reduced price. (Har, p. 586 .) You say also, mukisa , meaning, He (a man) suffered a diminution, or deduction, in selling or buying and the like. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps, or the reverse may be the case,] He wronged a man; treated him, or used him, wrongfully, injuriously, or tyrannically. (A, * K, * TK. [In the first and second, only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is mentioned.]) ― -b3- [Hence, also, app.,] He (the mak~aAs , Mgh, Msb) collected a tax; syn. jabaY ; [particularly, the tax termed makos :] (S, * M, Mgh, * Msb [in the first and third of which, only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is mentioned:]) or he collected property. (A.) Hence the saying, (Mgh,) in a trad., (S,) laA yadojulu SaAHibu makosK Aljan~apa (S, Mgh) [ The taker of the tax termed mks will not enter paradise ]; meaning, the Ea$~aAr . (TA.)

definition: Blood: or the blood of the heart: (S, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: Blood: or the blood of the heart: (S, K:) pl. muhajN . (A.) An Arab of the desert is related to have said, dafanotu muhojatahu , meaning damahu : so in the S: but in a marginal note in a copy of that work, it is said that this is a mistake; and that the correct expression, as mentioned by IKt and others, is dafaqotu muhojatahu I poured forth, or shed, his blood: and so it is in the copies of the A. (TA.) In like manner, dafaqa All~`hu muhojatahu (tropical:) May God destroy him! (A. [See also dafqa .]) ― -b2- Also, (tropical:) The soul, or spirit. (S, K.) Ex. xarajato muhojatuhu (tropical:) His soul went forth, or departed. (S.) A^unotuziEato muhojatuhu (tropical:) His soul was torn from him. (K.) ― -b3- Also, (tropical:) One's self: the best of one's self, and one's powers, efforts, endeavours, or energy. (L.) Ex. ba*alotu lahu muhojatiY (tropical:) I gave, or gave up, myself, and the best of my powers, efforts, endeavours, or energy, to him, or it. (T.) ― -b4- Also, (tropical:) The purest, choicest, or best, of anything. (L.) ― -b5- Also, (assumed tropical:) The heart. (MF.)

definition: [coll. gen. n.] A certain species of trees: (S:) poppy-plants; syn. $ajaru Alxa$oxaA$ : and other trees of a large kind: or the trees called xr~wb [see below]: (K:) or a kind of thorny trees, having...
sourceDefinition: [coll. gen. n.] A certain species of trees: (S:) poppy-plants; syn. $ajaru Alxa$oxaA$ : and other trees of a large kind: or the trees called xr~wb [see below]: (K:) or a kind of thorny trees, having branches and leaves, with a fruit of the kind called jirow , i. e., round; called in 'Omán gAf : n. un. with p : AHn says that there are two species of ynbwt ; one of these is a kind of thorny and short trees, also called xar~uwb [q. v.] having a fruit resembling a bubble, in which are red grains, having an astringent effect upon the bowels, used as a medicine; the other species is a large species of trees: ISd says, An Arab of the desert, of the tribe of Rabeea, described to me the ynbwtp as [ a tree ] resembling a large apple-tree, the leaves of which are smaller than those of the apple, having a fruit smaller than the zuEoruwr , intensely black and intensely sweet, with grains, or stones, which are put into scales, or balances: [evidently meaning the carob, or locust-tree, (see xar~uwb ,) whence our term “ carob, ” applied to a small weight, the twenty-fourth part of a grain]. (L [See gaAfN and furofuwrN ].)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. nasojN , He, or it, drew, collected, or gathered, together a thing: drew and joined, or adjoined, one thing to another. This is the primary signification. (L.) ― -b2- nasajati Alr~iyHu Alwaraqa wAlha$iyma The wind gathered together the leaves and the dry fragments of plants. Hence, accord. to some, nasaja Alv~awoba , because the weaver adjoins the warp to the woof. (TA.) ― -b3- nasajati Alr~iyHu Alt~uraAba (tropical:) The wind drew the dust together. (TA.) ― -b4- nasajati Alr~iyHu AlmaA='a , and Alr~amola , and Alt~uraAba , and rasoma Ald~aAri , (tropical:) The wind made rippling lines, in cross directions, upon the water, and the sand, and the dust, and [ with dust ] upon the traces of the dwelling. (A.) [And so] TaraAy^iqu kaA@loHubuki ↓ A_inotasajato (tropical:) Rippling lines were made, in cross directions, by the wind, upon the water, (S, * A,) and the sand, and the dust, and the traces of the dwelling. (A.) ― -b5- nasajati Alr~iyHu Alr~aboEa (tropical:) The wind, blowing in cross directions, obliterated the traces of the place where persons had alighted, (S, K,) [by covering it with dust or sand in such a manner as that it might be likened to a web]. ― -b6- nasaja (tropical:) It (a spider) wove, or spun, its web. (A.) ― -b7- nasaja Alv~awoba , aor. , and , (S, K,) inf. n. nasojN , (S,) He wove the piece of cloth, or the garment. (TA, &c.) And nasaja sayorFA He plaited a thong. (TA, in art. nsE .) ― -b8- nasaja Al$~iEora (tropical:) He wove, or composed verses. (TA.) ― -b9- nasaja AlkalaAma (tropical:) He (a liar, TA,) forged speech. (K.) ― -b10- Also, (tropical:) He explained, or expounded, language; syn. lax~aSahu . (K.) ― -b11- nasajati Aln~aAqapu fiY sayorihaA (tropical:) The she-camel moved her legs quickly in going along. (TA.)

definition: Smitten with the horn and so killed: fem.
sourceDefinition: Smitten with the horn and so killed: fem. with p : (L, K:) pl. naToHaY (L) and naTaAy^iHu : (Lh, L:) you say also naEojapN naTiyHN , as well as nTyHp . (L.) ― -b2- Also naTiyHapN A sheep or goat (Az) smitten with the horn and so killed. (Az, S,) and of which the flesh is therefore unlawful to be eaten: (Az:) the p is added because it is made a subst., not an epithet: (Az:) or because the quality of a subst. predominates in it, as in the case of fariysapN and A^akiylapN and ramiy~apN . (S.) ― -b3- naTiyHN and ↓ naATiHN (tropical:) What comes to thee from before thee, (or faces thee, L,) of birds and wild animals (S, L, K) &c., which one rouses by throwing a stone or by crying out, and from the course of which one augurs evil or good: (L:) contr. of qaEiydN . (S.) [The nTyH or ↓ nATH is of evil omen.] ― -b4- Hence, (TA,) naTiyHN (tropical:) An unfortunate, or unlucky, man. (K.) ― -b5- naTiyHN A horse having a blaze, or white mark on his face, extending to one of his ears, which is deemed unlucky: (L:) or a horse having on his forehead two circular or spiral curls of hair ( daAy^irataAni ), which are disliked: (S, L, K:) if there be but one, it is called daAy^irapu All~aTaApi ; and this is not disliked; (S;) or it is called laTomapN ; and the horse, laTiymN . (L.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Ks, S, A, Msb, K,) and , (S, A, K,) inf. n. nagoDN (S, Msb, K) and nuguwDN (S, K,) and nagaDaAnN and nagaDN , (K,) It was or became, in a state of motion, commotion, agitation, or convulsion; it shook; shook about; wabbled; tottered; wagged; nodded; syn. taHar~aka , (S, A, Msb, K,) and AiDoTaraba , (A, K,) fiY A@rotijaAfK ; (TA;) as also ↓ AngD (Msb, K) and ↓ tng~D : (K:) it is said of a man's head; (S, TA;) and also, (S, A,) with nagoDN and nagaDaAnN for its inf. ns., (S,) of a camel's saddle, (S, A,) and of the central incisor (S, TA) of a child, (S,) or of any tooth, as also ↓ the last of the verbs above mentioned; (A;) and of other things; (Msb, TA;) nagoDN signifying any moving in a shaking or tremulous or convulsive manner ( fiY A@rotijaAfK ); (S, TA;) and nagaDato and ↓ tanag~aDato , said of a tooth, being syn. with rajafato . (A.) ― -b2- Also, inf. n. nagaDaAnN , He, or it, was, or became, disquieted, agitated, or violently agitated. (TA.) ― -b3- nagaDuwA A_ilaY AlEaduw~i (tropical:) They rose and hastened and went forth to, or towards, the enemy. (A, TA.) ― -b4- nagaDa also signifies (assumed tropical:) It (a thing, TA) was, or became, dense: (so in some copies of the K) or much in quantity: (so in other copies of the K:) or much in quantity, and dense. (TA.) And (tropical:) It (a cloud) was, or became, dense, and then became ready to rain, and was seen to move about, one part into another, without its going along: (S:) or was seen to become ready to rain, without motion, not travel-ling along: (A:) or it travelled along. (IF.) [See naAgiDN , below.] ― -b5- nagaDa A^amoruhu (assumed tropical:) His affair, or case, was, or became, in a weak, or unsound, state; syn. wahaY . (TA.) -A2- See also 4, in two places.

A^afn ;) and so does ↓ tnAqS : (TA:) [or this last signifies it lost somewhat, decreased, &c., gradually; contr. of tzAyd .] It is said in a trad., (Mgh,) $ahoraA EiydK laA yanoquSaAni , (Mgh, K,) i. e. Ramadán and Dhu-l-Hijjeh, (Mgh,) meaning, Two months of festival are not defective virtually ( fiY AlHukomi ) though they be defective in number [of days]; (K;) i. e. let no doubt occur in your hearts when ye fast nine and twenty days [instead of thirty]; nor if there happen a mistake respecting the day of the pilgrimage, will there be any deficiency in your performance of the rites thereof: (TA:) or, as some say, two months of festival will not be defective in one and the same year; but Et- Taháwee disapproves of this explanation: some say that the meaning is, that though they be defective, or one of them be so, yet their recompense will be complete. (Mgh.) It is also said in a trad., A_in~a AlEamala fiY Ea$ori *iY AlHij~api laA yanoquSu vawaAbuhu Eam~aA fiY $ahori ramaDaAna [ Verily the deed that is done on the tenth of Dhu-l-Hijjeh, the recompense thereof will not fall short of that which is in the month of Ramadán: for naqaSa Eano ka*aA means It fell short of such a thing. ] (Mgh.) Dwz , and another in art. wks :] this is the [most] chaste form of the verb, and is that which occurs in the Kur.: (Msb:) ↓ AnqShu also signifies the same; (M, Msb, K;) and so does ↓ nq~Shu , (Msb, K,) inf. n. tanoqiySN : (TA:) but these two are of weak authority, and do not occur in chaste language: (Msb:) and ↓ AntqShu signifies the same: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) or this last signifies he took from it by little and little; as also ↓ tnq~Shu . definition: The Ealam [or ornamental border ] of a piece of cloth: (T, S, M, A, K:) pl.
sourceDefinition: The Ealam [or ornamental border ] of a piece of cloth: (T, S, M, A, K:) pl. A^anoyaArN . (M, K) It is related that 'Omar disliked it, (TA,) and that he forbade it. (T, TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (tropical:) The side ( Tur~ap ) of a road: (T:) or the side ( jaAnib ) and wide or widening part ( Sador ), of a road. (so in some copies of the K, and in the TA: but in some copies of the former, “ or ” is put in the place of “ and: ”) or the conspicuous part of a road: (S:) or the conspicuous furrowed part of a road. (M, A, K.) ― -b3- The unwoven end ( hudob ) of a piece of cloth. (Ibn-Keysán, M, K) ― -b4- The woof of a piece of cloth. (T, S, A, Mgh, K.) When cloth is woven with a double woof, ( EalaY niyrayoni ,) it is more close in texture and more lasting. (S.) vawobN *uw niyrayoni signifies A piece of cloth strongly woven, with a double woof: (A:) or a piece of cloth woven with double thread: (T:) and [in like manner] ↓ vawobN munay~arN a piece of cloth woven with a double woof; (Lh, M, K;) i. e., with a double thread: (TA:) also called dayaAbuw* , (T, TA,) an arabicized word; (TA;) in Persian duwo Puwdo , or duwo buwdo , (as in different copies of the K,) or duwo baAfo . (T.) This mode of weaving is termed mutaA='amahN , which is the making the woof of a double thread, and putting two threads together upon the Haf~ap [which here means the yarn-beam, on which the warp is rolled]. (T.) ― -b5- Hence, naAqapN daAtu niyrayoni (tropical:) A she-camel having an accession of fat upon former fat: (T:) or having, upon her, layers ( SaHaAy^if ) of fat; as also *aAtu A^anoyaArK : (A:) or advanced in years, yet having some remains of strength; (M, K;) and sometimes the epithet is applied in like manner to a woman: (M:) and naAqapN *aAtu A^anoyaArK a she-camel having thick flesh. (TS.) Also, rajulN *uw niyrayoni (tropical:) A man whose strength is double the strength of his companion: (S:) or strong and firm. (A.) And raA^aYN *uw niyrayoni (tropical:) Right opinion or counsel. (A.) And HarobN *aAtu niyrayoni (tropical:) Violent war. (T, A.) -A2- The canes ( qaSab ) and threads ( xuyuwTap ) [ in a loom ], when they are put together: (M, K:) [it is a coll. gen. n., of which the n. un. is with p , as appears from what here follows:] ↓ niyrapN is a subst., signifying the threads and canes, ( xuyuwTap and qaSabap , [or warp and, app., cane-roll, on which the warp is rolled when put into the loom, and from which it is gradually unrolled as the work proceeds, ] when they are put together: when they are separate, the threads are called xuyuwTapN ; and the cane, qaSabapN , or, if a staff, EaSFA : (AZ, Sh, T:) niyrapN is also explained as signifying one of the implements of the weaver, with which he weaves; namely, the transverse piece of wood [ in the loom; the same as is described above]. (T.) In the following verse of an unknown poet, ↓ taqosimu A^usotiy~FA lahaA binayori wataDoribu Aln~aAquwsa wasoTa Ald~ayori [ She divides warp that she has with cane-rolls, and beats the nákoos in the midst of the convent ], the author may mean biniyrK , and may have altered the word by necessity; or ↓ nayorN may be a dial. form of niyru . (M.) One says of a man who neither harms nor profits, maA A^anota bisataApK walaA luHomapK walaA niyrapK (tropical:) [lit. Thou art not a warp nor a woof nor a cane-roll ]. (T.) [See also a similar saying voce Haf~apN .] -A3- [The yoke of a bull; the piece of wood that is upon the neck of the bull, together with its apparatus: (M, K:) or the piece of wood that is placed transversely upon the necks of the two bulls (T, S) yoked together for ploughing: (T:) called niyru Alfad~aAni : (S:) pl. [of pauc.] A^anoyaArN and [of mult.] niyraAnN : (S, M, K:) of the dial. of Syria. (M.)

sourceDefinition: [in the senses assigned to it in what here follows] is an inf. n. of which the verb [ haAyaTa ] is obsolete. (L.) You say, maA zaAla fiY hiyaATK wamiyaATK He ceased not to be in a state of approaching, or drawing near, and retiring to a distance: (K:) or hiyaATN signifies the act of advancing: (Lh:) or hiyaATN and miyaATN respectively signify the most vehement driving in coming to water, and the most vehement driving in returning from water; and the meaning is, going and coming: (Aboo-Tálib:) or both signify the being in a state of commotion, tumult, or disturbance; as some say, arising from their saying “ No, by God, ” and “ Yes, by God: ” (TA:) [it is also said that] muhaAyaTapN [which is likewise an inf. n. of maAyaTa ] signifies the act of crying out, or vociferating; and raising a clamour, or confused noise; [(see also 1;) and so, app., hiyaATN ; for it is immediately added,] one says, waqaEa Alqawomu fiY hiyaATK wamiyaATK [as though meaning the people, or company of men, fell into vociferating, &c.]. (S.) bayonahumaA muhaAyaTapN is also said to signify Between them two is low, faint, or gentle, speaking. (TA.) [See miyaATN .] ― -b2- Accord. to IAar, hAyThu signifies He esteemed him weak. (TA.)

definition: He retained; he withheld. (Msb.) ― -b2- He maintained: he was tenacious, or niggardly. ― -b3- He, or it, held fast a thing: and arrested it. ― -b4- A^amosakahu He held, retained, detained,...
sourceDefinition: He retained; he withheld. (Msb.) ― -b2- He maintained: he was tenacious, or niggardly. ― -b3- He, or it, held fast a thing: and arrested it. ― -b4- A^amosakahu He held, retained, detained, restrained, stayed, confined, imprisoned, or withheld, him. (K.) ― -b5- A^amosaka Eani AlA^amori He held, refrained, or abstained, from the thing. (Msb.) ― -b6- A^amosakahu He grasped it, clutched it, laid hold upon it; or seized it, ( qabaDa Ealayohi ) biyadihi with his hand: (Msb:) or he took it; or took it with his hand, ( A^axa*ahu ,) namely, a rope, &c.: (Mgh:) or he held, or clung, to it: (TA:) [as also bihi ↓ tamaska ]. Also, A^amosaka bihi signifies [ the same; or] he laid hold upon, or seized, somewhat of his body, or what might detain him, as an arm or a hand, or a garment, and the like: but A^amosaqahu may signify he withheld him, or restrained him, from acting according to his own free will. (Mugh, art. bi .) ― -b7- A^amosaka baTonahu [ It bound, or confined, his belly (or bowels )]: said of medicine. (S, O, Msb, K; all in art. Eql .) ― -b8- AlA_imosaAk , in relation to taHojiyl : see an unusual application of it in art. Tlq , conj. 4.

definition: A time, whether night or day;
sourceDefinition: A time, whether night or day; (Msb;) time absolutely, whether night or not, little or not: this is the proper signification: (Kull, p. 390:) and day, meaning the period from the rising of the sun to its setting; (Lth, TA:) the time when the sun is above the earth: this is the common conventional acceptation: (Kull, ubi suprà:) and the period from the second [ or true ] dawn to sunset: (Msb, Kull:) this is the legal acceptation: (Kull:) and a civil day: the period of the revolution of the greatest firmament. (Kull) ― -b2- Also, An accident, or event; syn. kawonN and kaAy^inapN . Ex., niEoma A@loA^axu fulaAnN fiY Alyawomi A_i*aA nazala binaA Excellent is the brother, such a one, in the case of the accident, when it befalls us. (T.) ― -b3- See nahaArN . ― -b4- yaA^otiynaA yawoma yawoma He comes to us day after day, i. e., every day: (Sharh esh-Shudhoor:) and yawoma yawomK . (In a verse cited by IJ. in Mz, sect. on the Haqiyqap and majaAz .) ― -b5- yawomN A dayjourney, or day's journey. ― -b6- A day, as in our phrase “ he won the day; ” meaning contest, fight, or battle: I render it a day [ of conflict ]. ― -b7- A^ay~aAmu AlEarabi The [ days, (agreeably with an English, as well as Arabian, usage,) meaning] conflicts ( waqaAy^iE ) of the Arabs. (ISk, T.) ― -b8- Aibonu yawomihi He who thinks [ only of the present day, ] not of the morrow. (Er-Rághib. in TA, art. bnY .) ― -b9- yawomu Al$~ak~i : see $ak~N . ― -b10- bayon AlA^ay~aAmi and fiymaA bayona AlA^ay~aAmi : see nadorapN , in two places.
